children.title: Partial-Solution Search Spaces
children.top_down_role: Search trees organized by partial discrete decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Solution Search Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain implicit enumeration by consistent partial assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\) be the feasible set of a finite-domain problem. A partial-solution search tree labels each node \(v\) by an index set \(I_v\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and values \(a^v_i\in D_i\) for \(i\in I_v\). Its completion set is \[X_v=\{x\in X:x_i=a^v_i\text{ for every }i\in I_v\}.\] The root has \(I_v=\varnothing\). Each child extends its parent's assignment consistently, and the children satisfy \(X_v=\bigcup_{w\in\operatorname{ch}(v)}X_w\), ordinarily with pairwise-disjoint completion sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each node fixes some discrete decisions; its descendants consistently extend them, and its children collectively enumerate every feasible completion.
assumptions_latex: \(n<\infty\) and each \(D_i\) is finite.
\(X\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_v=\bigcup_{w\in\operatorname{ch}(v)}X_w\), with every child representing a consistent extension.

notation.meaning: Feasible completions of the partial assignment at node v.

children.title: Region-Partition Search Spaces
children.top_down_role: Search trees organized by recursively restricted regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Region-Partition Search Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound search represented by recursively restricted feasible regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the original search region. A region-partition search tree assigns each node \(v\) a region \(R_v\), with \(R_{\mathrm{root}}=X\). For every child \(w\) of \(v\), \(R_w\subseteq R_v\), and branching is exhaustive when \[R_v\cap X=\bigcup_{w\in\operatorname{ch}(v)}(R_w\cap X).\] If the sets on the right are pairwise disjoint, branching is a partition; otherwise it is a covering. Thus every feasible point retained below \(v\) lies in at least one child region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node represents a restricted region, and its child regions cover—or partition—all feasible points retained at that node.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the original feasible search region.
The search tree is rooted and every nonroot node has one parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_v\cap X=\bigcup_{w\in\operatorname{ch}(v)}(R_w\cap X)\).

notation.meaning: Search region associated with node v.

children.title: State-Space Search Representations
children.top_down_role: Search trees organized by combinatorial states and continuation classes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by identifying histories whose future-relevant continuation signatures differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K(h_1)\ne K(h_2)\) but \(\sigma(h_1)=\sigma(h_2)\), then a single outgoing-transition description cannot represent both histories exactly: it must omit a feasible or objective-relevant continuation of one history, admit an invalid continuation for the other, or assign incorrect continuation data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging histories with different feasible or objective-relevant futures makes the state representation inexact.
assumptions_latex: The state uses one common transition description and continuation data for all histories mapped to that state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma(h_1)=\sigma(h_2)\land K(h_1)\ne K(h_2)\Rightarrow\text{the quotient representation is not exact}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsound State Merging

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision histories represented by signatures sufficient for all feasibility- and objective-relevant continuations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H be a set of finite decision histories and let K(h) denote the feasibility- and objective-relevant continuation signature after h. A state representation is a map \(\sigma:H\to Q\) satisfying \[\sigma(h_1)=\sigma(h_2)\implies K(h_1)=K(h_2).\] Transitions induced by admissible next decisions unfold from \(\sigma(\varnothing)\) into a history tree; identifying equal states forms a quotient graph in which every represented history has the same future-relevant continuation signature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state may merge histories only when its label retains all information needed to determine their feasible, objective-relevant futures; the search tree is the unfolding of the resulting state transitions.
assumptions_latex: Each history has a well-defined feasibility- and objective-relevant continuation signature \(K(h)\).
State transitions are defined only for admissible next decisions and preserve the signature invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma(h_1)=\sigma(h_2)\Rightarrow K(h_1)=K(h_2)\).

notation.meaning: Future-relevant continuation signature after history h.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuation-Sufficient State Quotients
State-Space Search Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search histories compressed into states having equivalent admissible continuations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be the set of finite decision histories and let \(C(h)\) denote the admissible continuations after \(h\in H\). A state-space representation consists of a state set \(Q\), a map \(\sigma:H\to Q\), and transitions \(T(q,d)\), such that \[\sigma(h_1)=\sigma(h_2)\implies C(h_1)=C(h_2).\] A terminal state has no admissible continuation. Unfolding the transitions from \(q_0=\sigma(\varnothing)\) produces a search tree whose nodes are histories, while histories mapped to the same state share the same continuation class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state summarizes a decision history sufficiently to determine all admissible continuations; unfolding state transitions yields the search tree.
assumptions_latex: Every finite history \(h\in H\) has a well-defined continuation set \(C(h)\).
Transitions preserve admissibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma(h_1)=\sigma(h_2)\) implies that \(h_1\) and \(h_2\) have identical admissible continuations.

children.title: Node Ancestry
children.top_down_role: Parentage, depth, sibling position, and descendant relationships within the search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Ancestry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ancestry in a rooted subproblem tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a rooted tree \(T=(V,E)\), a node \(u\) is an ancestor of \(v\) if \(u\) lies on the unique path from the root to \(v\). It is a proper ancestor when additionally \(u\ne v\). Writing \(u\preceq v\) for ancestry, the relation is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive. The parent of a nonroot node \(v\) is the unique maximal proper ancestor of \(v\) under \(\preceq\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node is an ancestor of another precisely when it lies on the unique root-to-node path.
assumptions_latex: \(T=(V,E)\) is a rooted tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\preceq v\) exactly when \(u\) lies on the root-to-\(v\) path.

notation.meaning: Node u is an ancestor of node v.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Branch and Bound p. 113

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Branch and Bound p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Depth, Children, Siblings, and Rooted Subtrees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard structural coordinates and relations derived from ancestry in a rooted subproblem tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=(V,E)\) be rooted at \(r\). The depth of \(v\) is \(d(v):=|P(v)|\), the number of edges on the unique path from \(r\) to \(v\). Thus \(d(r)=0\), and if \(u\) is the parent of \(v\), then \(d(v)=d(u)+1\). A node \(v\) is a child of \(u\) exactly when \(u\) is its parent; distinct nodes are siblings exactly when they have the same parent. The rooted subtree at \(u\) has node set \(V_u:=\{v\in V:u\preceq v\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Depth counts root-path edges, children invert the parent relation, siblings share a parent, and a rooted subtree consists of a node and all its descendants.
assumptions_latex: \(T=(V,E)\) is a rooted tree with root \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(v)=|P(v)|\), and \(V_u=\{v\in V:u\preceq v\}\).

notation.meaning: Node set of the subtree rooted at u.

knowledge_statements.title: Depth, Children, Siblings, and Rooted Subtrees

children.title: Inherited Local Domains
children.top_down_role: Restrictions passed from ancestor subproblems into a node.

knowledge_statements.title: Inherited Local Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A node inherits every restriction imposed along its ancestry path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the root domain, and let each tree edge \(e\) carry a branch restriction \(B_e\). The local domain inherited by node \(v\) is \[D_v=D\cap\bigcap_{e\in P(v)}B_e,\] where \(P(v)\) is the edge set on the root-to-\(v\) path. Consequently, if \(u\preceq v\), then \(P(u)\subseteq P(v)\) and \(D_v\subseteq D_u\). Thus descendants cannot recover points excluded by an ancestral restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node's domain is the root domain intersected with every branch restriction on its ancestry path, so descendant domains are nested.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the root search domain.
Each edge restriction \(B_e\) is a subset of the ambient decision space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\preceq v\implies D_v\subseteq D_u\).

notation.meaning: Inherited local domain at node v.

children.title: Branch-Induced Domain Changes
children.top_down_role: Local restrictions attributable to the disjunction that created a child node.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Induced Domain Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Child domains result from intersecting the parent domain with branch predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose node \(v\) has local domain \(D_v\), and branching selects predicates with satisfaction regions \(B_{v,1},\ldots,B_{v,k}\). The child \(w_j\) inherits \[D_{w_j}=D_v\cap B_{v,j}.\] A valid exhaustive branch satisfies \(D_v=\bigcup_{j=1}^kD_{w_j}\); a partitioning branch additionally satisfies \(D_{w_i}\cap D_{w_j}=\varnothing\) whenever \(i\ne j\). Hence the only domain change on edge \((v,w_j)\) is the added branch restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching changes a child's domain by adding one branch predicate; valid children cover the parent domain and may partition it.
assumptions_latex: \(D_v\) is the parent's inherited local domain.
The branch regions \(B_{v,j}\) cover \(D_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{w_j}=D_v\cap B_{v,j}\) and \(D_v=\bigcup_{j=1}^kD_{w_j}\).

notation.meaning: Local domain at the parent node.
Region satisfying branch predicate j at node v.
Child created by branch predicate j.

children.title: Active-Node Frontier
children.top_down_role: Generated subproblems awaiting processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Node Frontier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generated subproblems currently awaiting selection and processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At search time \(t\), let \(G_t\) be the generated nodes, \(P_t\) the processed nodes, and \(C_t\) the nodes whose subtrees have been closed. The active-node frontier is \[F_t=\{v\in G_t\setminus P_t:\text{no ancestor of }v\text{ belongs to }C_t\}.\] Every unresolved generated leaf belongs to \(F_t\). Selecting a node removes it from the frontier for processing; branching inserts its generated children, whereas closure inserts none.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active frontier contains generated, unprocessed nodes not covered by a closed ancestor; selection removes nodes and branching adds children.
assumptions_latex: The search state records generated, processed, and closed nodes at time \(t\).
Closure of a node closes its entire represented subtree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_t=\{v\in G_t\setminus P_t:\text{no closed node is an ancestor of }v\}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage invariant maintained by an exact active-node frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_0\) be the root feasible region. Suppose each branching operation replaces a selected node region \(X_v\) by child regions covering every unresolved feasible point of \(X_v\), and every node removed without children has a valid closure or terminal-resolution certificate. Then every root-feasible point unresolved at time \(t\) belongs to \(X_v\) for some \(v\in F_t\): \[X_0^{\mathrm{unresolved}}(t)\subseteq\bigcup_{v\in F_t}X_v.\] If active nodes form an antichain and every branching disjunction partitions its parent feasible region, the active-node regions are pairwise disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correctly maintained frontier covers every unresolved feasible point; with partitioning branches, its active regions are also pairwise disjoint.
assumptions_latex: Every branch covers all unresolved feasible points of its selected parent.
A node is discarded without children only after valid closure or terminal resolution.
The maintained active nodes form a tree antichain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_0^{\mathrm{unresolved}}(t)\subseteq\bigcup_{v\in F_t}X_v\).

notation.meaning: Feasible region represented by node v.
Root-feasible points not validly resolved by time t.

knowledge_statements.title: Unresolved-Region Frontier Invariant

children.title: Closed-Node Status
children.top_down_role: Terminal processing states assigned to generated subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Node Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for declaring a minimization search node permanently resolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, a node \(v\) has closed status when a valid certificate establishes at least one of the following: its feasible set \(X_v\) is empty; a valid lower bound \(L_v\) satisfies \(L_v\ge U\), where \(U\) is the incumbent value; or a feasible point \(x_v\in X_v\) satisfies \(f(x_v)=L_v\). In the last case the incumbent is first updated with \(f(x_v)\). No child of a closed node need be generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node closes when it is infeasible, cannot improve the incumbent, or contains a feasible point attaining its valid local lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes \(f\) over the node feasible set \(X_v\).
\(L_v\le\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)\) is valid.
\(U\) is the value of a known feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node requires no further branching when infeasibility, bound dominance, or exact local optimality is certified.

notation.meaning: Feasible set represented by node v.
Valid lower bound at node v.

source_refs.locator: 7.4 LP-Based Branch and Bound p. 120

source_witnesses.locator: 7.4 LP-Based Branch and Bound p. 120

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality Cutoff Boundary for Solution Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference between closing a node when one optimum suffices and retaining ties when every optimal solution must be enumerated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_v\) be a valid lower bound for minimization node \(v\), and let \(U\) be a feasible incumbent value. If only one globally optimal solution or the optimal value is required, \(L_v\ge U\) safely closes \(v\). If every feasible solution of value \(U\) must be enumerated, equality is generally insufficient: \(L_v=U\) may permit undiscovered \(x\in X_v\) with \(f(x)=U\). In that regime, bound closure requires \(L_v>U\), unless separate evidence proves that no required tied solution remains in \(X_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A non-strict cutoff is safe when one optimum suffices, but equality cannot generally prune a node when every tied optimum must be enumerated.
assumptions_latex: \(L_v\le\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)\).
\(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{enumeration of all optima}\implies (L_v=U\not\Rightarrow\text{safe closure})\).
knowledge_statements.title: Equality Cutoff Boundary for Solution Enumeration

children.title: Pruned-Subtree Extent
children.top_down_role: Descendant regions excluded when a node is closed.

knowledge_statements.title: Pruned-Subtree Extent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure propagates from a node to every represented descendant subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) be closed and let \(w\) be any descendant of \(v\). Domain inheritance gives \(X_w\subseteq X_v\). If closure is by infeasibility, then \(X_w=\varnothing\). If closure is by a bound \(L_v\ge U\), every \(x\in X_w\) satisfies \(f(x)\ge L_v\ge U\). If closure is by a feasible point attaining \(L_v\), no descendant can improve that point. Therefore the pruned extent is the entire subtree rooted at \(v\), including ungenerated descendants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing a node safely prunes its entire rooted subtree because every descendant represents a subset of the closed node's feasible region.
assumptions_latex: \(X_w\subseteq X_v\) for every descendant \(w\) of \(v\).
Node \(v\) has a valid closure certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every descendant of \(v\) may be omitted; the pruned extent is the subtree rooted at \(v\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set represented by node v.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Branch and Bound p. 113

children.title: Closure-Reason Records
children.top_down_role: Stored grounds supporting removal of nodes from further exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure-Reason Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable records justifying why a node and its subtree were closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A closure-reason record for node \(v\) is a tuple \((v,r,c)\), where \(r\) identifies a reason and \(c\) is supporting data. It is valid if it verifies one predicate: \(r=\mathrm{infeasible}\) and \(c\) certifies \(X_v=\varnothing\); \(r=\mathrm{bound}\) and \(c=(L_v,U)\) verifies \(L_v\le\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)\) and \(L_v\ge U\); or \(r=\mathrm{exact}\) and \(c=(x_v,L_v)\) verifies \(x_v\in X_v\) and \(f(x_v)=L_v\). A valid record certifies that further branching below \(v\) is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closure record stores the node, reason, and checkable data proving infeasibility, bound dominance, or exact local optimality.
assumptions_latex: The underlying problem is a minimization problem.
Any recorded \(L_v\) is independently validated as a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid \((v,r,c)\) certifies that no descendant of \(v\) can produce a better required outcome.

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound for node v.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence of verified minimization closure records when the incumbent improves and the recorded node model remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a valid bound-closure record for node \(v\) verifies \(L_v\le\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)\) and \(L_v\ge U\). If the minimization incumbent improves to \(U'\le U\), then \(L_v\ge U'\), so the record continues to justify closure. A verified infeasibility record and a verified exact-local-optimum record likewise remain valid while the recorded node region, objective, and certificate interpretation are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified closure record remains sufficient after a minimization incumbent improves, provided the node model and certificate interpretation have not changed.
assumptions_latex: The original closure record is valid.
\(U'\le U\) under minimization.
The recorded node region, objective, and certificate semantics are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((L_v\ge U\land U'\le U)\Rightarrow L_v\ge U'\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound for node v.
Incumbent value stored or referenced by the original record.

children.title: Incumbent Solution Record
children.top_down_role: Identity, provenance, and retained metadata of the accepted feasible solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Solution Record
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best feasible solution discovered so far in a minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_t\subseteq X\) be the finite set of feasible solutions discovered by time \(t\) in a minimization search. If \(S_t\ne\varnothing\), an incumbent solution record is a pair \((x_t^{\mathrm{inc}},U_t)\) satisfying \[x_t^{\mathrm{inc}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S_t}f(x),\qquad U_t=f(x_t^{\mathrm{inc}}).\] If \(S_t=\varnothing\), the record contains no solution and uses \(U_t=+\infty\). The record must retain enough information to verify feasibility and recompute its objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The incumbent record stores the best feasible solution among the finitely many solutions discovered so far and its objective value, or an empty record with infinite value.
assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes \(f\) over \(X\).
At each finite search time \(t\), the discovered-solution set \(S_t\subseteq X\) is finite.
Every member of \(S_t\) has verified feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(S_t\ne\varnothing\), \(x_t^{\mathrm{inc}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S_t}f(x)\) and \(U_t=f(x_t^{\mathrm{inc}})\).

notation.meaning: Finite set of feasible solutions discovered by time t.

children.title: Primal-Bound Value
children.top_down_role: Objective benchmark induced by the current incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Bound Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent objective as a monotone upper bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization problem \(z^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), define the primal-bound value at time \(t\) by \[U_t=\inf_{x\in S_t}f(x),\] using \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), where \(S_t\subseteq X\) is the set of feasible solutions found by time \(t\). Then \(z^*\le U_t\). If discovered solutions are retained, \(S_t\subseteq S_{t+1}\), so \(U_{t+1}\le U_t\). Thus the primal bound is a valid, nonincreasing upper bound on the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best discovered feasible objective is an upper bound on the minimum and can only improve as feasible solutions accumulate.
assumptions_latex: \(z^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).
\(S_t\subseteq X\) contains all retained feasible solutions discovered by time \(t\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the minimization problem.
Retained feasible solutions discovered by time t.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximization analogue of the seed's minimization primal-bound value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z^*=\sup_{x\in X}f(x)\), let \(S_t\subseteq X\) be the retained feasible solutions discovered by time \(t\), and define \(L_t:=\sup_{x\in S_t}f(x)\), with \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\). Then \(L_t\le z^*\). If \(S_t\subseteq S_{t+1}\), then \(L_t\le L_{t+1}\le z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For maximization, the best retained feasible objective is a nondecreasing lower bound, initialized to negative infinity when no feasible solution is known.
assumptions_latex: \(z^*=\sup_{x\in X}f(x)\).
\(S_t\subseteq S_{t+1}\subseteq X\).

Retained feasible solutions discovered by time t.

children.title: Incumbent Replacement Events
children.top_down_role: Search-state changes caused by acceptance of a superior feasible solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Replacement Events
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict incumbent replacement for a minimization search; ties retain the existing incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization problem with incumbent solution-value pair \((x^I,U)\), where \(x^I\) is feasible and \(U=f(x^I)\). A newly obtained feasible point \(y\) triggers an incumbent replacement event exactly when \(f(y)<U\). The event updates the state by \[(x^I,U)\leftarrow (y,f(y)).\] If \(f(y)\ge U\), the incumbent state is unchanged. Before any feasible point is known, use \(U=+\infty\), so the first feasible point necessarily triggers replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible candidate replaces the incumbent exactly when its objective value is strictly smaller; the first feasible candidate replaces an infinite initial bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is minimized over the original feasible set.
Every replacement candidate \(y\) has been verified feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(y)<U\iff (x^I,U)\leftarrow(y,f(y))\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a node \(v\), let \(X_v\) be its feasible region and define \(z_v:=\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)\). A local node-bound state is a pair \((\ell_v,s_v)\), where \(\ell_v\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) is the stored bound value and \(s_v\in\{\mathrm{pending},\mathrm{certified},\mathrm{invalidated}\}\) is its computational status. The status \(s_v=\mathrm{certified}\) requires \[\ell_v\le z_v.\] If \(R_v\supseteq X_v\) and \(\underline f_v(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X_v\), then \(\ell_v:=\inf_{x\in R_v}\underline f_v(x)\) may be certified. Pending or invalidated values must not be used as valid node bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-bound state stores a candidate lower-bound value and its computational status; only a certified value may be used as a lower bound on the node optimum.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-wide minimization lower-bound state including both the incumbent and unresolved frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the incumbent value, let \(\mathcal F\) be an active frontier covering every unresolved feasible solution, and let \(\ell_v\) be a valid lower bound on node region \(X_v\). Define \[L=\min\bigl(\{U\}\cup\{\ell_v:v\in\mathcal F\}\bigr).\] Then \(L\le z^*\). If \(\mathcal F=\varnothing\), this convention gives \(L=U\); hence a finite incumbent closes the bound at its value, while \(U=+\infty\) represents certified infeasibility after every region has been validly closed. Replacing a node by exhaustive children whose bounds are at least the parent bound, tightening node bounds, or validly deleting fathomed nodes cannot decrease \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complete global lower bound is the minimum of the incumbent value and every active-node lower bound; this also defines the empty-frontier terminal states.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute gap and explicitly normalized relative-gap state for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite incumbent value \(U\) and a valid global lower bound \(L\le U\), define \[g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L.\] For any explicitly declared scale function \(s(U,L)>0\), define the corresponding relative gap by \[g_{\mathrm{rel}}^{(s)}=\frac{U-L}{s(U,L)}.\] Common scale conventions are not interchangeable and must state their denominator and zero-scale handling. If no finite incumbent exists, both reported gaps are \(+\infty\). For finite bounds, \[0\le U-z^*\le g_{\mathrm{abs}},\] so zero absolute gap certifies exact optimality and \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}\le\varepsilon\) certifies additive \(\varepsilon\)-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute gap is incumbent minus certified global lower bound; a relative gap is that difference divided by an explicitly declared positive scale.

For finite endpoints, \(L\le z^*\le U\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and symmetric-scale relative gaps for a minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite incumbent upper bound \(U\) and a valid global lower bound \(L\le U\), define the absolute and relative optimality-gap states by \[g_{\mathrm{abs}}:=U-L,\qquad g_{\mathrm{rel}}:=\frac{U-L}{\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}}.\] Both gaps are nonnegative. If no incumbent exists, set \(U=+\infty\) and both gaps to \(+\infty\). When \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=0\), the incumbent is globally optimal; termination at tolerance \((\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_r)\) is valid when \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}\le\varepsilon_a\) or \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon_r\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of global validity when aggregation omits an unresolved frontier region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the aggregated groups omit an active node \(u\), their minimum bound need not bound solutions in \(X_u\). In particular, if every included group has bound \(b\) while \(X_u\) contains a feasible point of value less than \(b\), reporting \(b\) for the entire unresolved frontier is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregation that omits an unresolved node can overstate the bound for the full frontier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of certified bounds after grouping active nodes into covering blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be an active frontier, with valid node lower bounds \(\ell_v\). Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) cover \(\mathcal F\), and let \(\gamma_j\le\inf\{f(x):x\in\bigcup_{v\in G_j}X_v\}\). Then \[L_{\mathrm{grp}}=\min_{1\le j\le m}\gamma_j\] is valid for every solution represented by the frontier. Nodewise aggregation is the singleton-block regime. Relative to stored node bounds, choosing \(\gamma_j=\min_{v\in G_j}\ell_v\) preserves the nodewise aggregate exactly; any smaller certified group bound remains valid but weakens it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active nodes may be aggregated individually or in covering groups; taking the minimum certified group bound is valid, and group minima preserve the nodewise result exactly.
assumptions_latex: Every active node belongs to at least one group \(G_j\).
Each \(\gamma_j\) is a valid lower bound on the union of node regions in its group.
The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathrm{grp}}\le\inf\{f(x):x\in\bigcup_{v\in\mathcal F}X_v\}.

Frontier Aggregation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cover-based aggregation of local lower bounds into one global bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) cover the unresolved feasible region, and suppose \(\beta_i\le\inf_{x\in C_i}f(x)\) for every \(i\). Then the valid global bound represented by this cover is \[L=\min_{1\le i\le m}\beta_i.\] Nodewise aggregation takes the \(C_i\) to be active node regions. Grouped aggregation replaces several nodes by any covering group region with its own certified bound. A coarser aggregation remains valid but may weaken \(L\); an aggregation is exact relative to stored local information when each group bound equals the minimum bound of its constituent nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any cover of the unresolved region yields a global lower bound by taking the minimum certified bound over its covering pieces.
assumptions_latex: \(\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\) contains every unresolved feasible point.
Each \(\beta_i\) is valid on its associated region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=\min_i\beta_i\le z^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a minimization node \(v\), let \(X_v\) be the mixed-integer feasible set defined by linear constraints and branching restrictions. Its linear-programming relaxation \(P_v\) is obtained by retaining those linear restrictions while replacing each required integrality condition by the corresponding continuous bounds. Thus \(X_v\subseteq P_v\), and, with \[\ell_v^{\mathrm{LP}}:=\inf\{c^{T}x:x\in P_v\},\qquad z_v:=\inf\{c^{T}x:x\in X_v\},\] one has \(\ell_v^{\mathrm{LP}}\le z_v\). If \(P_v=\varnothing\), then \(X_v=\varnothing\), so LP infeasibility certifies node infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping node integrality restrictions produces an LP superset whose optimum is a valid node lower bound; LP infeasibility proves node infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the node problem \(z_v:=\inf\{f(x):x\in X_v,\ g(x)\le0\}\), where \(g:X_v\to\mathbb R^m\) and the inequalities \(g(x)\le0\) are dualized. For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define \[\theta_v(\lambda):=\inf_{x\in X_v}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda^Tg(x)\bigr),\qquad L_v^{\mathrm{Lag}}:=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}\theta_v(\lambda).\] Weak duality gives \(\theta_v(\lambda)\le z_v\) for every admissible multiplier and hence \(L_v^{\mathrm{Lag}}\le z_v\). Any evaluated value \(\theta_v(\lambda)\) is therefore a valid node lower bound, even when the dual supremum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing node inequalities yields a multiplier problem whose every evaluated dual value, and hence its supremum, lower-bounds the node optimum.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural properties of the fixed node Lagrangian dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(\theta_v(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X_v}\{f(x)+\lambda^Tg(x)\}\) is concave on \(\mathbb R_+^m\). If the infimum is attained at \(x_\lambda\) and the relevant values are finite, then \[\theta_v(\mu)\leq\theta_v(\lambda)+g(x_\lambda)^T(\mu-\lambda)\qquad(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m),\] so \(g(x_\lambda)\) is a supergradient of \(\theta_v\) at \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The node dual function is concave, and constraint values at a globally minimizing Lagrangian subproblem solution form a supergradient.
assumptions_latex: The Lagrangian subproblem attains its finite infimum at \(x_\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_v\) is concave and \(g(x_\lambda)\in\partial^+\theta_v(\lambda)\).

Then \[L_v^{\mathrm{Lag}}=z_v.\] Without convex regularity, and particularly when \(X_v\) retains integrality, weak duality does not imply equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slater-regular convex node problems have no Lagrangian duality gap; integer or nonconvex nodes need not be exact.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonlinear minimization node with feasible set \(X_v\), objective \(f:X_v\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and value \(z_v:=\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)\), a convex nonlinear relaxation is a convex set \(C_v\supseteq X_v\) together with a convex function \(\underline f_v:C_v\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfying \(\underline f_v(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X_v\). Its optimal value \[\ell_v^{\mathrm{cvx}}:=\inf_{x\in C_v}\underline f_v(x)\] obeys \(\ell_v^{\mathrm{cvx}}\le z_v\). Convex relaxations of nonconvex constraints may equivalently be incorporated into \(C_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex feasible superset and convex objective underestimator define a convex program whose value lower-bounds the nonlinear node optimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex NLP bound and consistent underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-underestimator relaxation of a box-restricted mixed-binary nonlinear subproblem and the associated refinement-consistency definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P[U]=\min\{h_0(x):h_i(x)\le 0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ x\in[\underline x,\bar x]\cap U,\ x_B\text{ binary}\}\), define \(R[U]=\min\{\breve h_{0,U}(x):\breve h_{i,U}(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ x\in[\underline x,\bar x]\cap U\}\), where \(\breve h_{i,U}\) is a convex underestimator of \(h_i\) over \([\underline x,\bar x]\cap U\). The NLP bound is \(\underline v_{\mathrm{NLP}}(U)=\operatorname{val}(R[U])\) if \(R[U]\) is feasible and \(+\infty\) otherwise. The underestimator \(\breve h_{i,U}\) is consistent if, for every nested sequence \(\{U^j\}\) of partition elements converging to \(\widehat x\), \(\lim_{j\to\infty}\max_{x\in U^j}|h_i(x)-\breve h_{i,U^j}(x)|=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The node relaxation replaces the objective and constraint functions by convex underestimators and omits the binary restriction. Its NLP bound is the relaxation value when feasible and positive infinity otherwise. An underestimator is consistent when its maximum approximation error vanishes along every nested sequence of partition elements converging to a point.
assumptions_latex: x\in[\underline x,\bar x]\cap U
x_B\text{ is binary in }P[U]
\breve h_{i,U}(x)\le h_i(x)\quad\forall x\in[\underline x,\bar x]\cap U,\quad i=0,\ldots,m
\breve h_{i,U}\text{ is convex},\quad i=0,\ldots,m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \underline v_{\mathrm{NLP}}(U)=\begin{cases}\operatorname{val}(R[U]),&R[U]\text{ is feasible},\\+\infty,&R[U]\text{ is infeasible},\end{cases}\quad\text{and consistency requires }\lim_{j\to\infty}\max_{x\in U^j}|h_i(x)-\breve h_{i,U^j}(x)|=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) contain every feasible point of the search region under consideration, and let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). A relaxation function \(h:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is globally underestimating on \(D\) exactly when \[h(x)\le f(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in D.\] Consequently, for any node \(v\) with feasible set \(X_v\subseteq D\) and any relaxation set \(C_v\) satisfying \(X_v\subseteq C_v\subseteq D\), one has \[\inf_{x\in C_v}h(x)\le\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x).\] The same underestimator can therefore support every such node without node-specific revalidation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An underestimator valid throughout a common domain yields a valid lower bound for every node and relaxation region contained in that domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Globally Underestimating Relaxations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity Does Not Extend Beyond the Certified Domain

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inequality \(h\le f\) certified only on \(D\) gives no bound guarantee for a node whose relaxation set is not contained in \(D\). For example, let \(D=[0,1]\), let \(f(x)=0\), and define \(h(x)=0\) on \(D\) but \(h(2)=1\). For \(C_v=X_v=\{2\}\), one obtains \(\inf_{C_v}h=1>0=\inf_{X_v}f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global underestimator is global only relative to its certified domain; extrapolation can invalidate the bound.

C_v\nsubseteq D

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_v\) be a convex node domain, let \(X_v\subseteq D_v\) be the node feasible set, and suppose \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q f_i(x)\) for every \(x\in X_v\). For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), let \(f_i^{\mathrm{env}}\) denote the convex envelope of \(f_i\) on \(D_v\), namely the greatest convex function on \(D_v\) that does not exceed \(f_i\) there. Then \[\ell_v^{\mathrm{env}}:=\inf_{x\in D_v}\sum_{i=1}^q f_i^{\mathrm{env}}(x)\] satisfies \(\ell_v^{\mathrm{env}}\le z_v\), where \(z_v:=\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)\). Replacing exact envelopes by certified convex underestimators on \(D_v\) preserves validity, though it may weaken the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representing each objective term by its convex envelope on a node domain and minimizing their sum produces a valid node lower bound; certified convex underestimators remain valid substitutes.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node \(v\) with feasible set \(X_v\), a scalar \(\beta_v\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) is a valid local lower bound exactly when \[\beta_v\le\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x).\] Equivalently, \(f(x)\ge\beta_v\) for every \(x\in X_v\). This certificate is restricted to \(X_v\): it transfers automatically to a descendant \(w\) when \(X_w\subseteq X_v\), but it need not be valid for a region containing points outside \(X_v\). If \(X_v=\varnothing\), then \(\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)=+\infty\), so every finite scalar is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local lower bound is valid precisely when every feasible point in that node has objective value at least the bound; the bound transfers to descendant regions contained in the node region.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Approximate Objective Is Not a Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional example separating approximate primal feasibility from lower-bound validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the relaxation be \(R=[0,2]\), the node region be \(F=\{\tfrac12\}\subseteq R\), and minimize \(f(x)=x\). The relaxation optimum is \(z_R=0\), the node optimum is \(z_v=\tfrac12\), and the feasible approximate relaxation point \(\widetilde x=2\) has \(f(\widetilde x)=2>z_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective at a feasible but nonoptimal relaxation point can exceed even the node optimum and is not a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\widetilde x)=2>z_v=\tfrac12\).
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Approximate Objective Is Not a Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Interpretation of Intermediate Relaxation Output
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes intermediate feasible primal objectives from certified dual lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization relaxation with primal value \(z_R\) and a weak dual problem, a primal-feasible iterate \(x^k\) satisfies \(f(x^k)\geq z_R\) and therefore is not, merely by primal feasibility, a lower bound. A dual-feasible iterate \(y^k\) with dual objective \(d(y^k)\) satisfies \[d(y^k)\leq z_R\leq z_v,\] so its verified dual objective is a valid node lower bound even before either side is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intermediate primal-feasible objectives are upper estimates of the relaxation optimum, while verified dual-feasible objectives are lower-bound certificates.
assumptions_latex: The node feasible set is contained in the relaxation region.
The primal and dual pair satisfies weak duality.
The claimed primal or dual feasibility is verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(y^k)\leq z_R\leq z_v\), whereas primal feasibility alone does not imply \(f(x^k)\leq z_R\).

notation.meaning: objective value of a verified dual-feasible iterate

assumptions_latex: The relaxation optimum is \(z_R=\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\), and the node feasible set satisfies \(F\subseteq R\).
An algorithm returns an approximate relaxation point \(\widetilde x\in R\) or an approximate scalar \(\widetilde z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a certified error direction, neither \(f(\widetilde x)\leq z_R\) nor \(\widetilde z\leq z_R\) follows, so the reported value is not automatically a node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes approximate relaxation output from a certified lower bound in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, relaxation validity gives \(z_R\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). A feasible approximate relaxation point instead satisfies \(f(\widetilde x)\geq z_R\), so its objective value need not be a lower bound. Likewise, an approximate scalar \(\widetilde z\) is usable only when a certificate supplies a known \(\varepsilon\geq0\) such that \(\widetilde z-\varepsilon\leq z_R\); then \(\widetilde z-\varepsilon\) is a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate relaxation objective is not automatically a lower bound; validity requires a certified one-sided error guarantee.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Verification of Rational LP Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent post-verification procedure for rational node LP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rational data in \(\inf\{c^Tx:Ax\geq b\}\), convert a candidate multiplier to an exact rational vector \(y\), verify \(y\geq0\) and \(A^Ty=c\) exactly, and publish \(b^Ty\). Passing these checks certifies \(b^Ty\leq z_R\); failure to pass yields no bound from that candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact rational checking can qualify an LP dual certificate independently of the floating-point solver that produced it.
