The node feasible set is contained in the LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\geq0\land A^Ty=c\Rightarrow b^Ty\leq z_R\leq z_v\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Verification of Rational LP Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-aware qualification of an approximate LP dual multiplier over a bounded relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(R=\{x:Ax\geq b,\ l\leq x\leq u\}\) and \(z_R=\inf_{x\in R}c^Tx\). For a verified \(y\geq0\), let \(r=c-A^Ty\) and define \[q=b^Ty+\sum_{i=1}^n\min\{r_i l_i,r_i u_i\}.\] Then \(q\leq z_R\). If \(F\subseteq R\), also \(q\leq z_v\). The certificate remains numerically qualified when all quantities and comparisons are enclosed by outward-rounded interval or exact rational arithmetic so that the published value does not exceed the mathematical \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual residual can be conservatively minimized over variable bounds to turn an approximate nonnegative LP multiplier into a verified node lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(l,u\) are finite verified bounds with \(l\leq u\).
\(y\geq0\) is verified.
Arithmetic publishes a value no greater than the exact displayed expression.
\(F\subseteq R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\leq z_R\leq z_v\).
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Corrected LP Bound Certificate

assumptions_latex: The node feasible set satisfies \(F\subseteq R\), where \(R\) is the relaxation region.
A verifier establishes \(q\leq\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\) under its stated arithmetic tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), so \(q\) is a qualified node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualification means one-sided validity has been verified despite numerical approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reported relaxation value is numerically qualified as a node lower bound when a checkable certificate, interpreted with explicit feasibility, residual, and rounding tolerances, establishes \[q\leq\inf_{x\in R}f(x).\] Since \(F\subseteq R\), it follows that \[q\leq\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\] Qualification attaches to the certified value \(q\), not necessarily to the solver's unadjusted objective report.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound is numerically qualified when a verifiable, tolerance-aware certificate proves it lies below the relaxation optimum and therefore below the node optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerically Qualified Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication from a certified relaxation lower bound to a node lower bound is correct, and certificate is the appropriate content kind. No source is provided for what constitutes a checkable certificate under feasibility, residual, rounding, and arithmetic tolerances; that substantive numerical qualification requires authoritative support.

children.title: Bound-Safety Margins
children.top_down_role: Protective qualification of bounds near pruning thresholds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety-margin interpretation through a certified enclosure of the exact lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If verified numerical analysis encloses an exact valid node lower bound \(L\) in \([\underline L,\overline L]\), then \(\underline L\leq L\leq z_v\). Thus \(\underline L\) is a safe lower bound and bound fathoming against incumbent \(U\) is justified only when \(\underline L\geq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower endpoint of a certified enclosure is a safe node bound and is the endpoint usable for pruning.
assumptions_latex: \([\underline L,\overline L]\) is a certified enclosure of an exact valid lower bound \(L\).
The node is minimized and \(U\) is a feasible incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline L\leq z_v\), and \(\underline L\geq U\) certifies bound fathoming.

notation.meaning: certified lower endpoint of the bound enclosure
certified upper endpoint of the bound enclosure

knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Enclosed Bound Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example demonstrating why an uncertified reported bound cannot be compared directly with the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact node lower bound be \(L=0\), the reported value be \(\widetilde L=0.1\), and the feasible incumbent be \(U=0.05\). Direct comparison gives \(\widetilde L\geq U\) and would prune, although \(L<U\); the node may still contain an improving point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small upward error in a reported lower bound can reverse the pruning decision.
assumptions_latex: No certified correction or enclosure accompanies \(\widetilde L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde L\geq U\) does not imply \(L\geq U\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Upward-Error Pruning Example

assumptions_latex: A computed scalar \(\widetilde L\) has a certified overestimation error at most \(\delta\geq0\).
The exact valid node lower bound is denoted \(L\), with \(\widetilde L\leq L+\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L^{\mathrm{safe}}=\widetilde L-\delta\leq L\), and pruning is valid only when \(L^{\mathrm{safe}}\geq U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive one-sided safety margin for minimization-bound pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the numerical analysis certifies \(\widetilde L-L\leq\delta\) for some \(\delta\geq0\), define the conservative bound \[L^{\mathrm{safe}}=\widetilde L-\delta.\] Then \(L^{\mathrm{safe}}\leq L\), so it preserves lower-bound validity. With incumbent value \(U\), the node may be fathomed by bound only if \(L^{\mathrm{safe}}\geq U\). Subtracting an arbitrary margin without a justified error envelope does not itself certify validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a certified overestimation margin produces a safe lower bound; bound pruning must compare the incumbent with this adjusted value.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Safety Margins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive correction is mathematically valid under the stated certified overestimation envelope, and certificate fits the safety-margin leaf. The record lacks a source establishing the applicable numerical error model and certification conditions, so the operational claim remains source-dependent.

children.title: Unresolved Solver Statuses
children.top_down_role: Ambiguous node outcomes that cannot safely support ordinary pruning conclusions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safe Handling of Unresolved Relaxation Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage-preserving node policy after a relaxation solve returns no closure certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When a relaxation solve is unresolved, first validate any independently returned lower bound or infeasibility certificate. If none supports closure, retain the node as unresolved, retry with a certified procedure, or branch only through an exhaustive valid disjunction while preserving all resulting children. Do not delete the node solely because the relaxation solve stopped.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without independent closure evidence, unresolved nodes must remain represented in the search or be replaced by exhaustive children.
assumptions_latex: The search must preserve every unresolved feasible solution.
Any branching disjunction used is exhaustive over the node region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Search coverage is preserved despite the unresolved relaxation status.
knowledge_statements.title: Safe Handling of Unresolved Relaxation Solves

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Same Unresolved Label, Opposite Feasibility Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract counterexample family showing why an unresolved status has no universal feasibility meaning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A time or iteration limit can be reached on one instance whose node region is nonempty and on another whose node region is empty before either fact is certified. Therefore the same unresolved termination label is compatible with \(F\neq\varnothing\) and \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same limit status can occur on both feasible and infeasible nodes, so the label alone decides neither case.
assumptions_latex: The status contract reports only that a resource limit was reached.
knowledge_statements.title: Same Unresolved Label, Opposite Feasibility Outcomes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent boundary between an unresolved termination label and mathematical subtree-closure evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A termination label whose contract supplies neither certified infeasibility nor a certified one-sided bound has no mathematical implication that the node is infeasible or dominated. Such a label cannot by itself justify fathoming. Independently returned evidence may still close the node if that evidence separately satisfies the applicable infeasibility or bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unresolved status is not a closure certificate, although independent certified evidence returned with it may still be usable.
assumptions_latex: The status contract provides no certified optimality, infeasibility, or one-sided bound conclusion.
Exact subtree closure is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{unresolved status}\not\Rightarrow\text{node fathoming}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Status–Evidence Separation

assumptions_latex: A relaxation solver terminates without a certificate of optimality, infeasibility, or a certified one-sided bound.
The search algorithm requires logically valid subtree closure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node cannot be fathomed solely from the unresolved status or its associated unqualified objective value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to limits, numerical failures, interruptions, and ambiguous termination codes lacking certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A status such as iteration limit, time limit, numerical failure, interruption, or unknown has no universal mathematical implication about \(F\) or \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Unless separate output certifies infeasibility or supplies a valid lower bound \(L\geq U\), the status cannot justify fathoming. The node must remain open, be solved by another certified procedure, or be closed only through independent valid evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unresolved solver status does not certify infeasibility or bound dominance, so it cannot alone justify closing a subtree.
knowledge_statements.title: Unresolved Solver Statuses

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the core caution is sound: an unresolved status alone supplies no universal infeasibility or dominance certificate. A source is nevertheless required because the meanings and guarantees of termination statuses are solver- and interface-dependent.

children.title: Subtree-Closure Criteria Family
children.top_down_role: Canonical grounds for closing a node and its descendants.

children.title: Fathoming by Infeasibility
children.top_down_role: Subtree closure based on infeasibility evidence.

assumptions_latex: The node subproblem has feasible region \(F_v\).
A valid certificate establishes \(F_v=\varnothing\).
Every descendant feasible region \(F_w\) satisfies \(F_w\subseteq F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every descendant \(w\), \(F_w=\varnothing\); hence the subtree rooted at \(v\) may be fathomed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical subtree closure from certified infeasibility of the node subproblem.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a valid infeasibility certificate establishes \(F_v=\varnothing\), then every descendant \(w\) also satisfies \(F_w=\varnothing\), because branching yields \(F_w\subseteq F_v\). Consequently, no feasible solution can occur in the subtree rooted at \(v\), and that subtree may be removed from the search without changing the global feasible set or optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified infeasibility of a node makes every descendant infeasible, so the entire subtree can be closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Fathoming by Infeasibility

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fathoming from Infeasibility of a Valid Outer Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The relaxation may strictly contain the node region; certified emptiness and containment suffice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_v\subseteq R_v\), where \(R_v\) is a valid outer relaxation of the node feasible region. If \(R_v=\varnothing\) is certified, then \(F_v=\varnothing\). Because every descendant region satisfies \(F_w\subseteq F_v\), the subtree rooted at \(v\) may be fathomed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified emptiness of a valid outer relaxation proves the node and all its descendants infeasible.
assumptions_latex: F_v\subseteq R_v
R_v=\varnothing\text{ is certified}
F_w\subseteq F_v\text{ for every descendant }w
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_v=\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad F_w=\varnothing\text{ for every descendant }w

notation.meaning: valid outer relaxation of the node

knowledge_statements.title: Fathoming from Infeasibility of a Valid Outer Relaxation

children.title: Fathoming by a Resolving Relaxation Solution
children.top_down_role: Subtree closure when the node relaxation resolves the restricted problem.

assumptions_latex: The node feasible set \(F_v\) is contained in a relaxation region \(R_v\).
A point \(x^R\in R_v\) attains \(\inf_{x\in R_v}f(x)\).
The relaxation optimizer also satisfies \(x^R\in F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^R)=\inf_{x\in F_v}f(x)\), so \(x^R\) resolves the node and its subtree may be fathomed after incumbent processing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relaxation solution that is feasible for the restricted integer or mixed-integer node problem.

source_refs.locator: 7.4 LP-Based Branch and Bound p. 120

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(F_v\subseteq R_v\), relaxation optimality gives \(f(x^R)\leq\inf_{x\in F_v}f(x)\). Feasibility \(x^R\in F_v\) gives the reverse inequality, hence \[f(x^R)=\inf_{x\in F_v}f(x).\] Thus \(x^R\) is an optimal solution of the node subproblem. After recording it as an incumbent candidate, no descendant exploration is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an optimal relaxation solution is feasible for the node's original restrictions, it is node-optimal and resolves the subtree.
knowledge_statements.title: Fathoming by a Resolving Relaxation Solution

source_witnesses.locator: 7.4 LP-Based Branch and Bound p. 120

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Node Feasibility Without Relaxation Optimality Is Insufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of resolving-solution fathoming; an arbitrary relaxation-feasible point may supply an incumbent but does not resolve the node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_v\subseteq R_v\) and \(x\in F_v\). Without a certificate that \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in R_v}f(y)\), node feasibility alone does not imply \(f(x)=\inf_{y\in F_v}f(y)\). For \(F_v=R_v=\{0,1\}\) and \(f(z)=z\), the feasible point \(x=1\) is not node-optimal. It therefore cannot justify resolving-solution fathoming by itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point feasible for the node resolves it only when the point is also certified optimal for the containing relaxation.
assumptions_latex: F_v\subseteq R_v
x\in F_v
x\notin\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in R_v}f(y)\text{ is possible}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in F_v\centernot\implies f(x)=\inf_{y\in F_v}f(y)
knowledge_statements.title: Node Feasibility Without Relaxation Optimality Is Insufficient

children.title: Fathoming by Bound Dominance
children.top_down_role: Subtree closure based on comparison with the incumbent bound.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem and \(U=f(\bar x)\) for a globally feasible incumbent \(\bar x\).
The node has a valid lower bound \(L_v\leq\inf_{x\in F_v}f(x)\).
The certified comparison satisfies \(L_v\geq U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No point in \(F_v\) improves the incumbent, so the subtree rooted at \(v\) may be fathomed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimization criterion; strict comparison may be required when all optimal solutions must be enumerated.

source_refs.locator: 7.4 LP-Based Branch and Bound p. 120

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in F_v\), validity and bound dominance imply \[f(x)\geq\inf_{y\in F_v}f(y)\geq L_v\geq U=f(\bar x).\] Therefore the subtree contains no solution with objective value strictly better than the incumbent, and it may be fathomed when the task is to return one optimal solution and its value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node can be closed when its valid lower bound is no better than the feasible incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.title: Fathoming by Bound Dominance

source_witnesses.locator: 7.4 LP-Based Branch and Bound p. 120

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization cutoff for a search whose declared target is additive-\(\varepsilon\) optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=f(\bar x)\) for a globally feasible incumbent, let \(L_v\leq\inf_{x\in F_v}f(x)\), and let \(\varepsilon\geq0\). If \(L_v\geq U-\varepsilon\), then every \(x\in F_v\) satisfies \(f(x)\geq U-\varepsilon\). The node may therefore be fathomed when solutions improving the incumbent by at most \(\varepsilon\) need not be distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For additive-epsilon optimality, a node may be closed when its certified lower bound is at least the incumbent minus epsilon.
assumptions_latex: U=f(\bar x),\quad \bar x\text{ is globally feasible}
L_v\leq\inf_{x\in F_v}f(x)
\varepsilon\geq0
L_v\geq U-\varepsilon
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in F_v,\quad f(x)\geq U-\varepsilon
knowledge_statements.title: Additive-Tolerance Bound Fathoming

children.title: Relational State-Pruning Family
children.top_down_role: Subtree closure based on relations among generated subproblems.

children.title: Dominance-Based Pruning
children.top_down_role: Closure based on one generated subproblem rendering another unnecessary.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general sufficient certificate for minimization-state dominance; other problem-specific certificates may also establish dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For search states \(s,t\), let \(C(s)\) and \(C(t)\) be their feasible completion sets. If there is a map \(\phi:C(t)\to C(s)\) satisfying \(J(s,\phi(c))\leq J(t,c)\) for every \(c\in C(t)\), then every solution reachable from \(t\) is matched by a no-worse solution reachable from \(s\). State \(t\) may be pruned provided state \(s\), or equivalent coverage of all image completions, remains represented in the search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state may be pruned when every feasible completion it can produce is matched by a no-worse completion that remains represented elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: C(s),C(t)\text{ are the feasible completion sets of states }s,t
\phi:C(t)\to C(s)
J(s,\phi(c))\leq J(t,c)\quad\forall c\in C(t)
\text{Coverage of }\phi(C(t))\text{ remains in the search}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{d\in C(s)}J(s,d)\leq\inf_{c\in C(t)}J(t,c),\quad\text{and }t\text{ may be pruned}

notation.meaning: feasible completion set of state s
objective value obtained by completing state s with c

knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Preserving Dominance Certificate

assumptions_latex: For each search state \(s\), \(C(s)\) is its set of feasible completions and \(J(s,c)\) is the resulting objective value.
For states \(s,t\), every \(c\in C(t)\) has a corresponding \(\phi(c)\in C(s)\) with \(J(s,\phi(c))\leq J(t,c)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{d\in C(s)}J(s,d)\leq\inf_{c\in C(t)}J(t,c)\), so state \(t\) may be pruned while state \(s\) remains represented.

notation.meaning: feasible completion set of state s
objective after completing state s by c

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic dominance criterion for minimization search states, independent of a particular state encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: State \(s\) dominates state \(t\) if there exists a map \(\phi:C(t)\to C(s)\) such that \(J(s,\phi(c))\leq J(t,c)\) for every \(c\in C(t)\). Then every solution reachable from \(t\) is matched by a no-worse solution reachable from \(s\). Accordingly, \(t\) may be pruned provided \(s\), or equivalent coverage of all images \(\phi(c)\), remains in the search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state is prunable when every one of its feasible completions is matched by a no-worse completion of another retained state.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance-Based Pruning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The completion-mapping criterion is a coherent sufficient certificate for dominance pruning, including the necessary retained-coverage qualification. However, no source supports this general state-space formulation, so the exact pruning criterion cannot yet be admitted as candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Duplicate-State Pruning
children.top_down_role: Closure of repeated search states already represented elsewhere.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive minimization states with identical residual feasible sets and identical continuation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose states \(s,t\) have the same feasible continuation set \(C(s)=C(t)\), every completed objective has the form \(g(u)+h(c)\), and \(g(s)\leq g(t)\). Then \(g(s)+h(c)\leq g(t)+h(c)\) for every common continuation \(c\). Retaining \(s\) therefore preserves a no-worse representative of every completion available from \(t\), so \(t\) may be pruned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among duplicate residual states, retain a minimum-accumulated-cost representative and discard costlier duplicates.
assumptions_latex: C(s)=C(t)
\text{Completed objective from }u\text{ is }g(u)+h(c)
\text{The same continuation-cost function }h\text{ applies to both states}
g(s)\leq g(t)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(s)+h(c)\leq g(t)+h(c)\quad\forall c\in C(t),\quad\text{so }t\text{ may be pruned}

notation.meaning: feasible continuation set of state s

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-State Representative Pruning

assumptions_latex: Each state \(s\) has accumulated cost \(g(s)\), feasible continuation set \(C(s)\), and continuation cost \(h(c)\).
States \(s,t\) satisfy \(C(s)=C(t)\) and use the same continuation-cost function.
The retained state satisfies \(g(s)\leq g(t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(c\in C(t)\), \(g(s)+h(c)\leq g(t)+h(c)\), so \(t\) may be pruned.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate-state elimination for additive minimization search with identical residual subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(C(s)=C(t)\), each completed objective decomposes as \(g(u)+h(c)\), and \(g(s)\leq g(t)\). For every continuation \(c\in C(t)\), the same \(c\) is available from \(s\) and satisfies \[g(s)+h(c)\leq g(t)+h(c).\] Thus retaining \(s\) preserves a solution no worse than every solution obtainable from \(t\), so the duplicate state \(t\) may be discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among states with the same residual problem, retain one with minimum accumulated cost and prune costlier duplicates.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-State Pruning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive argument is correct under identical continuation sets and a shared continuation-cost function, and certificate fits the pruning leaf. No source is supplied for this duplicate-state model or its preservation conditions, so authoritative support is required.

children.title: State-Equivalence Classes
children.top_down_role: Groups of generated subproblems treated as interchangeable for search purposes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semantic equivalence of generated search states; compressed state keys require a separate sufficiency argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For search states \(s,t\in S\), define \(s\sim t\) when \(C(s)=C(t)\) and \(V_s(c)=V_t(c)\) for every common continuation \(c\). This is an equivalence relation on \(S\). Each equivalence class represents states with the same residual feasible completions and continuation values and may share one residual-subproblem representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two search states are equivalent when they have exactly the same feasible continuations and continuation values; the resulting classes represent identical residual problems.
assumptions_latex: s,t\in S
C(s),C(t)\text{ are feasible continuation sets}
V_s,V_t\text{ assign continuation values on their respective domains}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s\sim t\iff C(s)=C(t)\ \land\ \forall c\in C(s),\ V_s(c)=V_t(c),\quad\sim\text{ is an equivalence relation}

notation.meaning: continuation value associated with c from state s

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-State Equivalence Classes

assumptions_latex: Each search state \(s\in S\) induces a feasible continuation set \(C(s)\) and a continuation-value function \(V_s:C(s)\to\overline{\mathbb R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relation \(s\sim t\iff C(s)=C(t)\land V_s=V_t\) is an equivalence relation, and each class represents one residual optimization problem.

notation.meaning: objective contribution of a continuation from s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual-problem equivalence; weaker summaries require a separate sufficiency argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(s,t\in S\), define \[s\sim t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C(s)=C(t)\ \text{ and }\ V_s(c)=V_t(c)\ \text{ for every }c\in C(s).\] Equality of sets and functions makes \(\sim\) reflexive, symmetric, and transitive, so it partitions \(S\) into equivalence classes. Members of one class encode the same residual feasible completions with the same continuation values and may share one residual-subproblem representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two search states are equivalent when they have exactly the same feasible continuations and continuation values; equivalence classes represent identical residual problems.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Equivalence Classes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated equality of continuation sets and continuation-value functions defines an equivalence relation and matches the definition content kind. Because the particular residual-state model and its interpretation as one residual optimization problem are uncited, the record requires an authoritative source.

children.title: Unsafe Dominance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where incomplete state comparison invalidates dominance-based closure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Valid Bound Ordering Does Not Establish State Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of relational pruning based only on independently valid state bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization with state completion sets \(F_A=\{0\}\), \(F_B=\{1\}\), and objective \(f(x)=x\). The reported values \(L_A=L_B=0\) are valid lower bounds for their respective states, but discarding state \(A\) merely because state \(B\) has an equal bound removes the unique optimum \(x=0\). Thus equality or ordering of valid state bounds alone is not a dominance certificate. Safe pruning requires some additional verified relation that preserves no-worse representative coverage; a completion map is one sufficient form, not a universally necessary form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even individually valid equal or ordered bounds do not imply state dominance; an additional coverage-preserving comparison is required.
assumptions_latex: f(x)=x
L_A=L_B=0
L_A\leq\inf_{x\in F_A}f(x),\quad L_B\leq\inf_{x\in F_B}f(x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_A=L_B\centernot\implies B\text{ dominates }A

notation.meaning: feasible completion sets of states A and B
valid lower bounds reported for the two states

knowledge_statements.title: Valid Bound Ordering Does Not Establish State Dominance

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem and each search state has a valid relaxation lower bound.
A dominance rule compares states using only their reported lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality or ordering of valid lower bounds alone does not certify dominance or justify deleting a state.

notation.meaning: feasible completion sets of two states

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for pruning one search state by comparison with another in minimization.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Valid bounds do not by themselves establish state dominance. For example, let \(F_A=\{0\}\), \(F_B=\{1\}\), and minimize \(f(x)=x\). Suppose valid relaxations report \(L_A=L_B=0\). A rule that discards state \(A\) merely because state \(B\) has an equal bound deletes the unique global optimum. Safe dominance therefore additionally requires a verifiable mapping from every relevant completion of the discarded state to a feasible completion of the retained state having no larger objective value, together with preservation of any search restrictions needed for completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal or better relaxation bounds do not imply state dominance; pruning additionally requires a feasibility- and objective-preserving comparison of completions.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Dominance Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows that bound equality alone cannot justify dominance pruning, but the cited general bounds chapter does not specifically support state dominance. The statement also presents a completion mapping as necessary, although it is one sufficient relational certificate among other possible valid dominance arguments. A dominance-specific source and correction of that necessity claim are required.

children.title: Incumbent Management
children.top_down_role: Acquisition, qualification, and search-wide use of feasible solutions.

children.title: Relaxation-Derived Incumbents
children.top_down_role: Feasible solutions obtained from node-relaxation information.

assumptions_latex: At node \(v\), a relaxation solution or related relaxation information is available.
The original mixed-integer feasibility and objective tests can be evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only a validated feasible candidate may update the incumbent value; otherwise the relaxation information supplies no incumbent.

notation.meaning: node relaxation solution and derived candidate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-candidate construction from node-relaxation information in a minimization search.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34
2.3.1 Continuous relaxation p. 24

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given relaxation information at node \(v\), construct a candidate \(\hat x\) by an explicitly specified recovery map \(R_v\), so that \(\hat x=R_v(x^R_v)\); typical maps include rounding followed by repair or a restricted primal search. Test \(\hat x\in F\) using the original constraints and integrality requirements, and recompute \(f(\hat x)\). For minimization, if \(\hat x\in F\) and \(f(\hat x)<U\), set \(U\leftarrow f(\hat x)\) and store \(\hat x\); otherwise leave the incumbent unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transform relaxation information into a candidate, validate it against the original model, and update the minimization incumbent only when its objective improves the cutoff.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Derived Incumbents

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34
2.3.1 Continuous relaxation p. 24

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Naive Rounding of a Relaxation Optimizer Can Be Infeasible
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for direct componentwise rounding as incumbent recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\{0,1\}^2:x_1+x_2=1\}\) and \(C=\{x\in[0,1]^2:x_1+x_2=1\}\). The point \(x^R=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)\) lies in \(C\), but componentwise rounding with a common downward tie rule gives \((0,0)\notin F\), while a common upward tie rule gives \((1,1)\notin F\). Thus direct coordinatewise rounding is not an incumbent certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible relaxation point can round to an infeasible integer point, so a relaxation-derived candidate requires repair or validation.
assumptions_latex: x^R=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^R\in C\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{round}(x^R)\in F
knowledge_statements.title: Naive Rounding of a Relaxation Optimizer Can Be Infeasible

children.title: Auxiliary Incumbent Source Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Feasible solutions supplied by auxiliary methods or external sources.

children.title: Heuristic Incumbents
children.top_down_role: Feasible solutions produced by auxiliary primal heuristics.

assumptions_latex: The original mixed-integer problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\).
A primal heuristic terminates with a candidate or reports failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A heuristic output becomes an incumbent exactly after feasibility validation and strict improvement over the current incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbents produced by constructive, rounding, repair, neighborhood, or local-search heuristics.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run a primal heuristic using the current model, relaxation solution, incumbent, or search state as input. If it returns \(x^H\), independently verify \(x^H\in F\) and evaluate \(f(x^H)\) from the model data. If both tests succeed and \(f(x^H)<U\), replace the stored incumbent by \(x^H\) and set \(U\leftarrow f(x^H)\). A heuristic failure, an infeasible candidate, or a candidate with \(f(x^H)\ge U\) leaves the incumbent unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic candidate is only an incumbent after independent feasibility checking and objective improvement; heuristic failure does not affect correctness.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Incumbents

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Warm-Start Incumbents
children.top_down_role: Feasible solutions inherited from earlier or related optimization runs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualification of a previously available primal point for use as the current model's incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A warm-start incumbent candidate is a primal point \(x^W\) available before discovery by the current search, typically from an earlier solve or a related model. It becomes an incumbent for the current minimization problem only after verification that \(x^W\in F\) and recomputation of \(f(x^W)\); it replaces the current incumbent precisely when none exists or \(f(x^W)<U\). A changed constraint, bound, objective, variable mapping, or data version can invalidate an earlier solution, and reusable basis, tree, or solver metadata alone is not an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A previously available solution becomes a warm-start incumbent only after it is mapped to and validated for the current model and improves the current incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The current problem minimizes \(f\) over feasible set \(F\).
A previously available primal point can be mapped to the current model's variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^W\text{ is installed as the current incumbent}\Longleftrightarrow x^W\in F\text{ and }(U=+\infty\text{ or }f(x^W)<U).

notation.meaning: current minimization incumbent value, with infinity denoting absence

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Incumbent Qualification

assumptions_latex: A candidate solution is supplied before or during the search.
The current model can validate the candidate independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A supplied point is a warm-start incumbent only if it is feasible for the current model and improves the incumbent objective value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualification of a previously available primal solution as an incumbent for the current model.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A warm-start incumbent is a point \(x^W\) available before its discovery by the current search, commonly from an earlier solve or a related model, such that the current solver has verified \(x^W\in F\) and recomputed its objective value. For minimization, it is accepted as the incumbent precisely when no incumbent exists or \(f(x^W)<U\); acceptance sets \(U\leftarrow f(x^W)\). Basis, tree, or solution metadata alone does not establish incumbent status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A previous solution becomes a warm-start incumbent only after current-model feasibility and objective validation show that it improves the active incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Incumbents

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically plausible and locally appropriate, but the cited general chapter on bounds does not specifically support warm-start provenance, current-model revalidation, or the treatment of basis, tree, and solution metadata. A warm-start-specific source is required.

children.title: External Incumbents
children.top_down_role: Feasible solutions submitted by users or outside solver components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admission of a complete candidate supplied by a user, file, service, callback, or independent process outside the active solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization model with current feasible set \(F\), objective \(f\), and incumbent value \(U\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), treat an externally supplied vector \(x^E\) and claimed value \(z^E\) as advisory. Before cutoff propagation, construct a complete point for the current model, verify all domain, integrality, and constraint requirements under the declared feasibility tolerances, and recompute \(\bar z=f(x^E)\) from current model data. Admit \(x^E\) as the incumbent only if it passes the solver's declared improvement predicate, exactly \(\bar z<U\) under the strict convention. A partial vector may be used only after an authorized completion procedure produces a complete point that passes the same checks. Rejection, validation failure, or nonimprovement leaves the incumbent and correctness of the continuing exhaustive search unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An external solution is only an advisory candidate: complete and validate it against the current model, recompute its objective, and update the incumbent only when the declared improvement test passes.
assumptions_latex: The current model, objective, and validation tolerances are available.
\(U\) is the current feasible-incumbent value or \(+\infty\) when none exists.
The candidate is not classified primarily as a related-run warm-start incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cutoff propagation may use \(\bar z\) only after current-model validation and satisfaction of the declared incumbent-improvement predicate.

notation.meaning: externally supplied point and claimed objective value
objective value recomputed from the current model
current feasible set, objective, and incumbent value

knowledge_statements.title: External-Candidate Admission

assumptions_latex: A point and possibly a claimed objective value arrive from outside the active solver state.
The current model data and tolerances are available for independent validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: External provenance never substitutes for current-model feasibility, integrality, and objective validation.

notation.meaning: externally supplied point and claimed value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbents supplied by users, files, callbacks, services, or another optimization process.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An external incumbent candidate is a point \(x^E\) received from outside the active solver's certified search state. It becomes an incumbent only after the solver verifies \(x^E\in F\), checks all required integrality conditions, and computes \(f(x^E)\) from current model data. Any supplied value \(z^E\) is advisory and must agree with the recomputed value under the declared objective tolerance. Model-version mismatch, missing coordinates, or failed validation requires rejection rather than cutoff propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An externally supplied solution is only a candidate until the active solver independently validates feasibility, integrality, and its claimed objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: External Incumbents

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validation requirements are plausible, but the general bounds citation does not support the operational claims about external submissions, model versions, missing coordinates, or objective-tolerance agreement. The statement also does not explicitly require improvement over the current incumbent before the validated point becomes the incumbent. A source specific to external solution handling is required before fixing the complete qualification rule.

children.title: Source-Trust Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validation risks associated with incumbent provenance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validated Mutation of Certified Incumbent State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust boundary between candidate-producing sources and the certified incumbent and cutoff state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A candidate source may submit \(\tilde x\) and a claimed value \(\tilde z\), but certified incumbent state may be changed only after a trusted qualification step checks \(\tilde x\) against the current model and recomputes \(f(\tilde x)\). For minimization, setting \(U\leftarrow f(\tilde x)\) is sound only when \(\tilde x\in F\) and \(f(\tilde x)<U\). Directly accepting an infeasible candidate or an understated claimed value can create an invalid cutoff and prune a region containing the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Candidate producers may propose solutions, but only current-model validation and objective recomputation may authorize mutation of the certified incumbent and cutoff.
assumptions_latex: The original problem minimizes \(f\) over feasible set \(F\).
Candidate sources may be stale, incomplete, or otherwise unable to certify compatibility with the current model.
The incumbent value may be used for globally consequential pruning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) may be tightened from a submitted candidate only after \(\tilde x\in F\) and its current-model value \(f(\tilde x)\) are independently established.

notation.meaning: submitted candidate and claimed objective value

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Mutation of Certified Incumbent State

assumptions_latex: Candidate incumbents may originate from components with different reliability levels.
Incorrect incumbent acceptance can induce globally valid cutoff pruning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No untrusted source may directly modify the certified incumbent or global cutoff without independent qualification.

notation.meaning: candidate point and claimed objective value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust boundary between candidate-producing components and the certified incumbent state.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A source lies outside the incumbent trust boundary whenever it cannot certify its candidate against the current model, data version, and acceptance tolerances. Such a source may submit \((\tilde x,\tilde z)\), but it may not set \(U\) or trigger pruning. The trusted qualification component must independently check dimensions, bounds, constraints, integrality, and the recomputed objective. Bypassing this boundary is unsafe: an infeasible point or an understated minimization value can create an invalid cutoff and delete a subtree containing the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Candidate sources may propose solutions, but only a trusted validator may update the incumbent and global cutoff after checking the current model.
knowledge_statements.title: Source-Trust Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary is coherent, but its component trust model, authority separation, model-version checks, and prohibition on direct cutoff mutation are solver-policy claims not established by the cited general bounds chapter. A source addressing incumbent validation or solver trust boundaries is required.

children.title: Incumbent Qualification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Qualification of candidate incumbents under exact and numerical feasibility conventions.

children.title: Incumbent Feasibility Validation
children.top_down_role: Qualification of candidate solutions against model feasibility requirements.

assumptions_latex: The candidate has all coordinates required by the current mixed-integer model.
Constraint and bound residuals are evaluated using declared acceptance tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The validation record certifies incumbent feasibility exactly when every required bound, constraint, and integrality test passes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-based certificate required before a candidate can control branch-and-bound pruning.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Integrality constraints p. 10
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a model with bounds \(l\le x\le u\), inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), equalities \(h_j(x)=0\), and integer index set \(I\), a feasibility-validation certificate records that \(l_k-\varepsilon_f\le\hat x_k\le u_k+\varepsilon_f\) for every \(k\), \(g_i(\hat x)\le\varepsilon_f\) for every \(i\), \(|h_j(\hat x)|\le\varepsilon_f\) for every \(j\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(\hat x_k,\mathbb Z)\le\varepsilon_I\) for every \(k\in I\). Acceptance under these declared tolerances certifies solver-feasibility; exact feasibility requires zero tolerances or exact post-validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate passes feasibility validation only when every bound, constraint, equality, and integer-coordinate residual satisfies the declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Feasibility Validation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Integrality constraints p. 10
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf, and the record distinguishes tolerance acceptance from exact feasibility. However, the cited sections cover integrality and bounds generally, not the stated numerical certificate with uniform feasibility and integrality tolerances across bounds, inequalities, and equalities. A numerical-feasibility source specifying the residual and scaling conventions is required.

children.title: Objective-Value Validation
children.top_down_role: Qualification of the objective value used to update the primal bound.

assumptions_latex: A candidate \(\hat x\) has passed incumbent feasibility validation.
The current objective function and a declared objective-comparison tolerance are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recomputed value, rather than an unverified supplied value, determines incumbent improvement and cutoff propagation.

notation.meaning: current minimization incumbent and objective tolerance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent validation of the value used to update a minimization incumbent.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14
Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(z=f(\hat x)\) from the current objective coefficients, constants, and nonlinear terms. If a source supplied \(\tilde z\), accept its claim only when \(|\tilde z-z|\le\varepsilon_o\), but retain \(z\) as the certified value. For minimization, \(\hat x\) improves the incumbent only under the solver's declared strict comparison, for example \(z<U-\varepsilon_o\). The validation record must identify the model version and objective convention so that scaling, offsets, or sense changes cannot produce an erroneous cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute the candidate's objective on the current model, check any claimed value, and use only the recomputed value for incumbent improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Value Validation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14
Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is internally coherent, but the cited optimality-and-bounds sections do not specifically support recomputation rules, objective comparison tolerances, model-version recording, or handling of scaling and offsets. An objective-validation or solver-numerics source is required.

children.title: Feasibility-Tolerance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Acceptance regimes near numerical feasibility thresholds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact primal feasibility and feasibility accepted under a declared residual convention for incumbent qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a declared residual and scaling convention and let \(r_f(x)\ge0\) be the maximum resulting violation of variable bounds and row constraints. The candidate is tolerance-feasible when \(r_f(x)\le\varepsilon_f\). With exact evaluation and \(\varepsilon_f=0\), this test coincides with exact row-and-bound feasibility. For \(\varepsilon_f>0\), tolerance feasibility need not imply membership in the exact feasible set. Therefore an incumbent intended to support an exact global cutoff must either be revalidated exactly or with certified error control, or the search guarantee must explicitly incorporate the enlarged acceptance convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive feasibility tolerance can admit exactly infeasible points, so tolerance acceptance alone does not justify an exact incumbent cutoff.
assumptions_latex: A residual and scaling convention is fixed before candidate validation.
\(\varepsilon_f\ge0\) is the declared primal-feasibility tolerance.
Integrality qualification, when applicable, is handled separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_f(x)\le\varepsilon_f\text{ is an exact-feasibility certificate only under exact evaluation with }\varepsilon_f=0\text{, or under an additional certified implication to }x\in F.

notation.meaning: maximum declared row-and-bound violation after the fixed scaling convention

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Feasibility Versus Exact Feasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical one-row family showing why positive feasibility tolerance does not certify an exact incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\varepsilon_f>0\), consider the exact minimization problem \(\min\{x:x\ge1\}\) and the absolute violation test \(r_f(x)=\max\{0,1-x\}\). The point \(\hat x=1-\varepsilon_f/2\) satisfies \(r_f(\hat x)\le\varepsilon_f\) but is exactly infeasible and has claimed value \(1-\varepsilon_f/2\), strictly below the exact optimum \(1\). Treating that value as an exact incumbent cutoff can therefore reject every exact feasible solution and invalidate an exact optimality claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point just below a lower bound can pass a positive feasibility tolerance while supplying an objective value below the true optimum, making an exact cutoff unsafe.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_f>0\).
Constraint violation is measured by the stated absolute residual.
The tolerance-accepted point is used as though it were an exact feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_f(\hat x)=\varepsilon_f/2\le\varepsilon_f,\qquad \hat x\notin F,\qquad f(\hat x)<\min_{x\in F}f(x).

notation.meaning: exact feasible set of the counterexample

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Feasible Infeasible Cutoff Family

assumptions_latex: Constraint functions and variable bounds are evaluated at a candidate point.
A nonnegative feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon_f\) is declared before validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tolerance-feasibility is an acceptance convention and does not imply exact membership in the mathematical feasible set when \(\varepsilon_f>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact mathematical feasibility and tolerance-based solver acceptance.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_f(x)\) be the maximum violation over all variable bounds, inequality constraints, and equality constraints after applying the solver's declared scaling convention. A candidate is feasibility-tolerant precisely when \(r_f(x)\le\varepsilon_f\), where \(\varepsilon_f\ge0\). If \(\varepsilon_f=0\) and evaluation is exact, this condition coincides with exact primal feasibility. If \(\varepsilon_f>0\), the accepted set generally strictly contains the mathematical feasible set; consequently, any rigorous cutoff certificate must either account for this enlargement or revalidate the candidate more accurately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility tolerance bounds the largest declared residual, but positive tolerance enlarges the accepted set and does not establish exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Tolerance Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly separates tolerance feasibility from exact mathematical feasibility, but the cited general bounds chapter does not establish the residual definition, scaling convention, or consequences for rigorous cutoff certification. A tolerance-specific numerical optimization or solver source is required.

children.title: Integrality-Tolerance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Acceptance regimes near discrete-domain thresholds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate Rounding Need Not Preserve Coupling Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of coordinatewise integer reconstruction to preserve mixed discrete-continuous feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be integer-constrained, let \(y\) be continuous, and impose \(x-y=0\). For any \(0<\delta<\tfrac12\), the candidate \((x,y)=(\delta,\delta)\) satisfies the equality and passes the integrality test whenever \(\varepsilon_I\ge\delta\), but rounding only the integer coordinate to zero gives \((0,\delta)\), which violates the equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding a nearly integral coordinate can destroy a coupling constraint even though the unrounded candidate satisfies that constraint.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb Z\text{ in the original model}
y\in\mathbb R
x-y=0
0<\delta\le\varepsilon_I<\tfrac12
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\delta,\delta)\text{ passes the stated tests, whereas }(0,\delta)\text{ violates }x-y=0
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Rounding Need Not Preserve Coupling Constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp tolerance boundary for uniqueness of the integer associated with a nearly integral scalar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{dist}(t,\mathbb Z)<\tfrac12\), then \(t\) has a unique nearest integer. At \(t=m+\tfrac12\), both \(m\) and \(m+1\) are nearest. Hence an absolute tolerance below \(\tfrac12\) identifies at most one admissible integer per coordinate, whereas a tolerance of at least \(\tfrac12\) does not guarantee unique reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar less than one half from the integer lattice has a unique nearest integer, and the one-half threshold is sharp.
assumptions_latex: t\in\mathbb R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(t,\mathbb Z)<\tfrac12\Rightarrow\left|\operatorname*{argmin}_{k\in\mathbb Z}|t-k|\right|=1

notation.meaning: distance from t to the integer lattice

knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness Radius for Integer Reconstruction

assumptions_latex: The model designates an integer-coordinate index set \(I\).
A nonnegative integrality tolerance \(\varepsilon_I\) is declared before validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tolerance-integrality permits near-integer values and is not exact integrality unless \(\varepsilon_I=0\) under exact evaluation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact integrality and numerical acceptance of nearly integral coordinates.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Integrality constraints p. 10
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A candidate \(x\) satisfies the integrality-tolerance condition when \(\operatorname{dist}(x_i,\mathbb Z)=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z}|x_i-k|\le\varepsilon_I\) for every \(i\in I\). For binary variables, the associated rounded value must also belong to \(\{0,1\}\). When \(\varepsilon_I>0\), this predicate accepts points outside \(\mathbb Z^I\); thus rounding must not be assumed to preserve nonlinear constraints, equalities, or objective value. A cutoff based on the candidate requires feasibility and objective validation of the accepted or rounded point under a declared convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every integer coordinate must lie within the declared distance of an integer; positive tolerance alone does not make the original point exactly integral.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality-Tolerance Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Integrality constraints p. 10
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition and warning about rounding are mathematically appropriate, but the cited section on exact integrality constraints does not specifically support numerical integrality tolerances, binary rounding conventions, or subsequent cutoff validation. A tolerance-specific source is required.

children.title: Incumbent Cutoff Propagation Interface
children.top_down_role: Search-wide consequences of improving the primal bound.

children.title: Incumbent-Derived Cutoffs
children.top_down_role: Search thresholds induced by the current primal bound.

assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes \(f(x)\) over feasible set \(F\).
A validated incumbent \(x^I\in F\) with value \(U=f(x^I)\) is available.
Each node \(v\) has a valid lower bound \(L_v\) on all feasible completions in its subtree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent value is a valid global primal cutoff, and every node with \(L_v\ge U\) may be closed when only strict improvement is sought.

notation.meaning: validated incumbent and its objective value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimization cutoff induced by a validated incumbent.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14
Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(x^I\in F\), the value \(U=f(x^I)\) is an upper bound on the optimal minimization value \(z^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). For any node \(v\), validity of \(L_v\) means \(f(x)\ge L_v\) for every feasible completion \(x\) in its subtree. Hence \(L_v\ge U\) implies that the subtree contains no solution strictly better than the incumbent and may be closed. With numerical tolerances, the implemented comparison must preserve this logical inequality conservatively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A validated minimization incumbent supplies a global upper cutoff; any subtree whose valid lower bound reaches that cutoff cannot improve it.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Derived Cutoffs

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14
Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Frontier-Wide Cutoff Propagation
children.top_down_role: Consequences of an improved cutoff for active nodes.

assumptions_latex: A newly validated minimization incumbent has value \(U_{new}\le U_{old}\).
Every open node has a valid lower bound and uses the same certified incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Applying the new cutoff to every open node preserves completeness while possibly closing additional nodes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical propagation of an improved incumbent cutoff across the active search frontier.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14
Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After accepting an incumbent with \(U_{new}\le U_{old}\), publish \(U_{new}\) to every node \(v\in\mathcal F\). Reevaluate the cutoff predicate and remove each node satisfying \(L_v\ge U_{new}\) when the search seeks only strict improvement. Nodes with \(L_v<U_{new}\) remain eligible. Since lowering a valid minimization upper bound can only enlarge the set \(\{v\in\mathcal F:L_v\ge U\}\), frontier-wide propagation cannot reopen a correctly closed node; correctness requires that workers never prune using an unvalidated or understated incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broadcast an improved incumbent to all open nodes and close every node whose valid lower bound cannot beat the new cutoff.
knowledge_statements.title: Frontier-Wide Cutoff Propagation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14
Chapter 2. Optimality, Relaxation, and Bounds p. 25

children.title: Delayed Cutoff Recognition
children.top_down_role: Search behavior when open nodes do not immediately reflect an improved incumbent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbounded Redundant Work Under Delayed Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case work overhead attributable solely to delayed observation of a stronger incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is no finite instance-independent bound on the number of redundant nodes processed before a stronger cutoff is recognized. For every \(N\ge1\), a finitely branching search state can contain a subtree with at least \(N\) nodes whose valid lower bounds lie in \([U_t,U_s)\); a worker using \(U_s\) may process those nodes although immediate use of \(U_t\) closes the subtree at its root. This is an overhead statement, not a loss-of-correctness statement, provided all bounds and incumbent values used for pruning are valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delayed cutoff recognition can cause arbitrarily many avoidable node evaluations, although using an older feasible cutoff remains logically safe.
assumptions_latex: \(U_t<U_s\) are feasible incumbent values for a minimization problem.
The search may continue expanding a node while its local cutoff remains \(U_s\).
Node lower bounds in the redundant subtree are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall N\ge1\ \exists\text{ a search state with at least }N\text{ avoidable node evaluations caused by stale }U_s.

notation.meaning: arbitrary prescribed number of redundant node evaluations
range of bounds hidden from closure by the stale cutoff

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Redundant Work Under Delayed Recognition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search behavior at a node whose worker has not yet observed a stronger feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current feasible incumbent value be \(U_t\), let a worker use an older feasible incumbent value \(U_s\ge U_t\), and let \(L_v\) be a valid lower bound for node \(v\). Nodes satisfying \(U_t\le L_v<U_s\) are closable under the current cutoff but are not recognized as closable under the stale cutoff. Continuing such nodes is redundant but remains sound: a stale weaker minimization cutoff can suppress pruning, whereas pruning with an unvalidated or understated value can be unsound. Exact completion additionally requires that every retained region eventually be validly resolved or reconsidered under available certified state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale weaker cutoff can miss valid closures and cause redundant work without invalidating search; an unvalidated stronger cutoff can invalidate pruning.
assumptions_latex: Both \(U_t\) and \(U_s\) are values of feasible incumbents for the same minimization model.
\(L_v\) is a valid lower bound for every feasible completion represented by node \(v\).
The search's completion protocol eventually resolves every region not validly closed.

Delayed Cutoff Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization branch-and-bound with an incumbent cutoff not immediately propagated to every open node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_t\) be the incumbent objective value at time \(t\), and let an open node \(v\) have a valid relaxation lower bound \(L_v\). If \(L_v\ge U_t\), then \(v\) and all its descendants may be fathomed. If the worker processing \(v\) still uses an older cutoff \(U_s>U_t\), it may fail to recognize this closure whenever \(U_t\le L_v<U_s\). The resulting additional search is redundant but does not invalidate correctness, provided every reported incumbent is feasible and pruning uses only valid lower bounds and an incumbent value no smaller than the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale, weaker incumbent cutoff can delay valid pruning and cause redundant search, but it does not compromise correctness when bounds and incumbents remain valid.

\(L_v\) is a valid lower bound for every feasible solution in node \(v\).

children.title: Cutoff-Induced Subtree Closure

knowledge_statements.title: Cutoff-Induced Subtree Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-fathoming certificate for minimization branch-and-bound under a feasible incumbent cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_v\) be the feasible set represented by node \(v\), let \(L_v\le \inf\{f(x):x\in X_v\}\) be valid, and let \(U\) be the value of a feasible incumbent. The inequality \(L_v\ge U\) certifies that no point in \(X_v\) can improve the incumbent. Because every descendant \(w\) satisfies \(X_w\subseteq X_v\), the same comparison certifies closure of the entire subtree rooted at \(v\). Equality may be pruned when only strict incumbent improvement is sought; enumeration of all optimal solutions requires an appropriate tie convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node and its descendants close when the node lower bound cannot beat the feasible incumbent, subject to the solver’s treatment of ties.
assumptions_latex: \(X_w\subseteq X_v\) for every descendant \(w\) of \(v\).
\(L_v\) is a valid lower bound and \(U\) is attained by a feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\ge U\Longrightarrow \inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)\ge U\), so the subtree cannot improve the incumbent.

children.title: Variable-Domain Reduction
children.top_down_role: Contraction of variable ranges within a node subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Domain Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe coordinate-domain contraction at a branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), let the current domain be \(D_v=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\) and let \(F_v\subseteq D_v\) denote its feasible points. A variable-domain reduction is an operator \(R\) returning \(R(D_v)=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i'\) such that \(D_i'\subseteq D_i\) for every \(i\) and \(F_v\subseteq R(D_v)\). Thus no node-feasible point is removed. For an integer variable, endpoints are rounded inward to integer values after deriving valid real bounds. If some \(D_i'\) is empty, infeasibility of the node is certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-domain reduction safely contracts coordinate domains while retaining every feasible node solution; an empty reduced domain certifies node infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(D_v\) is a Cartesian product of current variable domains.
The reduction rule is valid for every constraint imposed at node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_v\subseteq R(D_v)\subseteq D_v\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smallest product domain retaining every point of a nonempty node-feasible set.

If representable components must be closed real intervals, the smallest interval box is \prod_i[\inf_{x\in F_v}x_i,\sup_{x\in F_v}x_i]. Every sound Cartesian reduction contains the corresponding hull.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the initial node domain, let the node constraints be \(g_j(x)\le 0\) for \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and define \(F=\{x\in D:g_j(x)\le 0\text{ for every }j\}\). For each \(j\), let \(C_j\) satisfy \(\{x\in B:g_j(x)\le 0\}\subseteq C_j(B)\subseteq B\) for every domain \(B\subseteq D\). Initialize \(D^{(0)}=D\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(j_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and set \(D^{(k+1)}=C_{j_k}(D^{(k)})\). Stop when a domain is empty, a prescribed tolerance is reached, or a complete sweep makes no change. Return the final domain. Every generated domain contains \(F\); hence emptiness certifies node infeasibility, while a nonempty result is a safe outer approximation of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from the node domain, repeatedly apply contractors that preserve all points satisfying their associated constraints. Every iterate contains the full node-feasible set, so an empty iterate certifies infeasibility and a nonempty terminal iterate is a safe outer approximation.

children.title: Node-Bound Tightening

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening of node objective bounds after safe domain or relaxation refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node \(v\), let \(R_v\supseteq F_v\) be its relaxation and \(L_v=\inf\{f(x):x\in R_v\}\). If valid reductions or cuts produce \(F_v\subseteq R_v'\subseteq R_v\), define \(L_v'=\inf\{f(x):x\in R_v'\}\). Then \(L_v'\ge L_v\), and \(L_v'\) remains a valid lower bound on the node optimum. Consequently, replacing \(L_v\) by \(L_v'\) cannot invalidate minimization pruning; if \(L_v'\ge U\) for a feasible incumbent value \(U\), the node may be fathomed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking a valid minimization relaxation cannot decrease its lower bound and can expose additional incumbent-based pruning opportunities.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\subseteq R_v'\subseteq R_v\).
Both relaxation infima are evaluated or bounded validly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\le L_v'\le \inf_{x\in F_v}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Stabilization Can Fail on Continuous Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to finite exact termination without a descending-chain condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For D_u=[0,u], u\in[0,1], let the feasible set be F=\{0\} and define R(D_u)=D_{u/2}. Starting from D_1 gives R^k(D_1)=D_{2^{-k}}. Every finite iterate strictly contracts and contains F, but no finite iterate equals the exact fixpoint D_0=\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound continuous-domain contractor can shrink forever without reaching its exact fixpoint.
assumptions_latex: Domains with arbitrarily small positive endpoints are representable.
Exact equality rather than tolerance-based stabilization is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R^k(D_1)=D_{2^{-k}}\ne D_0\quad\text{for every finite }k.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Stabilization Can Fail on Continuous Domains

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fair Monotone Reduction on a Finite Lattice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination, schedule independence, and strict-update complexity for exact finite-lattice propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let L be a finite lattice ordered by domain inclusion, let D^{(0)}\in L, and let R_1,\ldots,R_m:L\to L be monotone and contracting. Every fair iteration reaches a common fixpoint D^*. This fixpoint is the greatest common fixpoint below D^{(0)} and is independent of the fair order. If h is the maximum length of a strict descending chain below D^{(0)}, at most h strict domain updates occur; without a quantitative fairness rule, the number of no-change operator calls has no corresponding bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair monotone contraction on a finite domain lattice reaches the unique greatest common fixpoint; lattice height bounds strict changes but not arbitrary no-op scheduling.
assumptions_latex: L is finite and ordered by inclusion.
Every R_j is monotone and contracting.
The schedule is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D^*=\max\{E\in L:E\subseteq D^{(0)},\ R_j(E)=E\ \forall j\},\qquad \#\{\text{strict updates}\}\le h.

notation.meaning: Maximum strict descending-chain length below the initial domain

knowledge_statements.title: Fair Monotone Reduction on a Finite Lattice
Reduction Fixpoint Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination condition for repeated application of finitely many sound domain reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) be contracting, solution-preserving operators on node domains, and let one complete reduction sweep be \(T=R_m\circ\cdots\circ R_1\). A domain \(D^*\) is a reduction fixpoint for that schedule when \(T(D^*)=D^*\); it is a common fixpoint when \(R_j(D^*)=D^*\) for every \(j\). If domains are represented on a finite lattice and every strict update decreases the domain, repeated fair application terminates at a common fixpoint. Without finiteness, exact termination need not occur, so practical algorithms may stop at a tolerance-based approximate fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduction regime stabilizes when a full sweep changes nothing; finite-domain fair contraction terminates, while continuous domains may require tolerance-based stopping.
assumptions_latex: Each \(R_j\) is contracting and preserves all feasible node points.
For finite termination, representable domains form a finite lattice and the schedule is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_j(D^*)=D^*\) for all \(j\) at a common reduction fixpoint.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Cut Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strengthening a node relaxation by valid inequalities without removing node-feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a minimization node \(v\), let \(F_v\subseteq R_v\) and let \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\) be inequalities valid for every \(x\in F_v\). Define \(R_v'=R_v\cap\bigcap_k\{x:a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\}\). Then \(F_v\subseteq R_v'\subseteq R_v\), so the strengthened relaxation preserves every feasible node solution. Its optimal value \(L_v'=\inf\{f(x):x\in R_v'\}\) is a valid node lower bound satisfying \(L_v'\ge L_v\), where \(L_v\) is the value of the original relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding node-valid cuts preserves feasible solutions, shrinks the relaxation, and cannot weaken a minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\subseteq R_v\).
Every integrated inequality is valid for all points of \(F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_v\subseteq R_v'\subseteq R_v\) and \(L_v'\ge L_v\).

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Relaxation Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Re-solving a modified node relaxation while reusing a compatible parent or previous solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a previously solved relaxation \(R	o\min f(x)\), a modified node relaxation \(R'\), and a stored solver state \(s\), first update the changed bounds, rows, or columns defining \(R'\). If \(s\) is compatible, transform or repair it into an admissible initial state \(s'\); otherwise initialize normally. Run the relaxation solver from \(s'\) until its standard optimality, infeasibility, unboundedness, or prescribed-tolerance criterion holds. Return the resulting status, primal-dual solution when available, and a valid node bound. Reuse affects computational effort, not the mathematical termination criteria or bound validity.

Any reused state is checked or repaired to satisfy the solver's initialization requirements.

children.title: Basis Warm Starts

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex reoptimization initialized from a stored basis after node-relaxation modifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear relaxation in standard form, store a nonsingular basis matrix \(B\) and its basic-status information. After node bounds or rows change, retain \(B\) when its dimensions and columns remain compatible, augment or repair it otherwise, and compute the associated basic primal and dual quantities. If the repaired basis is primal feasible, apply primal simplex; if dual feasible, apply dual simplex; otherwise perform a feasibility-restoration phase. Stop under the ordinary simplex optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness criterion. The warm start changes initialization only and does not alter the linear program being solved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse and repair a compatible simplex basis, select a suitable simplex phase from its feasibility status, and solve the unchanged node LP normally.
assumptions_latex: The node relaxation is a finite-dimensional linear program.
The retained or repaired basis is nonsingular and dimensionally compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The terminal simplex certificate pertains to the modified node linear program, independently of whether \(B\) was reused.
