children.title: Relaxation-Infeasibility Candidates
children.top_down_role: Candidates exposed by fractional or otherwise unresolved relaxation solutions.

assumptions_latex: A relaxation solution \(\bar x\in R\) is available.
The original node requires \(x_i\in\mathbb{Z}\) for every \(i\) in an index set \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every index in \(C(\bar x)\) is eligible for an integrality-restoring split.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidates induced by violated integrality at a solved relaxation point.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.1 Continuous relaxation p. 24

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The relaxation-infeasibility candidate set at \(\bar x\) is \[C(\bar x)=\{i\in I:\bar x_i\notin\mathbb{Z}\}.\] For each \(i\in C(\bar x)\), the disjunction \(x_i\leq\lfloor\bar x_i\rfloor\) or \(x_i\geq\lceil\bar x_i\rceil\) excludes \(\bar x\) while covering every point satisfying the integrality requirement on \(x_i\). If \(C(\bar x)=\varnothing\), ordinary fractional-variable branching supplies no candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation-infeasibility candidate is an integer-constrained variable whose solved relaxation value is nonintegral; its floor-ceiling split excludes that relaxation point without excluding integer-feasible points.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Infeasibility Candidates

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.1 Continuous relaxation p. 24

children.title: Pseudo-Solution Candidates
children.top_down_role: Candidates available when no solved continuous relaxation drives branching.

assumptions_latex: No solved continuous-relaxation point is used to generate candidates.
A surrogate state \(s\) and a finite candidate generator \(G\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned candidates are admissible only when each associated disjunction covers the current node's integer-feasible set.

notation.meaning: Candidate set generated from the surrogate state.
Integer-feasible points at the current node.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract validity condition for branching without a solved relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pseudo-solution candidate generator maps the available surrogate state \(s\) to a finite set \(G(s)\). Each candidate \(c\in G(s)\) must provide a finite family of child predicates \(D_{c,1},\ldots,D_{c,k_c}\) satisfying \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{k_c}D_{c,j}\). Consequently, branching on \(c\) cannot discard any point in \(F\), although the predicates may overlap unless the solver interface additionally requires a partition. The generator is unavailable when \(G(s)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a solved relaxation, a surrogate state may generate candidates only if each candidate's child disjunction covers every integer-feasible point at the current node.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Solution Candidates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract coverage condition is plausible, but the meaning of a pseudo-solution candidate and whether overlapping child predicates are permitted depend on the solver interface. An authoritative interface or algorithm source is required.

children.title: Specialized Component Candidate Interface
children.top_down_role: Candidates supplied by specialized solver components.

children.title: Relaxator-Supplied Candidates
children.top_down_role: Branching candidates exposed by specialized relaxation components.

assumptions_latex: A specialized relaxator has computed state \(r\) for the current node.
The relaxator exposes a finite candidate interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every supplied candidate is valid only if its child disjunction covers the current node's feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract contract for candidates produced by a specialized relaxation component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relaxator-supplied candidate is an element \(c\in C_R(r)\) accompanied by child predicates \(D_{c,1},\ldots,D_{c,k_c}\). It is admissible for branching only if \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{k_c}D_{c,j}\); if exclusive branching is required, it must also satisfy \(F\cap D_{c,j}\cap D_{c,\ell}=\varnothing\) for \(j\neq\ell\). The relaxator supplies no candidate at state \(r\) precisely when \(C_R(r)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxator may supply branching candidates with child predicates, provided those predicates cover all feasible points at the node and satisfy any required exclusivity rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxator-Supplied Candidates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed validity contract is plausible but solver-specific. A source must establish what a relaxator may return, the relevant feasible set, and whether exclusivity is required.

children.title: Constraint-Handler Candidates
children.top_down_role: Branching candidates exposed by constraint-specific solver components.

assumptions_latex: A constraint handler represents a constraint family \(H\) at the current node.
The handler detects an unresolved state \(h\) and exposes candidate disjunctions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A handler candidate is admissible only when its branches preserve every point satisfying the handled constraints and the remaining node restrictions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract validity contract for candidates emitted by a constraint handler.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate \(c\in C_H(h)\), the constraint handler returns child predicates \(D_{c,1},\ldots,D_{c,k_c}\). The candidate is valid when \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{k_c}D_{c,j}\), so every feasible point satisfying the handled constraint family remains in at least one child. A candidate may encode a variable split, a structural disjunction, or another handler-specific decision; its origin does not replace the covering requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint handler may propose structural or variable candidates, but each candidate's branches must retain every point feasible for the node and handled constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Handler Candidates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement depends on solver-specific constraint-handler semantics and lacks evidence defining the candidate interface and its validity requirements.

children.title: Cross-Component Candidate Arbitration
children.top_down_role: Selection boundaries when multiple specialized components submit candidates.

assumptions_latex: Components indexed by a finite set \(P\) return finite candidate sets \(C_p\).
A deterministic priority \(\pi_p\) and score \(s_p(c)\) are defined for every returned candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule returns one globally selected candidate whenever at least one component supplies a candidate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic priority-and-score arbitration across component candidate sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(C=\{(p,c):p\in P,\ c\in C_p\}\), stop without a component candidate if \(C=\varnothing\). Otherwise select \[(p^*,c^*)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{(p,c)\in C}(\pi_p,s_p(c))\] under lexicographic order, resolving any remaining equality by a fixed total order on component-candidate identifiers. Output \(c^*\) and its associated branching disjunction. This rule makes component priority dominant; a score-comparable implementation may instead omit \(\pi_p\), but must specify that alternative explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Collect all component candidates, compare component priority and candidate score lexicographically, apply a deterministic final tie-break, and return the winning candidate and disjunction.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Component Candidate Arbitration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lexicographic priority-and-score algorithm fits the leaf, but it is one particular arbitration policy rather than a universal rule. A source specifying this policy is required.

children.title: Component-Candidate Availability
children.top_down_role: Search states distinguished by the presence or absence of specialized candidates.

assumptions_latex: A finite set of candidate-producing components \(P\) is active.
Each component \(p\) reports a candidate set \(C_p(s_p)\) from its current state \(s_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Specialized component branching is available exactly when the union of reported candidate sets is nonempty.

notation.meaning: State and reported candidates of component \(p\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Availability predicate for specialized component candidates at one node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(C_{\mathrm{comp}}=\bigcup_{p\in P}\{(p,c):c\in C_p(s_p)\}\). Component candidates are available if and only if \(C_{\mathrm{comp}}\neq\varnothing\). Availability therefore requires at least one active component to be callable in its current state and to return at least one admissible candidate. If \(C_{\mathrm{comp}}=\varnothing\), cross-component arbitration is undefined and the branching procedure must use another candidate source or declare that no branching candidate is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Component candidates are available exactly when at least one active specialized component returns an admissible candidate; otherwise arbitration cannot select one.
knowledge_statements.title: Component-Candidate Availability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nonemptiness of the aggregate set is internally coherent, but callability, activation, admissibility, and fallback behavior are solver-interface claims requiring an authoritative source.

children.title: Classical Branching Scores
children.top_down_role: Candidate rankings based on current relaxation and propagation information.

children.title: Fractional-Displacement Branching Scores
children.top_down_role: Candidate ranking by current fractional displacement.

children.title: Most-Infeasible Branching
children.top_down_role: Candidate ranking by the magnitude of current infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum Fractionality Does Not Predict Bound Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MILP relaxation separating fractional displacement from child-bound effect.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min y\quad\text{s.t.}\quad y\ge z-\tfrac12,\quad y\ge\tfrac12-z,\quad y\ge0,\quad x,z\in\{0,1\}.\] The LP relaxation has an optimum \((\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12,0)\), where both integer variables have score \(1/2\). Branching on \(x\) leaves lower bound \(0\) in both children, while branching on \(z\) gives lower bound \(1/2\) in both children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variables can tie at maximum fractionality even though branching on them has different child-bound effects.
assumptions_latex: The displayed binary model is relaxed to 0\le x,z\le1.
The selected current LP optimum is (\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)=(1/2,1/2,0).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_x=m_z=\frac12,\qquad \Delta_x^- =\Delta_x^+=0,\qquad \Delta_z^- =\Delta_z^+=\frac12.
review_flags: The fractional value of the objective-irrelevant variable x occurs at a nonunique LP optimum; the example concerns rules applied to the supplied optimal relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Fractionality Does Not Predict Bound Improvement

assumptions_latex: A relaxation solution \(\bar x\) is available.
The candidate set \(C(\bar x)=\{i\in I:\bar x_i\notin\mathbb{Z}\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected variable has maximum distance from the nearest integer among all fractional integer-variable candidates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical variable rule based solely on distance from integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(i\in C(\bar x)\), compute \(f_i=\bar x_i-\lfloor\bar x_i\rfloor\) and \(m_i=\min\{f_i,1-f_i\}\). Select \(i^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{i\in C(\bar x)}m_i\), using a fixed deterministic order to resolve ties. Create the two children \(x_{i^*}\leq\lfloor\bar x_{i^*}\rfloor\) and \(x_{i^*}\geq\lceil\bar x_{i^*}\rceil\). The rule stops without a selection when \(C(\bar x)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the fractional integer variable farthest from its nearest integer, break ties deterministically, and apply the standard floor-ceiling split.
knowledge_statements.title: Most-Infeasible Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is a standard-looking interpretation of most-infeasible branching, but the named score convention and selection direction require a precise branching-rule source.

children.title: Fractionality Branching
children.top_down_role: Candidate ranking by displacement from admissible discrete values.

assumptions_latex: A relaxation solution \(\bar x\) and a nonempty fractional candidate set \(C(\bar x)\) are available.
A scalar ranking function \(\phi:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule selects a candidate solely through the fractional part of its relaxation value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric fractional-part rule; the convention for \(\phi\) must be fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(f_i=\bar x_i-\lfloor\bar x_i\rfloor\) for each \(i\in C(\bar x)\), then select \(i^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{i\in C(\bar x)}\phi(f_i)\), resolving ties by a fixed total order. Branch into \(x_{i^*}\leq\lfloor\bar x_{i^*}\rfloor\) and \(x_{i^*}\geq\lceil\bar x_{i^*}\rceil\). The symmetric choice \(\phi(f)=\min\{f,1-f\}\) coincides with most-infeasible branching; nonsymmetric choices can favor one displacement direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank fractional candidates using a specified function of their fractional parts, choose a deterministic maximizer, and apply its floor-ceiling split.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractionality Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An arbitrary ranking function of the fractional part is too convention-dependent to validate as the named fractionality rule without a source fixing the intended score family and direction.

children.title: Fractionality Tie Regimes
children.top_down_role: Candidate pools with indistinguishable or nearly indistinguishable fractional scores.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tolerance-tie set for the nearest-integer score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_i=\min\{f_i,1-f_i\}=\tfrac12-|f_i-\tfrac12|\), \(m^*=\max_{j\in C}m_j\), and \(d^*=\min_{j\in C}|f_j-\tfrac12|\). For \(\delta\ge0\), define \(T_\delta=\{i\in C:m^*-m_i\le\delta\}\). Then \[T_\delta=\left\{i\in C:\left|f_i-\tfrac12\right|\le d^*+\delta\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The delta-tie pool contains exactly the candidates whose distance from one-half is at most delta worse than the best distance.
assumptions_latex: C\ne\varnothing
0<f_i<1\quad(i\in C)
\delta\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_\delta=\left\{i\in C:\left|f_i-\frac12\right|\le\min_{j\in C}\left|f_j-\frac12\right|+\delta\right\}.

notation.meaning: candidates within delta of the maximum score

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Tie Characterization for Symmetric Fractionality

assumptions_latex: Candidates are scored by \(m_i=\min\{f_i,1-f_i\}\), where \(0<f_i<1\).
A nonempty candidate set \(C\) is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ties occur exactly among candidates having equal fractional parts or complementary fractional parts.

notation.meaning: Fractional part and symmetric fractionality score.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tie characterization for the symmetric nearest-integer score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidates \(i,j\in C\), \(m_i=m_j\) if and only if \(f_i=f_j\) or \(f_i=1-f_j\). Consequently, with \(m^*=\max_{i\in C}m_i\), the tie set is \[T=\{i\in C:m_i=m^*\}.\] In particular, every candidate with \(f_i=1/2\) receives the largest possible score \(1/2\), so all such candidates tie globally. A deterministic branching rule must refine \(T\) using an additional score or a fixed total order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the symmetric fractionality score, candidates tie exactly when their fractional parts are equal or complementary; all half-integral candidates tie at the maximum possible score.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractionality Tie Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tie characterization is algebraically precise and fits a property container, but the record has no citation. Standard-field rationale alone does not satisfy this statement review's citation requirement for the named branching context.

children.title: Least-Infeasible Branching
children.top_down_role: Candidate ranking favoring proximity to a discrete value.

assumptions_latex: At the current branch-and-bound node, the relaxation solution is \(\bar x\), and the candidate set is \(F=\{j:\bar x_j\notin\mathbb Z\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected candidate minimizes distance to integrality.

notation.meaning: Distance of the relaxed value to its nearest integer.

review_flags: Exact convention and tie-breaking require a directly relevant branching reference.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical least-infeasible selection at one branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F\neq\varnothing\), compute \(d_j=\min\{\bar x_j-\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor,\lceil\bar x_j\rceil-\bar x_j\}\) for every \(j\in F\). Select any \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in F}d_j\), using a fixed deterministic rule to break ties. Create the usual two children \(x_{j^*}\le\lfloor\bar x_{j^*}\rfloor\) and \(x_{j^*}\ge\lceil\bar x_{j^*}\rceil\). Thus the rule favors a candidate whose current relaxed value is closest to an admissible integer value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a fractional integer variable closest to an integer, then create the standard down and up children.
knowledge_statements.title: Least-Infeasible Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf's ranking role and is internally well specified, but no citation supports that minimizing nearest-integer distance is the established meaning of least-infeasible branching or supports the stated tie-breaking convention.

children.title: Propagation-History Branching Scores
children.top_down_role: Candidate ranking by observed domain-reduction effects.

children.title: Inference Branching
children.top_down_role: Candidate ranking by anticipated domain-reduction influence.

assumptions_latex: For each candidate \(j\), tentative branching or propagation supplies nonnegative inference counts \(I_j^-\) and \(I_j^+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A candidate maximizing an aggregation of its two inference counts is selected.

notation.meaning: Numbers of domain reductions inferred in the down and up branches.
Monotone aggregation of directional inference counts.

review_flags: Inference-count definition and aggregation convention vary by solver and require a relevant source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate ranking by domain propagation caused in tentative child nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the current set of branching candidates. For every \(j\in F\), apply the prescribed propagation procedure separately under the down and up branching restrictions and record \(I_j^-\) and \(I_j^+\), counting only newly derived bound tightenings or fixings. For a coordinatewise nondecreasing aggregation \(A:\mathbb R_+^2\to\mathbb R\), define \(s_j=A(I_j^-,I_j^+)\) and choose \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in F}s_j\). The children are the two restrictions used to obtain the directional inference counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tentatively propagate both branches of each candidate and choose one with the best aggregated number of inferred domain reductions.
knowledge_statements.title: Inference Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches inference-based branching, but the definition of a counted inference, the tentative propagation procedure, and the admissible directional aggregation are solver-dependent and have no cited support.

children.title: Propagation-History Branching
children.top_down_role: Candidate ranking using recorded propagation effects from prior search.

assumptions_latex: Historical directional inference estimates \(\widehat I_j^-\) and \(\widehat I_j^+\) are available for every current candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branching candidates are ranked without repeating full tentative propagation.

notation.meaning: Historical estimates of directional propagation effects.

review_flags: Update, normalization, and aggregation conventions require a directly relevant source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-based approximation of inference branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with candidate set \(F\), assign each \(j\in F\) the score \(s_j=A(\widehat I_j^-,\widehat I_j^+)\), where \(A:\mathbb R_+^2\to\mathbb R\) is coordinatewise nondecreasing. Select \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in F}s_j\), apply its down and up branching restrictions, and run propagation in the resulting children. After observing counts \(I_{j^*}^-\) and \(I_{j^*}^+\), update the corresponding historical estimates by the solver's prescribed averaging rule. Unobserved directions retain their existing estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank candidates using past directional propagation effects, branch on the highest score, and update the selected candidate's history from observed children.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-History Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits a history-based approximation to inference branching, but its estimator, normalization, update rule, and retention of unobserved estimates are not established by any inspectable source.

children.title: Historical Inference Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of recorded domain-reduction evidence across related nodes.

assumptions_latex: A source context provides historical inference statistics for variables that can be matched to variables in a target instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transferred statistics define initial target-instance inference estimates.
review_flags: No supplied source supports a canonical transfer map or normalization rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-starting propagation histories across related formulations or instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) and \(T\) denote source and target variable sets, and let \(\pi:T\rightharpoonup S\) be a validated partial correspondence. For every matched target variable \(j\), initialize \(\widehat I_j^d=R_j^d(I_{\pi(j)}^d)\) for each direction \(d\in\{-,+\}\), where \(R_j^d\) accounts for any declared difference in scaling or counting conventions. Unmatched variables receive a target-default initialization. The transferred quantities are priors only: subsequent target observations update or replace them according to the target history rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matched variables may inherit normalized inference histories from related instances, while unmatched variables use defaults and target observations subsequently revise all priors.
knowledge_statements.title: Historical Inference Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is a plausible transfer principle for the leaf, but no source establishes the variable correspondence, rescaling operators, default initialization, or prior-update interpretation. The selected principle kind also cannot be confirmed without evidence that this is a recognized general principle rather than one particular transfer algorithm.

children.title: Misleading Propagation Histories
children.top_down_role: Regimes where prior propagation effects poorly predict current branching value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary propagation family whose historical and current inference rankings are reversed by context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K\ge1\), let \(a,b,t,z_1,\ldots,z_K,w_1,\ldots,w_K\) be binary with \(z_r=a\land t\) and \(w_r=b\land(1-t)\). Under exact propagation for these equalities, counting newly fixed auxiliary variables after tentative candidate fixings, observations at a node with \(t=1\) give \(H_a=K\) and \(H_b=0\), whereas a current node with \(t=0\) gives \(I_a=0\) and \(I_b=K\). A maximum-history rule therefore selects \(a\) despite an additive current-inference loss of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A context bit can reverse which of two candidates fixes K auxiliaries, so stored propagation history can incur unbounded additive inference loss.
assumptions_latex: K\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}.
Propagation is exact for the displayed binary AND equalities.
Only newly fixed auxiliary variables are counted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_a=K>0=H_b,\qquad I_a=0<K=I_b,\qquad I_b-I_a=K.

notation.meaning: historically recorded inference count for candidate j
current-node inference count for candidate j

knowledge_statements.title: Context-Reversal Construction for Propagation Histories

assumptions_latex: Propagation-history scores are computed from past observations rather than exact current-node propagation effects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Historical ranking can select a candidate with arbitrarily smaller current inference than the best candidate.

notation.meaning: Historical score and current realized inference count.

review_flags: Concrete realizability under a specified propagation system requires a directly relevant source or construction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by nonstationary or context-dependent propagation effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(M>0\), consider two candidates \(a\) and \(b\) whose stored historical scores satisfy \(H_a=1\) and \(H_b=0\), while their current-node inference counts satisfy \(I_a=0\) and \(I_b=M\). A rule selecting a maximum historical score chooses \(a\), although current inference branching chooses \(b\). Hence, without an assumption connecting historical and current propagation effects, neither a positive approximation ratio nor a finite additive loss bound follows from history-based selection alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When propagation effects change with context, history can prefer a useless candidate while another candidate produces arbitrarily many current inferences.
knowledge_statements.title: Misleading Propagation Histories

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon fits the leaf and the abstract score comparison is clear, but it is not a concrete realizable branching-and-propagation construction. Moreover, inference counts are discrete while the statement assigns the arbitrary real value M directly as a count. A source or construction is required to determine the valid quantified version.

children.title: Problem-Structure Branching Scores
children.top_down_role: Candidate rankings derived from application or formulation structure.

assumptions_latex: Each branching candidate has application or formulation metadata from which a real-valued structural feature vector can be computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A declared scoring map converts structural features into a branching ranking.

notation.meaning: Structural feature vector of candidate variable.

review_flags: The node denotes a broad solver family; no supplied source fixes a canonical structural score.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic formulation of application-aware branching scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node with candidate set \(F\), assign each \(j\in F\) a feature vector \(\phi_j\in\mathbb R^p\) derived only from declared problem structure, such as block membership, network position, symmetry class, or constraint incidence. Fix a scoring map \(g:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\), define \(s_j=g(\phi_j)\), and select any \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in F}s_j\). The feature construction, scaling, score map, and tie-breaking rule must be fixed independently of the candidate ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute declared structural features for each candidate, map them to scores, and branch on a maximum-scoring variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Structure Branching Scores

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle matches the broad role of structure-derived candidate rankings, but the arbitrary feature and scoring-map template is not supported by a branching reference. The inventory entries on block or network structure do not specifically support this branching rule.

children.title: Pseudocost Branching
children.top_down_role: History-based prediction of branching effects.

children.title: Pseudocost Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Alternative organizations of historical branching information.

children.title: Directional Pseudocosts
children.top_down_role: Separate historical estimates for alternative branching directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-equivalence of mean-of-ratios and pooled directional estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta_k>0\), define \(p_{\mathrm{mr}}=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n\Delta_k/\delta_k\) and \(p_{\mathrm{pool}}=(\sum_k\Delta_k)/(\sum_k\delta_k)\). They need not agree: for \((\Delta_1,\delta_1)=(1,1)\) and \((\Delta_2,\delta_2)=(9,3)\), \(p_{\mathrm{mr}}=2\) whereas \(p_{\mathrm{pool}}=5/2\). Therefore the accumulation convention must be specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging individual improvement rates can differ from dividing total improvement by total displacement.
assumptions_latex: n\ge1
\Delta_k\ge0
\delta_k>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_{\mathrm{mr}}\ne p_{\mathrm{pool}}\text{ in general}.

notation.meaning: ratio of total improvement to total displacement

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Estimator Convention Boundary

assumptions_latex: Observed branchings on variable \(j\) provide nonnegative relaxation-bound improvements and positive fractional displacements in each observed direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each directional pseudocost is the empirical mean bound improvement per unit displacement.

notation.meaning: Observed bound improvement and displacement for observation k in direction d.

review_flags: A directly relevant source is needed to certify treatment of infeasible children and censored improvements.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical directional bound-improvement rates for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For direction \(d\in\{-,+\}\), let \(n_j^d\ge 1\) observations be available, with relaxation-bound improvement \(\Delta_{j,k}^d\ge 0\) and branching displacement \(\delta_{j,k}^d>0\). The directional pseudocost is \[p_j^d=\frac{1}{n_j^d}\sum_{k=1}^{n_j^d}\frac{\Delta_{j,k}^d}{\delta_{j,k}^d}.\] For a current fractional value \(\bar x_j\), the predicted directional improvements are \(q_j^-=p_j^-(\bar x_j-\lfloor\bar x_j\rfloor)\) and \(q_j^+=p_j^+(\lceil\bar x_j\rceil-\bar x_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directional pseudocost averages observed relaxation-bound improvement per unit branching displacement, separately for down and up branches.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional Pseudocosts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the directional-pseudocost leaf, but pseudocost estimators differ between averaging individual improvement-to-displacement ratios and other cumulative conventions. No source verifies this choice or the treatment of infeasible and censored child observations.

children.title: Aggregated Pseudocosts
children.top_down_role: Combined historical estimates used to rank a branching candidate.

assumptions_latex: Nonnegative predicted directional improvements \(q_j^-\) and \(q_j^+\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A scalar score combines both directional predictions for candidate ranking.

notation.meaning: Predicted down and up bound improvements.

review_flags: The product and weighted min-max formulas are common variants but require a directly relevant source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar aggregation of two directional pseudocost predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate \(j\), an aggregated pseudocost score is obtained from a fixed map \(A:\mathbb R_+^2\to\mathbb R_+\) by \(s_j=A(q_j^-,q_j^+)\). Standard balance-sensitive representations include \[A_\mu(u,v)=(1-\mu)\min\{u,v\}+\mu\max\{u,v\},\qquad 0\le\mu\le 1,\] and the product representation \(A_\times(u,v)=uv\). Candidate ranking selects a maximizer of \(s_j\); therefore the aggregation map and its parameters are part of the branching rule, not merely notation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine predicted down and up improvements with a fixed scalar function, such as weighted min-max or product, and rank candidates by that score.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregated Pseudocosts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the aggregation leaf and the formulas are internally consistent, but no citation establishes the weighted min-max and product maps as the intended pseudocost-score variants or fixes the parameter convention.

children.title: Direction-Imbalance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Candidate histories with substantially unequal evidence across branching directions.

assumptions_latex: Both directional predictions are nonnegative, and at least one is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A ratio threshold defines when a candidate's directional predictions are substantially imbalanced.
review_flags: Threshold choice and zero-direction convention are modeling choices needing a relevant source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative classification of asymmetric directional predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a threshold \(\tau\ge 1\). For \(q_j^->0\) and \(q_j^+>0\), define \[\rho_j=\frac{\max\{q_j^-,q_j^+\}}{\min\{q_j^-,q_j^+\}}.\] Candidate \(j\) lies in the \(\tau\)-direction-imbalance regime exactly when \(\rho_j\ge\tau\). If precisely one of \(q_j^-\) and \(q_j^+\) is zero, set \(\rho_j=+\infty\); if both are zero, the ratio is undefined and the candidate is classified separately as having no predicted directional gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate is directionally imbalanced when its larger predicted branch gain exceeds the smaller by a declared factor, with one-sided zero gain treated as infinite imbalance.
knowledge_statements.title: Direction-Imbalance Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is precise and fits a direction-imbalance container, but the threshold classification and its zero-direction conventions are introduced without evidence that they are recognized pseudocost regimes rather than an ad hoc definition.

children.title: Aggregation-Sensitivity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Ranking instability attributable to the selected pseudocost aggregation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order information shared by the full class of coordinatewise nondecreasing scalar maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^2\). If \(u\ge v\) componentwise, then \(A(u)\ge A(v)\) for every coordinatewise nondecreasing \(A:\mathbb R_+^2\to\mathbb R\). If \(u_1>v_1\) and \(u_2<v_2\), the monotone maps \(A_1(w)=w_1\) and \(A_2(w)=w_2\) rank the pair oppositely. Thus componentwise dominance is the aggregation-independent order for this unrestricted monotone class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every monotone aggregation preserves componentwise dominance, while crossed directional gains can be ordered oppositely by different monotone maps.
assumptions_latex: u,v\in\mathbb R_+^2
A:\mathbb R_+^2\to\mathbb R\text{ is coordinatewise nondecreasing}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u\ge v\Rightarrow A(u)\ge A(v);\quad u_1>v_1,\ u_2<v_2\Rightarrow\text{opposite monotone-map rankings exist}.
review_flags: The converse concerns the unrestricted coordinatewise-monotone class; narrower symmetric or strictly increasing classes may preserve additional comparisons.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone-Aggregation Dominance Boundary

assumptions_latex: Candidate scores are formed from nonnegative directional predictions by a scalar aggregation map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Different admissible aggregations can reverse the candidate ranking when directional gains are imbalanced.
review_flags: The algebraic example is self-contained, but its status as a named branching boundary needs a source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ranking instability under alternative directional-score aggregations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let candidate \(a\) have directional predictions \((q_a^-,q_a^+)=(1,M)\) and candidate \(b\) have \((q_b^-,q_b^+)=(c,c)\), where \(M>c^2>1\). Product aggregation gives \(A_\times(a)=M>c^2=A_\times(b)\), so it ranks \(a\) above \(b\). Min aggregation, equal to \(A_0\), gives \(A_0(a)=1<c=A_0(b)\), reversing the ranking. Thus no aggregation-independent ordering exists without additional restrictions on directional imbalance or on the admissible aggregation maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An imbalanced candidate can beat a balanced candidate under product scoring but lose under minimum scoring, so aggregation choice can reverse rankings.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation-Sensitivity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic ranking reversal is correct and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf. However, no source supports presenting this example or its concluding restriction as an established aggregation-sensitivity boundary in pseudocost branching.

children.title: Pseudocost Cold-Start Transfer Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cold-start and inherited-information regimes for pseudocost estimates.

children.title: Pseudocost Initialization
children.top_down_role: Historical-score state before sufficient local branching observations exist.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pseudocount Representation of a Weighted Initializer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic representation of an initialized directional pseudocost as prior weight plus observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial value \(p_0\), weight \(w_0\geq0\), and observed normalized degradations \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\), define \(p_n=(w_0p_0+\sum_{t=1}^n y_t)/(w_0+n)\) whenever \(w_0+n>0\). Then \(p_{n+1}=((w_0+n)p_n+y_{n+1})/(w_0+n+1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted initial pseudocost is algebraically a pseudocount and supports the usual recursive weighted-mean update.
assumptions_latex: w_0\geq0

notation.meaning: Initial directional pseudocost and its effective weight.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudocount Representation of a Weighted Initializer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensional admissibility of an initial directional pseudocost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p_{j,0}^d\) predicts objective degradation per unit branching displacement, then under \(z'=\alpha z\) and \(x_j'=\beta_jx_j\), with \(\alpha,\beta_j>0\), scale compatibility requires \(p_{j,0}^{d\prime}=(\alpha/\beta_j)p_{j,0}^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An initial pseudocost must use the objective-per-displacement units of subsequent observations and transform accordingly under rescaling.
assumptions_latex: \alpha>0
\beta_j>0
p_{j,0}^d\text{ estimates objective degradation per unit displacement}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_{j,0}^{d\prime}=\frac{\alpha}{\beta_j}p_{j,0}^d

notation.meaning: Initial pseudocost for variable j and direction d.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Compatible Pseudocost Initialization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Influence of a Weighted Initializer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample persistence and asymptotic decay of initialization influence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p_n=(w_0p_0+\sum_{t=1}^ny_t)/(w_0+n)\), \(n\ge1\), and \(\bar y_n=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^ny_t\), one has \(p_n-\bar y_n=\frac{w_0}{w_0+n}(p_0-\bar y_n)\). Thus \(w_0>0\) retains initialization influence at every finite \(n\) unless \(p_0=\bar y_n\); if \(w_0<\infty\) and \((\bar y_n)\) is bounded, that influence tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive prior weight preserves a known finite-sample fraction of initialization error, although the influence vanishes for finite prior weight and bounded empirical means.
assumptions_latex: n\ge1
w_0\ge0
\bar y_n=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^ny_t
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_n-\bar y_n=\frac{w_0}{w_0+n}(p_0-\bar y_n)
review_flags: The asymptotic conclusion requires bounded empirical means, not merely pointwise finiteness.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Influence of a Weighted Initializer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational family covering fixed, direction-pooled, and structurally pooled cold-start values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each unobserved variable-direction pair \((j,d)\), choose a declared finite default \(q_j^d\) or a nonempty compatible reference multiset \(P_j^d\) and finite statistic \(T_j^d(P_j^d)\), and set \(p_{j,0}^d=q_j^d\) or \(p_{j,0}^d=T_j^d(P_j^d)\). Assign a finite effective weight \(w_{j,0}^d\ge0\). After normalized observations \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\), use \[p_{j,n}^d=\frac{w_{j,0}^dp_{j,0}^d+\sum_{t=1}^ny_t}{w_{j,0}^d+n}\] whenever the denominator is positive. Fixed defaults, direction-wide pools, and pools restricted by a declared structural class are obtained by the corresponding choices of \(q_j^d\) and \(P_j^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize each missing directional pseudocost from a declared finite default or compatible pool, give it an explicit prior weight, and blend it with subsequent normalized observations.
assumptions_latex: All pooled values and observations use the same objective-degradation-per-displacement units.
Each pool-eligibility rule and statistic is declared before scoring.
Every selected statistic is finite, and \(w_{j,0}^d+n>0\) when the estimate is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every missing directional estimate is finite and its transition to empirical data is explicitly defined.}

notation.meaning: declared compatible reference multiset for variable j and direction d
finite pool statistic such as a mean or median
effective weight assigned to the initializer

review_flags: This defines a policy family; predictive quality of any selected pool remains instance- and solver-dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameterized Pseudocost Initialization Policy

assumptions_latex: Some variable-direction pairs have no observed pseudocost, while a nonempty reference pool of observations or defaults is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every missing directional pseudocost receives a finite initial estimate before candidate scoring.

notation.meaning: Initial pseudocost for variable j and direction d.

review_flags: Initialization policies are solver-dependent and require a directly relevant source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cold-start completion of missing directional pseudocosts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each direction \(d\in\{-,+\}\), form a declared reference multiset \(P^d\subset[0,+\infty)\) from previously observed compatible rates or supplied defaults. For every pair \((j,d)\) with no observation, set \(p_{j,0}^d=T_d(P^d)\), where \(T_d\) is a fixed finite location functional, such as a mean or median. Retain empirical pseudocosts for observed pairs. Use these completed directional values to compute candidate scores until genuine observations for \((j,d)\) become available, at which point the initialization is updated or replaced by the prescribed estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fill each unobserved directional pseudocost from a declared reference statistic, then replace or update it as genuine branching observations arrive.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudocost Initialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits pseudocost initialization, but the reference pool, finite location functional, retention policy, and replacement rule describe a family of possible solver policies rather than a sourced initialization method.

children.title: Pseudocost Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of pseudocost information across nodes, variables, or related runs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensional condition for transferring a normalized objective-degradation rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p_S=\Delta z_S/\Delta x_S\), while target units satisfy \(\Delta z_T=\alpha\Delta z_S\) and \(\Delta x_T=\beta\Delta x_S\) with \(\alpha,\beta>0\), then the unit-consistent transferred rate is \(p_T=(\alpha/\beta)p_S\). Copying the numerical value unchanged is unit-invariant exactly when \(\alpha=\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transferred pseudocost must be rescaled by the objective-unit factor divided by the displacement-unit factor.
assumptions_latex: p_S=\Delta z_S/\Delta x_S
\Delta z_T=\alpha\Delta z_S
\Delta x_T=\beta\Delta x_S
\alpha,\beta>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_T=\frac{\alpha}{\beta}p_S
knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Consistent Pseudocost Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary structural and dimensional conditions for transferring a directional pseudocost observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direct transfer from source variable \(i\) to target variable \(j\) in direction \(d\in\{-,+\}\) is admissible only after validating the variable correspondence, matching the branch direction and rate definition, and declaring a positive conversion factor \(\gamma_j^d\). For matched rates this gives \(p_{j,T}^d=\gamma_j^dp_{i,S}^d\). If target objective and displacement units scale by \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), respectively, then \(\gamma_j^d=\alpha/\beta\). Passing these checks is necessary but does not establish predictive comparability of the search contexts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct transfer requires a validated variable and direction match, compatible rate definitions, and a positive unit conversion; these checks do not guarantee predictive similarity.
assumptions_latex: \gamma_j^d>0
\text{Source and target directional displacements are positive magnitudes under the same rate convention}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_{j,T}^d=\gamma_j^dp_{i,S}^d

notation.meaning: Declared conversion factor for the matched directional rate.

review_flags: Structural correspondence must be validated externally; dimensional consistency is not sufficient for predictive comparability.
knowledge_statements.title: Direction- and Unit-Compatible Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete transfer contract with mapping, conversion, unmatched-pair handling, and target updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi:T\rightharpoonup S\) be a validated target-to-source variable correspondence. For each matched \((j,d)\), set \(p_{j,0}^d=\gamma_j^dp_{\pi(j),S}^d\), where \(\gamma_j^d>0\) converts objective and displacement units, and assign a finite weight \(w_{j,0}^d>0\). Initialize unmatched pairs by the target initialization policy. After target observations \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\), update a matched pair by \[p_{j,n}^d=\frac{w_{j,0}^dp_{j,0}^d+\sum_{t=1}^ny_t}{w_{j,0}^d+n}.\] A replacement policy is the limiting special convention that discards \(p_{j,0}^d\) when the first target observation arrives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map and rescale matched source pseudocosts into finite-weight target priors, initialize unmatched pairs locally, and blend or explicitly replace transferred values as target evidence arrives.
assumptions_latex: The correspondence preserves the variable meaning and branch direction.
Source and target rates use compatible definitions after applying \(\gamma_j^d\).
Every prior weight is finite and declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The transferred estimate and its subsequent dependence on target evidence are fully specified.}

notation.meaning: effective weight of the transferred estimate

review_flags: Structural and dimensional admissibility does not guarantee predictive similarity; that risk belongs to Transfer-Bias Boundaries.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Source-to-Target Pseudocost Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample and asymptotic influence under weighted target updating.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the weighted transfer estimator and \(n\ge1\), let \(\bar y_n=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^ny_t\). Then \[p_{j,n}^d-\bar y_n=\frac{w_{j,0}^d}{w_{j,0}^d+n}\bigl(p_{j,0}^d-\bar y_n\bigr).\] Thus transferred information has nonzero finite-sample influence unless the displayed discrepancy vanishes, while its influence tends to zero for finite \(w_{j,0}^d\) when \((\bar y_n)\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-weight transferred value has an exactly quantifiable influence that vanishes as bounded target evidence accumulates.
assumptions_latex: n\ge1
0<w_{j,0}^d<\infty
\bar y_n=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^ny_t
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_{j,n}^d-\bar y_n=\frac{w_{j,0}^d}{w_{j,0}^d+n}(p_{j,0}^d-\bar y_n)
review_flags: The asymptotic conclusion requires finite prior weight and bounded target empirical means.
knowledge_statements.title: Decay of Finite-Weight Transfer Influence

assumptions_latex: Source and target models admit a validated variable correspondence and compatible objective-bound scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Normalized source pseudocosts provide target priors that are subsequently revised by target observations.
review_flags: No supplied source establishes a canonical transfer or normalization scheme.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-starting pseudocosts across related instances or formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi:T\rightharpoonup S\) match target variables to source variables. For every matched \(j\in T\) and direction \(d\in\{-,+\}\), initialize \(p_{j,T}^d=r_j^d p_{\pi(j),S}^d\), where \(r_j^d>0\) is the declared conversion factor for objective-bound and variable-displacement units. Initialize unmatched pairs by the target default rule. Treat each transferred value as a prior with declared effective sample weight \(w_{j,0}^d\ge 0\), and combine it with subsequent target rates using the target estimator; setting \(w_{j,0}^d=0\) discards the transferred value after the first observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map and rescale source pseudocosts into target priors, use defaults for unmatched variables, and revise the priors with target observations.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudocost Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the transfer leaf, but no citation establishes cross-instance pseudocost transfer with the stated correspondence, multiplicative normalization, effective sample weight, or first-observation behavior. These choices materially determine the mathematical algorithm.

children.title: Cold-Start Pseudocost Regimes
children.top_down_role: Early-search conditions with sparse candidate-specific evidence.

assumptions_latex: The current node LP relaxation has optimal value \(z\) and a nonempty set \(F\) of fractional integer variables.
For each \(j\in F\), branching distances are \(d_j^- = x_j^*-\lfloor x_j^*\rfloor\) and \(d_j^+=\lceil x_j^*\rceil-x_j^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cold-start pseudocost regime is specified by initialized directional estimates \((\widetilde p_j^-,\widetilde p_j^+)\) for every \(j\in F\) lacking observations, together with a transition threshold \(r\geq 1\). Before direction \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\) has been observed \(r\) times, its predicted degradation is \(\widehat\Delta_j^\sigma=d_j^\sigma\widetilde p_j^\sigma\); afterward, \(\widetilde p_j^\sigma\) is replaced by the empirical mean normalized degradation \(p_j^\sigma\). A branching score such as \(S_j=\min\{\widehat\Delta_j^-,\widehat\Delta_j^+\}+\mu\max\{\widehat\Delta_j^-,\widehat\Delta_j^+\}\), with \(\mu\geq0\), selects a maximizer over \(F\).

notation.meaning: downward and upward fractional branching distances
required observations before empirical pseudocost use

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes initialization and transition rules for pseudocost branching with no local observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cold-start pseudocost regime is specified by initialized directional estimates \((\widetilde p_j^-,\widetilde p_j^+)\) for every \(j\in F\) lacking observations, together with a transition threshold \(r\geq 1\). Before direction \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\) has been observed \(r\) times, its predicted degradation is \(\widehat\Delta_j^\sigma=d_j^\sigma\widetilde p_j^\sigma\); afterward, \(\widetilde p_j^\sigma\) is replaced by the empirical mean normalized degradation \(p_j^\sigma\). A branching score such as \(S_j=\min\{\widehat\Delta_j^-,\widehat\Delta_j^+\}+\mu\max\{\widehat\Delta_j^-,\widehat\Delta_j^+\}\), with \(\mu\geq0\), selects a maximizer over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unobserved branching directions use initialized pseudocosts until enough local observations exist, after which empirical pseudocosts determine predicted child-bound improvements and the branching score.
knowledge_statements.title: Cold-Start Pseudocost Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source supports the initialization rule, observation threshold, or scoring convention. The condition kind is plausible for this regime leaf, but the proposed regime is only one possible implementation and cannot be treated as canonical without targeted evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected as a generic decision-theoretic construction rather than a pseudocost-specific result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a deterministic selector receive identical observable information for candidates \(a,b\). If the admissible environment class contains observationally identical environments with opposite quality orderings, the selector is suboptimal in at least one environment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observationally indistinguishable environments with opposite candidate rankings defeat any deterministic selector in one environment.
assumptions_latex: \text{The selector is deterministic.}
\text{Candidate quality is not identified by the observable state.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The selector is not uniformly correct over the admissible environments.}
knowledge_statements.title: Cold-Start Indistinguishability

intermediate_metadata.reason: The leaf should characterize early-search pseudocost evidence regimes, but a canonical threshold and state classification are materially ambiguous. The Builder's indistinguishability statement is valid generic decision theory, not primarily a pseudocost cold-start result. Pseudocost Initialization, Pseudocost Transfer, and Transfer-Bias Boundaries were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Transfer-Bias Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Prediction risks created by inherited estimates from dissimilar search contexts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp sufficient score-error condition preserving a unique ideal branching choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\) be the unique maximizer of ideal scores \(S_j\), and let transferred scores be \(\widetilde S_j=S_j+e_j\) with \(|e_j|\leq\eta_j\). If \(S_a-S_k>\eta_a+\eta_k\) for every \(k\neq a\), then \(a\) remains the unique maximizer of \(\widetilde S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transferred ranking is preserved when every ideal score gap exceeds the combined error bounds of the winning and competing candidates.
assumptions_latex: a\in\operatorname*{argmax}_j S_j\text{ uniquely}
\widetilde S_j=S_j+e_j
|e_j|\leq\eta_j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[\forall k\neq a:\ S_a-S_k>\eta_a+\eta_k\right]\Longrightarrow\operatorname*{argmax}_j\widetilde S_j=\{a\}

notation.meaning: Transfer-induced score error and its bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Score-Margin Robustness to Transfer Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal score perturbation reversing a branching ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_a=1+\varepsilon\) and \(S_b=1\), where \(\varepsilon>0\). For transfer errors \(e_a=-\varepsilon\) and \(e_b=\varepsilon\), the transferred scores are \(\widetilde S_a=1\) and \(\widetilde S_b=1+\varepsilon\). Thus transfer replaces the unique ideal maximizer \(a\) by \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily small transfer errors can reverse candidates whose ideal score gap is correspondingly small.
assumptions_latex: \varepsilon>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in\{a,b\}}S_j=\{a\},\qquad\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in\{a,b\}}\widetilde S_j=\{b\}
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Candidate Transfer Reversal

assumptions_latex: A transferred directional pseudocost is \(\widetilde p_j^\sigma=p_j^\sigma+b_j^\sigma\), where \(p_j^\sigma\) is the target-regime value.
Candidate scores are computed from nonnegative predicted degradations by a coordinatewise nondecreasing function \(g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For candidate \(j\), let \(S_j=g(d_j^-p_j^-,d_j^+p_j^+)\) and \(\widetilde S_j=g(d_j^-\widetilde p_j^-,d_j^+\widetilde p_j^+)\). Transfer preserves the ideal choice whenever, for an ideal maximizer \(j^*\), \(S_{j^*}-S_k> |\widetilde S_{j^*}-S_{j^*}|+|\widetilde S_k-S_k|\) for every \(k\neq j^*\). At the boundary where this strict margin fails, transferred bias can reverse the ranking. Without uniform control of \(b_j^\sigma\), the reversal can be arbitrarily large even when all transferred pseudocosts are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a score-margin boundary beyond which transferred pseudocost bias can change the branching decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate \(j\), let \(S_j=g(d_j^-p_j^-,d_j^+p_j^+)\) and \(\widetilde S_j=g(d_j^-\widetilde p_j^-,d_j^+\widetilde p_j^+)\). Transfer preserves the ideal choice whenever, for an ideal maximizer \(j^*\), \(S_{j^*}-S_k> |\widetilde S_{j^*}-S_{j^*}|+|\widetilde S_k-S_k|\) for every \(k\neq j^*\). At the boundary where this strict margin fails, transferred bias can reverse the ranking. Without uniform control of \(b_j^\sigma\), the reversal can be arbitrarily large even when all transferred pseudocosts are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transferred pseudocosts preserve a branching choice only while their score errors remain below the ideal score margin; beyond that boundary, candidate rankings may reverse.
knowledge_statements.title: Transfer-Bias Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The score-margin inequality is a sufficient perturbation condition, but the claims about the boundary and arbitrarily large reversal require additional assumptions on the score function and biases. The failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, but the mathematical version needs a source.

children.title: Pseudocost History-Reliability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Reliability boundaries for history-based predictions.

children.title: Sparse-History Failures
children.top_down_role: Unreliable pseudocost predictions caused by too few observations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chebyshev sample-size bound for a stationary directional empirical pseudocost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) are independent with common mean \(p\) and variance \(v<\infty\), then for \(\widehat p_n=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nY_t\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\Pr(|\widehat p_n-p|\geq\varepsilon)\leq v/(n\varepsilon^2)\). Consequently, confidence at least \(1-\delta\) is guaranteed when \(n\geq v/(\delta\varepsilon^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under independent stationary finite-variance observations, directional pseudocost accuracy improves at the inverse-sample-size rate.
assumptions_latex: Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\text{ are independent}
\mathbb E[Y_t]=p
\operatorname{Var}(Y_t)=v<\infty
\varepsilon>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(|\widehat p_n-p|\geq\varepsilon)\leq\frac{v}{n\varepsilon^2}
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sample Pseudocost Accuracy Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-variance example in which sparse empirical pseudocosts reverse the true candidate ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let candidate \(a\) have one observation \(Y_a\in\{0,2\}\) with equal probabilities, and let candidate \(b\) have the deterministic observation \(Y_b=3/4\). Their true means satisfy \(p_a=1>p_b=3/4\), but with probability \(1/2\) the one-observation empirical scores satisfy \(\widehat p_a=0<\widehat p_b=3/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one observation per candidate, finite-variance empirical pseudocosts can select the candidate having the lower true mean.
assumptions_latex: Y_b=3/4\text{ surely}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_a>p_b\quad\text{and}\quad\Pr(\widehat p_a<\widehat p_b)=\frac12

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reliability boundary for missing or finitely many directional observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=0\), the empirical directional pseudocost \(\widehat p_n=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nY_t\) is undefined. For any finite \(n\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), finite-positive-variance observation laws exist for which \(\Pr(|\widehat p_n-p|>\varepsilon)>0\). Thus a finite observation count alone supplies neither a deterministic accuracy guarantee nor a uniform candidate-ranking guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unobserved directions have no empirical pseudocost, and finitely many observations alone cannot guarantee deterministic accuracy or correct ranking.
assumptions_latex: p=\mathbb E[Y_t]
0<\operatorname{Var}(Y_t)<\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: n=0\Rightarrow\widehat p_n\text{ undefined};\qquad n<\infty\not\Rightarrow |\widehat p_n-p|\leq\varepsilon\text{ surely}

assumptions_latex: Directional observations \(Y_{j,1}^\sigma,\ldots,Y_{j,n}^\sigma\) have mean \(p_j^\sigma\) and positive variance.
The empirical pseudocost is \(\widehat p_j^\sigma=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nY_{j,t}^\sigma\).

If some candidate directions have \(n=0\), their empirical pseudocosts are undefined. Consequently, a rule using raw empirical means without initialization, shrinkage, or reliability probing can assign undefined scores or misrank candidates with positive probability; no uniform ranking guarantee follows solely from finite sparse counts.

children.title: Pseudocost Nonstationarity
children.top_down_role: Historical-score drift across nodes, depths, or search phases.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Bias Under Alternating Search States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonstationary sequence for which a growing full-history mean does not estimate the current-state value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let deterministic observations satisfy \(Y_t=0\) for odd \(t\) and \(Y_t=1\) for even \(t\). For every even \(n\), \(\widehat p_n=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nY_t=1/2\), while the current-state value is \(Y_n=1\). Hence \(|\widehat p_n-Y_n|=1/2\) for every even \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expanding full-history average can retain constant current-state error when branch outcomes alternate between search regimes.
assumptions_latex: Y_t=\mathbf 1\{t\text{ is even}\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left|\widehat p_n-Y_n\right|=\frac12\quad\text{for every even }n
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Bias Under Alternating Search States

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stochastic definition separating realized observations from their state-dependent conditional means.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_t\) be a normalized directional branch-degradation observation collected in search state \(s_t\), and let \(p(s)=\mathbb E[Y_t\mid s_t=s]\). The directional pseudocost process is nonstationary on \(\mathcal S\) when \(p(s)\neq p(s')\) for some \(s,s'\in\mathcal S\). Conditional on states \(s_1,\ldots,s_n\), the full-history mean \(\widehat p_n=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nY_t\) has expectation \(n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^np(s_t)\), so its bias for the current state \(s\) is \(n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^n(p(s_t)-p(s))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pseudocosts are nonstationary when their conditional mean depends on search state; a full-history average then targets the average of past state means rather than necessarily the current mean.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb E[|Y_t|\mid s_t]<\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[\widehat p_n\mid s_1,\ldots,s_n]-p(s)=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n\bigl(p(s_t)-p(s)\bigr)

notation.meaning: Search state in which observation t is collected.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Dependent Pseudocost Nonstationarity

assumptions_latex: At search state \(s\), the conditional mean normalized degradation for candidate direction \((j,\sigma)\) is \(p_j^\sigma(s)\).
Historical observations arise at states \(s_1,\ldots,s_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pseudocosts are nonstationary on a state family \(\mathcal S\) when there exist \(s,s'\in\mathcal S\), a candidate \(j\), and \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\) such that \(p_j^\sigma(s)\neq p_j^\sigma(s')\). The historical mean estimates \(n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^np_j^\sigma(s_t)\), rather than the current value \(p_j^\sigma(s)\). Hence its current-state bias is \(n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^n[p_j^\sigma(s_t)-p_j^\sigma(s)]\), which need not vanish as \(n\) increases unless the sampled-state distribution concentrates appropriately or the conditional mean is stationary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines nonstationarity through state-dependent expected normalized bound improvements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Pseudocosts are nonstationary on a state family \(\mathcal S\) when there exist \(s,s'\in\mathcal S\), a candidate \(j\), and \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\) such that \(p_j^\sigma(s)\neq p_j^\sigma(s')\). The historical mean estimates \(n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^np_j^\sigma(s_t)\), rather than the current value \(p_j^\sigma(s)\). Hence its current-state bias is \(n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^n[p_j^\sigma(s_t)-p_j^\sigma(s)]\), which need not vanish as \(n\) increases unless the sampled-state distribution concentrates appropriately or the conditional mean is stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When expected normalized branch improvements depend on the search state, accumulated pseudocosts estimate a historical average that may remain biased for the current node.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudocost Nonstationarity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonstationarity definition fits the property container, but the record does not introduce the random historical observations needed to justify what an empirical mean estimates. The bias formula concerns an average of conditional means rather than the observed pseudocost estimator, and no source resolves this distinction.

children.title: Stale-History Failures
children.top_down_role: Ranking errors caused by outdated branching observations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sample Size Does Not Cure Staleness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ranking reversal caused by obsolete observations regardless of sample multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix any \(n\ge1\). Suppose every retained observation gives \(p_a=2\) and \(p_b=1\), while the current-state rates are \(p_a(s)=0\) and \(p_b(s)=3\). Then \(\overline p_a>\overline p_b\), but \(p_a(s)<p_b(s)\); duplicating the stale observations leaves the reversal unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily many consistent old observations can rank candidates oppositely from their current branching quality.
assumptions_latex: n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}
\text{The candidates have equal current branching displacement.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline p_a>\overline p_b\quad\text{and}\quad p_a(s)<p_b(s)\quad\text{for every }n.

notation.meaning: historical mean pseudocost for candidate j

knowledge_statements.title: Sample Size Does Not Cure Staleness

assumptions_latex: The current state is \(s\), while all retained observations for direction \((j,\sigma)\) were collected at states \(s_t\).
The drift satisfies \(|p_j^\sigma(s_t)-p_j^\sigma(s)|\leq L\rho(s_t,s)\) for a metric \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the historical mean \(\overline p_j^\sigma=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^np_j^\sigma(s_t)\), the drift component of current-state error satisfies \(|\overline p_j^\sigma-p_j^\sigma(s)|\leq L n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^n\rho(s_t,s)\). Thus a history is stale whenever its average state distance is too large relative to the score margin required to distinguish candidates. If no bound on \(L\) or on historical distances is imposed, increasing the observation count alone cannot bound current-state error, and an arbitrarily well-sampled but stale history may reverse the branching ranking.

notation.meaning: metric measuring separation of search states

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies staleness through drift between historical and current search states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the historical mean \(\overline p_j^\sigma=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^np_j^\sigma(s_t)\), the drift component of current-state error satisfies \(|\overline p_j^\sigma-p_j^\sigma(s)|\leq L n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^n\rho(s_t,s)\). Thus a history is stale whenever its average state distance is too large relative to the score margin required to distinguish candidates. If no bound on \(L\) or on historical distances is imposed, increasing the observation count alone cannot bound current-state error, and an arbitrarily well-sampled but stale history may reverse the branching ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a large history can be unreliable when observations come from distant search states; sample count alone does not control drift-induced ranking error.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-History Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed Lipschitz drift bound is mathematically plausible, but the staleness threshold relative to a score margin and the arbitrary ranking-reversal claim require a specified scoring rule and candidate-score assumptions. The failure_boundary kind is appropriate.

children.title: History-Coverage Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Candidate comparison problems caused by uneven observation counts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampling-precision consequence of unequal directional pseudocost histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each candidate direction \((j,\sigma)\), let \(\widehat p_j^\sigma=(n_j^\sigma)^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{n_j^\sigma}Y_{j,t}^\sigma\), where \(n_j^\sigma\geq1\) and the observations are independent with common variance \(v_j^\sigma<\infty\). Then \(\operatorname{Var}(\widehat p_j^\sigma)=v_j^\sigma/n_j^\sigma\). Thus unequal counts generally produce unequal precision; count ordering alone does not order precision when directional variances differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: More observations reduce a directional sample mean's variance, but unequal counts alone do not determine relative precision when outcome variances differ.
assumptions_latex: n_j^\sigma\geq1
Y_{j,t}^\sigma\text{ are independent with common finite variance }v_j^\sigma
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Var}(\widehat p_j^\sigma)=\frac{v_j^\sigma}{n_j^\sigma}
knowledge_statements.title: Unequal-Count Precision Imbalance

assumptions_latex: Each candidate direction \((j,\sigma)\) has observation count \(n_j^\sigma\geq0\).
A reliability threshold \(r\geq1\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Define directional coverage by \(c_j^\sigma=\min\{1,n_j^\sigma/r\}\). History coverage is imbalanced over candidate set \(F\) when \(\max_{j,k\in F,\,\sigma,\tau\in\{-,+\}}|c_j^\sigma-c_k^\tau|>0\), and it is fully reliable only if \(c_j^\sigma=1\) for all \(j\in F\) and both directions. Comparing raw pseudocost scores across unequal coverage levels compares estimates with unequal evidential support. In particular, a high score from a low-coverage direction cannot be assigned the same reliability as a score based on at least \(r\) observations without an additional calibration rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines imbalance among candidate-direction histories relative to a common reliability threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define directional coverage by \(c_j^\sigma=\min\{1,n_j^\sigma/r\}\). History coverage is imbalanced over candidate set \(F\) when \(\max_{j,k\in F,\,\sigma,\tau\in\{-,+\}}|c_j^\sigma-c_k^\tau|>0\), and it is fully reliable only if \(c_j^\sigma=1\) for all \(j\in F\) and both directions. Comparing raw pseudocost scores across unequal coverage levels compares estimates with unequal evidential support. In particular, a high score from a low-coverage direction cannot be assigned the same reliability as a score based on at least \(r\) observations without an additional calibration rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage is imbalanced when candidate directions have unequal normalized observation counts; raw scores then carry unequal reliability unless the branching rule explicitly calibrates them.
knowledge_statements.title: History-Coverage Imbalance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed normalized coverage measure is an uncited convention. Reaching an arbitrary count threshold does not by itself make an estimate fully reliable, so the reliability language needs targeted support or qualification. The condition kind is plausible for the leaf.

children.title: Strong Branching
children.top_down_role: Candidate evaluation through temporary descendant relaxations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporary evaluation of both child LP relaxations for selected fractional integer variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization problem, let C be a selected set of basic integer variables that are fractional in the current LP solution. For each j\in C, temporarily form the down and up branches and reoptimize each child LP either to optimality or for a prescribed number of dual-simplex pivots, obtaining upper bounds Z_j^D and Z_j^U. Select j^*\in\arg\min_{j\in C}\max\{Z_j^D,Z_j^U\} and perform the actual branch on j^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong branching probes both branches of each selected fractional basic integer variable, either fully or for a limited number of dual-simplex pivots. For maximization, it selects the variable having the smallest worst child upper bound. Because probing is costly, it may be used selectively.
assumptions_latex: \text{The problem is formulated as a maximization problem.}
C\text{ is a selected set of basic integer variables fractional in the current LP solution.}
Z_j^D\text{ and }Z_j^U\text{ are upper bounds obtained from the temporary down and up branches.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: j^*\in\arg\min_{j\in C}\max\{Z_j^D,Z_j^U\}.
