children.title: Full Strong Branching
children.top_down_role: Broad strong-branching evaluation over eligible candidates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-local relaxation-evaluation count for exhaustive two-child strong branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be finite. If both immediate children of every \(j\in F\) are evaluated without early termination or cached reuse, full strong branching performs exactly \(2|F|\) temporary child-relaxation evaluations. With valid cached evaluations, the number of newly solved child relaxations is at most \(2|F|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustively probing both children requires two evaluations per eligible candidate before valid reuse.
assumptions_latex: |F|<\infty
\text{Each candidate has two immediate branch children.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{eval}}=2|F|\text{ without reuse},\qquad N_{\mathrm{new}}\le2|F|\text{ with valid reuse}.
knowledge_statements.title: Immediate-Child Evaluation Count

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prevents undefined arithmetic when strong-branching scores include infeasible tentative children.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an infeasible tentative child is represented by degradation \(+\infty\), a real-valued score formula must not form an undefined term such as \(0\cdot(+\infty)\). A sound rule must instead handle infeasibility separately, use extended-real arithmetic only where defined, or impose parameters that avoid undefined products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasible tentative children require an explicit scoring convention; blindly substituting infinity can make a score undefined.
assumptions_latex: \text{At least one tentative child may be infeasible.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The candidate score is well-defined only under an explicit infeasible-child convention.}
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Child Score Convention Boundary

assumptions_latex: The current LP relaxation has value \(z\) and finite fractional integer candidate set \(F\).
Each temporary child relaxation can be solved or validly bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full strong branching evaluates every \(j\in F\) by temporarily imposing \(x_j\leq\lfloor x_j^*\rfloor\) and \(x_j\geq\lceil x_j^*\rceil\), obtaining child bounds \(z_j^-\) and \(z_j^+\). Infeasible children receive degradation \(+\infty\); otherwise set \(\Delta_j^\sigma=z_j^\sigma-z\) for minimization. Compute \(S_j=\min\{\Delta_j^-,\Delta_j^+\}+\mu\max\{\Delta_j^-,\Delta_j^+\}\), where \(\mu\geq0\), choose any \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in F}S_j\), discard all temporary child states, and branch permanently on \(j^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard minimization form evaluating both immediate child relaxations for every eligible fractional candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Full strong branching evaluates every \(j\in F\) by temporarily imposing \(x_j\leq\lfloor x_j^*\rfloor\) and \(x_j\geq\lceil x_j^*\rceil\), obtaining child bounds \(z_j^-\) and \(z_j^+\). Infeasible children receive degradation \(+\infty\); otherwise set \(\Delta_j^\sigma=z_j^\sigma-z\) for minimization. Compute \(S_j=\min\{\Delta_j^-,\Delta_j^+\}+\mu\max\{\Delta_j^-,\Delta_j^+\}\), where \(\mu\geq0\), choose any \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in F}S_j\), discard all temporary child states, and branch permanently on \(j^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full strong branching temporarily evaluates both children of every eligible fractional variable, scores their bound improvements, and branches on a maximum-score candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Full Strong Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, but no branching source supports the exact score and infeasible-child convention. With an infinite degradation and mu equal to zero, the displayed expression can contain the undefined product zero times infinity, so the precise algorithm cannot be validated as written.

children.title: Resource-Constrained Strong Branching
children.top_down_role: Candidate filtering and resource-limited strong branching.

children.title: Restricted Strong Branching
children.top_down_role: Strong branching applied to a filtered subset of candidates.

assumptions_latex: The eligible candidate set is \(F\), and a nonempty restriction \(R\subseteq F\) is supplied.
Both temporary child relaxations are evaluated for each \(j\in R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restricted strong branching computes child degradations \(\Delta_j^-\) and \(\Delta_j^+\) only for \(j\in R\), assigns \(S_j=g(\Delta_j^-,\Delta_j^+)\) using a fixed coordinatewise nondecreasing score \(g\), and outputs any \(j_R\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in R}S_j\). It agrees with full strong branching precisely when \(R\) contains at least one global maximizer of \(S_j\) over \(F\). Without that coverage condition, the restricted method guarantees only \(S_{j_R}=\max_{j\in R}S_j\leq\max_{j\in F}S_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong branching over a prescribed proper subset of eligible candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Restricted strong branching computes child degradations \(\Delta_j^-\) and \(\Delta_j^+\) only for \(j\in R\), assigns \(S_j=g(\Delta_j^-,\Delta_j^+)\) using a fixed coordinatewise nondecreasing score \(g\), and outputs any \(j_R\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in R}S_j\). It agrees with full strong branching precisely when \(R\) contains at least one global maximizer of \(S_j\) over \(F\). Without that coverage condition, the restricted method guarantees only \(S_{j_R}=\max_{j\in R}S_j\leq\max_{j\in F}S_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted strong branching evaluates a prescribed candidate subset and matches full strong branching exactly when that subset contains a globally maximum-score candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Strong Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the leaf, and the maximum-score comparison is elementary. However, exact agreement with full strong branching depends on tie handling and whether agreement means equal score or the same selected variable; no cited source fixes those semantics.

children.title: Budgeted Strong Branching
children.top_down_role: Strong branching constrained by a finite probing resource budget.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested Evaluated Prefixes Under an Additive Budget
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-order prefix probing with positive, budget-independent complete-evaluation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an ordering (j_1,\ldots,j_m), costs c_{j_t}>0, and R(B)=\{j_1,\ldots,j_{k(B)}\}, where k(B)=\max\{k\in\{0,\ldots,m\}:\sum_{t=1}^k c_{j_t}\le B\}. If B_1\le B_2, then R(B_1)\subseteq R(B_2). If R(B_1)\ne\varnothing and scores S_j are fixed independently of B, then \max_{j\in R(B_1)}S_j\le\max_{j\in R(B_2)}S_j.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed-order additive-cost probing, increasing the budget enlarges the affordable prefix and cannot reduce its best fixed score.
assumptions_latex: c_j>0\quad\forall j
B_1\le B_2
The candidate order, complete-evaluation costs, and scores do not change with B
R(B_1)\ne\varnothing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive allocation of remaining probe resources using the current partial-evaluation state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At state \(s\), form the set \(A_B(s)\) of probe actions admissible under the remaining budget. While \(A_B(s)\ne\varnothing\) and the stopping rule is false, select an action using a declared state-dependent priority \(u(a\mid s)\), execute it subject to the charging or interruption rule, update \(s\), and recompute admissible actions. On stopping, apply the declared fallback or selection rule to the information obtained. Because \(u\) may depend on observed probe outcomes, the evaluated candidates need not form a fixed prefix.

C\ge0

assumptions_latex: A nonnegative probing budget \(B\) and candidate ordering \((j_1,\ldots,j_m)\) are supplied.

Evaluating candidate \(j
e j_1\) consumes known cost \(c_j>0\).

For \(t=2,\ldots,m\), it evaluates both children of \(j_t\) and adds \(j_t\) to \(R\) only while \(C+c_{j_t}\leq B\), updating \(C\leftarrow C+c_{j_t}\); otherwise it stops. It computes a fixed strong-branching score \(S_j\) for every evaluated \(j\in R\) and outputs any maximizer over \(R\). The probing cost satisfies \(C\leq B\), provided the initialization itself is feasible, namely \(c_{j_1}\leq B\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Budgeted strong branching initializes \(R=\{j_1\}\), evaluates both children of \(j_1\), and sets spent cost \(C=c_{j_1}\). For \(t=2,\ldots,m\), it evaluates both children of \(j_t\) and adds \(j_t\) to \(R\) only while \(C+c_{j_t}\leq B\), updating \(C\leftarrow C+c_{j_t}\); otherwise it stops. children.title: Candidate-Pool Restriction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested Top-k Pools and Best Available Score
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Top-k screening under one fixed total order and tie rule.

1\le k<m
The screening order and tie rule are fixed for all k

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_F=\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in F}S_j\) and \(M_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in R}S_j\), where \(\varnothing\ne R\subseteq F\). Equality of deterministic selections additionally requires the restricted and full tie rules to choose the same element.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserving the best score, retaining a full-set maximizer, and reproducing the same tie-broken decision are distinct guarantees.
assumptions_latex: \varnothing\ne R\subseteq F
F\text{ is finite}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tie-rule failure of deterministic decision preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{a,b,c\}\), \(R=\{b,c\}\), and \(S_a=S_b=1>S_c=0\). The pool retains the full-set maximizer \(b\) and preserves the optimal score. Nevertheless, a full-set tie rule preferring \(a\) selects \(a\), while the restricted procedure selects \(b\).

assumptions_latex: S_a=S_b=1
S_c=0

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-independent eligibility screening before expensive candidate evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite nonempty candidate set \(F\), a candidate-pool rule maps the current search and screening state \(s\) to a nonempty subset \(R=\mathcal R(F,s)\subseteq F\). The rule may be eligibility-based, threshold-based, fixed-cardinality, or an intersection of such rules. Expensive strong evaluation is permitted only for candidates in \(R\).

assumptions_latex: F\text{ is finite and nonempty}
\varnothing\ne R\subseteq F
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dom}(S^{\mathrm{evaluated}})\subseteq R\subseteq F

assumptions_latex: The complete eligible set is a finite set \(F\).
A screening statistic \(h_j\in\mathbb R\) and pool size \(1\leq k\leq |F|\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A size-\(k\) candidate-pool restriction selects a subset \(R_k\subseteq F\) containing the \(k\) largest screening values \(h_j\), with a fixed tie rule, and permits strong probing only for \(j\in R_k\). If \(S_j\) denotes the score that full strong branching would assign, the restricted decision equals a full strong-branching decision if and only if \(R_k\cap\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in F}S_j\neq\varnothing\). Screening statistics alone provide no such guarantee unless their relation to \(S_j\) is assumed; an excluded candidate may have the unique largest strong-branching score.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines top-ranked candidate screening and its exact agreement condition with full strong branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A size-\(k\) candidate-pool restriction selects a subset \(R_k\subseteq F\) containing the \(k\) largest screening values \(h_j\), with a fixed tie rule, and permits strong probing only for \(j\in R_k\). If \(S_j\) denotes the score that full strong branching would assign, the restricted decision equals a full strong-branching decision if and only if \(R_k\cap\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in F}S_j\neq\varnothing\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A top-k screening pool preserves full strong branching only when it includes a globally best strong-branching candidate; arbitrary screening can exclude that candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Pool Restriction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a candidate-pool restriction, but the equivalence is exact only under a specified interpretation of ties and of equality with a full-branching decision. No source supports the proposed top-k convention or its claimed canonical role.

children.title: Probing-Budget Exhaustion
children.top_down_role: Search states where allocated strong-branching resources are depleted.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates exhaustion of a branching heuristic's resources from validity of the permanent branch disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose probing stops because its resource budget is exhausted. If the fallback selects an eligible branching disjunction whose children cover every integer-feasible solution of the current node, and every later pruning operation uses a valid certificate, then probe-budget exhaustion does not invalidate branch-and-bound completeness. It may change the generated tree and runtime but not the coverage invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhausting the probing budget affects branching quality, not correctness, provided fallback branching is exhaustive and later pruning is certified.
assumptions_latex: X_N\cap X_I\subseteq\bigcup_{r=1}^q X_{N,r}
Every permanent child restriction is valid
Only certified pruning closes a child region
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Probe-budget exhaustion preserves search completeness under exhaustive fallback branching and certified pruning.}
knowledge_statements.title: Search Correctness After Probe-Budget Exhaustion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable sufficient certificate for bounded score loss at exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every unevaluated candidate \(j\in U\) has a valid upper bound \(S_j\le u_j\), and let \(s_R=\max_{j\in R}S_j\) for \(R\ne\varnothing\). Then \(S^*\le\max\{s_R,\max_{j\in U}u_j\}\). Hence \(\max_{j\in U}u_j\le s_R+\varepsilon\) certifies that selecting a best evaluated candidate loses at most \(\varepsilon\) in strong-branching score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid upper bounds on every unseen score certify an additive bound on the score loss caused by exhaustion.
assumptions_latex: R\ne\varnothing
S_j\le u_j\quad(j\in U)
\varepsilon\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{j\in U}u_j\le s_R+\varepsilon\Rightarrow S^*-s_R\le\varepsilon

notation.meaning: Valid upper bound on unevaluated score j.

review_flags: This certifies score approximation, not global optimization quality or runtime.
knowledge_statements.title: Unseen-Score Upper-Bound Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-exhaustion criteria for indivisible and partially executed probes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let remaining resource be \(R_B=B-C\). For atomic complete probes, exhaustion holds when every currently admissible unevaluated action \(a\) has required cost \(c(a)>R_B\). For an interruptible probe, reaching \(R_B=0\) yields either a completed estimator-admissible observation or a censored partial result under the declared interruption rule; a censored result is not a complete strong score unless the estimator explicitly supports it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Atomic exhaustion means no complete probe fits; mid-probe exhaustion requires a rule distinguishing complete information from censored partial information.
assumptions_latex: 0\le C\le B
c(a)>0\text{ for each complete atomic probe}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall a\in A,\ c(a)>B-C\bigr)\Rightarrow\text{no further complete atomic probe is affordable}
knowledge_statements.title: Atomic and Interruptible Probe Exhaustion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbounded Loss from an Unseen Score
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation failure after exhaustion when unevaluated scores are unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=\{a\}\) with \(S_a=1\), and let an unaffordable candidate \(b\) remain unevaluated. For any \(M>1\), set \(S_b=M\). Selection from \(R\) obtains \(1\), while full strong branching obtains \(M\); the additive loss \(M-1\) is unbounded and the achieved-to-optimal ratio \(1/M\) tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without upper bounds on unseen nonnegative scores, exhaustion permits unbounded additive loss and an approximation ratio tending to zero.
assumptions_latex: S_j\ge0
S_a=1
S_b=M>1
b\text{ is unaffordable and unevaluated}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S^*-S_{\mathrm{obs}}=M-1\to\infty,\qquad S_{\mathrm{obs}}/S^*=1/M\to0
review_flags: The ratio statement requires nonnegative scores and a positive full optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Loss from an Unseen Score

assumptions_latex: Candidate evaluations have positive costs \(c_j\), total budget is \(B\), and spent cost is \(C\leq B\).
Unevaluated candidates form \(U\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Probing-budget exhaustion occurs when \(C+\min_{j\in U}c_j>B\); then no further complete candidate evaluation is feasible under the budget. The algorithm must select from the evaluated set \(R\), use a non-probing fallback, or violate the budget. If \(j^*\in U\) uniquely maximizes the full strong-branching score over \(R\cup U\), every rule constrained to choose the best observed score in \(R\) is strictly suboptimal in that score. Without an upper bound on scores of unevaluated candidates, exhaustion admits no finite additive or multiplicative approximation guarantee relative to full strong branching.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the point where no additional complete strong-branching probe fits within budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Probing-budget exhaustion occurs when \(C+\min_{j\in U}c_j>B\); then no further complete candidate evaluation is feasible under the budget. If \(j^*\in U\) uniquely maximizes the full strong-branching score over \(R\cup U\), every rule constrained to choose the best observed score in \(R\) is strictly suboptimal in that score. Without an upper bound on scores of unevaluated candidates, exhaustion admits no finite additive or multiplicative approximation guarantee relative to full strong branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The probing budget is exhausted when no unevaluated candidate fits. Without bounds on unseen scores, stopping then has no approximation guarantee versus full strong branching.
knowledge_statements.title: Probing-Budget Exhaustion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exhaustion condition fits the failure_boundary container. The no-approximation claim requires an explicit score range, sign convention, comparison metric, and treatment of zero denominators; these assumptions and a supporting source are absent.

children.title: Lookahead Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching evaluation extending beyond immediate child effects.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Leaf Lookahead Monotonicity and Rank Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive level-by-level lookahead scored by the minimum terminal minimization bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q_D(j)=\min_{\ell\in L_j^D}b(\ell). If every leaf in L_j^D is replaced at depth D+1 by descendants \ell' satisfying b(\ell')\ge b(\ell), then Q_{D+1}(j)\ge Q_D(j). Nevertheless, candidate rankings need not be stable with depth: there exist candidates a,b for which Q_D(a)>Q_D(b) but Q_{D+1}(a)<Q_{D+1}(b).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With minimum-leaf scoring and monotone descendant bounds, deeper exhaustive lookahead cannot lower an individual score, although it can reverse candidate rankings.
assumptions_latex: Q_D(j)=\min_{\ell\in L_j^D}b(\ell)
\forall \ell\in L_j^D,\ \forall \ell'\in\operatorname{desc}_{D+1}(\ell),\ b(\ell')\ge b(\ell)
Every depth-D terminal leaf is expanded when forming depth D+1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_{D+1}(j)\ge Q_D(j)\quad\text{for every }j,\qquad Q_D(a)>Q_D(b)\not\Rightarrow Q_{D+1}(a)\ge Q_{D+1}(b)

notation.meaning: minimum terminal bound for candidate j at lookahead depth D
temporary terminal leaves below candidate j at depth D
valid minimization lower bound at temporary node ell

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Leaf Lookahead Monotonicity and Rank Instability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case temporary-node count for exhaustive bounded-arity lookahead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every temporary node has at most \(q\ge2\) children and all nonroot temporary nodes through depth \(D\) are generated, then one first-action evaluation creates at most \(\sum_{h=1}^{D}q^h=q(q^D-1)/(q-1)\) temporary nodes. Evaluating \(m\) first actions independently creates at most \(m q(q^D-1)/(q-1)\) such nodes; early terminal states and pruning can only reduce the count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive depth-D lookahead has geometric worst-case temporary work in the lookahead depth.
assumptions_latex: q\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}
D\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}
m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W\le m\frac{q(q^D-1)}{q-1}

notation.meaning: Number of independently evaluated first actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporary-Subtree Work Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary for equating depth-one lookahead with immediate-child strong evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Depth-one lookahead and an immediate-child strong-branching rule are decision-equivalent when they use the same candidate set, tentative child solves, child-bound treatment, aggregation, infeasibility convention, and deterministic tie rule. Equality of depth alone does not imply equal scores or selections if any convention differs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Depth-one lookahead equals immediate-child strong branching only when all evaluation and tie conventions coincide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Matching evaluation conventions}\Rightarrow\operatorname{select}_{LA}=\operatorname{select}_{SB}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive formulation of exhaustive finite-depth lookahead for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix finite action sets, temporary child generation, terminal evaluation, fathoming, and tie rules. Let \(V_0(N)=b(N)\). For \(h\ge1\), define \(V_h(N)=\max_{a\in A(N)}\min_{C\in\operatorname{child}(N,a)}V_{h-1}(C)\), with terminal or fathomed nodes handled by the declared terminal rule. Selecting an action attaining \(V_D(N)\) is the exhaustive depth-\(D\) max-min lookahead rule under those conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive minimum-bound lookahead has a max-min recursion once expansion, terminal, fathoming, and tie conventions are fixed.
assumptions_latex: D\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}
A(N)\text{ and every child set are finite}
\text{Terminal, fathoming, expansion, and tie rules are fixed}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V_D(N)=\max_{a\in A(N)}\min_{C\in\operatorname{child}(N,a)}V_{D-1}(C)

notation.meaning: Remaining-depth-h lookahead value at temporary node N.
Declared depth-zero or terminal minimization evaluation.

review_flags: This representation covers exhaustive max-min lower-bound lookahead, not every possible terminal aggregation.

assumptions_latex: The current branch-and-bound state has candidate set \(F\) and a finite lookahead depth \(D\geq1\).
A deterministic node-expansion policy and terminal evaluation \(V\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each \(j\in F\), lookahead branching constructs the temporary binary subtree obtained by branching first on \(j\), then applying the fixed expansion policy until depth \(D\), infeasibility, or fathoming. Let \(L_j\) be its terminal leaves and assign \(Q_D(j)=\Phi(\{V(\ell):\ell\in L_j\})\), where \(\Phi\) is a specified monotone aggregation of minimization bounds, such as the minimum leaf bound. The method discards every temporary subtree and branches permanently on any \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in F}Q_D(j)\). Depth \(D=1\) recovers immediate-child evaluation under the corresponding aggregation.

notation.meaning: terminal leaves below first branch candidate j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-depth deterministic lookahead extending strong branching beyond immediate children.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(j\in F\), lookahead branching constructs the temporary binary subtree obtained by branching first on \(j\), then applying the fixed expansion policy until depth \(D\), infeasibility, or fathoming. Let \(L_j\) be its terminal leaves and assign \(Q_D(j)=\Phi(\{V(\ell):\ell\in L_j\})\), where \(\Phi\) is a specified monotone aggregation of minimization bounds, such as the minimum leaf bound. The method discards every temporary subtree and branches permanently on any \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{j\in F}Q_D(j)\). Depth \(D=1\) recovers immediate-child evaluation under the corresponding aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lookahead branching builds a temporary depth-limited subtree for each candidate, aggregates its terminal evaluations, and branches on a candidate with maximum lookahead score.
knowledge_statements.title: Lookahead Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the leaf, but the subtree evaluation and aggregation are only one possible lookahead construction. The claim that depth one recovers immediate-child evaluation depends on the terminal evaluation and aggregation matching the strong-branching score, which is not explicitly assumed or sourced.

children.title: Strong-Probing Cost-Quality Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Performance boundaries created by expensive or weakly predictive probing.

children.title: Strong-Probing Cost
children.top_down_role: Node-processing burden attributable to temporary candidate evaluation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full and Partial Strong-Probing Work Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential additive accounting for tentative child-relaxation work; candidate generation, score computation, parallel wall time, and downstream tree work are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite candidate set J, let I_{j,-},I_{j,+}\in\{0,1\} indicate whether the corresponding tentative child relaxation is solved, with work T_{j,-},T_{j,+}\ge0. Then C_{\mathrm{probe}}=\sum_{j\in J}(I_{j,-}T_{j,-}+I_{j,+}T_{j,+}) and N_{\mathrm{solve}}=\sum_{j\in J}(I_{j,-}+I_{j,+})\le2|J|. Equality in the solve-count bound holds exactly when both children of every candidate are solved. If every performed solve costs at most T_{\max}, then C_{\mathrm{probe}}\le2|J|T_{\max}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential strong probing performs at most two tentative child solves per candidate; complete two-child probing attains that count, and bounded per-solve work gives a linear total-work bound.
assumptions_latex: J\text{ is finite}
I_{j,\sigma}\in\{0,1\}\quad(\sigma\in\{-,+\})
T_{j,\sigma}\ge0
I_{j,\sigma}=1\Rightarrow T_{j,\sigma}\le T_{\max}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{solve}}\le2|J|,\quad N_{\mathrm{solve}}=2|J|\iff I_{j,-}=I_{j,+}=1\ \forall j,\quad C_{\mathrm{probe}}\le2|J|T_{\max}

notation.meaning: indicator that tentative child sigma of candidate j is solved
sequential work of that tentative child solve

knowledge_statements.title: Full and Partial Strong-Probing Work Bounds

assumptions_latex: At a branch-and-bound node, the candidate set is \(J\).
Probing candidate \(j\) solves both tentative child relaxations to prescribed limits.
The work of a relaxation solve is measured by \(T_{j,-}\) and \(T_{j,+}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{probe}}(J)=\sum_{j\in J}(T_{j,-}+T_{j,+})\), so exhaustive strong probing requires \(2|J|\) tentative child-relaxation solves.

notation.meaning: work for the down and up tentative child solves of candidate \(j\)

review_flags: Exact source for the strong-branching work model is missing from the supplied locator hints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts relaxation work only; candidate generation and score computation are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J\) be the candidates considered at one branch-and-bound node. For each \(j\in J\), strong probing temporarily creates the down and up children and spends work \(T_{j,-}\) and \(T_{j,+}\) solving their relaxations to fixed stopping limits. Its probing cost is
\[C_{\mathrm{probe}}(J)=\sum_{j\in J}\bigl(T_{j,-}+T_{j,+}\bigr).\]
Consequently, exhaustive probing performs exactly \(2|J|\) tentative child-relaxation solves. If every solve costs at most \(T_{\max}\), then \(C_{\mathrm{probe}}(J)\le 2|J|T_{\max}\); if every solve costs at least \(T_{\min}\), then \(C_{\mathrm{probe}}(J)\ge 2|J|T_{\min}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive strong probing solves two tentative child relaxations per candidate, and its total work is the sum of those solve costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Probing Cost

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits Strong-Probing Cost, and the counting formula is coherent under the stated two-child probing convention. However, no cited source supports that convention, the work model, or the exact solve count, so source uncertainty prevents acceptance.

children.title: Branching-Prediction Quality
children.top_down_role: Reliability of probing outcomes as indicators of later search performance.

assumptions_latex: Each candidate \(j\in J\) has a probing score \(s_j\) and an observed downstream outcome \(y_j\).
A loss function \(\ell\) and an evaluation distribution over node-candidate pairs are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Prediction quality is measured by \(Q(s)=1-\mathbb{E}[\ell(s_J,y_J)]\), or by the explicitly specified ranking success probability when only candidate order matters.

notation.meaning: realized downstream quality of branching on \(j\)

review_flags: No supplied source fixes a canonical downstream outcome or quality metric for branching prediction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A metric-dependent definition for evaluating tentative strong-branching scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a distribution of branch-and-bound nodes and eligible candidates. For a sampled candidate \(J\), let \(s_J\) be its probing score and let \(y_J\) be a specified downstream outcome, such as processed subtree nodes or dual-bound improvement. Given a normalized loss \(\ell\), define branching-prediction quality by
\[Q(s)=1-\mathbb{E}\!\left[\ell(s_J,y_J)\right].\]
When only the selected candidate matters, a ranking version is
\[Q_{\mathrm{rank}}(s)=\mathbb{P}\!\left(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j\in J}s_j\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j\in J}y_j\right),\]
with a declared tie rule. The outcome, loss, sampling distribution, and tie rule are part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching-prediction quality compares probing scores with a declared downstream outcome under a fixed loss or candidate-ranking criterion.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Prediction Quality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the container, but the proposed loss-based and ranking-based quantities are protocol-dependent constructions rather than a sourced canonical notion of branching-prediction quality. A source must fix or justify the downstream outcome, normalization, sampling distribution, and ranking criterion.

children.title: Cost–Quality Frontier
children.top_down_role: Performance regimes balancing probing effort against ranking value.

assumptions_latex: A family \(\mathcal{P}\) of probing policies is fixed.
Every policy \(p\in\mathcal{P}\) has comparable expected cost \(C(p)\) and expected quality \(Q(p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cost-quality frontier is \(\mathcal{F}=\{p\in\mathcal{P}:\nexists q\in\mathcal{P},\ C(q)\le C(p),\ Q(q)\ge Q(p)\text{ with at least one strict inequality}\}\).

notation.meaning: expected probing cost and prediction quality of policy \(p\)

review_flags: The Pareto definition is standard, but its application to strong probing lacks a supplied supporting locator.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto frontier for policies evaluated on a common node distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be probing policies evaluated on the same distribution of branch-and-bound nodes. For \(p\in\mathcal{P}\), let \(C(p)\) be expected probing work and \(Q(p)\) expected branching-prediction quality, with smaller cost and larger quality preferred. Policy \(q\) dominates \(p\) when \(C(q)\le C(p)\), \(Q(q)\ge Q(p)\), and at least one inequality is strict. The cost-quality frontier is
\[\mathcal{F}=\left\{p\in\mathcal{P}:\nexists q\in\mathcal{P}\text{ that dominates }p\right\}.\]
Equivalently, its image consists of the nondominated points \(\{(C(p),Q(p)):p\in\mathcal{F}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The frontier contains exactly those probing policies for which no alternative is both no costlier and no less predictive, with one strict improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Cost–Quality Frontier

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role and Pareto nondominance formula fit Cost–Quality Frontier. Nevertheless, no cited locator supports applying this frontier to strong-probing policies or supplies the required common definitions of cost and prediction quality.

children.title: Weakly Predictive Probing
children.top_down_role: Regimes where expensive probes provide little useful candidate discrimination.

assumptions_latex: Candidate scores \(s_j\) are produced by a probing policy.
Realized downstream qualities \(y_j\) are evaluated on a fixed node distribution.
Ties are resolved by a fixed rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The probing is weakly predictive when \(Q_{\mathrm{rank}}\le Q_0+\varepsilon\), where \(Q_0\) is the declared noninformative baseline and \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is the tolerance.

notation.meaning: probability that probing selects a downstream-optimal candidate
quality of the declared noninformative baseline

review_flags: Weak predictiveness has no unique canonical threshold in the supplied material.
The baseline and tolerance must be fixed by an evaluation protocol.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational boundary relative to a declared noninformative candidate-selection baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[Q_{\mathrm{rank}}=\mathbb{P}\!\left(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j\in J}s_j\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j\in J}y_j\right)\]
be the probability that probing selects a candidate having maximal realized downstream quality. Fix a noninformative selection rule with success probability \(Q_0\) and a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Probing is weakly predictive on the evaluation distribution when
\[Q_{\mathrm{rank}}\le Q_0+\varepsilon.\]
Thus additional probing lies beyond the useful prediction boundary whenever its incremental cost is positive but its ranking quality remains within \(\varepsilon\) of the baseline. This condition concerns predictive usefulness, not validity of the resulting branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probing is weakly predictive when its probability of selecting a downstream-best candidate is within a declared tolerance of a noninformative baseline.
knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Predictive Probing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the terminal container, but the baseline-plus-tolerance condition is an invented operational convention unless an evaluation protocol or authoritative source specifies it. The meaning of downstream-best, the baseline, and the tolerance remain source-dependent.

children.title: Reliability-Hybrid Branching Synthesis
children.top_down_role: Adaptive combinations of strong branching and historical prediction.

children.title: Reliability-Threshold Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing transitions between probing and historical estimates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Probing Budget for a Monotone Reliability Counter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional per-counter bound on mandatory probing before threshold eligibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a reliability counter starts at \(n_j^0\ge0\), every mandatory probe increases that same counter by at least one, and the counter never decreases. If probing is mandatory exactly while \(n_j<r\), then at most \(\max\{0,r-n_j^0\}\) mandatory probes occur before \(n_j\ge r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone counter needs at most its remaining threshold deficit in mandatory probes.
assumptions_latex: r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}
n_j^0\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}
n_j^{t+1}\ge n_j^t+1\text{ after each counted mandatory probe}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_j^{\mathrm{probe}}\le\max\{0,r-n_j^0\}.

notation.meaning: number of counted mandatory probes before threshold eligibility

review_flags: The bound is conditional on the declared counter semantics and does not choose between variable-level and direction-specific reliability.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Probing Budget for a Monotone Reliability Counter

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic transition from tentative probing to historical scoring under an explicit counter convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a reliability predicate \(\rho_j(n)\), such as a directional, two-sided, or aggregate threshold, and a declared observation-update rule. For an eligible candidate \(j\), perform the required tentative probes while \(\rho_j(n)\) is false, update only counters supported by estimator-admissible outcomes, and compute its score from the resulting probe information. Once \(\rho_j(n)\) is true, the declared historical estimator may be used without mandatory probing. Candidate selection uses a fixed score and tie convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reliability branching probes a candidate until its declared reliability predicate holds, then permits historical scoring without mandatory probing.
assumptions_latex: \rho_j\text{ and the observation-update rule are fixed in advance}
\text{Probe and historical scores use compatible conventions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_j(n)=\mathrm{false}\Rightarrow\text{required probing},\qquad \rho_j(n)=\mathrm{true}\Rightarrow\text{historical scoring is eligible}

notation.meaning: Declared reliability predicate for candidate j.

review_flags: This generic statement does not select one solver-specific counter convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Declared-Threshold Reliability Switch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counter treatment of completed, infeasible, truncated, and censored tentative solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A directional counter \(n_j^d\) may be incremented only when the tentative solve supplies an observation admissible to the estimator used after transition. A certified finite child bound with positive branching displacement supplies a finite rate. A certified infeasible child may be counted only under a declared capped or categorical convention. An interrupted, truncated, or numerically failed solve must not increment an exact-rate counter, although a declared censored-data estimator may maintain a separate compatible count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reliability counter increases only for the kind of directional information used by its post-threshold estimator.
assumptions_latex: \text{Counter semantics and the historical estimator are declared in advance}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta n_j^d=1\Rightarrow\text{an estimator-admissible directional observation was obtained}
knowledge_statements.title: Estimator-Admissible Counter Updates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an aggregate reliability count to ensure bidirectional support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=3\), \(n_j^-=3\), and \(n_j^+=0\). Then \(n_j^-+n_j^+\ge r\) declares aggregate reliability, while \(\min\{n_j^-,n_j^+\}<r\), and the up direction has no observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A total count can reach its threshold even though one branching direction has never been observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: n_j^-+n_j^+\ge r\quad\text{and}\quad\min\{n_j^-,n_j^+\}<r
knowledge_statements.title: Premature Aggregate-Count Transition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative counter semantics for deciding when historical pseudocost estimates are eligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n_j^-\) and \(n_j^+\) count informative directional observations. Directional reliability declares \((j,d)\) reliable when \(n_j^d\ge r_d\). Two-sided variable reliability declares \(j\) reliable when \(\min\{n_j^-,n_j^+\}\ge r\). Aggregate reliability instead uses \(n_j^-+n_j^+\ge r\); it is weaker and need not imply support in both directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reliability can be direction-specific, require both directions, or use an aggregate count; these regimes are not equivalent.
assumptions_latex: n_j^-,n_j^+\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}
r,r_d\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{n_j^-,n_j^+\}\ge r\Rightarrow n_j^-+n_j^+\ge2r,\quad\text{but the converse fails.}

notation.meaning: Informative count for variable j and direction d.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Level and Directional Reliability Regimes

assumptions_latex: For every integer variable \(j\), \(n_j\) counts sufficiently informative historical branch observations.
A reliability threshold \(r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\) is fixed.
Tentative child solves and historical estimates use the same score convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Candidate \(j\) is probed exactly when \(n_j<r\); once \(n_j\ge r\), its score is computed from historical estimates without mandatory probing.

notation.meaning: number of informative historical observations for variable \(j\)

review_flags: A source specifying reliability branching and its observation-count convention is not among the supplied locators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold switch between tentative probing and accumulated historical estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an observation count \(n_j=0\) for every integer variable \(j\), and fix \(r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\). At a node, for each eligible candidate \(j\), if \(n_j<r\), solve its tentative children, compute \(S_j\) from their bound changes, and update the relevant historical estimates and \(n_j\). If \(n_j\ge r\), compute \(S_j\) from those historical estimates without mandatory tentative solves. Select a candidate maximizing \(S_j\) under a fixed tie rule. Hence \(r=0\) gives the historical-estimate regime immediately, finite \(r>0\) gives a probing-to-history transition, and unattained \(r\) retains probing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate is probed until its historical observation count reaches the reliability threshold; afterward its score may use historical estimates alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Reliability-Threshold Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithm is an appropriate role for the threshold-switching procedure, and the regimes are internally coherent. Acceptance requires a reliability-branching source specifying what counts as an observation, whether reliability is variable- or direction-specific, and when tentative solves cease to be mandatory.

children.title: Hybrid Branching Scores
children.top_down_role: Composite rankings combining multiple candidate-quality indicators.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pareto Monotonicity of Nonnegative Additive Scores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance property of the additive hybrid-score variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_j=\sum_{k=1}^m w_kq_{jk}\) with \(w_k\ge0\). If \(q_{ak}\ge q_{bk}\) for every \(k\), then \(H_a\ge H_b\). If \(q_{ak}>q_{bk}\) for some \(k\) with \(w_k>0\), then \(H_a>H_b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative additive score preserves indicator-wise dominance.
assumptions_latex: w_k\ge0\quad(k=1,\ldots,m)
q_{ak}\ge q_{bk}\quad(k=1,\ldots,m)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_a\ge H_b,\text{ strictly when a positively weighted component is strictly larger}.
review_flags: Applies only to the additive variant and does not establish that this variant is canonical for hybrid branching.
knowledge_statements.title: Pareto Monotonicity of Nonnegative Additive Scores

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of additive hybrid rankings to be invariant under component rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H_j=q_{j1}+q_{j2}\), let \(q_a=(2,0)\) and \(q_b=(0,1)\). Initially \(H_a=2>1=H_b\). After replacing the second indicator by \(q'_{j2}=3q_{j2}\) without compensating its weight, \(H'_a=2<3=H'_b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncompensated positive rescaling of one indicator can reverse an additive hybrid ranking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_a>H_b\quad\text{and}\quad H'_a<H'_b
knowledge_statements.title: Ranking Reversal Under Uncalibrated Rescaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct score-level mechanisms for combining multiple branching-quality indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given consistently oriented indicators \(q_j=(q_{j1},\ldots,q_{jm})\), a hybrid ranking may use an additive score \(H_j=\sum_kw_kq_{jk}\); a multiplicative score \(H_j=\prod_kg_k(q_{jk})^{w_k}\) on positive factors; lexicographic comparison under a declared component priority; or a gated rule that first retains candidates satisfying a predicate \(G_j\) and then ranks the survivors. Each construction requires declared domains and tie handling, and the four forms are not generally rank-equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid branching rankings can combine indicators additively, multiplicatively, lexicographically, or through gating; these forms generally rank candidates differently.
assumptions_latex: J\text{ is finite}
\text{Every component has a declared orientation and domain}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A hybrid ranking is determined only after its combination and tie rules are declared.}

notation.meaning: Eligibility predicate in a gated rule.

review_flags: This is a mathematical taxonomy, not a claim that every form is implemented by a particular solver.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Branching Score Taxonomy

assumptions_latex: Each candidate \(j\in J\) has normalized indicators \(q_{jk}\) with a common larger-is-better orientation.
Weights satisfy \(w_k\ge0\) and \(\sum_{k=1}^m w_k=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hybrid score \(H_j=\sum_{k=1}^m w_kq_{jk}\) induces the ranking, with a fixed rule for ties.

notation.meaning: normalized value of indicator \(k\) for candidate \(j\)

review_flags: The supplied sources do not identify a canonical hybrid score or normalization.
This record states a generic convex-combination representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic weighted composite after indicator orientation and normalization are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each candidate \(j\in J\), let \(q_{j1},\ldots,q_{jm}\) be normalized quality indicators, all oriented so that larger values are preferred. Choose weights \(w_k\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{k=1}^m w_k=1\). The additive hybrid branching score is
\[H_j=\sum_{k=1}^m w_kq_{jk},\]
and the selected candidate belongs to \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j\in J}H_j\), with a declared tie rule. Indicators may encode tentative bound gains, historical estimates, inference, or balance, but their normalization is part of the representation; otherwise rescaling one indicator can change the ranking without changing its underlying information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid score ranks candidates by a weighted sum of consistently oriented, normalized quality indicators, using declared nonnegative weights and a fixed tie rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Branching Scores

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits Hybrid Branching Scores, but a normalized convex combination is only one possible composite scoring rule. No source establishes this additive form, its normalization, or the listed indicator families as the intended local mathematical content.

children.title: Branching-Quality Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Tree-growth failures caused by ineffective partition choices.

children.title: Ineffective Partition Failure Family
children.top_down_role: Partitions that divide the search region ineffectively.

children.title: Unbalanced Partitions
children.top_down_role: Branching partitions with sharply unequal child-region difficulty or size.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Valid Partitions Can Be Arbitrarily Unbalanced
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counting-measure family showing that partition validity gives no uniform balance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\ge1\), let \(F_M=\{0,1,\ldots,M\}\), \(F_M^-=\{0,1,ldots,M-1\}\), and \(F_M^+=\{M\}\). The children are nonempty, disjoint, and exhaustive, but \(|F_M^-|/|F_M|=M/(M+1)\to1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid binary partition can leave all but one parent point in a single child.
assumptions_latex: M\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}
F_M=\{0,1,\ldots,M\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_M^-\mathbin{\dot\cup}F_M^+=F_M,\qquad \frac{|F_M^-|}{|F_M|}=\frac{M}{M+1}\longrightarrow1.
knowledge_statements.title: Valid Partitions Can Be Arbitrarily Unbalanced

assumptions_latex: A node region \(P\) is partitioned into child regions \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\).
A nonnegative size measure \(\mu\) satisfies \(0<\mu(P)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition is \(\varepsilon\)-unbalanced when \(\max_i\mu(P_i)/\mu(P)\ge1-\varepsilon\), and repeated occurrence permits a surviving branch to shrink by at most the factor \(1-\varepsilon\) per level.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports this quantitative imbalance convention.
The appropriate size measure is problem dependent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies imbalance using a declared measure of remaining search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be a node region and let \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\) be its children. Fix a nonnegative size measure \(\mu\) with \(0<\mu(P)<\infty\) and a tolerance \(\varepsilon\in[0,1)\). The partition is \(\varepsilon\)-unbalanced when
\[\max_{1\le i\le k}\frac{\mu(P_i)}{\mu(P)}\ge1-\varepsilon.\]
If at every level a surviving child satisfies this inequality, then after depth \(d\) its size may remain at least \((1-\varepsilon)^d\mu(P)\). Thus no depth bound based on a uniformly stronger contraction can follow without an assumption excluding such unbalanced partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition is unbalanced when one child retains at least a declared fraction of the parent region, allowing slow contraction along a surviving branch.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbalanced Partitions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits Unbalanced Partitions, but the proposed measure-based epsilon threshold is not canonical and the choice of measure can materially change the condition. The contraction interpretation therefore needs a source fixing the measure and imbalance convention.

children.title: Redundant Partitions
children.top_down_role: Branching alternatives that preserve unnecessary overlap or equivalent search work.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proper Nonempty Children Can Be Union-Redundant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of nonemptiness and proper restriction as redundancy tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{0,1,2\}\), \(F_1=\{0\}\), \(F_2=\{0,1\}\), and \(F_3=\{2\}\). Every child is nonempty and a proper subset of \(F\), but \(F_1\cup F_2\cup F_3=F_2\cup F_3=F\). Thus \(F_1\) is union-redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty proper child can add no feasible point beyond the other children.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_1\cup F_2\cup F_3=F_2\cup F_3.
knowledge_statements.title: Proper Nonempty Children Can Be Union-Redundant

assumptions_latex: The parent feasible set is \(F=P\cap X\), where \(X\) encodes the original constraints.
Child regions are \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A child \(P_i\) is redundant when \(P_i\cap X=F\), and a partition is redundant when removing some child leaves the union of child feasible sets unchanged.

notation.meaning: set satisfying the original model constraints

review_flags: The supplied locator hints do not address redundant branching partitions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic redundancy relative to the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the feasible set at a node be \(F=P\cap X\), and let branching create child regions \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\). A child \(P_i\) is parent-redundant when
\[P_i\cap X=F,\]
so entering that child imposes no effective restriction. More generally, child \(P_i\) is union-redundant when
\[\bigcup_{h=1}^k(P_h\cap X)=\bigcup_{h\ne i}(P_h\cap X).\]
A branching partition is redundant if it contains either form. Parent redundancy can reproduce the entire unresolved parent problem in a descendant; union redundancy creates a child whose feasible points are already covered by other children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching child is redundant if it preserves the entire parent feasible set or contributes no feasible points beyond those covered by other children.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Partitions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is a plausible role for Redundant Partitions, and the two set-theoretic notions are internally distinct. No cited source supports treating either parent redundancy or union redundancy as the intended branching-partition definition, so the proposed taxonomy of redundancy remains unverified.

children.title: One-Sided Tree Growth
children.top_down_role: Tree shapes dominated by repeatedly difficult child regions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Frontier Width Does Not Bound Surviving-Path Depth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided growth with a single unresolved descendant at every level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a rooted branching tree contain a path \(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_D\), where at each \(v_d\) every child except \(v_{d+1}\) is immediately closed and \(v_{d+1}\) remains open. Then the active frontier can have cardinality one throughout these expansions while the surviving-path depth is \(D\). The same construction permits an infinite path. Thus a uniform frontier-width bound, or immediate closure of one side at each branch, gives no finite depth bound without a separate uniform-progress condition on the surviving child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search can retain only one open node at a time yet follow that surviving child to arbitrary or infinite depth; bounded frontier width alone does not bound depth.
assumptions_latex: The tree contains a path \(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_D\), or an infinite path.
At each path node, all children except the next path node are closed before further expansion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_t|\mathcal{F}_t|\le1\ \not\Rightarrow\ \operatorname{depth}(T)<\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Frontier Width Does Not Bound Surviving-Path Depth

assumptions_latex: A rooted branching tree has a distinguished infinite or length-\(D\) path \(v_0,v_1,\ldots\).
At each \(v_d\), all siblings of \(v_{d+1}\) are immediately pruned or finitely resolved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unresolved tree width can remain one while its depth reaches \(D\) or is infinite; therefore bounded width alone gives no finite search bound.
review_flags: No supplied source explicitly states this tree-growth failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural failure where only one unresolved descendant persists at each depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a rooted branching tree containing a path \(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_D\), or an infinite path \(v_0,v_1,\ldots\). Suppose that at every \(v_d\), each child other than \(v_{d+1}\) is immediately pruned or completely resolved, while \(v_{d+1}\) remains unresolved. Then the number of simultaneously unresolved nodes may be at most one, but the tree depth is \(D\) or infinite. This is one-sided tree growth. It shows that controlling frontier width or rapidly disposing of one child at every branch does not imply a finite depth bound without uniform progress along the surviving child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided growth occurs when every branch quickly disposes of all but one child, yet the surviving descendant continues to arbitrary depth.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Tree Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role matches One-Sided Tree Growth, and the tree construction correctly distinguishes width from depth. An inspectable source is still required for this named failure phenomenon and its relevance to branching search bounds.

children.title: Partition-Overlap Failures
children.top_down_role: Duplicated exploration caused by insufficiently distinct child regions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Overlap Without Redundancy or Identical Children
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite example isolating overlap from equality and union redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{0,1,2\}\), \(P_1\cap F=\{0,1\}\), and \(P_2\cap F=\{1,2\}\). Then the distinct children cover \(F\), neither is contained in the other, and \(P_1\cap P_2\cap F=\{1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two distinct, nonredundant children can cover the parent while sharing a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (P_1\cap P_2\cap F)=\{1\}\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Overlap Without Redundancy or Identical Children

assumptions_latex: Child regions \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\) are intended to partition the parent feasible set \(F\).
Distinct-child overlap is measured relative to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A partition-overlap failure occurs when \((P_i\cap P_j\cap F)\ne\varnothing\) for some \(i\ne j\); duplicated feasible points may then generate repeated subproblems.
review_flags: The supplied sources do not support this explicit overlap formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of pairwise disjointness on the parent feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be the feasible set at a parent node and let \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\) be child regions satisfying \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\). A partition-overlap failure occurs when
\[(P_i\cap P_j\cap F)\ne\varnothing\quad\text{for some }i\ne j.\]
For \(x\in F\), define its multiplicity by \(m(x)=|\{i:x\in P_i\}|\). Any point with \(m(x)>1\) is assigned to multiple children. Unless duplicate states are detected or later restrictions separate them, such overlap permits the same feasible decisions and equivalent descendant subproblems to be explored more than once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlap failure occurs when a feasible parent point belongs to multiple children, permitting duplicated descendant subproblems unless duplicates are detected.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Overlap Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits Partition-Overlap Failures, and the multiplicity notation is well defined. However, no source supports this exact overlap criterion or the asserted connection from shared feasible points to repeated equivalent descendant subproblems.

children.title: Symmetry-Induced Tree Duplication
children.top_down_role: Equivalent subtrees generated by symmetric decisions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact node overhead under fully equivariant independent processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(q\ge2\) child subproblems form one symmetry orbit, each independently generates an isomorphic \(N\)-node subtree, and no cross-orbit reuse or pruning occurs. Processing every orbit member generates \(qN\) nodes, whereas retaining one representative generates \(N\); the excess is \((q-1)N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exploring q independently processed symmetric copies of an N-node subtree multiplies the work by q.
assumptions_latex: q\ge2
N\ge1
The child roots form one symmetry orbit.
Processing is equivariant and has no cross-orbit reuse or pruning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{all}}=qN,\qquad N_{\mathrm{representative}}=N,\qquad N_{\mathrm{excess}}=(q-1)N.
knowledge_statements.title: Orbit Multiplicity of Duplicated Subtrees

assumptions_latex: A group \(G\) acts on feasible solutions and preserves feasibility and objective value.
The branching rule does not impose a canonical representative for each \(G\)-orbit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If two child subproblems satisfy \(P_2=gP_1\) for some \(g\in G\), their search subtrees are isomorphic and exploring both duplicates equivalent work.

notation.meaning: a symmetry mapping one child to another

review_flags: A symmetry-specific branch-and-bound source is absent from the supplied locator hints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree duplication under objective- and feasibility-preserving group actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a group \(G\) act on the decision space so that, for every \(g\in G\), feasibility and objective value are invariant under \(x\mapsto gx\). Suppose two children satisfy
\[P_2=gP_1\quad\text{for some }g\in G.\]
If node processing and subsequent branching are equivariant under this action, the subtree rooted at \(P_2\) is isomorphic to the subtree rooted at \(P_1\), with equal node bounds and corresponding incumbents. Exploring both children therefore duplicates symmetry-equivalent work. This failure persists until symmetry breaking, orbit pruning, or a canonical-representative rule removes all but one equivalent branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric children generate isomorphic search subtrees with equal bounds and corresponding solutions, so exploring every orbit member duplicates work.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Induced Tree Duplication

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits Symmetry-Induced Tree Duplication. The subtree-isomorphism conclusion appropriately adds equivariance of node processing and later branching, but that nontrivial conclusion and the stated remedies require a symmetry-aware branch-and-bound source.

children.title: Branching–Relaxation Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Partitions poorly represented by the node relaxation.

assumptions_latex: At a minimization node, candidate \(j\) has true child value improvements \(\Delta_{j,-},\Delta_{j,+}\ge0\).
The node relaxation predicts improvements \(\widehat{\Delta}_{j,-},\widehat{\Delta}_{j,+}\ge0\).
A monotone aggregation function \(\phi\) defines branching quality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mismatch is quantified by \(M_j=|\phi(\widehat{\Delta}_{j,-},\widehat{\Delta}_{j,+})-\phi(\Delta_{j,-},\Delta_{j,+})|\); unbounded \(M_j\) prevents relaxation-score guarantees for true branching quality.
review_flags: The path does not determine a canonical true-quality target or aggregation function.
No supplied locator establishes a quantitative mismatch bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrepancy between relaxation-implied gains and gains in the original subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For branching candidate \(j\), let \(\widehat{\Delta}_{j,-}\) and \(\widehat{\Delta}_{j,+}\) be child improvements predicted from the node relaxation, and let \(\Delta_{j,-}\) and \(\Delta_{j,+}\) be the corresponding improvements for the original child subproblems under a fixed evaluation convention. For a coordinatewise nondecreasing aggregator \(\phi\), define
\[M_j=\left|\phi(\widehat{\Delta}_{j,-},\widehat{\Delta}_{j,+})-\phi(\Delta_{j,-},\Delta_{j,+})\right|.\]
Branching-relaxation mismatch is uncontrolled on a family when \(\sup_jM_j=\infty\), or when relaxation-score order reverses true-score order. Without a uniform error or order-preservation assumption, selecting the largest relaxation score need not select a truly improving partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mismatch occurs when relaxation-predicted child gains substantially misstate or reverse the ranking of gains in the original child subproblems.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching–Relaxation Mismatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits Branching–Relaxation Mismatch, but the true child improvements, evaluation convention, aggregator, and mismatch threshold are not canonical. No source supports the proposed discrepancy measure or the guarantee-failure conclusion for this exact setting.

children.title: Tailing-Off Under Repeated Branching
children.top_down_role: Extended search phases with little bound improvement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Bounds Do Not Preclude Tailing-Off
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound sequence with arbitrarily long negligible-improvement runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a continuing root-to-descendant path have lower bounds \(L_d=1-(d+1)^{-1}\) at depths \(d\ge0\). Then \(L_d\uparrow1\), but \(L_{d+1}-L_d=((d+1)(d+2))^{-1}\to0\). Hence, for every \(\varepsilon>0\) and integer \(r\ge1\), some block of \(r\) consecutive branchings improves the bound by at most \(\varepsilon\) per step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly increasing convergent bounds can still have arbitrarily long stretches of negligible per-branch progress.
assumptions_latex: L_d=1-\frac{1}{d+1}\quad(d\ge0)
The path continues to arbitrary depth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_d\uparrow1,\qquad L_{d+1}-L_d=\frac{1}{(d+1)(d+2)}\longrightarrow0.

notation.meaning: node lower bound at depth d

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Bounds Do Not Preclude Tailing-Off
Tailing-Off Under Repeated Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure criterion for negligible dual-bound progress along an extended branch-and-bound path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization branch-and-bound with node lower bounds \(L(v)\) and a path \(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_k\), where each \(v_{i+1}\) is a child of \(v_i\). For tolerances \(\varepsilon\ge 0\) and integer \(r\ge 1\), tailing-off occurs at \(v_j\) when \[0\le L(v_{i+1})-L(v_i)\le\varepsilon\quad\text{for every }i=j,\ldots,j+r-1.\] In particular, if branching leaves the relaxation value invariant along arbitrarily long paths, then \(\varepsilon=0\) tailing-off can persist despite continued growth of the search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tailing-off means that many consecutive branchings improve the node lower bound by at most a prescribed tolerance, possibly by zero while the tree keeps growing.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem and every node relaxation supplies a valid lower bound.
Child relaxations strengthen or preserve their parent relaxation, so \(L(v_{i+1})\ge L(v_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated branching may generate \(r\) or more nodes while increasing the path lower bound by at most \(r\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: relaxation lower bound at node v

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed epsilon-and-run-length criterion is mathematically coherent and fits a failure-boundary container, but the cited general branch-and-bound outline does not specifically support this definition of tailing-off or the arbitrarily-long-path claim. A source addressing branch-and-bound tailing-off or negligible bound improvement is required.

children.title: Search-Frontier Traversal Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies for selecting active subproblems and balancing primal progress, dual progress, and memory.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: A Computational Study of Search Strategies for Mixed Integer Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: A Computational Study of Search Strategies for Mixed Integer Programming

children.title: Depth-First Backtracking Calculus
children.top_down_role: Path-oriented traversal with deferred sibling exploration.

children.title: Pure Depth-First Traversal
children.top_down_role: Stack-oriented continuation through the current branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Pure Depth-First Traversal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LIFO node selection for a finite branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a root node \(r\), a valid fathoming test, and an ordered child generator. Initialize a stack \(S=[r]\). While \(S\neq\varnothing\), remove its top node \(v\) and solve or update the node relaxation. Fathom \(v\) if its region is infeasible or its bound is dominated by the incumbent; if the relaxation supplies a feasible integral solution, update the incumbent when appropriate and then fathom \(v\). Otherwise generate ordered children \(c_1,\ldots,c_q\) and push them in reverse order \(c_q,\ldots,c_1\), so \(c_1\) is processed next. When \(S=\varnothing\), return the incumbent, or report infeasibility if no feasible incumbent was found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure depth-first traversal stores open nodes on a LIFO stack, processes the first ordered child next, updates the incumbent at feasible integral nodes, and backtracks when the current continuation is exhausted or fathomed.
assumptions_latex: The reachable branch-and-bound tree is finite, and every branching operation produces finitely many children whose regions cover the unfathomed node region.
Node bounds, incumbent updates, and fathoming tests are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every nonterminal iteration, the next processed open node is the most recently pushed live node; exhaustion of the finite stack yields a valid incumbent or a valid infeasibility report.

children.title: Depth-Oriented Traversal Variants
children.top_down_role: Depth-oriented traversal shaped by preferred children and fallback choices.

children.title: Preferred-Child Diving
children.top_down_role: Depth-oriented traversal following preferred child choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Preferred-Child Diving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth-oriented traversal using a local child preference score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an unfathomed nonterminal node \(v\), generate its finite nonempty child set \(C(v)\) and evaluate a deterministic preference score \(s(c\mid v)\) for every \(c\in C(v)\). Select \[c^*\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{c\in C(v)}s(c\mid v),\] resolving ties by a fixed rule, and process \(c^*\) immediately. Place every other child on a LIFO open-node stack \(S\) in reverse fallback order. Repeat from successive preferred children until the current node is fathomed, is terminal, or a specified reversal trigger fires; then invoke fallback backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preferred-child diving repeatedly processes the locally most favored child, stacking alternatives for later backtracking until fathoming, termination, or a reversal trigger ends the dive.
assumptions_latex: Every unfathomed nonterminal node to which the selection rule is applied has a finite nonempty child set.
The preference score and deterministic tie-breaking rule are defined for every generated child.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Before reversal or termination, the traversal follows a single path formed by successive score-minimizing children.

notation.meaning: local preference score for child c
LIFO stack of unprocessed alternative children

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness condition for local preferred-child ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each branching node \(v\), suppose one child is processed immediately and every other unresolved child remains on the live frontier. Replacing one deterministic preference score or tie rule by another then changes traversal order but not the union of represented child regions. Preference alone cannot remove a feasible solution; exactness additionally requires exhaustive branching, valid fathoming, and eventual processing of retained alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing a preferred child changes traversal order but not search coverage when all other unresolved children remain live. Exactness still requires exhaustive branching, sound pruning, and eventual processing.
assumptions_latex: The child regions cover the unresolved parent region.
Every nonselected unresolved child is retained.
Each retained alternative is eventually processed unless validly fathomed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_v^{\rm unresolved}\subseteq X_{c^*}\cup\bigcup_{c\in C(v)\setminus\{c^*\}}X_c\quad\text{independently of the preference score}.
knowledge_statements.title: Preference Changes Order, Not Coverage

children.title: Fallback Backtracking
children.top_down_role: Traversal behavior after a dive can no longer continue.

knowledge_statements.title: Fallback Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Return rule after a depth-oriented continuation terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a LIFO stack \(S\) containing generated but unprocessed alternatives. When the current node \(v\) is fathomed or its dive is reversed, repeatedly discard from the top of \(S\) every node already fathomed by updated global information. If a live node \(u\) remains, pop \(u\) and resume processing there; otherwise terminate the search. Thus backtracking returns to the deepest stored ancestor alternative that remains eligible, rather than regenerating the path from the root.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a dive ends, fallback backtracking discards newly fathomed stack entries and resumes at the deepest stored live alternative, terminating if none remains.
assumptions_latex: Unprocessed alternatives are pushed in an order consistent with the intended depth-first traversal.
Global incumbent or bound updates may safely fathom stored nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resumed node is the topmost live element of \(S\), if such an element exists.

notation.meaning: node at which the current dive ends

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed invariant deferred as duplicative of the accepted fallback algorithm and general closure-certificate theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: During fallback backtracking, a stored entry may be discarded only if a valid certificate closes its represented region; after closed top entries are removed, the deepest remaining live entry is processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fallback backtracking discards only certified-closed entries and resumes at the deepest remaining live alternative.
assumptions_latex: Every deferred unresolved alternative is represented on the stack.
Every discarded entry has a valid closure certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The residual stack and selected live node continue to represent all unresolved stored alternatives.}

Preferred-child selection, reversal conditions, and compact path-frame storage are excluded sibling scopes.

children.title: Dive-Reversal Triggers
children.top_down_role: Events governing movement from diving to fallback traversal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for policy-based termination of a dive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reversal trigger is traversal-safe only if every unresolved region represented immediately before reversal remains represented afterward by the current continuation, a stored alternative, or another live frontier entry. A trigger based solely on depth, elapsed effort, gap, or another search statistic may alter node order, but it may discard a region only when an independent valid fathoming certificate applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy trigger may end a dive without harming exactness only if every unresolved alternative remains live. Depth, effort, and gap thresholds do not themselves justify pruning.
assumptions_latex: Exact search requires continued representation of every unresolved feasible region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal U_{\rm before}\subseteq\bigcup_{w\in F_{\rm after}}X_w\quad\text{unless omitted regions possess valid closure certificates}.

notation.meaning: unresolved region represented immediately before reversal
region represented by live entry w

knowledge_statements.title: Traversal-Safe Reversal Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition from preferred-child descent to declared fallback selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dive-reversal event occurs when the search stops selecting successive preferred children of the current dive and transfers control to its declared fallback node-selection rule. Reversal changes which live node is selected next; it does not by itself fathom the current node or any deferred alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dive reversal ends successive preferred-child descent and hands control to fallback selection. It changes traversal order but is not itself pruning.
assumptions_latex: A preferred-child diving mode and fallback node-selection rule have been declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{reversal}\Longrightarrow\text{leave diving mode and invoke fallback selection}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dive-Reversal Event
Dive-Reversal Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate determining when preferred-child descent must stop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a current dive state \(z=(v,d,L(v),U,\rho)\), define a reversal predicate \[R(z)=R_{\rm fathom}(v)\lor[d\ge d_{\max}]\lor[U-L(v)\le\tau]\lor R_{\rm policy}(\rho).\] Here \(R_{\rm fathom}\) records infeasibility, integrality, or incumbent domination; \(d_{\max}\) is an optional depth limit; \(\tau\ge0\) is a gap tolerance; and \(R_{\rm policy}\) is any declared deterministic trigger based on search state \(\rho\). Continue diving exactly while \(R(z)\) is false, and invoke fallback backtracking when it becomes true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dive reverses when its node is fathomed, a depth or gap threshold is met, or another declared deterministic policy trigger fires.
assumptions_latex: The search is a minimization problem with valid node lower bound \(L(v)\) and incumbent value \(U\).
Every optional trigger used by the implementation is declared before it controls traversal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fallback backtracking is invoked if and only if \(R(z)=\mathrm{true}\).
