children.title: Depth-First Resource-Reuse Regime
children.top_down_role: Resource behavior associated with path-oriented traversal.

children.title: Path-Stack Memory
children.top_down_role: Storage associated with the active root-to-node path.

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Stack Memory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact traversal-state representation for depth-first backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At depth \(d\), represent the active traversal state by \[S=((v_0,j_0),\ldots,(v_{d-1},j_{d-1}),v_d),\] where \(v_0,[0m[0m\ldots,v_d\) is the current root-to-node path and \(j_i\) identifies the next unexplored child of \(v_i\). Require that the remaining children of \(v_i\) can be generated or reconstructed from \((v_i,j_i)\), and restore ancestor modifications from bounded frame data or reversible updates when a frame is popped. Excluding node payloads, relaxation workspaces, and globally retained information, the path-stack traversal metadata then occupies \(O(d)\) frames.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Depth-first traversal can represent its active path and each ancestor's next unexplored child using metadata linear in the current depth, provided remaining children are reproducible from their stack frames.
assumptions_latex: Each stack frame contains bounded-size traversal metadata.
Remaining children can be generated or reconstructed from the stored node and child index.
Ancestor traversal modifications can be restored from frame data or reversible updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The path-stack traversal metadata occupies \(O(d)\) memory at depth \(d\), excluding node payloads, solver workspaces, and global data.

notation.meaning: node at depth i on the active path
next unexplored child index at v_i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary of the linear-in-depth path-stack estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the frame attributable to depth \(i\) occupies \(m_i\) memory units, then the live path stack at depth \(d\) occupies \(\Theta\!\left(\sum_{i=0}^{d}m_i\right)\). Consequently it occupies \(O(d)\) memory when \(\sup_i m_i=O(1)\), whereas depth alone gives no linear-memory guarantee if frames retain growing node payloads, solver workspaces, or nonconstant undo logs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path-stack memory is the sum of its live frame sizes. It is linear in depth only for uniformly bounded frames; retained payloads, workspaces, or growing undo logs can make it superlinear.
assumptions_latex: Each \(m_i\) includes all nonglobal storage retained solely because frame \(i\) remains live.
Shared storage is counted once rather than once per referencing frame.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M(d)=\Theta\!\left(\sum_{i=0}^{d}m_i\right),\qquad \sup_i m_i=O(1)\Longrightarrow M(d)=O(d).

notation.meaning: memory attributable to the live frame at depth i
total live path-stack memory at depth d

children.title: Relaxation-State Reoptimization
children.top_down_role: Reoptimization behavior across nearby nodes on a depth-first path.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-State Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Re-solving a child relaxation from compatible parent relaxation state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let node \(v\) have relaxation \(R_v\), certified solver result \((\sigma_v,L(v),x_v)\), and reusable solver state \(B_v\), where \(x_v\) is present only when the solver returns a relaxation solution. For a child \(c\) obtained by adding known branching restrictions, construct \(R_c\) by applying those restrictions to \(R_v\). Initialize the solver with the compatible portion of \(B_v\); if that state is rejected or invalid, use a valid default initialization. Reoptimize \(R_c\) to obtain a certified status \(\sigma_c\), a valid bound \(L(c)\), an optional solution \(x_c\), and a new reusable state \(B_c\). Retain \(B_c\) only as required by the traversal or warm-start policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A child relaxation is formed by adding its branching restrictions and is reoptimized from compatible parent solver state, with a valid default initialization when reuse fails; the solver returns a certified status and bound and, when available, a relaxation solution.
assumptions_latex: The child relaxation differs from its parent by explicitly known branching restrictions.
The solver can validate or safely reject an inherited state.
From either an accepted inherited state or the default initialization, the solver terminates with the required certified status and valid bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reoptimization returns a certified child-relaxation status and valid bound, and returns \(x_c\) when the certified status supplies a relaxation solution.

notation.meaning: reusable solver state at node v
certified relaxation bound at node v
certified solver status at node v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed nested-relaxation bound property; deferred because its canonical home is inherited domains or joint subdivision interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_c\subseteq R_v\) be child and parent minimization relaxations with the same objective \(f\). For exact extended-real values \(L(v)=\inf_{x\in R_v}f(x)\) and \(L(c)=\inf_{x\in R_c}f(x)\), one has \(L(c)\ge L(v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a minimization relaxation cannot decrease its exact optimal value.

The parent and child use the same minimization objective.
L(v) and L(c) are exact extended-real relaxation values.

exact parent and child relaxation values

children.title: Warm-Start State Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of solver state between successive path-oriented node solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start State Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility-controlled reuse of solver state between adjacent nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each solved node \(v\) with a warm-start object \(W_v\), such as a basis, primal-dual iterate, or incumbent relaxation point. Before solving a related node \(u\), apply a compatibility map \(P_{v\to u}\) to produce a candidate state \(\widehat W_u=P_{v\to u}(W_v)\). Validate \(\widehat W_u\) against the variables, constraints, and solver requirements of \(u\); use it if valid and otherwise use the default initialization. Warm starting may change computational effort but must not change the relaxation being solved or its certified optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reusable parent or sibling solver state is mapped into a node, validated, and used only when compatible; it may affect effort but not the relaxation optimum.
assumptions_latex: The target relaxation is fixed independently of initialization.
The solver either validates candidate states or safely rejects incompatible ones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid warm start preserves the mathematical relaxation optimum while potentially reducing reoptimization work.

notation.meaning: solver state retained from node v
candidate warm-start state for node u

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates initialization data from certified target-node results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A transferred state \(\widehat W_u\), even if feasible or optimal for a related node \(v\), is only initialization data for node \(u\). Unless it independently passes the target solver's required feasibility, optimality, or infeasibility checks, it supplies neither a valid target-node bound nor a fathoming certificate. Rejection must cause repair or default initialization, not closure of \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start from another node is not itself a bound or fathoming certificate. The target node must pass its ordinary certification tests, and incompatible state must be repaired or discarded.
assumptions_latex: The source and target nodes may have different restrictions or model versions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat W_u\text{ alone certifies neither feasibility, optimality, infeasibility, nor a valid bound for }u.

notation.meaning: transferred candidate state for target node u

knowledge_statements.title: Warm Starts Are Not Certificates

children.title: Unproductive-Subtree Entrapment
children.top_down_role: Delayed global progress within weak subtrees.

knowledge_statements.title: Unproductive-Subtree Entrapment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth-first delay caused by exhaustive work inside a weak subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a depth-first traversal enter a child subtree \(T_a\) while another open node \(b\notin T_a\) remains on the stack. If every processed node of \(T_a\) avoids fathoming and produces a continuation until \(M\) nodes of \(T_a\) have been processed, then \(b\) cannot be selected during those \(M\) iterations. Hence any incumbent or stronger global lower bound obtainable only from \(b\) is delayed by at least \(M\) node evaluations. Families with unbounded \(M\) exhibit unbounded depth-first entrapment delay.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Depth-first search can process an arbitrarily large weak subtree before revisiting an open alternative that would improve the incumbent or global bound.
assumptions_latex: Traversal uses strict LIFO depth-first selection without periodic global-node overrides.
The active subtree is not fathomed before the stated number of node evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selection delay of an external open node \(b\) is at least \(M\) node evaluations and can be unbounded across instances.

notation.meaning: open node outside the active subtree
number of active-subtree nodes processed before escape

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tree family exhibiting exponentially delayed access to a useful sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(D\ge0\), construct a root with ordered children \(a,b\). Let the subtree rooted at \(a\) be a full binary tree of depth \(D\) whose \(2^{D+1}-1\) nodes are not fathomed before processing, and let \(b\) immediately yield an improving incumbent. Strict depth-first traversal selecting \(a\) first processes every node of its subtree before selecting \(b\). Measured from the time \(b\) becomes a deferred open node, its selection is therefore delayed by exactly \(2^{D+1}-1\) node evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A useful depth-one sibling can be delayed behind an unpruned full binary subtree of depth D, causing exactly 2^(D+1)-1 intervening node evaluations.
assumptions_latex: Traversal is strict depth first and orders \(a\) before \(b\).
No node in the \(a\)-subtree is fathomed before processing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{delay}(b)=2^{D+1}-1=\Theta(2^D).

notation.meaning: depth of the unproductive full binary subtree
deferred root child yielding an improving incumbent

children.title: Best-Bound Node Selection

children.title: Pure Best-Bound Traversal
children.top_down_role: Frontier ordering dominated by node bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Pure Best-Bound Traversal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global node selection by the strongest minimization lower-bound priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, maintain the set \(F\) of open nodes and a valid relaxation lower bound \(L(v)\) for every \(v\in F\). Initialize \(F\) with the root. At each iteration choose \[v^*\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{v\in F}L(v),\] using a fixed tie-breaking rule, remove \(v^*\), and process, fathom, or branch it. Insert every unfathomed child with its valid bound. Stop when \(F=\varnothing\), or when the incumbent satisfies the prescribed optimality gap relative to \(\min_{v\in F}L(v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure best-bound traversal always processes an open node with the smallest valid lower bound, using a fixed secondary rule only for ties.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
Every open-node value \(L(v)\) is a valid lower bound for that node region.
Branching and fathoming preserve branch-and-bound validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each selected node \(v^*\) satisfies \(L(v^*)=\min_{v\in F}L(v)\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound at node v

children.title: Best-Bound Tie-Breaking Families
children.top_down_role: Secondary priorities for equal-bound nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Bound Tie-Breaking Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic refinement of best-bound node selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the open-node set for a minimization problem, and let \(L(v)\) be the valid lower bound of each \(v\in F\). For each declared secondary priority, define an oriented key \(\widetilde t_i(v)\) so that a smaller value always means higher priority; append a final unique creation key oriented in the same way. Select the lexicographic minimum of \[(L(v),\widetilde t_1(v),\ldots,\widetilde t_k(v)).\] Choices of oriented keys yield deepest-first, shallowest-first, earliest-created, latest-created, or best-estimate tie-breaking. Because the secondary keys are consulted only among nodes attaining \(\min_{u\in F}L(u)\), every such family preserves the pure best-bound primary rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best-bound ties are resolved lexicographically by secondary keys normalized so that smaller means preferred, without allowing depth, creation order, or estimate priorities to override the minimum-bound requirement.
assumptions_latex: Every oriented secondary key is defined for every open node.
A final deterministic key makes the selected node unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected node \(v^*\) satisfies \(L(v^*)=\min_{u\in F}L(u)\), irrespective of the declared tie-breaking family.

notation.meaning: i-th oriented secondary key, with smaller values preferred

Both traversals obey the same exact best-bound primary rule and differ only in their tie rule.

children.title: Global-Bound Progress Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Bound Progress Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-wide dual-bound behavior under best-bound traversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, define the global search lower bound at iteration \(k\) by \[D_k=\min_{v\in F_k}L_k(v),\] with \(D_k=+\infty\) when the open frontier \(F_k\) is empty. Suppose node bounds are valid, child bounds are no smaller than their parent bound, and any global strengthening never decreases stored bounds. Under pure best-bound traversal, the processed node has bound \(D_k\), and after its removal, fathoming, or replacement by children, \(D_{k+1}\ge D_k\). Thus traversal exposes the nodes currently determining the global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With monotone valid child bounds, best-bound traversal processes a node attaining the global lower bound, and that bound cannot decrease between iterations.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with frontier \(F_k\).
Every child bound is at least its parent bound.
Global relaxation updates do not decrease valid stored bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global lower-bound sequence is monotone: \(D_{k+1}\ge D_k\), and the selected node at iteration \(k\) attains \(D_k\).

children.title: Frontier Memory-Growth Boundary
children.top_down_role: Large active frontiers created by broad bound-oriented exploration.

children.title: Active-Frontier Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion patterns of the live node frontier under broad exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Frontier Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact accounting for the live-node frontier of a finitely branching branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0\) be a finite active frontier, let \(t\in\mathbb N_0\), and suppose exactly one active node is expanded at each of the first \(t\) iterations. Write \(A_i=|F_i|\), where \(F_i\) is the frontier after \(i\) expansions, and let \(c_i\in\mathbb N_0\) be the number of children retained after immediate fathoming at expansion \(i\). Then \[A_t=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^{t}(c_i-1).\] If \(c_i\le q\) for an integer \(q\ge0\), then \[A_t\le A_0+(q-1)t.\] Equality holds if and only if \(c_i=q\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,t\}\). In particular, binary branching gives \(A_t\le A_0+t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each expansion changes the active-frontier size by the number of retained children minus one. If at most q children are retained per expansion, the frontier grows by at most q minus one nodes per expansion; binary branching therefore adds at most one live node per expansion.
assumptions_latex: \(F_0\) is finite.
\(t\in\mathbb N_0\), and each of the first \(t\) iterations expands exactly one current frontier node.
\(q\in\mathbb N_0\), and \(0\le c_i\le q\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,t\}\).

number of children retained at expansion i
integer upper bound on retained children per expansion

children.title: Node-Record Memory Pressure
children.top_down_role: Storage pressure attributable to retained active-node records.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Shared-Storage Boundary for Per-Node Memory Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of cardinality-based lower bounds without a positive incremental storage charge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a finite frontier \(F\) uses shared storage \(s\ge0\) and node-specific increments \(d(v)\ge0\), so \[M=s+\sum_{v\in F}d(v).\] If \(d(v)\ge d_{\min}>0\), then \(M\ge s+d_{\min}|F|\). Without a positive lower bound on \(d(v)\), no inequality \(M\ge c|F|\) with \(c>0\) follows; shared, implicit, or recomputable representations may have zero incremental charge for arbitrarily many nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear memory growth in frontier cardinality requires a positive per-node incremental storage charge.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite.
Shared and incremental storage are counted without duplication.
\(s\ge0\) and \(d(v)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\ge s+d_{\min}|F|\text{ requires }d_{\min}>0;\ d(v)\ge0\text{ alone gives no positive linear lower bound.}
knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Storage Boundary for Per-Node Memory Bounds
Node-Record Memory Pressure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory required to retain an explicit finite active frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_t\) be a finite active frontier. Suppose each \(v\in F_t\) has a separately retained record of size \(m(v)>0\) bytes, and define \[M_t=\sum_{v\in F_t}m(v).\] If constants \(m_{\min},m_{\max}\) satisfy \(0<m_{\min}\le m(v)\le m_{\max}<\infty\) for every \(v\in F_t\), then \[m_{\min}|F_t|\le M_t\le m_{\max}|F_t|.\] Consequently, for any memory budget \(B\in[0,\infty)\), the condition \(M_t\le B\) implies \[|F_t|\le\left\lfloor\frac{B}{m_{\min}}\right\rfloor,\] independently of the node-selection order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit frontier-record memory is bounded above and below by constant multiples of the number of active records. A nonnegative memory budget therefore caps the number of simultaneously stored active nodes.
assumptions_latex: \(F_t\) is finite.
Every \(v\in F_t\) has a separately retained record.
\(0<m_{\min}\le m(v)\le m_{\max}<\infty\) for every \(v\in F_t\).
\(B\in[0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_{\min}|F_t|\le M_t\le m_{\max}|F_t|\), and \(M_t\le B\) implies \(|F_t|\le\lfloor B/m_{\min}\rfloor\).

notation.meaning: finite active frontier at snapshot t

nonnegative available memory budget in bytes

children.title: Frontier Compression Limits
children.top_down_role: Boundaries on reducing frontier storage without changing search behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-length representation when only behaviorally distinguishable frontier states must remain distinct.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a finite family of frontier states and let \(\sim\) identify states having identical required behavior under every admissible continuation. If \(E:\mathcal F\to\{0,1\}^b\) satisfies \(E(f)=E(g)\Rightarrow f\sim g\), then distinct classes in \(\mathcal F/\!\sim\) receive distinct codes. Therefore \[b\ge \left\lceil\log_2|\mathcal F/\!\sim|\right\rceil.\] Merging two distinct classes changes some required continuation behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A behavior-preserving encoding must distinguish all frontier-state equivalence classes that can require different future behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is finite.
\(\sim\) captures every behavior required by the solver contract.
No uncounted side information distinguishes equal codes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\ge\lceil\log_2|\mathcal F/\!\sim|\rceil.
knowledge_statements.title: Behavior-Preserving Frontier Quotients
Frontier Compression Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information lower bound for lossless encoding of distinguishable active frontiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a finite family of active-frontier states that can require different future branching, pruning, or reconstruction decisions. Any lossless encoding \(E:\mathcal F\to\{0,1\}^{*}\) from which the exact state is recoverable must be injective. If all codewords have length at most \(b\), then \(|\mathcal F|\le 2^{b+1}-1\); for fixed-length \(b\)-bit records, \(|\mathcal F|\le2^b\). Hence exact fixed-length representation requires \(b\ge\lceil\log_2|\mathcal F|\rceil\). Compression below this boundary must merge distinguishable states or use external information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lossless compression must assign distinct codes to frontier states requiring distinct future behavior, so its bit length is bounded below by their logarithmic count.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is a finite set of distinguishable frontier states.
Decoding must reconstruct the exact state without uncounted side information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed-length lossless codes, \(b\ge\lceil\log_2|\mathcal F|\rceil\).

notation.meaning: maximum or fixed code length in bits

children.title: Best-Estimate Node Selection
children.top_down_role: Traversal guided by estimates of attainable feasible solutions.

children.title: Estimate-Based Frontier Priority
children.top_down_role: Node ordering by predictions of subtree solution quality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordering Independence of Exact Search Correctness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between heuristic estimate ordering and certificate-based branch-and-bound logic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite branch-and-bound tree whose branching disjunctions exhaust every unresolved feasible solution and whose nodes are removed only after processing or valid fathoming. If search continues until the frontier is empty, any rule selecting an active node at every nonterminal iteration—including arbitrary estimate-based ordering—preserves exhaustive-search correctness. Estimate accuracy can change order and work but not the final exact conclusion. An uncertified estimate used by itself to fathom a node need not preserve correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary estimates may safely order a finite exhaustive search, but they cannot replace valid pruning or termination certificates.
assumptions_latex: The generated search tree is finite.
Branching exhaustively covers each unresolved parent region.
Fathoming is valid independently of the priority estimate.
A node is selected whenever the frontier is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Estimate ordering preserves exactness under exhaustive valid processing; estimate-only fathoming is unjustified.}
knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Independence of Exact Search Correctness
Estimate-Based Frontier Priority
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-estimate selection for a minimization branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every active node \(v\), maintain an estimate \(e(v)\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) of the best feasible objective attainable in its subtree. Initialize the frontier with the root and its estimate. At iteration \(t\), first remove every node certified fathomed; then choose \[v_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in F_t}e(v),\] using a fixed tie rule, expand \(v_t\), compute estimates for retained children, and insert them into the frontier. Stop when the frontier is empty or a prescribed valid termination criterion holds; return the incumbent and its certificate when exact termination is claimed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best-estimate search expands the active node predicted to contain the best attainable solution, while pruning and termination remain governed by valid branch-and-bound certificates.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
Every retained active node receives an estimate.
Exact termination uses valid fathoming and bound tests rather than estimates alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next expanded node belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in F_t}e(v)\).

notation.meaning: predicted best objective in node v's subtree

children.title: Estimate Calibration Boundary
children.top_down_role: Traversal sensitivity to inaccurate subtree estimates.

children.title: Estimate Calibration
children.top_down_role: Agreement between subtree estimates and realized search outcomes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Calibration Does Not Imply Pointwise Ranking Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-mean calibration does not guarantee correct ordering of individual frontier nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\in\{0,1\}\) with both values having positive probability. Conditional on \(E=0\), let \(Y\) equal \(-1\) or \(1\), each with probability \(1/2\); conditional on \(E=1\), let \(Y\) equal \(0\) or \(2\), each with probability \(1/2\). Then \(\mathbb E[Y\mid E]=E\). Nevertheless, independent nodes drawn from the two strata have \(E(u)=0<E(v)=1\) but \(Y(u)=1>Y(v)=0\) with probability \(1/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfect mean calibration can coexist with incorrect realized ordering of individual nodes.
assumptions_latex: Smaller objectives and estimates are preferred.
Both prediction strata have positive probability.
Compared nodes are independently drawn from their strata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[Y\mid E]=E\not\Rightarrow\bigl(E(u)<E(v)\Rightarrow Y(u)\le Y(v)\bigr).
knowledge_statements.title: Calibration Does Not Imply Pointwise Ranking Accuracy
Estimate Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-mean calibration of finite subtree-quality predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((Y,E)\) be integrable real random variables, where \(Y\) is the realized best feasible objective in a sampled node's subtree and \(E\) is its prediction. The estimator is mean-calibrated when \[\mathbb E[Y\mid E]=E\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Equivalently, for every Borel set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R\) with \(\mathbb P(E\in C)>0\), \[\mathbb E[Y-E\mid E\in C]=0.\] Empirical bin calibration approximates this condition by comparing average outcomes and predictions within prespecified prediction bins.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subtree estimate is mean-calibrated when nodes receiving a given predicted value have that value as their conditional average realized subtree quality.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) and \(E\) are real-valued and integrable.
Nodes are sampled from a specified frontier-generating distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[Y\mid E]=E\) almost surely.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-mean calibration condition is coherent and the content kind fits, but its application to sampled subtree-quality predictions and the required frontier-generating distribution have no supporting source.

children.title: Systematic Estimate Bias
children.top_down_role: Persistent directional errors in subtree estimates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-class example separating systematic bias from residual noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two deterministic node classes \(A,B\) with \(Y_A=0\), \(Y_B=1\), \(E_A=2\), and \(E_B=1\). Then \(b(A)=2\), \(b(B)=0\), and the residual errors are zero. Although class \(A\) has better true quality, its estimate is worse: \(E_A>E_B\). Adding the same constant to both estimates preserves this reversal, while replacing the differential biases by any common bias restores the true ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group-dependent systematic bias alone can reverse frontier priorities even with no residual noise; a common offset cannot.
assumptions_latex: Smaller values are preferred.
The two classes are compared using their deterministic estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y_A<Y_B\quad\text{but}\quad E_A>E_B.
knowledge_statements.title: Differential-Bias Ranking Reversal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and expected-ranking effect of group- or feature-dependent additive bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) describe a sampled node, and let the finite integrable variables \(Y\) and \(E\) be its realized subtree-best objective and estimate. Define \[b(X)=\mathbb E[E-Y\mid X],\qquad \eta=(E-Y)-b(X),\] so \(\mathbb E[\eta\mid X]=0\). Writing \(\mu(X)=\mathbb E[Y\mid X]\), one has \(\mathbb E[E\mid X]=\mu(X)+b(X)\). For two feature classes \(x_u,x_v\) with \(\mu(x_u)<\mu(x_v)\), their expected estimated ordering is reversed exactly when \[b(x_u)-b(x_v)>\mu(x_v)-\mu(x_u).\] A common additive bias cancels from every such comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Systematic bias is conditional mean prediction error. Common bias preserves expected ranking, while differential bias reverses it when it exceeds the true conditional-quality margin.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) and \(E\) are finite and integrable.
The node population and conditioning variable \(X\) are fixed.
Smaller objectives and estimates are preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[E\mid X]=\mu(X)+b(X),\quad b(x_u)-b(x_v)>\mu(x_v)-\mu(x_u)\iff\text{expected-order reversal}.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Systematic-Bias Decomposition
Systematic Estimate Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive bias and its effect on best-estimate frontier ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sampled active node, define the prediction error \(\varepsilon=E-Y\) and systematic additive bias \(b=\mathbb E[\varepsilon]\), assuming integrability. A common constant shift \(E'(v)=E(v)+c\) leaves every pairwise frontier ordering unchanged. In contrast, node-dependent biases can reverse a true ordering: for nodes \(u,v\) with \(Y(u)<Y(v)\), the estimates misrank them exactly when \[\varepsilon(u)-\varepsilon(v)>Y(v)-Y(u).\] Thus global offset affects numerical calibration but not selection, whereas differential bias can alter the search trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common additive bias does not change node ranking, but differences in node-specific bias can reverse a true subtree-quality ordering when they exceed its margin.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized by selecting smaller estimates.
The compared subtree outcomes and estimates are finite.
Prediction errors are integrable when their mean is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A true pair \(Y(u)<Y(v)\) is reversed precisely when \(\varepsilon(u)-\varepsilon(v)>Y(v)-Y(u)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise reversal identity concerns realized node errors, whereas the surrounding claim describes node-dependent systematic biases without defining them. A direct source is needed to establish the intended bias notion and its connection to frontier ordering.

children.title: Frontier Misranking Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Traversal consequences of inaccurate relative node priorities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharpness of the Uniform Misranking Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-node frontier attaining regret arbitrarily close to twice the uniform error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\epsilon>0\), \(0<\delta<2\epsilon\), and \(F=\{u,v\}\). Set \[Y(u)=0,\quad Y(v)=2\epsilon-\delta,\quad E(u)=\epsilon,\quad E(v)=\epsilon-\delta.\] Then \(|E(w)-Y(w)|=\epsilon\) for both nodes, but \(E(v)<E(u)\). Estimate-based selection chooses \(v\) and incurs regret \(2\epsilon-\delta\). Hence the factor \(2\) in the uniform-error bound cannot be reduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite-sign errors can make estimate-based selection almost two epsilon worse than the truly best node.
assumptions_latex: \(\epsilon>0\).
\(0<\delta<2\epsilon\).
Smaller values are preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{\|E-Y\|_\infty\le\epsilon}\left(Y(\widehat v)-\min_{w\in F}Y(w)\right)=2\epsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Uniform Misranking Bound
Frontier Misranking Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive selection sensitivity under uniformly accurate frontier estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite nonempty frontier, let \(Y,E:F\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\epsilon\ge0\). Suppose \(|E(v)-Y(v)|\le\epsilon\) for every \(v\in F\). If \(\widehat v\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in F}E(v)\) and \(v^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in F}Y(v)\), then \[Y(\widehat v)\le Y(v^*)+2\epsilon.\] Moreover, if \(Y(u)+2\epsilon<Y(v)\), then \(E(u)<E(v)\); hence only pairs whose true-quality gap is at most \(2\epsilon\) can be reversed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every frontier estimate has absolute error at most epsilon, the node selected by the estimates is at most two epsilon worse than the truly best frontier node, and estimates preserve every pairwise quality gap larger than two epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and nonempty.
\(Y,E:F\to\mathbb R\).
\(\epsilon\ge0\), and \(|E(v)-Y(v)|\le\epsilon\) for every \(v\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y(\widehat v)-\min_{v\in F}Y(v)\le2\epsilon\).

notation.meaning: true subtree-best objective at node v
estimated subtree-best objective at node v

children.title: Depth–Best-Bound Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Combinations of depth-oriented and bound-oriented traversal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth-oriented dives whose roots are selected globally by valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an active frontier \(F\). When no dive is active, choose \(r\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in F}L(v)\). After expanding a dive node, continue with a prescribed retained child when one exists; otherwise end the dive and again choose a minimum-bound node from the whole frontier. Every unchosen retained child remains in \(F\), and pruning uses only valid branch-and-bound certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method starts a dive at a best-bound node, follows one child depthwise, and returns to global best-bound selection when the dive ends.
assumptions_latex: L(v)\text{ is a valid lower bound for every }v\in F.
\text{Every unchosen retained child remains active.}
\text{The child-continuation and tie rules are specified.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every dive root has minimum frontier bound, while intra-dive continuation is depth-oriented.}

notation.meaning: valid lower bound at node v

knowledge_statements.title: Dive-Then-Best-Bound Hybrid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous depth and bound priority with explicit frontier scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite frontier \(F_t\), normalize bounds by \(\bar L_t(v)=0\) when all bounds coincide and otherwise by \((L(v)-L_{\min})/(L_{\max}-L_{\min})\). Normalize depths analogously as \(\bar d_t(v)\). Given \(\alpha_t\in[0,1]\), select a deterministic minimizer of \(\alpha_t\bar L_t(v)-(1-\alpha_t)\bar d_t(v)\). The endpoints recover best-bound and deepest-node priority up to the fixed tie rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize frontier bounds and depths and minimize a weighted score interpolating between best-bound and deepest-node selection.
assumptions_latex: F_t\text{ is finite and nonempty}.
L(v)\text{ is valid and }d(v)\text{ is finite for every }v\in F_t.
\text{A deterministic tie rule is fixed}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_t=1\Rightarrow\text{best-bound priority},\qquad\alpha_t=0\Rightarrow\text{deepest-node priority}.
review_flags: This is a precise policy template, not a universal performance claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Scalarized Depth–Bound Priority

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient scheduling condition preventing starvation in dive-based hybrids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every dive performs at most \(K<\infty\) expansions, unchosen live nodes remain in the frontier, and between dives a fair global rule eventually selects or validly closes every persistent live node. Then intra-dive continuation cannot starve a persistent live node. If the underlying search tree is finite, the frontier is eventually exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded dives with fair global reselection prevent starvation and preserve finite-tree completeness.
assumptions_latex: K<\infty.
\text{Unchosen live nodes remain in the frontier}.
\text{The between-dive selection rule is fair}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Finite underlying tree}\Longrightarrow\text{eventual frontier exhaustion}.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Dive Fairness Condition
Depth–Best-Bound Hybrids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted hybrid of depth preference and relaxation-bound priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each active node \(v\), let \(L(v)\) be its valid lower bound and \(d(v)\) its depth. At iteration \(t\), normalize these quantities over the finite frontier to values \(\bar L_t(v),\bar d_t(v)\in[0,1]\), assigning zero when the corresponding range is zero. Given \(\alpha_t\in[0,1]\), select a nonfathomed node minimizing \[S_t(v)=\alpha_t\bar L_t(v)-(1-\alpha_t)\bar d_t(v).\] Expand it, update bounds and the frontier, and stop only under a valid branch-and-bound termination rule. The endpoints recover normalized best-bound and deepest-node selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hybrid minimizes a weighted score combining a small relaxation bound with large depth; changing the weight interpolates between best-bound and depth-first priorities.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
Every active node has a valid lower bound and finite depth.
The frontier normalization rule and tie rule are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in F_t}\{\alpha_t\bar L_t(v)-(1-\alpha_t)\bar d_t(v)\}\).

children.title: Best-Estimate Hybrid Search
children.top_down_role: Traversal combining subtree estimates with depth or bound priorities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimate-led frontier ordering with certified-bound and depth refinements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite nonempty frontier \(F_t\), let \(E_t(v)\) be a subtree-quality estimate, \(L_t(v)\) a valid lower bound, \(d(v)\) depth, and \(\kappa(v)\) a unique deterministic tie key. Select the lexicographic minimum of \((E_t(v),L_t(v),-d(v),\kappa(v))\). Estimates affect priority only; pruning and exact termination require valid bounds, feasibility information, and exhaustive frontier accounting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lexicographic best-estimate hybrid prioritizes predicted subtree quality, then bound and depth, without treating predictions as certificates.
assumptions_latex: F_t\text{ is finite and nonempty.}
E_t(v),L_t(v),d(v)\text{ are defined for every }v\in F_t.
\kappa\text{ is injective on }F_t.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in F_t}^{\mathrm{lex}}(E_t(v),L_t(v),-d(v),\kappa(v)),\quad E_t(v)\text{ alone does not certify fathoming.}

notation.meaning: predicted subtree quality at node v

knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Best-Estimate Hybrid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tree failure boundary for estimate-led traversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(m\ge1\), let a frontier contain a node \(u\), which yields an improving incumbent when processed, and nodes \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\), which yield no improvement. If \(E(v_i)=0<E(u)=1\) and none is validly fathomed earlier, pure increasing-estimate selection processes all \(m\) misleading nodes before \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incorrect estimates can delay an improving node by an arbitrarily large finite number of expansions.
assumptions_latex: \text{Selection uses increasing }E\text{ with deterministic ties}.
\text{No displayed node is validly fathomed before selection}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall m\ge1\ \exists T_m:\operatorname{delay}(u)\ge m.
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Delay from Misleading Estimates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A standard estimate of completion value below a fractional relaxation node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a minimization node \(v\) with relaxation value \(L(v)\) and fractional integer variables \(J(v)\), let \(p_j^-,p_j^+\ge0\) be directional pseudocosts and \(\delta_j^-=x_j^v-\lfloor x_j^v\rfloor\), \(\delta_j^+=\lceil x_j^v\rceil-x_j^v\). A completion estimate is \[E(v)=L(v)+\sum_{j\in J(v)}\min\{p_j^-\delta_j^-,p_j^+\delta_j^+\}.\] Unless separately validated, \(E(v)\) is a prediction rather than a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pseudocost estimate adds predicted integrality-repair degradation to the relaxation value and is normally only a priority score.
assumptions_latex: L(v)\text{ is the node relaxation value}.
p_j^-,p_j^+\ge0\text{ are defined directional pseudocost estimates}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E(v)\text{ need not satisfy }E(v)\le z^*(v).

notation.meaning: fractional integer variables at node v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid priority combining predicted subtree quality with bound and depth information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each active node \(v\), maintain normalized estimate, valid lower-bound, and depth scores \(\bar E_t(v),\bar L_t(v),\bar d_t(v)\in[0,1]\). Choose fixed or adaptively predetermined weights \(a_t,b_t,c_t\ge0\) with \(a_t+b_t+c_t=1\), and select a nonfathomed node minimizing \[S_t(v)=a_t\bar E_t(v)+b_t\bar L_t(v)-c_t\bar d_t(v).\] After expansion, compute child scores and update the frontier. Predictions determine priority only: pruning, optimality certification, and exact stopping must use valid bounds and feasibility information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This hybrid ranks nodes by a weighted combination of predicted subtree quality, valid bound, and depth, while reserving pruning and certification for rigorous information.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
All three normalized scores are defined on the active frontier.
Weights and tie-breaking are fixed before each selection.

children.title: Phase-Switching Search
children.top_down_role: Priority changes across primal, dual, and resource-management phases.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fairness boundary for state-dependent switching among traversal priorities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) remain live from iteration \(t_0\) onward. If every subsequently active phase uses a selection rule that never chooses \(v\), and no valid certificate closes \(v\), then the traversal is unfair and cannot exhaust its frontier. Validity of each phase-specific priority alone therefore does not imply asymptotic completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individually valid phase priorities do not ensure complete search when switching can starve a persistent live node.
assumptions_latex: v\in F_t\text{ for all }t\ge t_0.
\text{No valid certificate closes }v.
\text{The selected node is never }v\text{ for }t\ge t_0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The traversal is unfair and cannot exhaust the active frontier.}
knowledge_statements.title: Phase-Starvation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical phase roles and admissible switching triggers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal phase may prioritize favorable feasible-solution estimates, a dual phase may prioritize minimum valid lower bound, and a resource-control phase may prioritize depth, age, or subtree closure. Predetermined triggers may include incumbent improvement, a prescribed count without incumbent improvement, certified global-bound improvement, or a frontier-memory threshold. Phase keys, thresholds, and ties are part of the policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phases may emphasize incumbent discovery, global-bound progress, or frontier reduction, using explicit progress or resource triggers.
assumptions_latex: \text{Every phase key, trigger threshold, and tie rule is specified}.
\text{Only valid bounds and feasibility information are used for fathoming}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Phase changes alter priority but not pruning validity}.
review_flags: Precise estimates and threshold choices are solver dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual–Resource Phase Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive definition using explicit phase states and switching events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A phase-switching traversal policy consists of a finite phase set \(P\), a deterministic frontier priority \(\pi_p\) for each \(p\in P\), and a switching map \(\phi\) from recorded state and events to the next phase. At iteration \(t\), it sets \(p_t=\phi(p_{t-1},s_t)\) and selects by \(\pi_{p_t}\). Every uncertified live region remains represented across switches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase-switching search selects among explicit phase-specific priorities through a predetermined state or event map while preserving unresolved regions.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is finite}.
\pi_p\text{ and }\phi\text{ include deterministic tie conventions}.
\text{Uncertified regions remain explicitly or losslessly represented}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_t=\phi(p_{t-1},s_t),\qquad v_t=\pi_{p_t}(F_t).

notation.meaning: recorded search state and trigger events

knowledge_statements.title: Phase-Switching Traversal Policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for completeness despite repeated phase changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every uncertified live node is preserved and the combined phase schedule is fair—each node remaining live indefinitely is eventually selected or validly closed—then phase changes cannot prevent frontier exhaustion on a finite search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State-preserving fair phase switching remains complete on a finite search tree.
assumptions_latex: \text{The underlying generated tree is finite}.
\text{Live nodes are preserved across switches}.
\text{The combined schedule is fair}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Finite tree and fair switching}\Longrightarrow\text{frontier exhaustion}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fair Phase-Scheduling Completeness
Phase-Switching Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-dependent switching among primal, dual, and memory-control node priorities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an incumbent value \(U_t\), a global valid lower bound \(L_t\), frontier memory \(M_t\), and phase \(p_t\). A predetermined switching map \(\phi\) sets \(p_t=\phi(U_t,L_t,M_t)\). In a primal phase, select by a feasible-solution estimate; in a dual phase, select by smallest node lower bound; in a memory phase, select by a depth-oriented key that tends to close subtrees. Expand the selected node, update all state variables, and re-evaluate \(\phi\). Exactness is retained only if switching changes priority without invalidly discarding live nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase-switching search changes its node priority according to incumbent, global bound, and memory state while preserving rigorous pruning and exact termination rules.
assumptions_latex: Every node lower bound used for certification is valid.
The switching map and phase-specific tie rules are specified.
Priority changes do not discard uncertified live nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_t=\phi(U_t,L_t,M_t)\), and the phase-specific key selects the next node without changing validity of fathoming.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The phase-switching algorithm matches the leaf conceptually, but neither the switching map nor the stated primal, dual, and memory phases are supported by the cited general branch-and-bound outline.

children.title: Restart Diversification Regimes
children.top_down_role: Controlled departure from persistent traversal trajectories.

children.title: Restart Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Timing regimes for abandoning persistent traversal trajectories.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness failure when an epoch boundary discards an unresolved region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a restart deletes a live node \(v\) whose region contains a feasible solution better than the incumbent, without a valid fathoming certificate and without preserving or losslessly reconstructing that region. Subsequent search need not visit that solution, so exhaustion of the reduced frontier does not certify optimality for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarding an unresolved region at restart can destroy exactness even when every later epoch is searched exhaustively.
assumptions_latex: v\text{ is live immediately before the restart.}
\text{Its region is neither validly fathomed nor losslessly reconstructible afterward.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Reduced-state frontier exhaustion is not an original-problem optimality certificate.}
knowledge_statements.title: Destructive-Restart Incompleteness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed, increasing, geometric, and adaptive epoch schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Budget families include fixed schedules \(\tau_k=\tau\), nondecreasing schedules \(\tau_{k+1}\ge\tau_k\), geometric schedules \(\tau_k=\lceil\tau_1\rho^{k-1}\rceil\) with \(\rho>1\), and adaptive schedules whose next budget or trigger is a predetermined function \(\psi(s_k)\) of recorded progress state. Exactness additionally requires state preservation and valid fathoming.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart budgets may be fixed, increasing, geometric, or adaptively determined from recorded progress.
assumptions_latex: \tau,\tau_1\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\quad\rho>1.
\text{Adaptive update rules are specified before their decisions}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau_k\in\{\tau,\ \text{a nondecreasing sequence},\ \lceil\tau_1\rho^{k-1}\rceil,\ \psi(s_k)\}.

notation.meaning: predetermined adaptive budget or trigger rule

knowledge_statements.title: Restart-Budget Families

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restart epochs, budgets or triggers, and retained exact-search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restart schedule is a sequence of epochs. Epoch \(k\) ends after a prescribed positive budget \(\tau_k\) or event \(e_k\), after which traversal parameters may change. An exact state-preserving restart retains the incumbent, all valid global information, and every uncertified live region explicitly or by lossless reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restart schedule divides search into budgeted or event-triggered epochs and changes traversal parameters without losing unresolved regions.
assumptions_latex: \tau_k>0\text{ for a budget-triggered epoch}.
\text{Every uncertified live region is retained or losslessly reconstructible}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Restarting changes traversal state, not the union of unresolved regions}.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Preserving Restart Schedule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient completeness condition across infinitely many epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume restarts preserve every uncertified live region and the cross-epoch traversal is fair: every region remaining live indefinitely is eventually expanded or validly fathomed. If an infinite execution allocates unbounded total expansion budget, \(\sum_{k\ge1}\tau_k=\infty\), then restarts do not destroy completeness; in particular, a finite underlying exhaustive tree is eventually exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State preservation, cross-epoch fairness, and unbounded total effort preserve completeness on a finite search tree.
assumptions_latex: \sum_{k\ge1}\tau_k=\infty.
\text{Restart state is losslessly preserved}.
\text{The cross-epoch schedule is fair}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Finite underlying tree}\Longrightarrow\text{eventual frontier exhaustion}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fair-Restart Completeness
Restart Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted restart epochs that preserve exact branch-and-bound state or reconstruct it losslessly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose positive epoch budgets \(\tau_1,\tau_2,\ldots\). During epoch \(k\), perform at most \(\tau_k\) node expansions using a selected traversal seed or priority parameter. At the epoch boundary, preserve the incumbent, valid global bounds, and every uncertified live subproblem, either explicitly or by lossless reconstruction; then change the traversal seed or priority and begin epoch \(k+1\). Stop on a valid optimality, infeasibility, or resource-limit criterion. For an unbounded exact run, require \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\tau_k=\infty\) and a fair policy that eventually expands or validly fathoms every persistent live node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart scheduling allocates expansion budgets to successive search epochs while preserving all exact-search state; infinite schedules additionally require unbounded effort and fairness.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau_k\) is a positive integer for every epoch.
Restarts preserve or losslessly reconstruct all uncertified live subproblems.
Exact infinite execution uses a fair traversal policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact restarts require state preservation; completeness additionally requires \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\tau_k=\infty\) and fairness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restart algorithm and its state-preservation requirements fit the leaf, but the infinite-budget and fairness conditions require a direct algorithmic source.

children.title: Search Diversification Targets
children.top_down_role: Regions or search attributes targeted when redirecting traversal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of feature-distance target selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an arbitrary feature map \(z\) and metric \(d\), a large value of \(d(z(u),z(v))\) alone does not imply disjoint feasible regions, different incumbent prospects, or different computational work. Any such implication requires additional assumptions connecting the features and metric to the underlying subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large feature distance does not by itself certify mathematical or computational diversity.
assumptions_latex: z\text{ is an arbitrary node-feature map and }d\text{ is a metric on its image.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d(z(u),z(v))\text{ alone certifies neither region nor workload diversity.}
knowledge_statements.title: Feature-Distance Proxy Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classes of search attributes toward which traversal may be redirected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A diversification target may be specified in tree space by a node, subtree, depth, or branching history; in decision space by variable fixings or distance from previously emphasized assignments; or in priority-feature space by bounds, estimates, age, or other node attributes. Targeting changes preference among retained nodes and does not itself justify deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diversification may target tree regions, assignments, or node features, but target selection alone never certifies fathoming.
assumptions_latex: \text{Targets refer to live nodes or to regions recoverable without losing unresolved solutions.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Diversification target selection is a traversal operation, not a fathoming certificate.}
knowledge_statements.title: Diversification Target Spaces

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Age-based diversification among retained frontier regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign every eligible active target \(v\) a timestamp \(r(v)\) equal to its most recent emphasis epoch, using \(-\infty\) for a never-emphasized target. At diversification epoch \(k\), select a deterministic minimizer of \(r(v)\) and update its timestamp to \(k\). Every unselected uncertified region remains active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Age-based diversification redirects search to the eligible live region least recently emphasized.
assumptions_latex: F_k\text{ is finite and nonempty}.
\text{Eligibility and deterministic tie rules are specified}.
\text{Unselected live regions remain represented}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in F_k}r(v).

notation.meaning: last epoch in which target v was emphasized

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Recently-Emphasized Target Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage property of least-recently-emphasized selection on a fixed frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a finite eligible frontier \(F\) remains unchanged and the least-recently-emphasized rule assigns the selected target the current, hence newest, timestamp, then every target in \(F\) is selected at least once within the next \(|F|\) diversification epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a fixed finite frontier, age-based target selection visits every target within one full round.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is finite, nonempty, and unchanged during the stated epochs}.
\text{The selected target receives a timestamp newer than every prior timestamp}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall v\in F,\quad v\text{ is selected within at most }|F|\text{ epochs}.
review_flags: Dynamic-frontier fairness requires additional admission and eligibility conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Frontier Round-Robin Coverage
Search Diversification Targets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximin selection of structurally distinct frontier regions at diversification epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each active node \(v\) a feature vector \(z(v)\) in a metric space with distance \(d\), and let \(H_k\) contain feature vectors of regions emphasized in earlier epochs. At diversification epoch \(k\), select \[v_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{v\in F_k}\min_{h\in H_k}d(z(v),h),\] with a prescribed convention when \(H_k\) is empty. Use \(v_k\) or its region as the next traversal target, then add \(z(v_k)\) to the history. Diversification affects priority only; exact search must retain every uncertified active subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximin diversification target is the active region farthest from previously emphasized regions under a chosen feature metric, without sacrificing uncertified nodes.
assumptions_latex: \(F_k\) is finite and nonempty.
Node features and their metric are specified.
Diversification changes priority but not valid fathoming.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_k\) maximizes its minimum feature distance from the prior target history \(H_k\).

notation.meaning: feature representation of node v's region

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximin rule is a coherent diversification algorithm, but no source supports this particular feature-space target policy in branch-and-bound search.

children.title: Restart Overhead
children.top_down_role: Search-state loss and repeated work associated with restarts.

assumptions_latex: The search is a deterministic branch-and-bound procedure for a minimization problem.
A restart discards or suspends the current traversal state and reinitializes node selection, while retaining only explicitly declared reusable information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restart overhead is the additional resource consumption attributable to restarting, relative to uninterrupted execution under the same node-processing rules.

notation.meaning: work of the corresponding uninterrupted run

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports a formal restart-overhead accounting convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive work accounting for deterministic branch-and-bound restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed instance and fixed node-processing rules, let \(W_{\mathrm{rst}}\) be the measured work of a run using restarts and let \(W_{\mathrm{base}}\) be the work of its uninterrupted reference run. Define the additive restart overhead by \[H_{\mathrm{rst}}=W_{\mathrm{rst}}-W_{\mathrm{base}}.\] If restart \(j\) incurs reinitialization work \(c_j\), repeats work \(r_j\), and avoids work \(s_j\), then under additive accounting, \[H_{\mathrm{rst}}=\sum_j(c_j+r_j-s_j).\] The resource unit must be fixed, such as processed nodes, relaxation solves, or elapsed time; overhead values using different units are not directly comparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart overhead is restarted-run work minus uninterrupted-run work, including reinitialization and repeated work and subtracting work avoided through diversification.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Overhead

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No evidence supports the proposed accounting convention, and the decomposition into reinitialization, repeated, and avoided work is valid only if those terms exhaust the measured difference. The record is a definition or representation, not a complexity bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Net Restart Effect Has No Universal Sign
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional statement under an explicitly chosen restarted-versus-baseline work convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If one defines \(H=W_{\mathrm{rst}}-W_{\mathrm{base}}\) for runs using the same resource unit and stopping criterion, then no universal sign follows: redirection may reduce total work, whereas reinitialization or repeated processing may increase it. This \(H\) is a net comparative effect, not necessarily a nonnegative gross restart cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a baseline-difference convention, the net work effect of restarting may be positive or negative and should not be confused with gross restart cost.
assumptions_latex: W_{\mathrm{rst}}\text{ and }W_{\mathrm{base}}\text{ use the same resource unit and stopping criterion.}
H\text{ is expressly defined as their difference.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ has no universal sign under this convention.}

notation.meaning: work of the reference uninterrupted run

knowledge_statements.title: Net Restart Effect Has No Universal Sign

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf should own resource costs attributable to restarting, excluding restart timing and diversification destinations. Its essential term is presently ambiguous between gross cost and a signed counterfactual difference; therefore the proposed claim is deferred and the topic remains deferred.

children.title: Search Outcome Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Exact, approximate, and incomplete search outcomes.

children.title: Frontier Exhaustion
children.top_down_role: Completion after closure of the active search frontier.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem searched by an exact branch-and-bound procedure.
Every generated region is either represented by an active node or has been validly closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An empty active frontier certifies completion; it certifies optimality if an incumbent exists and infeasibility otherwise.

notation.meaning: incumbent objective value, with infinity when absent
optimal objective value, with infinity for infeasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact completion after all branch-and-bound regions have been closed.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the active frontier is empty, \(\mathcal F=\varnothing\), and every generated search region has been closed by verified infeasibility, dominance by the incumbent, or exact resolution. Then the search is complete. If a feasible incumbent of value \(U<+\infty\) exists, every feasible point belongs to a closed region whose evidence excludes an objective value below \(U\), so \(z^*=U\). If no feasible incumbent exists and every region was closed by valid evidence, then the original problem is infeasible and \(z^*=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When no active nodes remain and every generated region was validly closed, the search is complete: the incumbent is optimal, or the problem is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Frontier Exhaustion

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Primal-Dual Gap Termination Family
children.top_down_role: Approximate completion organized by primal-dual gap conventions.

children.title: Absolute Gap Termination
children.top_down_role: Approximate completion governed by an absolute primal-dual gap convention.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
A feasible incumbent supplies an upper bound \(U\), and the unresolved frontier supplies a valid global lower bound \(L\).
The tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination is valid when \(U-L\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\), and the incumbent is absolutely \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\)-optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute primal-dual gap for finite minimization bounds.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\le z^*\le U\) be finite valid bounds on the optimal value \(z^*\), where \(U\) is attained by the incumbent. Absolute-gap termination at tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\ge 0\) is permitted exactly when \[U-L\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}.\] Because \(L\le z^*\le U\), the returned incumbent then satisfies \[0\le U-z^*\le U-L\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}.\] Thus the condition certifies absolute objective error at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\); tolerance zero yields exact optimality under exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, stop when the finite incumbent upper bound minus the valid global lower bound is at most the absolute tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Gap Termination

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

children.title: Relative Gap Termination
children.top_down_role: Approximate completion governed by a scale-relative primal-dual gap convention.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with finite bounds \(L\le z^*\le U\).
The incumbent attains \(U\), and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge 0\).
A positive scaling floor \(\delta>0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination is valid when \((U-L)/\max\{|U|,\delta\}\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\) under the stated convention.
review_flags: Relative-gap denominator conventions vary across solvers; this record fixes the incumbent-scaled convention explicitly.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-scaled relative gap with a positive denominator floor.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the relative-gap convention \[g_{\mathrm{rel}}=\frac{U-L}{\max\{|U|,\delta\}},\] where \(L\le z^*\le U\), the incumbent attains \(U\), and \(\delta>0\). Relative-gap termination at tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge 0\) is permitted when \[g_{\mathrm{rel}}\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}.\] Equivalently, the certified absolute objective error obeys \[0\le U-z^*\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{|U|,\delta\}.\] The denominator convention and floor are part of the condition and must accompany any reported relative gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an incumbent-scaled convention, stop when the absolute bound gap divided by the larger of incumbent magnitude and a positive floor meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Gap Termination

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

children.title: Gap-Convention Edge Cases
children.top_down_role: Scaling and sign regimes that complicate gap-based status interpretation.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
The reported gap is computed from an incumbent bound \(U\) and a global lower bound \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A gap-based certificate is unavailable or convention-dependent when a bound is nonfinite, the denominator vanishes, or numerical values violate \(L\le U\).

notation.meaning: incumbent upper bound and global lower bound

review_flags: Solver conventions for inconsistent or nonfinite bounds require implementation-specific review.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure cases for minimization gap calculations and reporting.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The formula \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L\) yields a finite certificate only when both bounds are finite and valid. If no incumbent exists, then \(U=+\infty\), so neither an absolute nor a finite relative gap certifies termination. A relative formula \((U-L)/d(U,L)\) is undefined when \(d(U,L)=0\) unless a positive floor is specified. If numerical computation produces \(L>U\), the negative raw gap must not be interpreted as stronger optimality; the bound inconsistency must first be resolved. When \(U=L=0\), absolute-gap termination is exact, while an unfloored relative gap is undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonfinite bounds, zero relative-gap denominators, and numerically inconsistent bounds prevent a clean gap certificate unless an explicit convention resolves them.
knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Convention Edge Cases

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

children.title: Resource-Limit Termination
children.top_down_role: Incomplete search under time, memory, node, or solution limits.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Incumbent Before Cutoff Does Not Imply Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal incomplete-search family separating failure to discover feasibility from exhaustive exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a search root branch into two regions, the first infeasible and the second containing a feasible point. If a resource limit stops the run after the first region is processed but before the second is examined, no incumbent has been found although the original problem is feasible. Therefore absence of an incumbent at a resource stop is not an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource limit may occur before a feasible branch is explored, so finding no incumbent does not prove infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The branching regions cover the root region.
A resource limit occurs before every branch is resolved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No incumbent at resource-limited termination does not imply infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: No Incumbent Before Cutoff Does Not Imply Infeasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incomplete termination caused by a time, memory, processed-node, or solution limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a finite resource limit is reached at time \(T\) before frontier exhaustion or a requested gap condition is certified. If unresolved regions remain, the run is incomplete. A feasible incumbent of value \(U_T\) remains a valid upper bound and a certified global lower bound \(L_T\) remains a valid lower bound, but these one-sided facts imply optimality only if an applicable gap condition is met. If no incumbent exists, the run establishes only that no feasible point was found before the limit, not that the problem is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource limit reached with unresolved search causes incomplete termination; valid incumbent and bound information survives, but optimality or infeasibility does not follow without a separate certificate.
assumptions_latex: A time, memory, node, solution, or comparable finite resource limit is reached.
Neither exact frontier exhaustion nor the requested gap certificate has been established.
At least one unresolved search region remains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The run is incomplete; retained valid bounds keep their one-sided guarantees but do not alone certify optimality or infeasibility.

notation.meaning: certified global lower bound at termination

review_flags: Accepted despite the missing locator because the claim follows directly from the meanings of valid bounds and unresolved search.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Limit Termination

children.title: Numerically Ambiguous Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination without a clean numerical certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: False Closure from an Uncertified Prune
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal family showing why uncertain node closure prevents a completion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:x\in\{0,1\}\}\). If the region \(x=0\) is incorrectly pruned as infeasible while \(x=1\) supplies an incumbent, the remaining recorded frontier may be empty and the reported incumbent value may be \(1\), although the true optimum is \(0\). Thus frontier emptiness after an uncertified numerical prune is not an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single erroneous numerical prune can remove the true optimum and leave a falsely completed tree.
assumptions_latex: A pruning decision may incorrectly exclude a feasible node.
Frontier emptiness is assessed after that decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An empty recorded frontier does not certify optimality when a node closure is uncertified.
knowledge_statements.title: False Closure from an Uncertified Prune

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision termination with an unresolved premise required by a completion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A terminated search is numerically ambiguous if at least one premise required for its claimed status remains uncertified—for example, incumbent feasibility, validity of a global bound, or soundness of a pruning decision. Computed values such as \(\widehat L>\widehat U\) do not themselves strengthen an optimality claim; absent a validated error convention that reconciles them, they reveal inconsistent certificate data. Such a run establishes neither optimality nor infeasibility solely from its reported incumbent, bound, or empty frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination is numerically ambiguous when finite-precision uncertainty leaves a required feasibility, bound, or pruning premise uncertified, so the reported search state is not a clean completion certificate.
assumptions_latex: The search uses finite-precision or otherwise inexact computations.
At least one premise needed for the asserted completion status has not been independently validated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported termination state alone does not certify optimality or infeasibility.
review_flags: Accepted as a solver-independent certificate-soundness boundary; implementation-specific status names and recovery policies are excluded.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerically Ambiguous Termination

children.title: Tree-Search Optimality Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Certificate families connecting primal feasibility with exhaustive exclusion of superior regions.

children.title: Incumbent Evidence Certificate
children.top_down_role: Certificate material associated with the incumbent solution.

children.title: Primal Feasibility Evidence
children.top_down_role: Certificate material supporting feasibility of the incumbent solution.

assumptions_latex:
The mixed-integer feasible set is \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n: g_i(x)\le 0,\ h_j(x)=0,
 x_k\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }k\in I\}\).
Feasibility tolerances are zero, or are explicitly incorporated into the predicates being checked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A displayed point \(\bar x\) is primal-feasibility evidence exactly when every defining constraint and integrality condition can be checked at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directly checkable feasibility evidence for a mixed-integer incumbent.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the feasible set \[X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\le 0\text{ for all }i,\ h_j(x)=0\text{ for all }j,\ x_k\in\mathbb Z\text{ for all }k\in I\},\] primal-feasibility evidence for an incumbent is a point \(\bar x\) together with checkable evaluations establishing \[g_i(\bar x)\le 0,\qquad h_j(\bar x)=0,\qquad \bar x_k\in\mathbb Z\quad(k\in I).\] Under declared nonzero tolerances, the evidence must state the modified residual and integrality predicates rather than silently treating approximate satisfaction as exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-feasibility evidence records an incumbent point and checkable constraint, equality, and integrality evaluations showing that it belongs to the mixed-integer feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility Evidence
