children.title: Incumbent Objective Evidence
children.top_down_role: Certificate material supporting the reported incumbent objective value.

assumptions_latex: The objective function \(f\) is evaluable at the feasible incumbent \(\bar x\).
The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((\bar x,U)\) with \(U=f(\bar x)\) certifies the primal bound \(z^*\le U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value evidence establishing a minimization primal bound.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a verified feasible point for the minimization problem \(z^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X\}\). Incumbent objective evidence consists of \(\bar x\), the objective specification, and a reproducible evaluation \[U=f(\bar x).\] Feasibility of \(\bar x\) implies \[z^*\le f(\bar x)=U,\] so \(U\) is a valid primal upper bound. If objective evaluation is approximate, the certificate must provide a rigorously outward-rounded upper value \(U\ge f(\bar x)\); an unqualified floating-point value alone need not certify the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluating the objective at a verified feasible incumbent gives a primal upper bound; approximate evaluation requires a certified outward-rounded value.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Objective Evidence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Incumbent Evidence Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements across incumbent records and reported status.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
A stored incumbent point \(\bar x\), stored objective value \(U\), and declared feasibility and objective-evaluation conventions are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent evidence is consistent exactly when \(\bar x\) passes the declared feasibility checks and the stored \(U\) agrees with a certified evaluation of \(f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-check between incumbent feasibility and its reported objective bound.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Incumbent evidence \((\bar x,U)\) is consistent when two independently checkable requirements hold: \(\bar x\) satisfies every declared primal-feasibility and integrality predicate, and the stored value \(U\) satisfies \(U=f(\bar x)\) under exact evaluation or is a certified upper enclosure of \(f(\bar x)\) under approximate evaluation. The evidence is inconsistent if the stored point fails feasibility, if the objective value belongs to a different point or objective version, or if rounding can make \(U<f(\bar x)\). Only consistent evidence supplies a valid incumbent upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incumbent evidence is consistent when the stored point is verifiably feasible and its stored objective value is the correct certified evaluation for that same point.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Evidence Consistency

children.title: Subtree-Closure Evidence
children.top_down_role: Certificate material associated with pruned regions.

assumptions_latex: A minimization branch-and-bound tree partitions the original feasible candidates among node regions.
Each closed node has checkable evidence of infeasibility, dominance by the incumbent, or exact resolution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Closure evidence certifies that no feasible point in the closed subtree can improve the incumbent.

notation.meaning: feasible candidates contained in the subtree rooted at node v
valid lower bound for the subtree

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local certificates justifying closure of branch-and-bound subtrees.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a node \(v\) with subtree candidate set \(X_v\), valid closure evidence establishes at least one of the following: \(X_v=\varnothing\); a certified lower bound satisfies \(L_v\le\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)\) and \(L_v\ge U\); or the subtree has been exactly resolved and its best feasible value is at least \(U\). In every case, \[
\inf_{x\in X_v}f(x)\ge U,\] with the infimum interpreted as \(+\infty\) when \(X_v=\varnothing\). Hence no feasible point in the closed subtree can strictly improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subtree may be closed when verifiable infeasibility, a bound dominated by the incumbent, or exact resolution proves that the region cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Subtree-Closure Evidence

children.title: Global-Bound Evidence
children.top_down_role: Certificate material aggregating bounds across unresolved regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Bound Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of valid active-node lower bounds with the incumbent bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a valid incumbent upper bound, with \(U=+\infty\) when no incumbent exists. Suppose the finite active frontier \(\mathcal F\) covers every unresolved feasible candidate, each active node \(v\in\mathcal F\) has a valid lower bound \(L_v\), and every closed region has valid evidence that it contains no feasible point with objective below \(U\). Define \[B=\min\left\{U,\min_{v\in\mathcal F}L_v\right\},\] using \(\min_{v\in\varnothing}L_v=+\infty\). Then \(B\le z^*\le U\) in the extended-real sense. In particular, an empty frontier gives \(B=U\): a finite \(U\) certifies optimality, whereas \(U=+\infty\) certifies infeasibility under the stated coverage and closure assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid global lower bound is the minimum of the incumbent upper bound and all active-node lower bounds. With an empty frontier it equals the incumbent value, or positive infinity when no feasible incumbent exists and all regions have been validly closed.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with optimal value \(z^*\).
A valid incumbent upper bound \(U\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is available, with \(U=+\infty\) when no incumbent exists.
The finite active frontier \(\mathcal F\) covers every unresolved feasible candidate, and each \(v\in\mathcal F\) has a valid lower bound \(L_v\).
Every closed region has valid evidence excluding feasible objective values below \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate \(B=\min\{U,\min_{v\in\mathcal F}L_v\}\) is a valid global lower bound, using \(\min_{v\in\varnothing}L_v=+\infty\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound at active node v
valid incumbent upper bound, or positive infinity when absent
optimal objective value in the extended-real sense

children.title: Partition-Coverage Evidence
children.top_down_role: Certificate material connecting the search tree to the original region.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Coverage Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate that branching descendants collectively retain every point of the parent search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the root region be \(R_0\), and let every internal node \(v\) have region \(R_v\) and children \(C(v)\). Partition-coverage evidence consists of checkable branching records satisfying \[R_v=\bigcup_{w\in C(v)}R_w\] for every internal node. Disjointness is optional. If \(L\) is the set of leaves of the finite recorded tree, recursive substitution gives \[R_0=\bigcup_{\ell\in L}R_\ell.\] Thus every point of the original search region occurs in at least one terminal region and can be accounted for by its terminal certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified parent-to-child union identities certify that the recorded leaves cover the entire original search region, even when child regions overlap.
assumptions_latex: \(R_0\) and every \(R_v\) are explicitly represented sets.
The recorded tree is finite and every nonleaf has a complete child list.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_0=\bigcup_{\ell\in L}R_\ell\).

notation.meaning: search region associated with node v

source_refs.locator: 1.2.1 The Branch-and-Bound Method p. 6

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.1 The Branch-and-Bound Method p. 6

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution-relative coverage certificate when child regions need not reproduce the entire parent region exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the original feasible set, let a finite rooted tree associate a region \(R_v\) with each node, and define \(S_v=X\cap R_v\). If every internal node satisfies \[S_v\subseteq\bigcup_{w\in C(v)}S_w,\] then, for the leaf set \(L\), \[X\cap R_0=S_0\subseteq\bigcup_{\ell\in L}S_\ell.\] Thus every feasible root candidate reaches at least one recorded leaf. Equality of the raw regions, pairwise disjointness, and coverage of infeasible points are unnecessary for feasible-solution coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: It suffices that every feasible parent point occurs in some child; exact equality or disjointness of raw regions is unnecessary for feasible-solution coverage.
assumptions_latex: The recorded rooted tree is finite and has a complete child list at every internal node.
\(S_v=X\cap R_v\) denotes the feasible candidates represented at node \(v\).
Every internal node satisfies \(S_v\subseteq\bigcup_{w\in C(v)}S_w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\cap R_0\subseteq\bigcup_{\ell\in L}(X\cap R_\ell).

notation.meaning: feasible candidates represented at node v
leaf set of the recorded tree

children.title: Infeasibility Proof-Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Tree-based infeasibility evidence and independently checkable search records.

children.title: Local Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility evidence attached to terminal regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract, certificate-system-independent definition for an infeasibility witness attached to one terminal node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_v\) be the feasible set defined by the original constraints, branch restrictions, and node-valid local constraints at terminal node \(v\). A local infeasibility certificate is finite witness data \(w_v\) for which the declared sound verification rules establish \(F_v=\varnothing\). Its conclusion is regional: without separate exhaustive coverage evidence, it proves neither root infeasibility nor infeasibility of any other node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local infeasibility certificate is finite checkable evidence that one terminal node is empty; global infeasibility additionally requires coverage and aggregation.
assumptions_latex: The verified constraints are exactly those defining \(F_v\).
The witness is checked under sound declared arithmetic and inference semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{VerifyLocal}(I,v,w_v)=\mathrm{ACCEPT}\Longrightarrow F_v=\varnothing.
review_flags: Verifier mechanics were minimized because independent replay belongs to the proof-checking sibling.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Infeasibility Certificate
Local Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-type certificate for infeasibility of a linear terminal-node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the terminal region at node \(v\) is contained in \(P_v=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_vx\le b_v\}\). A local infeasibility certificate is a vector \(y_v\) satisfying \[y_v\ge0,\qquad y_v^{\mathsf T}A_v=0,\qquad y_v^{\mathsf T}b_v<0.\] Multiplying any hypothetical system \(A_vx\le b_v\) by \(y_v\) would require \(0\le y_v^{\mathsf T}b_v<0\). Hence \(P_v=\varnothing\), so the terminal region contains no feasible continuous, integer, or mixed-integer point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative Farkas multiplier producing a strict contradiction certifies that a terminal node's linear relaxation, and therefore its feasible region, is empty.
assumptions_latex: All node constraints, including branching restrictions, are included in \(A_vx\le b_v\).
The certificate inequalities are checked under sound arithmetic semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_v=\varnothing\), and consequently the terminal node is infeasible.

notation.meaning: linear relaxation of terminal node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Farkas certificate is mathematically correct for the stated inequality convention and fits the container, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Search-Tree Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Tree-wide aggregation of local infeasibility and partition evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite tree certificate aggregating complete branching coverage with certified infeasible leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite rooted search tree associate region \(R_v\) with each node \(v\). Assume every internal node satisfies the certified coverage identity \(R_v=\bigcup_{w\in C(v)}R_w\), and every leaf \(\ell\) carries a locally checkable certificate that \(R_\ell\cap F=\varnothing\), where \(F\) is the original feasible set. Then \[R_0\cap F=\bigcup_{\ell\in L}(R_\ell\cap F)=\varnothing.\] The tree, its branching records, and its leaf certificates therefore constitute a search-tree infeasibility certificate for the original instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete branching coverage plus a valid infeasibility certificate at every leaf certifies infeasibility of the original problem.
assumptions_latex: The recorded tree is finite.
Every internal-node coverage identity and every leaf certificate is independently valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_0\cap F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the original instance
region represented by tree node v

children.title: Proof-Logging Verification Interface
children.top_down_role: Machine-checkable representations of search and pruning evidence.

children.title: Proof-Log Representation
children.top_down_role: Machine-readable organization of search and pruning evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dependency-DAG Representation of a Proof Log
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph representation equivalent to an antecedent-complete sequential proof log.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finitely many typed records, create an edge \(r_j\to r_i\) whenever \(r_i\) cites \(r_j\) as an antecedent. If every actual dependency is cited, every cited antecedent exists and is regionally applicable, the graph is acyclic, and unrelated records have order-independent semantics, then every topological ordering yields a valid sequential log. Conversely, every valid antecedent-complete sequential log induces such an acyclic dependency graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An antecedent-complete proof log can be represented as an acyclic dependency graph, with topological orders giving equivalent valid sequences.
assumptions_latex: The record set is finite.
Every actual inference dependency is explicitly cited.
Unrelated records have order-independent semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{antecedent-complete dependency DAG}\Longleftrightarrow\text{valid topologically ordered sequential form}.
review_flags: Equivalence requires disclosure of all semantic dependencies, not merely the antecedents recorded by an untrusted producer.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-DAG Representation of a Proof Log
Proof-Log Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential representation of branching, derivation, and terminal-closure evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proof log is a finite sequence \(\Pi=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\) interpreted against an instance \(I\). Each record is typed as node creation, branching, valid-bound derivation, incumbent insertion, infeasibility derivation, or node closure, and contains identifiers for all antecedent records. Starting from the root region, a checker deterministically applies each record's specified inference rule to a state \(S_{i-1}\), producing \(S_i\) only when its syntax, antecedents, arithmetic, and regional applicability are valid. The representation is complete for a claimed conclusion when \(S_m\) contains that conclusion and no uncovered open node remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof log is an ordered, typed, antecedent-linked sequence whose deterministic replay derives the claim and closes every relevant search region.
assumptions_latex: The instance encoding and inference-rule semantics are fixed independently of the producer.
Every record names its rule, operands, antecedents, and affected node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi\) represents a checkable certificate exactly when deterministic replay reaches an accepting terminal state \(S_m\).

notation.meaning: typed proof record at position i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and local scope fit, but the proposed record types, replay semantics, and completeness condition depend on a particular proof-log standard for which no source is supplied.

children.title: Independent Certificate Checking
children.top_down_role: External validation of recorded search evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Soundness of Independent Proof Replay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness contract for an independent checker using fixed rules and terminal acceptance conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be an instance and \(\Pi\) a proof log. Assume every checker rule is sound under the declared arithmetic semantics, every node-creation rule preserves the required regional coverage invariant, and acceptance requires derivation of the claimed conclusion together with certified closure of every required region. Then \(\operatorname{Check}(I,\Pi)=\mathrm{ACCEPT}\) implies that the claimed conclusion is valid for \(I\). Organizational independence from the producer reduces common-mode implementation risk but does not replace rule soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceptance implies the logged conclusion only when every replay rule is sound, coverage is preserved, and the terminal acceptance invariant is satisfied.
assumptions_latex: Every supported inference rule is sound under the checker arithmetic semantics.
Node creation preserves the declared coverage invariant.
Acceptance requires the claim and certified closure of every required region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Check}(I,\Pi)=\mathrm{ACCEPT}\Longrightarrow I\models\operatorname{claim}(\Pi).
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Soundness of Independent Proof Replay
Independent Certificate Checking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic validation of a proof log without rerunning the certificate-producing solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an encoded instance \(I\), a proof log \(\Pi=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\), a fixed rule set \(\mathcal R\), and explicit arithmetic semantics. Initialize \(S_0\) with the root region and instance constraints. For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), parse \(r_i\), verify its antecedents in \(S_{i-1}\), check the indicated rule from \(\mathcal R\), and update the state; reject immediately if any check fails. Accept only if the final state contains the claimed conclusion, every created node has a valid parent, and every required search region is certified closed. Output ACCEPT or the first failing record.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replay each logged inference under fixed semantics, rejecting malformed or invalid steps and accepting only a fully covered, certified final state.
assumptions_latex: The checker implementation is independent of the certificate-producing solver.
The rule set and arithmetic semantics are part of the verification specification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Check}(I,\Pi,\mathcal R)=\mathrm{ACCEPT}\) only after every record and the terminal coverage condition pass.

notation.meaning: fixed set of admissible inference rules

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits independent certificate checking, but its acceptance conditions and claimed verification interface require a cited checker specification or authoritative proof-logging reference.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed format-relative accounting identity for sequential replay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For records \(r_1,\ldots,r_m\), if \(T_i\) denotes all work required to parse, locate antecedents, and validate \(r_i\), then sequential replay takes \(O(|I|+\sum_iT_i)\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replay time is the sum of the costs assigned to replaying its records.
assumptions_latex: Every lookup and arithmetic operation is already included in \(T_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{check}}=O\!\left(|I|+\sum_iT_i\right).

notation.meaning: total cost assigned to parsing and checking record \(i\)

review_flags: A meaningful asymptotic bound requires a fixed proof format, arithmetic cost model, and rule complexities.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Proof-Replay Cost

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is deterministic independent replay from the deferred seed and its conditional soundness contract. The proposed generic complexity formula was deferred because it merely sums undefined per-record costs. Log syntax belongs to Proof-Log Representation, while unsupported operations and semantic gaps belong to Proof-Logging Coverage Boundaries.

children.title: Proof-Logging Coverage Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Search events or solver operations that may lack complete logged evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A checked proof log certifies only the exact instance and semantic environment to which it is bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Pi\) is accepted for encoded instance \(I\), acceptance does not certify a different encoding \(I'\). Reuse is sound only if the checker verifies canonical identity \(I'=I\), or verifies a sound transformation certificate transporting every required logged assertion and the final conclusion from \(I\) to \(I'\). Instance binding includes objective sense, coefficients, variable domains, tolerances, and arithmetic semantics referenced by the log.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof log is bound to its exact encoded instance and semantics; a modified instance requires verified identity or a sound transport certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) was checked against encoded instance \(I\).
The claimed conclusion concerns encoded instance \(I'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Check}(I,\Pi)=\mathrm{ACCEPT}\not\Longrightarrow I'\models\operatorname{claim}(\Pi)\text{ without verified identity or sound transport}.

notation.meaning: instance against which the log was checked
instance for which the conclusion is claimed

knowledge_statements.title: Instance-Binding Boundary for Proof Logs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonessential Unlogged Computation Does Not Limit Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes harmless unlogged activity from an omitted premise needed by the accepted derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Unlogged heuristics, experiments, or redundant transformations do not compromise certification when the accepted conclusion has a complete supported derivation independent of their outputs. If an unlogged computation instead supplies a necessary premise for a retained bound, node closure, transformation, or final conclusion, the log is incomplete unless that premise is replaced by a supported derivation or separately checkable witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unlogged work is harmless when the checked derivation does not depend on it; omitting a necessary premise creates a coverage failure.
assumptions_latex: Acceptance is derived solely from recorded or separately verified premises.
Dependencies are interpreted according to the declared proof rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A necessary unlogged premise without a supported replacement prevents complete certification}.
review_flags: The builder's biconditional was weakened to the sound one-way failure criterion.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonessential Unlogged Computation Does Not Limit Certification
Proof-Logging Coverage Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of conclusions justified by a checker’s rule set and arithmetic semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) be the inference rules implemented by a checker. Acceptance of a log certifies only conclusions obtained by sound applications of rules in \(\mathcal R\) under the specified arithmetic semantics. A node closure based solely on an unsupported heuristic, an unlogged presolve transformation, an unverified nonlinear oracle, or a floating-point comparison lacking a certified error enclosure lies outside this coverage. Such a step cannot support the final conclusion unless it is translated into supported records or accompanied by a separately checkable witness whose soundness bridges the omitted computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof log certifies only supported, replayed inferences; opaque heuristics, omitted transformations, and uncertified numerical comparisons remain outside its guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The checker accepts only records belonging to its declared rule set \(\mathcal R\).
Soundness is interpreted under the declared arithmetic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unsupported or semantically unchecked closures do not imply a certified global conclusion.

notation.meaning: inference rules supported by the checker

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate, but the asserted treatment of presolve, nonlinear oracles, heuristics, and floating-point steps depends on the checker formalism and lacks supporting evidence.

children.title: Finite Discrete-Search Termination
children.top_down_role: Finite-termination families for discrete search spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Discrete-Search Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of exhaustive branching over a finite discrete domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization over a finite discrete domain \(D\). Suppose each open node represents a subset of \(D\); branching replaces it by finitely many children whose union equals the parent; every nonterminal branch strictly reduces the represented subset; and no identical region is generated twice. If each iteration processes one open node by fathoming it with a valid certificate or branching it, then only finitely many distinct nonempty node regions can be generated. Consequently the open list becomes empty after finitely many iterations. With valid bound and feasibility tests, the final incumbent is globally optimal, or absence of an incumbent certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive, nonrepeating strict branching over a finite domain terminates finitely and returns an optimum or an infeasibility conclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite.
Branching is coverage-preserving and strictly reduces every nonterminal node region.
All fathoming tests are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search terminates after finitely many node operations with a globally valid resolution.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case node-operation bound when nodes are identified by distinct nonempty subsets of a finite discrete domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(|D|=m<\infty\). If every generated nonempty node region is a subset of \(D\), no identical region is generated twice, and each iteration permanently processes one open region, then at most \(2^m-1\) nonempty node regions and at most \(2^m-1\) node-processing iterations occur. If every child on a root-to-leaf chain is a strict subset of its parent, that chain has at most \(m\) nonempty regions and at most \(m-1\) branching edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonrepeating search over subsets of an m-element domain processes at most 2^m−1 nonempty regions, while strict inclusion limits branch depth to m−1.
assumptions_latex: \(|D|=m<\infty\).
Every generated nonempty region is a subset of \(D\), and no region is generated twice.
Every child on a root-to-leaf chain is a strict subset of its parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{regions}}\le2^m-1,\qquad \operatorname{depth}\le m-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Region-Count Bound

children.title: Consistent-Bound Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence families based on compatible bounding and refinement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global convergence when accurate bounds are not coupled to feasible incumbent generation at every globally competitive frontier node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\), \(f(0)=0\), and \(f(1)=1\). Store the feasible incumbent \(1\), so \(U_k=1\), and leave the node \(\{0\}\) perpetually active with the exact valid lower bound \(L=0\). Refinement and bound accuracy on any other processed nodes cannot change \(B_k=0\). Thus \(U_k-B_k=1\) for every \(k\), even though the competitive node's lower bound is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact local lower bounds do not force convergence if a globally competitive node is never used to generate or certify a matching feasible value.
assumptions_latex: The node containing the optimizer may remain active indefinitely.
No feasible value from that node is incorporated into the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_k=0,\quad U_k=1,\quad U_k-B_k=1\text{ for all }k.
knowledge_statements.title: Unprocessed Competitive-Node Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient convergence condition coupling the globally least active lower bound to feasible incumbent generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iteration \(k\), let \(U_k\) be a finite feasible incumbent value and let \(B_k=\min\{U_k,\min_{v\in\mathcal F_k}L_{k,v}\}\), where the finite active frontier \(\mathcal F_k\) covers every unresolved feasible candidate and every \(L_{k,v}\) is a valid regional lower bound. Suppose that whenever \(B_k<U_k\), a node \(v_k\in\mathcal F_k\) attaining \(B_k=L_{k,v_k}\) has a feasible point \(y_k\) whose value has been incorporated into the incumbent and satisfies \[U_k\le f(y_k)\le L_{k,v_k}+\varepsilon_k,\qquad \varepsilon_k\downarrow0.\] Then \[0\le U_k-B_k\le\varepsilon_k,\qquad U_k-B_k\to0.\] If \(f^*\) is finite, frontier coverage and bound validity give \(B_k\le f^*\le U_k\), hence \(B_k\to f^*\) and \(U_k\to f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a feasible value within vanishing error of the least active lower bound is incorporated into the incumbent, the global gap vanishes and both bounds converge to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The active frontier is finite and covers every unresolved feasible candidate.
Every active-node lower bound is valid, and \(U_k\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
A feasible value within \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) of a node attaining the least active bound is incorporated into \(U_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_k-B_k\to0;\text{ if }f^*\in\mathbb R,\text{ then }B_k,U_k\to f^*.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for active node v

knowledge_statements.title: Frontier-Minimum Consistency Convergence
Consistent-Bound Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence from valid bounds, exhaustive refinement, and vanishing local bound error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with finite optimum \(f^*\), let \(U_k\) be the best feasible objective value found by iteration \(k\), and let \(B_k\) be the least lower bound among open regions. Assume all lower bounds are valid, so \(B_k\le f^*\le U_k\); every region capable of containing an optimizer is eventually processed or refined; and along every infinite refinement chain relevant to an optimizer, the local feasible upper value minus the regional lower bound tends to zero. Then \[U_k-B_k\longrightarrow0,\qquad U_k\longrightarrow f^*,\qquad B_k\longrightarrow f^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid bounds, exhaustive refinement, and vanishing local bound error force both incumbent and global lower bound to converge to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The optimum \(f^*\) is finite and attained.
Regional lower bounds are valid and the node-selection policy is exhaustive.
Relevant infinite refinement chains have vanishing local bound error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-B_k\to0\) and \(U_k,B_k\to f^*\).

children.title: Spatial-Subdivision Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence families for recursively refined continuous regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of spatial convergence when an optimizer-containing frontier region remains at positive diameter and is never resolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\) and \(f(x)=x\). Start with incumbent \(U_0=1\), retain \([0,\tfrac12]\) forever with its exact lower bound \(0\), and recursively subdivide only \([\tfrac12,1]\). Even if all processed regions have exact bounds and yield feasible values approaching \(\tfrac12\), the retained competitive region has diameter \(\tfrac12\), the global lower bound remains \(B_k=0\), and the incumbent need not fall below \(\tfrac12\). Hence the global gap need not vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking only noncompetitive regions does not ensure convergence when an optimizer-containing region remains unresolved at positive diameter.
assumptions_latex: Subdivision preserves coverage but does not have vanishing mesh.
The unresolved optimizer-containing region need not generate a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_k=0\text{ while }U_k\ge\tfrac12\text{ may hold for all }k.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonshrinking Competitive-Region Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence under vanishing frontier mesh and uniform regional lower- and upper-approximation errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and let each finite frontier \(\mathcal F_k\) consist of compact regions covering \(X\). For every region meeting \(X\), define \(\phi(R)=\min_{x\in X\cap R}f(x)\). Suppose \[\delta_k:=\max_{R\in\mathcal F_k}\operatorname{diam}(R)\to0,\] every regional lower bound satisfies \(0\le\phi(R)-L_k(R)\le\alpha_k\), and each such region supplies a feasible point \(y_{k,R}\in X\cap R\) satisfying \(f(y_{k,R})-\phi(R)\le\beta_k\), where \(\alpha_k,\beta_k\to0\). Let \(B_k=\min_{R\in\mathcal F_k}L_k(R)\), and let the incumbent satisfy \(U_k\le\min_{R\in\mathcal F_k}f(y_{k,R})\). Then \[0\le U_k-B_k\le\alpha_k+\beta_k,\] so \(B_k,U_k\to f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). A sufficient geometric realization is uniform consistency with \(\alpha_k,\beta_k\) bounded by moduli tending to zero with \(\delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage-preserving frontiers with vanishing mesh and uniformly consistent regional lower and feasible upper values force both global bounds to converge to the minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and \(f\) is continuous.
Finite compact frontiers cover \(X\) and have maximum diameter tending to zero.
Regional lower-bound and feasible-value errors are uniformly bounded by \(\alpha_k\to0\) and \(\beta_k\to0\).
All supplied feasible values are incorporated into the incumbent comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le U_k-B_k\le\alpha_k+\beta_k\to0,\qquad B_k,U_k\to f^*.

notation.meaning: minimum over the feasible part of region R

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of exhaustive branch-and-bound over shrinking compact continuous regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact and let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. Suppose branching produces coverage-preserving compact subregions, every infinite nested chain \(R_1\supset R_2\supset\cdots\) has \(\operatorname{diam}(R_j)\to0\), and each regional lower bound \(L(R)\) is valid and consistent in the sense that \(\inf_{x\in R}f(x)-L(R)\to0\) whenever \(\operatorname{diam}(R)\to0\). If node selection is exhaustive and feasible upper bounds are generated consistently on relevant chains, then the global lower and upper bounds converge to \(f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain, exhaustive shrinking subdivision with consistent regional bounds makes global upper and lower bounds converge to the minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and \(f\) is continuous.
Subdivision preserves coverage and nested infinite chains have vanishing diameter.
Lower and feasible upper bounds are consistent, with exhaustive node selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global bound gap tends to zero and both bounds converge to \(f^*\).

children.title: Asymptotic Convergence Without Finite Resolution
children.top_down_role: Continuous-search regimes lacking exact finite closure.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Convergence Without Finite Resolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality obtained only as the limit of successively tighter certified gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*\in\mathbb R\) be the optimal value of a minimization problem. For each \(k\), let \(B_k\) be a certified global lower bound and let \(U_k\) be the objective value of a feasible incumbent, so that \(B_k\le f^*\le U_k\). If \(U_k-B_k\to0\), then \[\lim_{k\to\infty}U_k=\lim_{k\to\infty}B_k=f^*.\] For every \(\varepsilon>0\), some finite iteration has \(U_k-f^*\le\varepsilon\). If \(U_k>B_k\) at every finite iteration and no separate finite exact-optimality certificate is produced, then these iterations provide no finite zero-gap resolution; exact resolution is obtained only in the limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing gap between certified lower bounds and feasible-incumbent values yields convergence and finite epsilon-optimality, while strict positive gaps and the absence of another exact certificate leave exact resolution asymptotic.
assumptions_latex: \(f^*\in\mathbb R\) is the optimal value.
\(B_k\le f^*\le U_k\) for every \(k\), with \(U_k\) attained by a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k,B_k\to f^*\); if every finite gap is positive and no separate exact certificate exists, finite exact resolution does not occur.

notation.meaning: objective value of a feasible incumbent at iteration k
certified global lower bound at iteration k

children.title: Incomplete Partition Coverage

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted Validity Under Incomplete Leaf Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical scope of terminal evidence when recorded terminal regions do not cover the root region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be the root region and \(C=\bigcup_{\ell\in L}R_\ell\) the union of all recorded terminal regions. If \(C\subsetneq R\), certificates attached only to the \(R_\ell\) establish conclusions only on \(C\). They imply root infeasibility only if \(R\setminus C\) is separately certified infeasible, and certify global optimality of an incumbent \(\bar x\) only if \(R\setminus C\) is separately certified to contain no point improving \(f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificates on incompletely covering leaves apply only to their union; the omitted region requires separate evidence before any global conclusion follows.
assumptions_latex: \(R_\ell\subseteq R\) are all recorded terminal regions.
Every local certificate is valid on its stated region.
\(C=\bigcup_{\ell\in L}R_\ell\subsetneq R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Terminal evidence over \(C\) alone does not certify the corresponding conclusion over \(R\).

notation.meaning: recorded terminal region indexed by leaf \(\ell\)

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Validity Under Incomplete Leaf Coverage
Incomplete Partition Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Omitted search regions invalidate global conclusions despite valid certificates on recorded leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{-x:x\in[0,1]\}\). Suppose a recorded search tree retains only the child region \(R_1=[0,1/2]\), omitting \((1/2,1]\), and completely verifies the restricted optimum \(-1/2\) on \(R_1\). Every local calculation on the recorded region may be correct, but the root coverage identity fails because \([0,1]\ne R_1\). The true optimum is \(-1\), attained at \(x=1\) in the omitted region. Therefore terminal certificates over an incompletely covering leaf family cannot certify a global bound, global optimality, or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimizing minus x on [0,1], certifying only [0,1/2] misses the true optimizer and invalidates any global conclusion.
assumptions_latex: The claimed root region is \([0,1]\).
The log contains no certified child covering \((1/2,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Correct local certificates on \(R_1\) do not certify the problem over \([0,1]\).

children.title: Unsafe or Missing Pruning Evidence
children.top_down_role: Closed nodes lacking adequate certification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for closing a minimization node without evidence that it cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_v\) be a node region and \(U\) the value of a verified feasible incumbent. Closure of \(R_v\) is certified only if checkable evidence establishes that \(R_v\) is infeasible, that a valid regional lower bound \(L_v\le\inf\{f(x):x\in R_v\cap F\}\) satisfies \(L_v\ge U\), or that exact regional resolution finds no solution improving \(U\). A closure assertion lacking all such evidence leaves \(R_v\) unresolved and cannot support a completed-tree certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node closed without checkable infeasibility, bound-dominance, or exact-resolution evidence remains uncertified.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\).
The incumbent defining \(U\) is verified feasible.
Comparisons use the semantics claimed by the final certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No valid closure witness for }R_v\Longrightarrow R_v\text{ remains uncertified}.
review_flags: Recast negatively to avoid duplicating the positive subtree-closure topic.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary for Certified Node Closure
Unsafe or Missing Pruning Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A closed node without valid pruning evidence can contain a better feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{-x:x\in\{0,1\}\}\). Let the incumbent be \(x=0\) with value \(0\). If the node \(R=\{1\}\) is closed using an asserted lower bound \(L(R)=1\), then the usual minimization pruning comparison would declare that region unable to improve the incumbent. The assertion is false because \(\inf_{x\in R}(-x)=-1<1\); indeed \(x=1\) is the global optimizer. Thus a closure record lacking a valid, checkable bound or infeasibility witness can discard the optimizer, and the resulting completed tree is not an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invalid bound can prune the node containing the optimizer, so an otherwise complete tree cannot certify optimality.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized over \(\{0,1\}\).
The closure of \(R\) has no valid supporting certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pruning step is unsound and the reported incumbent \(x=0\) is not certified optimal.

children.title: Tolerance–Certificate Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between computational tolerances and certification claims.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance–Certificate Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-gap certification for minimization under bounded numerical errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat U\in[U-\delta_U,U+\delta_U]\) be the exact objective value of the reported incumbent and let \(\widehat L\in[L-\delta_L,L+\delta_L]\) be a valid exact lower bound satisfying \(\widehat L\le z^*\). Then \(\widehat U-z^*\le \widehat U-\widehat L\le U-L+\delta_U+\delta_L\). Consequently, \(U-L+\delta_U+\delta_L\le\varepsilon\) is sufficient to certify \(\widehat U-z^*\le\varepsilon\). If only \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) is checked while \(U-L+\delta_U+\delta_L>\varepsilon\), the stated error bounds do not support the claimed certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After accounting for incumbent and lower-bound errors, the worst gap supported by the reported data is U−L+δU+δL. A stopping test using only the reported gap does not support the requested certificate when this adjusted gap exceeds the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with true optimum \(z^*\).
The exact incumbent objective value \(\widehat U\) lies in \([U-\delta_U,U+\delta_U]\).
A valid exact lower bound \(\widehat L\le z^*\) lies in \([L-\delta_L,L+\delta_L]\).
The claimed absolute optimality tolerance is \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated data certify \(\widehat U-z^*\le\varepsilon\) whenever \(U-L+\delta_U+\delta_L\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: exact objective value of the reported incumbent

The gap test certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality, but \(\bar x\) is not optimal because \(x=0\) has smaller value.

children.title: Size–Depth Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Relationships between broad tree growth and long search paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Size–Depth Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial size bounds under bounded integer branching arity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the size of a finite rooted tree whose maximum edge depth is \(D\) and whose nodes have at most \(b\) children, where \(b\in\{2,3,\ldots\}\). Then \[D+1\le S\le 1+b+\cdots+b^D=\frac{b^{D+1}-1}{b-1}.\] The lower bound is attained by a path and the upper bound by a full \(b\)-ary tree. Thus bounded depth permits size exponential in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integer branching-arity bound b, a rooted tree of maximum depth D has between D+1 nodes and the corresponding geometric-series number of nodes.
assumptions_latex: The finite rooted tree has maximum out-degree at most \(b\), where \(b\in\{2,3,\ldots\}\).
Its maximum edge depth is \(D\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Its size satisfies \(D+1\le S\le (b^{D+1}-1)/(b-1)\), and a full \(b\)-ary tree of depth \(D\) attains the upper bound.

notation.meaning: integer upper bound on the number of children per node

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp necessity of a branching-arity bound for controlling tree size by depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: No function of maximum depth alone bounds the size of finite rooted trees. For every \(N\ge1\), the rooted star with \(N\) children has maximum edge depth \(1\) and size \(N+1\). Hence the geometric size bound in terms of depth requires a finite uniform out-degree bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Depth alone cannot bound tree size: depth-one stars can contain arbitrarily many nodes, so the size–depth upper bound requires bounded branching arity.
assumptions_latex: Finite rooted trees may have arbitrarily large root out-degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(D=1\), tree size is unbounded; therefore no bound \(S\le f(D)\) holds without restricting branching arity.

notation.meaning: number of children of the root in the star tree

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An arithmetic-operation bound \(A(v)\) for processing node \(v\) is not by itself a Turing-time bound. If every operation acts on encodings of at most \(B(v)\) bits and costs at most \(q(B(v))\) bit operations, then \(C_{\mathrm{bit}}(v)\le A(v)q(B(v))\). Without a bound on operand growth or required precision, polynomial \(A(v)\) need not imply polynomial bit complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial node-level arithmetic count yields polynomial bit time only when intermediate encoding lengths and operation costs are also polynomially bounded.

\(A(v)\) bounds the number of arithmetic operations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a sequential additive-cost model, if \(V\) is the generated node set, \(C(v)\) is the processing cost charged to node \(v\), and \(C_0\) is all remaining initialization and finalization cost, then \[C_{\mathrm{tot}}=C_0+\sum_{v\in V}C(v)\le C_0+|V|C_{\max}.\] Consequently, a tree-size bound becomes a runtime bound only after controlling per-node cost.
