knowledge_statements.title: Structured Convex Solver Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies node relaxations by the preserved convex structure and corresponding exact convex solver class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the node relaxation be \(\inf\{f(x):x\in C\}\), where \(C\) is convex and \(f\) is convex. It is in the convex-quadratic regime when \(f\) is convex quadratic and \(C\) is described by affine and convex-quadratic constraints. It is in a conic regime when auxiliary variables give an equivalent formulation \(\inf\{c^Tz:Az=b,\ z\in K\}\) for a closed convex cone \(K\). In either regime, solving the structured formulation yields a valid lower bound for every feasible descendant whose domain is contained in the node domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex node relaxation may retain quadratic or conic structure; solving that structured convex problem gives a lower bound for every descendant subdomain.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every nonlinear constraint function are convex on the node domain.
The structured reformulation is equivalent to the node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N=\inf\{f(x):x\in C\}\leq \inf\{f(x):x\in F_D\}\) for every descendant feasible set \(F_D\subseteq C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Domain Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial branching of a bounded continuous box into exhaustive child regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a node box \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), choose an index \(j\) with \(\ell_j<u_j\), and choose \(s\in(\ell_j,u_j)\). Create \(B^- = B\cap\{x:x_j\leq s\}\) and \(B^+ = B\cap\{x:x_j\geq s\}\). Attach to each child a valid underestimating relaxation. Discard a child only when a sound infeasibility or bound-dominance certificate applies; otherwise retain it for further subdivision or processing until the prescribed algorithmic termination test is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split a continuous box along one coordinate, construct valid bounds for both exhaustive children, and retain each child unless a sound pruning certificate applies.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a bounded box.
Each child relaxation supplies a valid lower bound.
Every pruning test used by the algorithm is sound.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Underestimation Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex underestimators provide node lower bounds over continuous spatial subdomains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem \(v(B)=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap B\}\), replace each nonconvex objective or constraint function \(h\) by a convex underestimator \(\underline h_B\) satisfying \(\underline h_B(x)\leq h(x)\) for every \(x\in B\). Define \(R_B\) by imposing \(\underline h_B(x)\leq0\) in place of each constraint \(h(x)\leq0\), together with all retained convex constraints. Then \(F\cap B\subseteq R_B\), and \(L(B)=\inf_{x\in R_B}\underline f_B(x)\) is a valid node lower bound: \(L(B)\leq v(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing nonconvex functions by convex underestimators enlarges the feasible region and yields a valid lower bound on the node optimum.
assumptions_latex: Every underestimator is convex on \(B\) and never exceeds its original function there.
The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap B\subseteq R_B\) and \(L(B)\leq v(B)\).

An overestimator \(\overline h(x)\ge h(x)\) imposed as \(\overline h(x)\le0\) can remove feasible points: on \([-1,1]\), \(h(x)=x^2-1\le0\) is satisfied everywhere, whereas the overestimator \(\overline h(x)=1\) rejects every point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact leaf and depth counts for a prescribed coordinatewise midpoint-bisection schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_0=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) have widths \(w_i\), let \(\delta_i>0\), and set \(k_i=\max\{0,\lceil\log_2(w_i/\delta_i)\rceil\}\). If every root-to-leaf path bisects coordinate \(i\) exactly \(k_i\) times, every terminal width is at most \(\delta_i\), every path has depth \(D=\sum_i k_i\), and the complete binary partition has exactly \(2^D=\prod_i2^{k_i}\) leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed midpoint schedule reaches coordinate tolerances after the sum of the per-coordinate logarithmic depths and creates exponentially many leaves in that depth.
assumptions_latex: w_i=u_i-\ell_i\ge0.
\delta_i>0.
\text{The stated complete midpoint schedule is applied on every path.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D=\sum_i k_i,\qquad N_{\mathrm{leaf}}=2^D,\qquad \operatorname{width}_i(L)\le\delta_i.

notation.meaning: number of midpoint bisections scheduled for coordinate i
root-to-leaf depth under the fixed schedule

review_flags: This is an algorithm-specific attainable count, not a lower bound for every adaptive partition.
knowledge_statements.title: Midpoint-Bisection Resolution Count

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient geometric condition for resolution along an infinite branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_k\) be nested boxes along an infinite midpoint-bisection branch. If every coordinate having positive width is selected infinitely often unless its width has already converged to zero, then every coordinate width tends to zero, \(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0\), and \(\bigcap_kB_k\) is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair repeated midpoint bisection makes every infinite branch shrink to one point.
assumptions_latex: B_{k+1}\subseteq B_k.
\text{All selected-coordinate splits are midpoint bisections.}
\text{No persistently positive-width coordinate is selected only finitely often.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0,\qquad \left|\bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}B_k\right|=1.
review_flags: For arbitrary interior splits, fairness alone is insufficient without a uniform shrinkage condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Fair Midpoint-Bisection Diameter Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spatial Width Alone Does Not Certify Value Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary when no continuity modulus or relaxation-error estimate is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is no universal function of box diameter alone that bounds objective variation over all real-valued functions. On \([0,\delta]\), let \(f_M(0)=0\) and \(f_M(x)=M\) for \(x>0\). Its oscillation is \(M\) for every \(\delta>0\). Hence a width stopping rule gives no objective-gap certificate without regularity or a direct relaxation-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small boxes do not by themselves imply small objective error.
assumptions_latex: \delta>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{diam}([0,\delta])=\delta,\qquad \sup f_M-\inf f_M=M.
knowledge_statements.title: Spatial Width Alone Does Not Certify Value Accuracy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unfair Partitioning Can Leave Positive Width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of geometric resolution when an unresolved coordinate is never selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(B_0=[0,1]^2\), repeatedly bisect only the first coordinate and follow the child containing zero. Then \(B_k=[0,2^{-k}]\times[0,1]\), so the second-coordinate width and Euclidean diameter remain at least one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive local splits do not imply vanishing diameter when coordinate selection is unfair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{diam}(B_k)\ge1\quad\text{for every }k.
knowledge_statements.title: Unfair Partitioning Can Leave Positive Width

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of box diameter into objective-value accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on a nonempty compact box \(B\), then for any representative \(x_B\in B\), \(0\le f(x_B)-\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\le L\operatorname{diam}(B)\). Thus diameter at most \(\varepsilon/L\) is sufficient for \(\varepsilon\)-value resolution when \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A known Lipschitz constant converts spatial diameter into a certified objective-value tolerance.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is }L\text{-Lipschitz on }B.
B\text{ is nonempty and compact.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le f(x_B)-\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\le L\operatorname{diam}(B).
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Spatial-Value Resolution Bound
Spatial Resolution Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case box count required to reach a prescribed coordinatewise spatial resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_0=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), with widths \(w_i=u_i-\ell_i\), and require every terminal box to have each coordinate width at most \(\delta_i>0\). Any exhaustive axis-aligned partition may require \(\prod_{i=1}^n\lceil w_i/\delta_i\rceil\) terminal boxes, and a uniform grid attains this count. Under midpoint bisection, depth \(D=\sum_{i=1}^n\lceil\log_2(w_i/\delta_i)\rceil_+\) suffices along every root-to-leaf path when coordinates are bisected the indicated number of times; the full binary tree can therefore contain exponentially many leaves in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolving every coordinate to fixed width can require a product number of boxes, exposing the dimension-dependent worst-case cost of spatial search.
assumptions_latex: The initial domain is an axis-aligned bounded box.
Branching uses axis-aligned subdivisions and resolution is measured coordinatewise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{leaf}}\leq\prod_i\lceil w_i/\delta_i\rceil\) is attainable by a grid, while worst-case exhaustive resolution scales as that product.

notation.meaning: required terminal width in coordinate i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the exact covering and bisection formulas. The statement alternates between a required/worst-case box count and an attainable upper bound, while the conclusion writes an upper-bound inequality without defining whether the count is minimal, algorithm-specific, or arbitrary. An exact sourced formulation is required.

children.title: Discrete-Variable Branching
children.top_down_role: Partitioning driven by integral variable decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Variable Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive branching on an unfixed bounded integer variable in mixed-integer spatial search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with integer variable \(z_j\in\{L_j,\ldots,U_j\}\), choose an integer split index \(k\) with \(L_j\leq k<U_j\). Create children by adding respectively \(z_j\leq k\) and \(z_j\geq k+1\), inherit all other node restrictions, and compute a valid relaxation bound for each child. Prune a child only by certified infeasibility, integrality-compatible dominance, or comparison with the incumbent. Continue until every integer coordinate is fixed or integral in an accepted feasible solution, or every child is pruned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split an integer variable into two disjoint exhaustive ranges, bound each child, and continue until integrality is attained or all children are pruned.
assumptions_latex: \(z_j\) has finite integer bounds at the current node.
Each child bound is valid for its restricted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{L_j,\ldots,U_j\}=\{L_j,\ldots,k\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{k+1,\ldots,U_j\}\).

children.title: Continuous-Domain Subdivision
children.top_down_role: Spatial partitioning of nonconvex continuous regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Domain Subdivision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial subdivision of continuous coordinates within a mixed-integer node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a mixed-integer node with continuous box \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), choose \(j\) and \(s\in(\ell_j,u_j)\). Form two children by replacing \([\ell_j,u_j]\) with \([\ell_j,s]\) and \([s,u_j]\), respectively, while retaining all discrete restrictions. Recompute domain-dependent relaxations on each child. Process or prune each child using its valid lower bound, and repeat until its continuous widths meet the prescribed resolution or another valid pruning test applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subdivide a continuous coordinate while preserving discrete restrictions, then rebuild domain-dependent bounds on both exhaustive child boxes.
assumptions_latex: The continuous node domain is a bounded box.
Domain-dependent child relaxations provide valid lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two child domains cover the parent mixed-integer domain without changing its allowed discrete assignments.

notation.meaning: continuous box at the mixed-integer node

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exhaustive Splits Need Not Produce Vanishing Mesh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary separating exhaustive coverage from spatial refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(B^0=[0,1]^2\), repeatedly bisect only the first coordinate and follow either nested child. Every split is exhaustive, but the second-coordinate width remains one. Consequently, exhaustive subdivision alone does not imply \(\max_i\operatorname{wid}_i(B^k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly refining one coordinate leaves another width unchanged, so exhaustive coverage alone does not guarantee a vanishing mesh.
assumptions_latex: The branching rule may ignore a positive-width coordinate indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{wid}_2(B^k)=1\) for every \(k\), hence \(\max_i\operatorname{wid}_i(B^k)\not\to0\).

notation.meaning: box on the selected nested branch after k splits

knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive Splits Need Not Produce Vanishing Mesh

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Longest-Width Midpoint Subdivision Has Vanishing Mesh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolution guarantee for repeated continuous subdivision along an infinite nested branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B^0\supset B^1\supset\cdots\) be nested boxes in \(\mathbb R^n\). At iteration \(k\), bisect at its midpoint a coordinate of maximum width in \(B^k\), and let \(B^{k+1}\) be either child. Then \(\max_i\operatorname{wid}_i(B^k)\le 2^{-\lfloor k/n\rfloor}\max_i\operatorname{wid}_i(B^0)\), and therefore the maximum width tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Midpoint bisection of a widest coordinate drives every box width to zero along each infinite nested branch.
assumptions_latex: \(B^0\) is a bounded box in \(\mathbb R^n\).
Each split bisects a coordinate whose current width is maximal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i\operatorname{wid}_i(B^k)\le 2^{-\lfloor k/n\rfloor}\max_i\operatorname{wid}_i(B^0)\to0\).

notation.meaning: width of box B in coordinate i

knowledge_statements.title: Longest-Width Midpoint Subdivision Has Vanishing Mesh

children.title: Joint Subdivision Interaction
children.top_down_role: Coordination between discrete branching and continuous spatial partitioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Subdivision Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete and continuous branches jointly form exhaustive restrictions; nested child relaxations yield monotone node lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a mixed-integer node by \(N=(Z,B)\), where \(Z\) is its allowed discrete set and \(B\) its continuous box. If \(\{Z_a\}_a\) partitions \(Z\) and \(\{B_b\}_b\) covers \(B\), then applying both branching operations produces domains \(Z_a\times B_b\) whose union is \(Z\times B\), independently of operation order. For a minimization problem, let \(Q(N)\) and \(Q(N')\) be the parent and descendant relaxation feasible sets under a common objective. If \(Q(N')\subseteq Q(N)\), then their relaxation values satisfy \(L(N')\geq L(N)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete and spatial branching commute at the domain level and jointly cover the parent. A descendant lower bound cannot decrease when its relaxation feasible set is nested inside the parent's relaxation feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(\{Z_a\}_a\) is an exhaustive partition of \(Z\).
\(\{B_b\}_b\) is an exhaustive cover of \(B\).
For each descendant \(N'\), the relaxation uses the same minimization objective and satisfies \(Q(N')\subseteq Q(N)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcup_{a,b}(Z_a\times B_b)=Z\times B\), and relaxation nesting implies \(L(N')\geq L(N)\).

notation.meaning: relaxation feasible set at node N

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Domain Restriction Alone Does Not Ensure Bound Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for lower-bound monotonicity when descendant relaxations are rebuilt without nesting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization of \(x\) in variables \((x,y)\). Let the parent node domain contain \(0\le y\le1\), let its true feasible set and relaxation both be \(\{(0,0)\}\), and hence let \(L(N)=0\). A descendant may impose \(y\le1/2\) yet be assigned the valid but nonnested outer relaxation \(Q(N')=\{(x,0):-1\le x\le0\}\). Then \(L(N')=-1<L(N)\). Thus restriction of the node domain does not imply monotone relaxation values unless the relaxation sets are nested or the parent bound is inherited explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller descendant domain can receive a weaker nonnested relaxation and consequently a lower bound below its parent's bound.
assumptions_latex: Each relaxation need only contain the true feasible set of its own node.
The rebuilt descendant relaxation is not required to lie within the parent relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(N')\nsubseteq Q(N)\) can permit \(L(N')<L(N)\).

notation.meaning: relaxation optimum for the common minimization objective

children.title: Factorable Expression Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Spatial search organized through factorable nonlinear expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorable Expression Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reformulates a factorable nonlinear expression as an acyclic graph of elementary operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A factorable expression \(f(x)\), constructed by finitely composing constants, variables, sums, products, quotients on nonzero-denominator domains, and admitted univariate functions, can be represented by a directed acyclic graph. Introduce one variable \(w_v\) for each internal vertex \(v\) and one defining equality \(w_v=\phi_v(w_{p_1},\ldots,w_{p_r})\) for its elementary operation. The root variable equals \(f(x)\). Projecting the lifted equality system onto the original variables and root therefore reproduces exactly the graph \(\{(x,t):t=f(x)\}\) on the stated domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factorable expression can be lifted into an acyclic graph of elementary equalities whose projection exactly recovers the original expression graph.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has a finite factorable construction on the specified domain.
Every elementary operation is defined at each domain point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}\mathcal G=\{(x,t):t=f(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: auxiliary value at expression-graph vertex v

children.title: Expression-Graph Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxation structure organized over nonlinear expression graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Graph Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composes local convex graph relaxations into a global relaxation of a factorable expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a factorable expression graph have elementary equalities \(w_v=\phi_v(w_{p_1},\ldots,w_{p_r})\), with valid interval bounds on every operand. Replace each equality graph by a convex set \(R_v\) containing that graph over the operand bounds, and define \(R=\bigcap_v R_v\) together with the original variable bounds. Every exact evaluation of the expression graph belongs to \(R\); hence the projection of \(R\) onto the original variables and root value contains the graph of the original expression and is a valid convex relaxation when every \(R_v\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing each elementary expression node over valid intervals yields a lifted convex set containing every exact evaluation of the complete expression.
assumptions_latex: The expression graph is finite and acyclic.
Operand intervals are valid, and every \(R_v\) contains its exact elementary graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G\subseteq R\), so \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}R\supseteq\{(x,t):t=f(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: local relaxation of elementary vertex v

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local-Containment Certificate for an Assembled Graph Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient validity test for a lifted expression-graph relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every vertex \(v\), certify valid operand bounds and \(\mathcal G_v\subseteq R_v\), where \(\mathcal G_v\) is the exact elementary graph on those bounds. If auxiliary variables shared by incident vertices are identified consistently, every exact evaluation of the full acyclic graph belongs to \(\bigcap_vR_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid operand bounds, factor-graph containment, and consistent shared auxiliaries certify the assembled relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \text{The expression graph is finite and acyclic.}
\mathcal G_v\subseteq R_v\text{ on certified operand bounds for every }v.
\text{Shared auxiliary variables are represented consistently.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal G\subseteq\bigcap_vR_v.

notation.meaning: exact elementary graph at vertex v

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Containment Certificate for an Assembled Graph Relaxation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Factorwise Convexification Need Not Give the Global Graph Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit boundary between local and global ideality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(0\le x\le1\), decompose \(t=x^3\) as \(w=x^2\) and \(t=wx\). Use the exact convex hull \(x^2\le w\le x\) for the first graph and the McCormick hull for \(t=wx\) over \([0,1]^2\). The point \((x,w,t)=(1/2,1/2,0)\) satisfies both local hulls, but its projection \((1/2,0)\) is outside \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,x^3):0\le x\le1\}\), which satisfies \(t\ge x^3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even exact hulls for individual expression nodes can compose into a non-ideal relaxation of the whole expression.
assumptions_latex: 0\le x\le1.
w=x^2\text{ and }t=wx\text{ are relaxed separately using their graph hulls on the stated boxes.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_{x,t}(R_{x^2}\cap R_{wx})\supsetneq\operatorname{conv}\{(x,x^3):0\le x\le1\}.
review_flags: Equality can still hold for special graph structures or stronger formulations.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorwise Convexification Need Not Give the Global Graph Hull

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global effect of strengthening factor-level graph relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=\bigcap_vR_v\) and \(R'=\bigcap_vR'_v\) use the same lifted variables, bounds, and objective. If \(R'_v\subseteq R_v\) for every vertex, then \(R'\subseteq R\), so minimizing the common objective over \(R'\) gives a lower bound no smaller than minimizing it over \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightening every local graph relaxation can only strengthen the assembled minimization bound.
assumptions_latex: R'_v\subseteq R_v\text{ for every }v.
\text{Both assembled problems use the same lifted objective.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R'\subseteq R,\qquad \inf_{z\in R'}\psi(z)\ge\inf_{z\in R}\psi(z).
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Under Local Relaxation Tightening

children.title: Expression-Graph State Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of graph-based relaxation information across spatial subregions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe incremental update after a child-domain restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cache each vertex interval and local outer relaxation at the parent. After child branching changes input bounds in a set \(S\), mark \(S\) and every vertex reachable from \(S\). Reuse unmarked state, recompute marked intervals in topological order, and rebuild marked local relaxations when child-tight state is required. Parent outer relaxations may also be retained on a restricted child as valid but potentially weaker artifacts. Before bounding, verify cache identity, domain containment, and validity of every newly built artifact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse unaffected graph state and recompute the forward dependency cone; parent-valid outer relaxations remain safe on contained child domains but may be weaker.
assumptions_latex: \text{The expression graph is finite and acyclic.}
\text{Parent cache entries are valid on their recorded domains.}
\text{The child operand domains are contained in the recorded parent domains.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The assembled child relaxation contains every exact child evaluation.}

notation.meaning: vertices whose input bounds changed directly

review_flags: Recomputation of affected outer relaxations is required for child-tightness, not merely for validity when the child domain is contained in the cached domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-Cone State Reuse

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work bound for dependency marking and topological recomputation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With adjacency lists and a stored topological order, marking the forward dependency cone \(A(S)\) and rebuilding it takes \(O(|V_A|+|E_A|+\sum_{v\in V_A}T_v)\) time, where \(V_A=A(S)\), \(E_A\) contains the scanned affected edges, and \(T_v\) bounds reconstruction at vertex \(v\). Full recomputation is recovered when \(A(S)=V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental work scales with the affected dependency subgraph plus its vertex-rebuild costs.
assumptions_latex: \text{The DAG uses adjacency lists and has a stored topological order.}
T_v\text{ bounds interval and relaxation reconstruction at }v.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{update}}=O\!\left(|V_A|+|E_A|+\sum_{v\in V_A}T_v\right).

notation.meaning: affected vertices and scanned affected edges

knowledge_statements.title: Affected-Subgraph Update Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reuse Requires Domain and Artifact Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for cache reuse across spatial regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cached local relaxation valid on operand domain \(D\) is reusable on a new domain \(D'\) only when its validity covers \(D'\), for example when \(D'\subseteq D\). Without this condition, reuse can exclude exact evaluations: the secant inequality \(y\le x\), valid as an upper graph bound for \(y=x^2\) on \([0,1]\), is invalid on \([1,2]\) and rejects \((x,y)=(2,4)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cached graph artifacts cannot be transferred to an incompatible domain merely because they were valid where created.
assumptions_latex: \text{The cached artifact is domain dependent.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{valid}_{D}(R)\not\Longrightarrow\operatorname{valid}_{D'}(R)\quad\text{when }D'\nsubseteq D.

notation.meaning: recorded cache domain and proposed reuse domain

review_flags: For an ordinary child restriction D' subseteq D, an unchanged parent outer relaxation remains valid, although it may be weak.
knowledge_statements.title: Reuse Requires Domain and Artifact Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency condition guaranteeing identical deterministic vertex state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(S)\) be the vertices reachable from changed inputs \(S\). If \(v\notin A(S)\), none of \(v\)'s operand states depends on a changed input. Therefore any deterministic construction depending only on the operation and current operand states returns the same state at \(v\). Membership in \(A(S)\) does not prove that the state changed; it only identifies vertices that may require recomputation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Non-reachability from changed inputs guarantees exact cache reuse; reachability is a conservative affectedness test.
assumptions_latex: \text{Vertex state depends only on its operation and current operand states.}
\text{The graph and operation definitions are unchanged.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\notin A(S)\Longrightarrow\operatorname{state}_{child}(v)=\operatorname{state}_{parent}(v).

notation.meaning: forward dependency cone of changed inputs

review_flags: Non-reachability is sufficient, not necessary; an affected vertex may coincidentally retain identical state.
knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Unaffected-Vertex Reuse Criterion
Expression-Graph State Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safely reuses graph structure and unaffected relaxation data after spatial branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store the expression directed acyclic graph, vertex intervals \(I_v\), and local relaxations \(R_v(I_{p_1},\ldots,I_{p_r})\) at a parent node. After branching changes an input interval, mark that input and every reachable descendant vertex dirty. Copy all unmarked intervals and local relaxation descriptions unchanged; recompute marked intervals in topological order and rebuild each affected \(R_v\). Before using the child bound, verify that every copied or rebuilt interval contains all attainable child values and every local set contains its elementary graph. The resulting assembled child relaxation is then valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After branching, reuse unaffected expression-graph data and recompute only vertices downstream of changed inputs, while revalidating interval and relaxation containment.
assumptions_latex: The expression graph is finite and acyclic.
Cached intervals and relaxations were valid at the parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If all containment checks pass, the assembled child relaxation contains every exact child-domain graph evaluation.

children.title: Combinatorial Tree-Search Interface
children.top_down_role: Problem-specific partial-solution search linked to dedicated combinatorial optimization chapters.

children.title: Partial-Solution Search States
children.top_down_role: Problem-specific representations of incomplete combinatorial solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness failure caused by omitting completions during child generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C(S)\not\subseteq\bigcup_{S'\in\operatorname{ch}(S)}C(S')\), then a completion in the set difference disappears when \(S\) is replaced by its children. Even if every subsequent bound and pruning decision is valid, the resulting search need not find or certify the optimum when an optimal completion lies in that difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Child containment is insufficient: omitting part of the parent's completion set can lose the optimum even when all later pruning is sound.
assumptions_latex: State \(S\) is removed from the active search after its children are generated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C(S)\setminus\bigcup_{S'\in\operatorname{ch}(S)}C(S')\ne\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{search coverage may be lost}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonexhaustive State Expansion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Refinement and Exhaustive Expansion of Partial States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic contract connecting a combinatorial state to its child states and feasible completions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial state \(S\) represents a set \(C(S)\) of feasible full completions. A refinement \(S'\) preserves every decision fixed by \(S\) and adds restrictions, so \(C(S')\subseteq C(S)\). A child family \(\operatorname{ch}(S)\) is exhaustive when \[C(S)=\bigcup_{S'\in\operatorname{ch}(S)}C(S').\] The children may overlap unless disjoint branching is required. Consequently, replacing an unpruned state by an exhaustive child family preserves every completion represented by the parent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Children refine a partial state, and exhaustive children collectively preserve every feasible completion of their parent.
assumptions_latex: \(C(S)\) denotes the feasible full completions consistent with state \(S\).
Every child preserves the decisions already fixed by its parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall S'\in\operatorname{ch}(S),\ C(S')\subseteq C(S),\qquad C(S)=\bigcup_{S'\in\operatorname{ch}(S)}C(S').

notation.meaning: Feasible completion set represented by state S.

knowledge_statements.title: Refinement and Exhaustive Expansion of Partial States
Partial-Solution Search States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a combinatorial search node by a consistent partial assignment and its completions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\) be a finite product domain, and let \(F\subseteq X\) be the feasible set. A partial-solution search state is a pair \(S=(I,a_I)\), where \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(a_I\in\prod_{i\in I}D_i\). Its completion set is \(C(S)=\{x\in F:x_i=a_i\text{ for every }i\in I\}\). A child extends the assignment to a larger index set without altering previously assigned values. A state is terminal when \(I=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), or when a valid pruning certificate establishes \(C(S)=\varnothing\) or bound dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial-solution state fixes some discrete decisions and represents all feasible completions consistent with them; children extend those fixed decisions.
assumptions_latex: Each decision domain \(D_i\) is finite.
Partial assignments choose values from their corresponding domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(S'\) is a child of \(S\), then \(C(S')\subseteq C(S)\).

children.title: Combinatorial Bounding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Connections to problem-specific lower or upper bounding mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Bounding Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the validity contract for lower and upper bounds attached to combinatorial states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem and partial state \(S\) with completion set \(C(S)\), a bounding interface returns \((L(S),U(S),x^S)\). Validity requires \(L(S)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in C(S)\); if a feasible completion \(x^S\in C(S)\) is returned, then \(U(S)=f(x^S)\), and otherwise \(U(S)=+\infty\). Given a globally feasible incumbent of value \(\bar U\), the inequality \(L(S)\geq\bar U\) certifies that pruning \(S\) cannot remove a strictly improving completion; a certified empty completion set also permits pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state interface supplies a valid lower bound and optional feasible completion; comparison with the incumbent yields a directly checkable pruning certificate.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized over a finite combinatorial feasible set.
\(L(S)\) is valid for every feasible completion represented by \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(S)\geq\bar U\Rightarrow f(x)\geq\bar U\) for all \(x\in C(S)\).

notation.meaning: value of a returned feasible completion

children.title: Problem-Specific Pruning Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Connections to dedicated dominance and infeasibility tests.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract certificate needed to turn a problem-specific dominance relation into safe pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dominance certificate for state \(s\) identifies already preserved states or feasible completions \(D(s)\) such that for every \(x\in C(s)\) there exists \(y\in D(s)\) with \(f(y)\le f(x)\). If every \(y\in D(s)\) remains represented by the search or is a verified feasible incumbent, then discarding \(s\) cannot remove the unique opportunity to obtain a better objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dominance pruning is safe only when every completion of the discarded state has a no-worse representative that remains preserved elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized.
Every dominating representative remains searchable or is already recorded as feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall x\in C(s)\ \exists y\in D(s):f(y)\le f(x)\bigr)\Longrightarrow\inf_{y\in D(s)}f(y)\le\inf_{x\in C(s)}f(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance-Pruning Certificate Contract

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Soundness of a Problem-Specific Pruning Oracle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness contract for dominance, infeasibility, or other specialized pruning tests in minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C(s)\) be the feasible completions of state \(s\), let \(f:C(s)\to\mathbb R\) be the objective, and let \(U\) be a verified incumbent value. A pruning oracle \(P\) is sound when \[P(s,U)=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \{x\in C(s):f(x)<U\}=\varnothing.\] The implication may be certified by infeasibility, a valid lower bound, dominance, or another problem-specific argument. Returning zero on a safely prunable state only loses efficiency; returning one without the implication can discard a strictly improving completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A specialized oracle may prune only when it certifies that the state has no completion strictly better than the incumbent; missed pruning is safe, but false-positive pruning is not.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized.
\(U\) is the value of a verified feasible incumbent.
The search convention preserves ties and seeks completions with objective strictly less than \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P(s,U)=1\Longrightarrow\inf_{x\in C(s)}f(x)\ge U.

notation.meaning: Feasible completions represented by state s.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Soundness of a Problem-Specific Pruning Oracle

assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a set of partial search states for a minimization problem.
\(F(s)\) is the set of feasible completions of state \(s\), and \(U\) is the incumbent objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(s,U)=1\) certifies that state \(s\) may be discarded without removing any completion whose objective is less than \(U\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: abstract sound-pruning condition for combinatorial minimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness contract for a problem-specific pruning oracle in deterministic minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A problem-specific pruning interface is a predicate \(P:S\times\overline{\mathbb R}\to\{0,1\}\) satisfying \[P(s,U)=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \{x\in F(s):f(x)<U\}=\varnothing.\] It may establish this implication through infeasibility, a valid lower bound \(L(s)\ge U\), dominance, or another problem-specific certificate. The search algorithm may discard \(s\) only when the predicate returns one. Failure to recognize a prunable state affects efficiency but not correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pruning oracle may discard a partial state only when it certifies that no feasible completion can improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Specific Pruning Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sound-pruning condition fits the leaf and condition is the correct knowledge kind, but no inspectable citation is supplied and the objective function f is not introduced in the assumptions or notation.

children.title: Combinatorial Linkage Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Scope boundaries between generic tree search and specialized combinatorial machinery.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure of pruning when an auxiliary state model excludes a genuine completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the true completion set be \(F(s)=\{(0,1)\}\). If an auxiliary interface additionally imposes \(x_1=x_2\), then \(\widehat F(s)=\varnothing\) although \(F(s)\ne\varnothing\). Therefore an infeasibility certificate for \(\widehat F(s)\) cannot justify pruning state \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An auxiliary model can be infeasible merely because it incorrectly excludes a true completion, so its infeasibility certificate need not transfer.
assumptions_latex: The auxiliary equality \(x_1=x_2\) is not valid for every true completion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat F(s)=\varnothing\not\Rightarrow F(s)=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Spurious Auxiliary Infeasibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certificate Transfer Across Linked Completion Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary for transferring infeasibility and objective-bound conclusions from an auxiliary completion model to the true state model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(s)\) be the true completion set and \(\widehat F(s)\) an auxiliary completion set. An auxiliary infeasibility conclusion transfers whenever \(F(s)\subseteq\widehat F(s)\). For minimization, suppose the true objective is \(f\), the auxiliary objective is \(\widehat f\), and \(\widehat L(s)\le\widehat f(y)\) for every \(y\in\widehat F(s)\). Then \(\widehat L(s)\) is a valid true lower bound whenever \(F(s)\subseteq\widehat F(s)\) and \(\widehat f(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F(s)\). Without these linkage conditions, auxiliary pruning need not be sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary infeasibility and lower bounds may prune a true state only when set containment and, for objective bounds, objective compatibility make the certificate valid for every true completion.
assumptions_latex: \(F(s)\) and \(\widehat F(s)\) are completion sets expressed in a common space or connected by an explicit validity-preserving map.
The problem is minimized when an objective-bound certificate is transferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(s)\subseteq\widehat F(s),\quad \widehat f|_{F(s)}\le f|_{F(s)}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \widehat L(s)\le\inf_{x\in F(s)}f(x).

notation.meaning: True feasible completion set of state s.
Completion set used by the auxiliary interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Transfer Across Linked Completion Models

assumptions_latex: \(F(s)\) is the true completion set of state \(s\).
\(\widehat F(s)\) is the completion set used by an auxiliary combinatorial interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pruning transferred from the auxiliary interface is sound only when its certificate lifts to \(F(s)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certificate lifting is the basic soundness boundary between linked search models
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for transferring pruning conclusions between linked combinatorial state models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An auxiliary combinatorial pruning certificate may be used at state \(s\) only if it is valid for every point of the true completion set \(F(s)\). For an infeasibility or minimization lower-bound certificate computed on \(\widehat F(s)\), a sufficient linkage condition is \(F(s)\subseteq\widehat F(s)\). Without certificate lifting, pruning can be unsound. For example, with \(F(s)=\{(0,1)\}\), an auxiliary model that incorrectly adds \(x_1=x_2\) has \(\widehat F(s)=\varnothing\); its infeasibility certificate does not certify infeasibility of \(F(s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pruning result transfers between combinatorial models only when its certificate remains valid for every true completion.
knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Linkage Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary and counterexample fit the container. However, the lower-bound transfer claim requires the true and auxiliary models to use compatible objective functions, which are not specified, and no source supports the linkage criterion.

children.title: Search-Embedded Reduction Calculus
children.top_down_role: Global and node-local reduction mechanisms embedded in tree search.

children.title: Global Presolve Interface
children.top_down_role: Root-level reductions inherited by the search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Presolve Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving root reduction inherited by descendant search nodes, with explicit recovery and restriction transformation requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A global presolve interface returns a reduced problem \((F',f')\), a recovery map \(R:F'\to F\), and an offset \(\delta\in\mathbb R\) such that \[R(F')\subseteq F,\qquad f(R(y))=f'(y)+\delta\quad\text{for every }y\in F',\] and \[\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=\inf_{y\in F'}f'(y)+\delta.\] If the reduced problem has an optimizer \(y^*\), then \(R(y^*)\) is an optimizer of the original problem. A descendant node may be formulated over reduced variables only when each applicable original branching restriction is translated into a reduced restriction whose recovered points satisfy that original restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global presolve replaces the root problem by an equivalent reduced problem, recovers an original optimizer from any reduced optimizer, and requires sound translation of descendant branching restrictions.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the original feasible set with objective \(f\).
\(F'\) is the presolved feasible set with objective \(f'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(y^*\) minimizes \(f'\) over \(F'\), then \(R(y^*)\) minimizes \(f\) over \(F\); descendant restrictions require a sound reduced-space translation.

notation.meaning: Recovery mapping from presolved to original variables.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additional interface condition required when descendant search restrictions are represented in presolved variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every original-space restriction \(H\) generated by the search and its reduced-space translation \(H'\), sound descendant search requires \[R(F'\cap H')\subseteq F\cap H\] and restricted-value completeness \[\inf_{x\in F\cap H}f(x)=\inf_{y\in F'\cap H'}f'(y)+\delta.\] Consequently, any optimizer of the reduced restricted problem recovers to an optimizer of the corresponding original restricted problem. Merely ensuring that recovered reduced points satisfy \(H\) is insufficient: the translation may otherwise omit the best or every original completion compatible with \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve must preserve each generated descendant subproblem's optimum, not merely map retained reduced points into the original restriction.
assumptions_latex: \((F',f',R,\delta)\) satisfies the root presolve interface.
\(H\) is an original-space search restriction and \(H'\) is its reduced-space translation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(F'\cap H')\subseteq F\cap H\quad\text{and}\quad\inf_{F\cap H}f=\inf_{F'\cap H'}f'+\delta.

notation.meaning: Corresponding original-space and reduced-space descendant restrictions.
Recovery map from reduced to original variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Restriction-Aware Presolve Equivalence

children.title: Node Propagation Interface
children.top_down_role: Local reductions driven by node restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Propagation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound local product-domain contraction induced by a node's branching restrictions, without assuming finite convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node propagation interface supplies an operator \(P_s\) on admissible product domains satisfying \[F(s)\cap D\subseteq P_s(D)\subseteq D\] for every admissible \(D\subseteq D_s\). Starting with \(D^0=D_s\), propagation sets \(D^{k+1}=P_s(D^k)\), possibly cycling through several operators satisfying the same preservation condition. If an iterate has an empty component, then it contains no feasible completion and the node is infeasible. If the process terminates at a common fixed point \(D^*\), then \(F(s)\cap D_s\subseteq D^*\). Finite convergence requires an additional condition, such as finite domains or a terminating implementation policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node propagation contracts product domains without removing feasible completions. An empty component certifies infeasibility, while reaching a fixed point is guaranteed only under an additional termination condition.
assumptions_latex: \(D_s\) is the initial product domain at node \(s\).
\(F(s)\) is the node's feasible completion set in the ambient variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate preserves \(F(s)\cap D_s\); an empty component certifies infeasibility, and any attained common fixed point contains all initially feasible completions.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Constraint programming (CP) p. 17

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Constraint programming (CP) p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sound Contraction Need Not Terminate Finitely
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that soundness and contraction do not imply finite propagation closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let admissible domains be \(D_u=[0,u]\) for \(0\le u\le1\), let the feasible completion set be \(F=\{0\}\), and define \(P(D_u)=D_{u/2}\). Then \(F\subseteq P(D_u)\subseteq D_u\), and \(P\) is monotone under inclusion. Starting from \(D_1\), however, \(P^k(D_1)=[0,2^{-k}]\ne D_0\) for every finite \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound monotone propagator can generate an infinite strictly descending sequence and need not reach closure finitely.
assumptions_latex: Admissible domains include every interval \([0,u]\) with \(u\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^k(D_1)=[0,2^{-k}]\ne D_0\quad\text{for every finite }k.
knowledge_statements.title: Sound Contraction Need Not Terminate Finitely

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination, closure, and strict-contraction bound for monotone contracting propagators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal D,\subseteq)\) be a finite lattice of admissible product domains, let \(D^0\in\mathcal D\), and let \(P_1,\ldots,P_m:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D\) be monotone contracting operators. Under a fair schedule \(D^{k+1}=P_{i_k}(D^k)\), the sequence stabilizes at the greatest domain \(D^*\subseteq D^0\) fixed by every \(P_i\), independently of the fair order. If \(h(D^0)\) is the maximum length of a strict descending chain below \(D^0\), at most \(h(D^0)\) strict contractions occur, although mere fairness gives no finite bound on calls that make no change. If every \(P_i\) preserves the node-feasible set, then \(D^*\) contains every feasible completion initially present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair iteration on a finite domain lattice reaches the order-independent greatest common fixed point after at most the lattice height's number of strict contractions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\) is finite.
Every \(P_i\) is monotone and contracting.
Every operator is scheduled fairly.
For soundness, every \(P_i\) preserves the node-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D^*=\max_{\subseteq}\{D\subseteq D^0:P_i(D)=D\ \forall i\},\qquad\#\{k:D^{k+1}\subsetneq D^k\}\le h(D^0).

notation.meaning: Finite lattice of admissible product domains.
Greatest common fixed point below the initial domain.
Maximum number of strict descents below \(D^0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Lattice Fair Propagation Closure

children.title: Conflict-Learning Interface
children.top_down_role: Reuse of infeasibility information across the tree.

children.title: Conflict Extraction
children.top_down_role: Derivation of reusable information from local infeasibility events.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deletion Filtering for an Irreducible Conflict
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-based shrinking of a certified infeasible set of active restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each active restriction \(r\) have model set \(M(r)\), and let a finite set \(C\) of size \(m\) satisfy \[F\cap\bigcap_{r\in C}M(r)=\varnothing.\] Process each \(r\in C\) once. Delete \(r\) whenever an exact feasibility oracle certifies \(F\cap\bigcap_{s\in C\setminus\{r\}}M(s)=\varnothing\); otherwise retain it. The final set \(C^*\) is infeasible and irreducible: for every \(r\in C^*\), \[F\cap\bigcap_{s\in C^*\setminus\{r\}}M(s)\ne\varnothing.\] At most \(m\) oracle calls are used after the initial infeasibility certificate. Irreducibility is inclusion-minimality and does not imply minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-pass deletion filter uses at most one exact feasibility test per initial restriction and returns an inclusion-minimal, but not necessarily smallest, conflict.
assumptions_latex: Each literal or bound restriction \(r\) has an explicitly declared model set \(M(r)\).
The initial conjunction is certified infeasible relative to \(F\).
Every deletion query is answered by an exact feasibility oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C^*\text{ is infeasible},\quad \forall r\in C^*,\ F\cap\bigcap_{s\in C^*\setminus\{r\}}M(s)\ne\varnothing,\quad N_{\mathrm{oracle}}\le m.

notation.meaning: Set of assignments satisfying restriction or literal \(r\).

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion Filtering for an Irreducible Conflict

assumptions_latex: \(A_s=\{\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m\}\) is the conjunction of literals active at an infeasible node.
\(F\cap\bigcap_{\ell\in A_s}\ell=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nogood \(\bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\) is a conflict certificate whenever \(C\subseteq A_s\) and \(F\cap\bigcap_{\ell\in C}\ell=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nogood extraction from an infeasible set of active search literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conflict extraction returns a subset \(C\subseteq A_s\) together with a checkable derivation of \[F\cap\bigcap_{\ell\in C}\ell=\varnothing.\] The associated learned nogood is \[\bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell,\] which excludes the simultaneous recurrence of all literals in \(C\). A valid procedure may begin with \(C=A_s\) and remove literals while the infeasibility derivation remains valid. Minimality of \(C\) is optional; soundness requires the displayed infeasibility implication and a derivation accepted by the certificate checker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict extraction finds an infeasible subset of active literals and learns the nogood forbidding their simultaneous recurrence.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Extraction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is the correct kind and the nogood condition is mathematically standard, but no specialized source is supplied. The record also treats literals as sets without explicitly defining their model-set interpretation.

children.title: Learned-Constraint Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of conflict-derived constraints across search nodes.

assumptions_latex: \(N_C=\bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\) is a learned nogood.
\(K\) is a node context in which the derivation assumptions of \(N_C\) hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding \(N_C\) at context \(K\) preserves every globally feasible completion compatible with \(K\).

notation.meaning: Learned nogood generated by conflict set \(C\).
Node context where the nogood is reused.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reuse follows directly from the scope of a valid learned implication
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scope-aware reuse of learned nogoods during later propagation and node processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the learned nogood \(N_C\) is globally valid, it may be inserted into every open or subsequently created node. If its derivation is conditional on a context predicate \(H_C\), it may be reused only at nodes \(K\) satisfying \(K\Rightarrow H_C\). In either case, reuse intersects the current completion set with the models of \(N_C\). Because validity gives \(F\cap K\subseteq N_C\), this intersection removes no feasible completion. Reuse may trigger propagation, detect infeasibility, or strengthen a node relaxation without repeating extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned constraint may be reused globally or under its derivation context, and sound reuse preserves all feasible completions.
knowledge_statements.title: Learned-Constraint Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits learned-constraint reuse, but no source supports the global-versus-contextual reuse rule. The expressions involving F, K, and H_C also require an explicit convention identifying predicates or contexts with their model sets.

children.title: Learned-Constraint Validity
children.top_down_role: Global and local applicability regimes for learned constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) denotes the original feasible set.
\(H\) denotes contextual assumptions used in deriving a learned constraint \(g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The learned constraint is valid in context \(H\) exactly when \(F\cap H\subseteq\{x:g(x)\le 0\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validity is the semantic implication defining a sound learned constraint
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic validity criterion for global and context-dependent learned constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A learned inequality \(g(x)\le 0\) derived under context \(H\) is valid precisely when \[F\cap H\subseteq\{x:g(x)\le 0\}.\] It is globally valid when this inclusion holds with \(H\) equal to the entire ambient domain. A learned nogood \(\bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\) satisfies the same criterion when interpreted as its model set. A constraint derived using node-local assumptions is not globally reusable unless those assumptions are discharged; otherwise its validity is restricted to nodes whose contexts imply \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned constraint is valid exactly where every original feasible point satisfying its derivation context also satisfies the constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Learned-Constraint Validity

children.title: Conflict-Learning Overhead
children.top_down_role: Search costs associated with conflict analysis and retained learning.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage accounting for retained learned constraints with per-representation metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K_r\) learned constraints are retained, constraint \(i\) has \(|C_i|\) stored entries, and each retained representation has \(O(1)\) metadata, then retained storage is \[O\!\left(K_r+\sum_{i=1}^{K_r}|C_i|\right).\] The \(O(K_r)\) term is absorbed by the entry term only when every retained representation has at least one charged entry or metadata is included in \(|C_i|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retained learned constraints generally require storage for both their entries and one metadata record per representation.
assumptions_latex: \(K_r\) learned constraints are retained.
Each retained constraint has constant-size metadata and \(|C_i|\) charged entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=O\!\left(K_r+\sum_{i=1}^{K_r}|C_i|\right).

notation.meaning: Number of charged entries in retained constraint \(i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Metadata-Aware Retained Storage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive comparison of learning overhead with search work avoided by learning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W_0\) be baseline search work, \(H\ge0\) the additional extraction, insertion, propagation, and maintenance work caused by learning, and \(S\ge0\) the baseline work avoided because learning changes propagation or the generated tree. Under this accounting, \[W_{\mathrm{learn}}=W_0-S+H.\] Thus learning reduces total work exactly when \(S>H\); learned-constraint validity alone gives no performance guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict learning reduces runtime only when the search work it avoids exceeds its added overhead.
assumptions_latex: Baseline, avoided, and additional work are measured in one additive cost model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_{\mathrm{learn}}<W_0\iff S>H.
knowledge_statements.title: Net Runtime Benefit Criterion

assumptions_latex: \(K\) conflicts are extracted during the search.
\(C_i\) is the learned constraint from conflict \(i\), and \(E_i\) is its extraction cost.
\(Q\) counts learned-entry inspections during propagation and maintenance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The overhead is \(O(\sum_{i=1}^{K}E_i+\sum_{i=1}^{K}|C_i|+Q)\) time and \(O(\sum_{i=1}^{K}|C_i|)\) retained storage.
