knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-sensitive accounting for extraction, storage, and learned-constraint inspection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a unit-cost RAM model, suppose conflict \(i\) costs \(E_i\) operations to extract and produces a representation with \(|C_i|\) stored entries. If insertion and deletion are linear in representation size and later propagation or maintenance performs \(Q\) total entry inspections, then additional running time is \[O\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{K}E_i+\sum_{i=1}^{K}|C_i|+Q\right).\] Without deletion or representation sharing, retained storage is \[O\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{K}|C_i|\right).\] This accounting excludes any reduction in the underlying search-tree size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Learning costs extraction time, linear storage for retained constraints, and the work spent inspecting them during later processing.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Learning Overhead

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A complexity bound is appropriate here, but the accounting model is implementation-specific and uncited. Unless every learned representation has positive size and all metadata is charged to its entries, retained storage generally also has an O(K) term.

children.title: Solver Extension Architecture
children.top_down_role: Extension points for search control and node-level information exchange.

children.title: Branching-Rule Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension interfaces for candidate generation and partition selection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of branch-family admissibility from performance-oriented scoring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every candidate family admitted for selection satisfies \(F(s)\subseteq\bigcup_j B_j\), and the host creates children with feasible completion sets \(F(s)\cap B_j\). Replacing the scoring or tie-breaking rule cannot by itself remove a feasible completion, because it selects only among exhaustive families. It may change depth, generated-tree size, and runtime. Conversely, no score can make a nonexhaustive family sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch scoring affects search performance but cannot replace the exhaustive-cover condition required for correctness.
assumptions_latex: Every family eligible for scoring has passed the exhaustive-cover requirement.
The host constructs the declared child intersections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{coverage is determined by admissibility, while scoring selects among admissible families}.

notation.meaning: Feasible completions of the current node.
A branch region in a candidate family.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Score Correctness Separation

assumptions_latex: \(F(s)\) is the feasible completion set at a nonterminal node \(s\).
\(B_1,\ldots,B_r\) are candidate branch regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Children with completion sets \(F(s)\cap B_j\) preserve completeness when \(F(s)\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{r}B_j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: abstract branching plugin contract is the exhaustive-cover condition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent contract for generating and selecting an exhaustive branching disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonterminal node \(s\), a branching-rule plugin generates candidate families \(\mathcal B=\{B_1,\ldots,B_r\}\), rejects every family failing \[F(s)\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{r}B_j,\] scores the remaining families, and selects one according to its declared rule. It then returns children \(s_j\) satisfying \(F(s_j)=F(s)\cap B_j\). The regions may overlap, although a disjoint family avoids duplicate completions. If no admissible family is returned, the plugin reports no decision and leaves node handling to the host solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching plugin generates and scores branch disjunctions whose children collectively cover every feasible completion of the current node.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Rule Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exhaustive-cover condition is a sound abstract branching algorithm and fits the plugin container, but no solver-interface or branching reference supports the stated generation, rejection, scoring, and fallback protocol.

children.title: Node-Selector Plugins
children.top_down_role: Extension interfaces for active-frontier prioritization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Priority Selection Can Starve a Persistent Node
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that minimum-priority selection need not be fair on an infinite search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an active node \(s\) have priority \(\pi(s)=1\). At each selection step \(k\), suppose processing another node creates a new active node \(t_k\) with \(\pi(t_k)=0\). A selector that always chooses a minimum-priority node can select a priority-zero node at every step while \(s\) remains active forever. Thus \(s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathcal A_k}\pi(u)\) at every step does not imply fairness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict priority rule can postpone a persistent node forever when higher-priority nodes continually arrive.
assumptions_latex: The search may generate infinitely many nodes.
New priority-zero nodes continue to enter the frontier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s\in\mathcal A_k\ \forall k\quad\text{but}\quad s_k\ne s\ \forall k.
knowledge_statements.title: Priority Selection Can Starve a Persistent Node

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A_k\) is the finite active-node frontier at selection step \(k\).
\(\pi_k(s)\) is the priority key for active node \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Priority selection is complete for finite trees; infinite trees additionally require fairness.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: frontier selection and fairness are standard abstract search contracts
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority-based active-frontier selection with the fairness condition needed for completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At step \(k\), a node-selector plugin receives the nonempty frontier \(\mathcal A_k\), computes priority keys \(\pi_k(s)\), and returns \[s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathcal A_k}\pi_k(s),\] using a declared deterministic or randomized tie rule. The host removes \(s_k\), processes it, and inserts any surviving children. For an infinite search tree, completeness requires fairness: every node that remains continuously active must be selected after finitely many subsequent selections. On a finite tree, any selector that always returns an active node is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-selector plugin prioritizes the active frontier; infinite-tree completeness requires that no persistent node be postponed forever.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Selector Plugins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and finite-versus-infinite distinction fit the node-selector leaf. The fairness formulation is plausible, but the plugin protocol and completeness claim have no inspectable source.

children.title: Specialized Constraint Callback Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces supplying bounds, candidates, propagation, and feasibility information.

children.title: Relaxator Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Extension points supplying node bounds and relaxation information.

assumptions_latex: \(F(s)\) is the feasible completion set at node \(s\).
\(f\) is minimized and \(U\) is the incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bound pruning is permitted only when \(L(s)\le\inf_{x\in F(s)}f(x)\) is certified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound lower-bound callback contract for a minimization search node.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relaxator callback receives node \(s\) and returns a status plus, when successful, a value \(L(s)\) certified by \[L(s)\le\inf_{x\in F(s)}f(x).\] It may also return a feasible point \(\widehat x\in F(s)\), which updates the incumbent to \(\min\{U,f(\widehat x)\}\). The host may prune when \(L(s)\ge U\), declare infeasibility when given a valid infeasibility certificate, or continue branching otherwise. An uncertified or interrupted result must not be used as a valid bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxator callback returns a certified node lower bound and optionally a feasible solution; only certified results may justify pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxator Callbacks

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relaxation Iterate Is Not Automatically a Node Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes a feasible relaxation iterate's objective value from a certified minimization lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization relaxation with feasible set \(R\), optimum \(z_R\), and node feasible set \(F(s)\subseteq R\), an arbitrary relaxation-feasible iterate \(y\in R\) satisfies \(f(y)\ge z_R\). Its objective value therefore does not generally provide a lower bound on \(\inf_{x\in F(s)}f(x)\). Bound pruning requires an optimality certificate or another certificate establishing a reported value \(L\le\inf_{x\in F(s)}f(x)\); an interrupted or merely feasible iterate is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible relaxation iterate is not by itself a certified node lower bound; pruning requires independently valid lower-bound evidence.
assumptions_latex: The node problem and relaxation are minimization problems.
The relaxation feasible set contains the node feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\in R\centernot\implies f(y)\le\inf_{x\in F(s)}f(x).

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the node relaxation.
Original feasible completion set at node s.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Iterate Is Not Automatically a Node Bound

children.title: Constraint-Handler Propagation
children.top_down_role: Extension points supplying domain reduction through constraint-specific processing.

assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the current product domain.
\(X_h\subseteq D\) is the solution set of constraint handler \(h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed-point handler propagation preserves every point satisfying all handled constraints; an empty domain certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compositional fixed-point propagation performed by specialized constraint handlers.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Constraint programming (CP) p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each handled constraint \(h\), the propagation callback supplies a contracting operator \(P_h\) satisfying \[X_h\cap D\subseteq P_h(D)\subseteq D.\] Starting from node domain \(D^0\), the host schedules handlers and sets \(D^{k+1}=P_{h_k}(D^k)\) until no handler changes the domain or some component becomes empty. Under fair scheduling, every handler affected by a change is reconsidered before termination. The final domain contains every point in \(D^0\cap\bigcap_h X_h\); an empty component therefore certifies infeasibility of the handled system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint handlers repeatedly contract variable domains while preserving all joint solutions; an empty domain certifies node infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Handler Propagation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Constraint programming (CP) p. 17

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination condition supplementing the accepted sound handler-propagation algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) be a finite-height family of representable product domains ordered by inclusion, and let every handler operator \(P_h:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D\) be monotone, contracting, and solution-preserving. A worklist procedure that reschedules every handler affected by a strict reduction performs only finitely many strict reductions. If it terminates only after every handler has been processed since the last relevant change, its terminal domain \(D^*\) is a common fixed point: \(P_h(D^*)=D^*\) for every \(h\). Without finite height or another well-founded progress condition, sound contraction alone need not terminate finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On finite-height domains, fair event-driven handler propagation makes finitely many strict reductions and terminates at a common fixed point; sound contraction alone does not ensure finite termination.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\) has finite height under inclusion.
Every \(P_h\) is monotone, contracting, and solution-preserving.
Every handler affected by a strict change is rescheduled, and termination requires an empty worklist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K<\infty:\ D^K=D^*\quad\text{and}\quad\forall h,\ P_h(D^*)=D^*.

notation.meaning: Ordered family of representable product domains.
Propagation operator supplied by handler h.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Height Fair Propagation Termination

children.title: Constraint-Handler Feasibility Checks
children.top_down_role: Extension points reporting candidate or node feasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which specialized handler checks collectively decide global candidate feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the model feasible set and \(X_h\) the set defined by the requirements owned by active handler \(h\). If the ownership family is exact, \(X=\bigcap_{h\in H}X_h\), and each handler correctly decides membership in \(X_h\), then a fully specified candidate \(x\) is globally feasible exactly when every handler reports \(x\in X_h\). If ownership is incomplete or a positive handler result is only sufficient for a weaker property, unanimous success need not establish \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unanimous handler success decides global feasibility only when the handlers exactly cover all model requirements and correctly decide their owned sets.
assumptions_latex: The candidate assigns every value required by the checks.
The handler-owned sets exactly cover the model feasible set.
Every handler correctly decides membership in its owned set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X=\bigcap_{h\in H}X_h\implies\left(x\in X\iff\forall h\in H,\ x\in X_h\right).

notation.meaning: Set of active specialized constraint handlers.
Set satisfying the requirements owned by handler h.

knowledge_statements.title: Handler-Coverage Feasibility Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unknown or Omitted Handler Checks Are Noncertifying
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary for incomplete specialized-handler evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an active requirement has not been decided by its responsible handler, the collected results alone do not decide membership in the global feasible set. An unknown, interrupted, or omitted result is therefore equivalent to neither a feasible verdict nor an infeasible verdict without additional evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unknown, interrupted, or omitted handler result certifies neither global feasibility nor global infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Global feasibility requires satisfaction of every handled requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists h\in H:\operatorname{check}_h(x)=\mathrm{unknown}\implies\text{the handler results alone do not decide }x\in X.

notation.meaning: Outcome of handler h's feasibility check at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown or Omitted Handler Checks Are Noncertifying
Constraint-Handler Feasibility Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local feasibility predicate for a candidate evaluated by specialized constraint handlers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be a candidate and let \(H\) be the set of active constraint handlers. Handler \(h\in H\) owns predicates \(g_{hi}(x)\le 0\), equalities \(q_{hi}(x)=0\), or other explicitly defined membership tests, together with tolerances \(\varepsilon_h\ge 0\). It returns \(v_h(x)\in\{\mathrm{feasible},\mathrm{infeasible},\mathrm{unknown}\}\). The global feasibility check accepts \(x\) exactly when every handler returns feasible. Any violated owned constraint implies an infeasible verdict, while an unknown verdict must trigger further checking and must not be interpreted as feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate is accepted only when every active handler certifies its owned constraints; unknown results require further checking.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) assigns every variable inspected by the handlers.
Each handler uses its declared feasibility tolerance consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\text{ is accepted}\iff \forall h\in H,\ v_h(x)=\mathrm{feasible}.\)

notation.meaning: Set of active specialized constraint handlers.
Feasibility verdict returned by handler h.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the three-valued verdict protocol and the claim that global acceptance occurs exactly when every handler returns feasible are solver-specific and unsupported.

children.title: Callback Information Exchange
children.top_down_role: Transfer of bounds, candidates, and validity information between callback components.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scope Loss Makes Exchanged Deductions Noncertifying
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for reusing callback information outside its declared invocation or node domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a callback deduction \(r\) is known valid only on domain \(D\), then using \(r\) on a state outside \(D\) is not justified by the original callback result. Likewise, absence of an available field cannot be replaced by a value retained from another invocation unless a separate compatibility argument establishes its validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-scoped deduction or unavailable field cannot safely be reused outside its justified domain without an independent compatibility argument.
assumptions_latex: The original callback result supplies no validity claim beyond \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s\notin D\implies r\text{ alone does not certify a deduction at }s.

notation.meaning: A deduction returned by a callback.
Declared validity domain of the deduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Scope Loss Makes Exchanged Deductions Noncertifying

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-neutral representation of information transferred between a host and specialized constraint callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A callback exchange consists of an invocation context \(C\), a set of explicitly available host data \(A(C)\), and a response \(R\). Every deduction in \(R\) must be derived only from available data and must declare a validity domain containing every state on which the host will use it. An unavailable quantity has no implied value, and information valid only for a node domain may not be promoted to global scope without an independent validity justification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Callbacks may use only information declared available in the invocation and must return deductions with an explicit validity scope; unavailable or node-local data cannot silently be reused globally.
assumptions_latex: The host declares the information available in each invocation context.
Returned deductions are interpreted only within their declared validity domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r\in R\implies \operatorname{useDomain}(r)\subseteq\operatorname{validDomain}(r).

notation.meaning: Host information declared available in context C.
Callback response containing scoped deductions or reports.

knowledge_statements.title: Scoped Callback Information Exchange
Callback Information Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed request-response representation for communication between a solver and constraint callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At callback invocation \(k\), represent solver-to-handler information by a read-only snapshot \(S_k=(x_k,B_k,D_k,\tau_k)\), containing the current candidate or relaxation solution, valid local bounds, available dual data, and invocation context. Represent the handler response by \(R_k=(v_k,P_k,C_k,M_k)\), containing a verdict, bound tightenings, generated constraints, and metadata. Every component of \(R_k\) must cite the snapshot version \(k\); generated information must be valid for the node domain encoded by \(B_k\), and unavailable fields must be marked unavailable rather than populated with stale values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Callbacks consume a versioned solver snapshot and return typed, domain-valid deductions whose unavailable fields and scope are explicit.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\) is immutable throughout invocation \(k\).
Each returned deduction has a declared validity scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k\text{ is admissible}\implies \operatorname{version}(R_k)=k\text{ and }R_k\text{ is valid on the domain encoded by }B_k.\)

notation.meaning: Solver state exposed at callback invocation k.
Local variable-bound domain in the snapshot.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but versioned snapshots, response fields, immutability, and stale-value rules describe a particular callback protocol for which no source is supplied.

children.title: Primal-Solution Callback Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces supplying and validating primal solutions.

children.title: Heuristic Solution Submission
children.top_down_role: Interface boundaries for supplying candidate primal solutions during search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-neutral boundary between conveying a heuristic candidate and validating or installing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A heuristic-solution submission is a request that conveys candidate values \(y\), together with whatever identity and scope information the declared interface requires, to the host solver. The interface may require a complete assignment or may permit omitted values to be completed by a documented host procedure. Submission alone asserts neither \(y\in X\) nor installation of \(y\) as the incumbent; both require subsequent validation and the host's incumbent policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Submitting a heuristic candidate only conveys it to the solver; completeness rules are interface-defined, and submission alone proves neither feasibility nor incumbency.
assumptions_latex: The callback follows a declared candidate-value and variable-identity convention.
Any host completion of omitted values is part of the declared interface rather than an implicit mathematical guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{submit}(y)\centernot\implies y\in X\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{submit}(y)\centernot\implies y\text{ is incumbent}.

notation.meaning: Candidate values supplied by the heuristic callback.
Feasible set of the original model.

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Candidate Submission Contract
Heuristic Solution Submission
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Submission protocol for a heuristic candidate without presuming incumbent acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a minimization model with variable set \(I\), a heuristic constructs a candidate \(\hat x\). It maps values into the solver's current variable representation, supplies every required component \(\hat x_i\) for \(i\in I\), and tags the candidate with its origin and applicable node. The submission operation sends \(\hat x\) to the solver's validation routine and returns a status in \(\{\mathrm{accepted},\mathrm{rejected},\mathrm{deferred}\}\). Submission alone neither installs \(\hat x\) as incumbent nor permits pruning; those effects occur only after independent feasibility and objective validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic submits a complete mapped candidate for validation; submission itself does not establish feasibility, incumbency, or pruning authority.
assumptions_latex: \(\hat x_i\) is finite for every required variable \(i\in I\).
The candidate is mapped to the solver's current variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{submit}(\hat x)\in\{\mathrm{accepted},\mathrm{rejected},\mathrm{deferred}\}.\)

notation.meaning: Candidate solution produced by the heuristic.
Set of model variables requiring submitted values.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate, but the required completeness, node tagging, and accepted/rejected/deferred status set are not universal solver semantics and require an API source.

children.title: Incumbent Acceptance Validation
children.top_down_role: Checks governing whether submitted candidates become incumbent solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-neutral necessary conditions for installing a submitted candidate as an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a submitted candidate \(y\), sound incumbent installation requires that the host can evaluate the required model values, classifies every required bound, constraint, and integrality condition as satisfied under its declared validation convention, obtains a valid objective value \(f(y)\), and applies its declared incumbent policy. These conditions are necessary but are not a universal sufficient rule: a host may additionally reject duplicates, ties, stale submissions, or candidates failing a stricter improvement policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Installing a submitted point requires successful model validation, objective evaluation, and the declared incumbent policy; passing those generic gates does not impose a universal tie or replacement rule.
assumptions_latex: The host declares its numerical validation convention and incumbent policy.
The optimization direction and objective evaluation convention are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\text{ installed as incumbent}\implies y\text{ passes all required validation and policy gates}.

notation.meaning: Candidate objective value under the host's evaluation convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Sound Incumbent-Acceptance Gate
Incumbent Acceptance Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance condition for a submitted candidate in a minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_j(x)\le0\ (j\in J),\ x_i\in\mathbb{Z}\ (i\in I)\}\), with feasibility and integrality tolerances \(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_I\ge0\). A submitted \(\hat x\) is eligible for acceptance only if its values are finite, all variable bounds and constraints hold within \(\varepsilon_f\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(\hat x_i,\mathbb{Z})\le\varepsilon_I\) for every \(i\in I\). If the incumbent value is \(U\), it replaces the incumbent only when the solver's improvement rule, for example \(f(\hat x)<U-\varepsilon_o\), is also satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceptance requires finite values, bound and constraint feasibility, integrality, and sufficient objective improvement over the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The model is a minimization problem with objective \(f\).
All active constraints participate in validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat x\text{ replaces the incumbent}\iff \hat x\text{ passes validation and }f(\hat x)<U-\varepsilon_o.\)

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited primal-bounds section does not establish the solver-specific validation tolerances or the stated if-and-only-if replacement rule. Passing validation and an example improvement test need not be sufficient under every incumbent policy.

children.title: Callback Rejection Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Solver responses to invalid, infeasible, stale, or otherwise unacceptable candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Callback Rejection Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limits of conclusions justified by rejecting a callback-submitted solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a submitted candidate \(\hat x\), distinguish rejection causes: malformed or nonfinite values, failed feasibility, failed integrality, insufficient objective improvement, stale model state, or unsupported submission context. Rejection establishes only that \(\hat x\) was not installed as incumbent under the current validation state. In particular, rejection for malformed data, staleness, or insufficient improvement does not imply \(\hat x\notin X\); rejection of one candidate does not imply node infeasibility; and no dual bound or pruning decision may be derived solely from the rejection status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rejecting a submitted candidate prevents incumbent installation but generally proves neither candidate infeasibility nor node infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The rejection status identifies or refines its cause.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\mathrm{rejected}(\hat x)
ot\Rightarrow \hat x
otin X\quad	ext{and}\quad\mathrm{rejected}(\hat x)
ot\Rightarrow X=\varnothing.\)

notation.meaning: Feasible set at the current search node.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf and the cautions are plausible, but the enumerated rejection causes and consequences depend on the callback API and have no cited support.

children.title: Bound-Generation Interface Family
children.top_down_role: Bound-generation interfaces whose detailed theory belongs to cutting-plane and decomposition chapters.

children.title: Cut-Generation Interface
children.top_down_role: Integration boundary for dynamically generated inequalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical solver-interface contract for returning and admitting dynamically generated inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a current relaxation point \(\bar x\), a separation callback may return finitely many inequalities \(a_r^{\mathsf T}x\le b_r\), each with a declared validity domain \(D_r\). An inequality is admissible only if it is well-defined in the current formulation and satisfies \(a_r^{\mathsf T}x\le b_r\) for every feasible solution \(x\in D_r\). A globally valid cut may be propagated throughout the tree; a node-local cut may be used only within the subtree where its validity assumptions hold. After admitting a violated cut, the solver must reoptimize before treating a cut-dependent solution or strengthened relaxation value as current.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut callback may add only formulation-compatible inequalities valid throughout their declared global or node-local scope, and cut-dependent solver state requires reoptimization.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) belongs to the current relaxation state.
Each returned inequality has a declared domain on which its validity is asserted.
The solver distinguishes global validity from validity conditional on node restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_r^{\mathsf T}x\le b_r\) may exclude \(\bar x\) only if it preserves every feasible \(x\in D_r\); its use outside \(D_r\) is not certified.

notation.meaning: declared validity domain of returned cut r

knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Scoped Cut Callback Contract

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for admitting a cut outside the domain on which it is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an inequality is valid only under node restrictions defining \(D\) but is installed at a node whose feasible set is not contained in \(D\), it may remove a feasible solution. Any infeasibility conclusion, bound, pruning decision, or optimality claim depending on that inequality is then uncertified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagating a node-local cut outside its validity domain can remove feasible solutions and invalidate dependent bounds or pruning decisions.
assumptions_latex: The cut is not known to be valid outside \(D\).
The receiving node may contain feasible points outside \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_{N'}\nsubseteq D\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{validity on }D\text{ alone does not justify adding the cut at }N'.

notation.meaning: domain on which the cut is certified valid
feasible domain of the receiving node

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Scope Violation Invalidates Search
Cut-Generation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface contract for adding valid inequalities generated at a relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a node domain \(X_N\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and relaxation solution \(\bar x\), a separation callback returns finitely many pairs \((a_r,b_r)\) and a validity scope. A returned inequality \(a_r^{\mathsf T}x\le b_r\) is admissible only if \(a_r^{\mathsf T}x\le b_r\) for every integer-feasible \(x\in X_N\) within its declared scope. It is efficacious at \(\bar x\) when \(a_r^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b_r+\varepsilon_s\). The solver validates dimensions, finiteness, scope, and duplicate policy before adding an admissible cut and reoptimizing the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut callback separates the current relaxation point using inequalities valid for every integer-feasible point in their declared scope.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is the relaxation solution for the callback's current node state.
\(\varepsilon_s\ge0\) is the separation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_r^{\mathsf T}x\le b_r\ \forall x\in X_N\cap(\mathbb{Z}^{I}\times\mathbb{R}^{n-|I|})\) is required before cut admission.

notation.meaning: Node-local domain before adding generated cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Callback Contract
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduced-cost pricing contract for a minimization restricted master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a restricted master problem over columns \(p\in P_k\), let \(\pi_k\) and \(\sigma_k\) be current dual multipliers. The pricing callback receives these multipliers and the current node restrictions, and solves \(\min_{p\in\mathcal P_N}\bar c_k(p)\), where \(\bar c_k(p)=c(p)-\pi_k^{\mathsf T}a(p)-\sigma_k\). It returns either a valid column \(p\in\mathcal P_N\) with \(\bar c_k(p)<-\varepsilon_p\), or an exact certificate that \(\bar c_k(p)\ge-\varepsilon_p\) for all \(p\in\mathcal P_N\). Heuristic failure to find a column is not such a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing returns a node-valid negative-reduced-cost column or an exact certificate that none exists within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The dual multipliers correspond to the current optimized restricted master.
The pricing domain \(\mathcal P_N\) incorporates current node restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\text{ returned}\Rightarrow\bar c_k(p)<-\varepsilon_p\), or \(\min_{p\in\mathcal P_N}\bar c_k(p)\ge-\varepsilon_p\) is certified.

notation.meaning: Columns currently present in the restricted master.
Reduced cost of column p under current dual multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Synchronization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Version consistency between the restricted master, its dual state, and pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k\) be the columns defining restricted-master version \(k\), and let \((z_k,\pi_k,\sigma_k)\) be the primal value and dual multipliers obtained after optimizing precisely that version under the current node restrictions. A synchronized pricing invocation uses \((\pi_k,\sigma_k)\), the same restrictions, and the same coefficient conventions that define \(P_k\). After admitting a new column, the master version advances to \(k+1\). The old multipliers may be retained as a warm start, but they must not be presumed to provide a valid reduced-cost or optimality certificate for version \(k+1\) unless their required dual feasibility and optimality conditions are independently verified for the new version.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing duals, columns, coefficients, and node restrictions must share one master version; after a column is added, old duals are only a warm start unless their validity for the new master is verified.
assumptions_latex: Restricted-master optimization reports dual multipliers for its current version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{k+1}\ne P_k\Rightarrow(\pi_k,\sigma_k)\text{ alone do not certify pricing optimality for version }k+1.\)

notation.meaning: Column set in restricted-master version k.
Dual multipliers obtained for version k.

children.title: Column Admission Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Solver integration points governing candidate-column acceptance, activation, retention, or retirement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical lifecycle from a proposed priced column to an active restricted-master variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be a proposed column at node \(N\). Before admission, verify that \(p\in\mathcal P_N\), including inherited branching restrictions, and that its objective coefficient, row vector, bounds, and integrality type use the current restricted-master convention. If admitted, append the corresponding variable to the restricted master and reoptimize before using new dual multipliers or invoking exact pricing again. For minimization, adding a column enlarges the restricted-master feasible set, so its optimal value cannot increase; neither the old nor new restricted-master value is a certified full-master node bound until pricing over every eligible omitted column is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An eligible, formulation-compatible candidate becomes an active master variable; the enlarged restricted master must be reoptimized and remains uncertified until complete pricing.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_N\) is the universe of columns eligible under the current node restrictions.
The restricted master and proposed column use the same coefficient convention.
The restricted master is reoptimized after insertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{k+1}=P_k\cup\{p\}\ \Longrightarrow\ v(P_{k+1})\le v(P_k)\text{ for minimization, with full-master certification requiring complete pricing}.

notation.meaning: active restricted-master column set before admission
optimal value of the restricted master over P_k

knowledge_statements.title: Eligible Column Admission and Activation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness condition for removing a column from the active restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A column may be deactivated or removed from the restricted master without changing the represented full master only if it remains part of the eligible pricing universe and can be regenerated when improving. Removing columns can increase a minimization restricted-master value, but that value is not a certified full-master bound unless exact final pricing also tests every inactive or retired eligible column under the current dual state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retired columns must remain priceable and recoverable; otherwise restricted-master optimality cannot certify the full master.
assumptions_latex: Inactive or retired columns remain eligible whenever they satisfy current node restrictions.
Exact pricing ranges over active and inactive eligible columns alike.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{p\in\mathcal P_N}\bar c(p)\ge0\text{ must include retired eligible columns before full-master optimality is certified}.

notation.meaning: complete node-eligible column universe, including recoverable retired columns
current reduced cost of column p

Column Admission Lifecycle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation, insertion, and reoptimization lifecycle for a priced column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a priced column \(p\), first verify \(p\in\mathcal P_N\), finite objective and row coefficients, and compatibility with current branching restrictions. Recompute its reduced cost from the synchronized dual state and reject it as nonimproving when \(\bar c_k(p)\ge-\varepsilon_p\). Apply the solver's duplicate and numerical-scaling checks; if admitted, append the column to obtain \(P_{k+1}=P_k\cup\{p\}\), invalidate the version-\(k\) dual state, reoptimize the restricted master, and invoke pricing again. Terminate exact column generation only after a synchronized exact pricing certificate finds no improving column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A priced column is validated, deduplicated, inserted, and followed by master reoptimization and renewed pricing until exact certification.
assumptions_latex: Pricing and admission use the same node domain and coefficient convention.
The restricted master can be reoptimized after insertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\text{ admitted}\Rightarrow P_{k+1}=P_k\cup\{p\}\text{ and the version-}k\text{ dual state is invalidated}.\)

notation.meaning: Column proposed by the pricing callback.

children.title: Pricing Interface Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Handling of stale pricing state, incompatible columns, incomplete pricing, or callback failures.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Interface Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which pricing output cannot certify a valid bound or termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pricing invocation cannot certify completion when its dual multipliers are stale, its pricing domain omits node-feasible columns, reduced costs use coefficients inconsistent with the restricted master, or the oracle is merely heuristic. If an omitted column \(p\in\mathcal P_N\) has \(\bar c_k(p)<-\varepsilon_p\), then declaring no improving column is false. Likewise, a structurally invalid returned column must not be inserted. Under any such failure, the current restricted-master objective remains a restricted value and must not be reported as the full-master optimum or used as an exact node bound without an independent valid correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stale duals, incomplete pricing, inconsistent coefficients, or invalid columns destroy exact termination and bound certification.
assumptions_latex: The intended termination test is absence of negative-reduced-cost columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists p\in\mathcal P_N:\bar c_k(p)<-\varepsilon_p\Rightarrow\text{pricing completion is not certified}.\)

notation.meaning: Reduced cost under synchronized dual multipliers.

children.title: Decomposition Callback Interface
children.top_down_role: Integration boundary for decomposition-based bounds and feasibility information.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Callback Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical linear Benders callback returning certified subproblem feasibility information and valid master cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a Benders model with master variable \(y\in Y\) and subproblem value \(Q(y)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}x:Bx\ge b-Ay,\ x\ge0\}\). Given a master candidate \(\bar y\), the callback solves this linear subproblem. If it is infeasible and returns a Farkas ray \(r\ge0\) satisfying \(B^{\mathsf T}r\le0\) and \((b-A\bar y)^{\mathsf T}r>0\), the callback may return the feasibility cut \((b-Ay)^{\mathsf T}r\le0\). If the subproblem has a finite optimum and returns a dual-feasible multiplier \(u\ge0\) satisfying \(B^{\mathsf T}u\le q\), it may return the optimality cut \(\theta\ge(b-Ay)^{\mathsf T}u\). The master admits only cuts whose certificates and declared validity domain have been validated, and then reoptimizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a classical linear Benders subproblem, the callback returns a certificate-backed feasibility cut from a Farkas ray or an optimality cut from a dual-feasible multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(y)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}x:Bx\ge b-Ay,\ x\ge0\}\) is a linear subproblem for each master point \(y\in Y\).
A reported optimality cut uses a dual-feasible multiplier and finite certified subproblem value information.
\(\theta\) is the master variable representing a lower approximation of \(Q(y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((b-A\bar y)^{\mathsf T}r>0\Rightarrow(b-Ay)^{\mathsf T}r\le0\text{ is a violated feasibility cut at }\bar y\), while \(B^{\mathsf T}u\le q,\ u\ge0\Rightarrow\theta\ge(b-Ay)^{\mathsf T}u\text{ is a valid optimality cut}.\)

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the parameterized linear subproblem.
Dual-feasible multiplier generating an optimality cut.
Master variable approximating the subproblem value from below.

children.title: Relaxation Basis Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of continuous-relaxation basis state across related search nodes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-neutral meaning of transferring an LP basis between related node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relaxation basis transfer uses the row and column statuses of a source LP basis, after applying a valid correspondence for the target LP, as an initialization for target reoptimization. Acceptance of the initialization requires a valid target basis under the target representation. Transfer affects only the starting state and computational effort; every target feasibility, optimality, infeasibility, or bound claim must be established by the target solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis transfer maps a source LP basis into a valid target initialization; it may change reoptimization effort but does not itself certify the target result.
assumptions_latex: A declared correspondence identifies the source information applicable to the target LP.
The target solver validates any transferred initialization before relying on it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{transfer}(B_s)=B_t\implies B_t\text{ is only an initialization; target claims require target certification}.

notation.meaning: Target initialization obtained from the transferable basis information.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Basis Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical basis-transfer case when a child LP changes only variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a child LP changes only variable bounds while retaining the source constraint matrix and objective. The source basis matrix remains algebraically nonsingular. If target nonbasic statuses are compatible with the changed bounds and preserve dual feasibility, the transferred basis is an admissible dual-simplex starting basis even when the changed bounds make its associated basic solution primal infeasible. This conclusion does not apply when target status compatibility or dual feasibility is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bound-only child LP, an unchanged nonsingular basis can start dual-simplex reoptimization when target statuses preserve dual feasibility, even if primal feasibility is lost.
assumptions_latex: The target changes only variable bounds; its constraint matrix and objective are unchanged.
The source basis matrix is nonsingular.
Target nonbasic statuses are compatible with the new bounds and preserve dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_s\text{ nonsingular and target-dual-feasible}\implies B_s\text{ is an admissible dual-simplex start}.

notation.meaning: Basis transferred from the source relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Change Dual-Simplex Reoptimization

children.title: Warm-Start State Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of solver initialization state beyond the relaxation basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness invariant separating initialization from the fixed target relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a target relaxation \(R_v\). If runs initialized from \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) each correctly certify a global optimum of \(R_v\), both objective values equal \(\inf_{x\in R_v}f(x)\). Likewise, correctly certified infeasibility is a property of \(R_v\), not its initialization. Transfer may change computational effort or the solution path, but not a correctly certified result for the unchanged target model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different starts may change solve effort, but correctly certified solves of the same relaxation have the same mathematical result.
assumptions_latex: Both runs solve exactly the same target relaxation and objective.
Each reported status satisfies the ordinary correctness certificate for that relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{certopt}(R_v,S_1)=\operatorname{certopt}(R_v,S_2)=\inf_{x\in R_v}f(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Relaxation Result Is Initialization-Invariant

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bound Projection Need Not Repair a Primal Start
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of coordinatewise bound projection as a general warm-start repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:x_1+x_2=1,\ 0\le x_1,x_2\le1\}\) and let the transferred point be \(z=(2,2)\). Coordinatewise projection onto the target bounds gives \(\Pi_{[0,1]^2}(z)=(1,1)\notin R\). Thus bound projection alone does not generally produce a feasible target-relaxation start.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clipping a transferred point to target bounds can still violate target rows and therefore does not certify a feasible repaired start.
assumptions_latex: Warm-start repair uses only coordinatewise projection onto target variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pi_{[l,u]}(z)\in[l,u]\centernot\Longrightarrow\Pi_{[l,u]}(z)\in R.

notation.meaning: Coordinatewise projection onto the target bound box.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Projection Need Not Repair a Primal Start

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent protocol for constructing a nonbasis initialization from eligible source components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given source state \(S_u\) and target relaxation \(R_v\), enumerate the state components exposed by the solver. For each component, apply the target correspondence and its eligibility predicate; transfer verified components, pass permitted but nonvalid components only as untrusted predictions, and replace rejected, unmatched, or unresolved components by target defaults. Any repaired primal vector is marked feasible only after all target rows and bounds are checked. Solve \(R_v\) and publish a status or bound only after the ordinary target certificates succeed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer components one by one, default anything unverified, and certify the target result independently of the warm start.
assumptions_latex: The solver identifies exposed components and their permitted initialization roles.
A valid default initialization exists.
The target solver has ordinary status and bound tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_v^0\text{ is an initialization only; correctness follows from certificates for }R_v.

notation.meaning: Source state and constructed target initialization.

review_flags: component details remain governed by the solver contract
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Warm-Start Transfer Protocol
Warm-Start State Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of a continuous-relaxation solver state from a processed tree node to a compatible node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a solved relaxation \(R_u\), its solver state \(S_u\), and a target relaxation \(R_v\), first verify that every state component has a defined correspondence in \(R_v\). Transfer the corresponding primal point, dual estimates, active-set information, and solver parameters to obtain \(S_v^0\). Project or discard primal components violating the bounds of \(R_v\), invalidate dual or factorization data affected by changed rows or columns, and initialize all unmatched components by the solver default. Start the continuous solver from \(S_v^0\); the resulting relaxation bound is accepted only after the ordinary feasibility and optimality tests for \(R_v\) succeed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer matched solver data, repair or discard incompatible components, and accept the target relaxation bound only after normal feasibility and optimality validation.
assumptions_latex: \(R_u\) and \(R_v\) have explicitly identifiable rows and variables.
The continuous solver exposes transferable state components and independent termination tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transferred state supplies an initialization for \(R_v\) but does not itself certify feasibility or optimality.

notation.meaning: source solver state and constructed target initialization

review_flags: implementation-specific state semantics require an authoritative solver or algorithm source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Warm-Start State Transfer leaf, and the statement correctly treats transferred state as initialization rather than certification. However, no source supports the asserted transferable components, correspondence rules, invalidation behavior, or validation protocol; these details vary materially among continuous solvers.

children.title: Reuse Eligibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural or numerical conditions limiting safe transfer between node relaxations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Source Feasibility Does Not Imply Target Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal counterexample to inheriting feasible-primal-start status across a tightened node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_u=\{x\in\mathbb R:0\le x\le1\}\), let \(R_v=R_u\cap\{x\le\tfrac12\}\), and let the stored source point be \(x_u=1\). Then \(x_u\in R_u\) but \(x_u\notin R_v\). Thus source feasibility alone cannot certify that a transferred point is a feasible primal start for the target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point feasible at a parent can violate a child's tighter bound, so target feasibility must be checked separately.
assumptions_latex: The target node may impose restrictions absent from the source node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_u\in R_u\centernot\Longrightarrow x_u\in R_v.
knowledge_statements.title: Source Feasibility Does Not Imply Target Feasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact validation of transferred dual multipliers against the target linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the target LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\), a transferred tuple \((y,\alpha,\beta)\), with \(y\) free and \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\), is dual feasible for the target when \(c-A^{\mathsf T}y-\alpha+\beta=0\) under the target model and scaling. Then \(b^{\mathsf T}y+l^{\mathsf T}\alpha-u^{\mathsf T}\beta\) is a valid target lower bound. Source-model dual feasibility alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transferred dual multipliers retain certifying meaning only after their signs and stationarity equation are checked against the target LP.
assumptions_latex: R_v=\{x:Ax=b,\ l\le x\le u\}\text{ is the target linear relaxation.}
y\text{ is unrestricted and }\alpha,\beta\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c-A^{\mathsf T}y-\alpha+\beta=0\Longrightarrow b^{\mathsf T}y+l^{\mathsf T}\alpha-u^{\mathsf T}\beta\le\inf_{x\in R_v}c^{\mathsf T}x.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative multipliers for target lower and upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Target-LP Dual-State Validation Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on generic claims about active sets, scaling caches, factorizations, and other solver-internal state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\) be a transferred state component and let \(C_q(R_u,R_v)\) be the target solver's documented compatibility predicate. The component may be treated as valid at \(R_v\) only after \(C_q(R_u,R_v)\) is verified. If the solver exposes no such predicate, or any required correspondence, version, scaling, or dependency check is false or unresolved, \(q\) has no correctness-relevant validity at \(R_v\); it may be discarded or used only as an untrusted initialization when the solver permits this.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solver-internal state is valid only under its documented component contract; absent or unresolved compatibility checks, it cannot serve as a certificate.
assumptions_latex: The source and target relaxations are identifiable.
Correctness-relevant validity is distinguished from heuristic initialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\operatorname{verified}C_q(R_u,R_v)\Longrightarrow q\text{ is not a correctness certificate for }R_v.
review_flags: component-specific predicates must come from the applicable solver contract
knowledge_statements.title: Contract-Relative Eligibility of Solver-Internal State
Reuse Eligibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary compatibility conditions for reusing continuous-solver state between node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A state component from relaxation \(R_u\) is eligible for reuse at \(R_v\) only if its referenced rows, columns, variable types, scaling conventions, and objective sense have unchanged meanings under an explicit correspondence. A primal vector may be reused as a feasible start only if it satisfies every constraint and bound of \(R_v\). A dual vector, basis, active set, or factorization may be treated as valid only when the target solver's corresponding validity conditions hold; otherwise it may be used solely as an untrusted prediction or must be discarded. Any relaxation modification lacking a verified compatibility rule places the affected component outside the reuse boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse requires semantic correspondence and component-specific validity; unverified or invalidated state must be downgraded to a prediction or discarded.
assumptions_latex: The source and target relaxations have identifiable model versions.
Validity is assessed separately for each transferable state component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only components satisfying their compatibility predicate are eligible for correctness-relevant reuse at \(R_v\).
review_flags: needs a source defining solver-state compatibility and invalidation boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the Reuse Eligibility Boundaries leaf. The component-specific distinction between a valid state and an untrusted prediction is plausible, but no source establishes the listed semantic, scaling, basis, active-set, dual, and factorization compatibility boundaries.

children.title: Reoptimization Recovery
children.top_down_role: Fallback handling when transferred solver state is rejected, unstable, or ineffective.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Warm-Start Rejection Is Not a Relaxation Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between initialization failure and the target relaxation's mathematical status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_v\) be a target relaxation and \(S_v^0\) a transferred initialization. Rejection or numerical failure of \(S_v^0\) does not imply that \(R_v\) is infeasible, unbounded, or optimally solved. Without an independent status certificate for \(R_v\), the attempt is unresolved and recovery must try another initialization or leave the node unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure of a transferred start says nothing by itself about feasibility, boundedness, or optimality of the target relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The failure concerns initialization or numerical reoptimization rather than an independently validated model certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{reject}(S_v^0)\centernot\Longrightarrow\operatorname{infeasible}(R_v)\lor\operatorname{unbounded}(R_v)\lor\operatorname{optimal}(R_v).
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Rejection Is Not a Relaxation Status

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent recovery contract after transferred-state rejection or reoptimization failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given target relaxation \(R_v\) and transferred initialization \(S_v^0\), attempt reoptimization using \(S_v^0\). Accept a result only when the ordinary target-model validation certifies the reported optimal, infeasible, or unbounded status and every published bound. If initialization is rejected, numerical failure occurs, or validation fails, discard the transferred state and solve \(R_v\) from a valid cold initialization. If the cold solve also lacks a certified status, return \(\operatorname{unresolved}\) and publish no pruning bound. Componentwise intermediate fallbacks may be inserted only when the solver declares them valid target initializations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate the warm attempt normally; otherwise cold-start, and leave the node unresolved if no run certifies the target relaxation.
assumptions_latex: A valid cold initialization for \(R_v\) is available.
Published bounds and statuses pass the ordinary target-model certification tests.
Uncertified runs are not used for pruning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{output}\in\{\operatorname{certifiedStatus}(R_v),\operatorname{unresolved}\},\qquad \operatorname{unresolved}\Rightarrow\text{no pruning bound is published}.
review_flags: No solver-dependent ordering of partial state removal is asserted.
knowledge_statements.title: Validation-Gated Cold-Start Recovery
Reoptimization Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe recovery when a transferred continuous-solver state fails validation or numerical reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given target relaxation \(R_v\) and transferred initialization \(S_v^0\), attempt reoptimization while monitoring model consistency, primal and dual residuals, numerical status, and solver termination. If the attempt reports an invalid state, numerical failure, or an uncertified bound, successively remove suspect components: first stale factorization data, then basis or active-set status, then dual estimates, and finally the primal start. Reinitialize the remaining state and resolve after each removal. If no warm configuration passes the ordinary validation tests, solve \(R_v\) from the solver's cold initialization. Return a bound only from a run that independently certifies the required relaxation status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On warm-start failure, progressively discard transferred data and eventually cold-start; return only an independently validated relaxation bound.
assumptions_latex: The solver can restart \(R_v\) after selected state components are cleared.
A cold solve of \(R_v\) is available as the terminal fallback.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recovery either produces a normally certified result for \(R_v\) or reports failure without using the transferred state as a certificate.
review_flags: recovery ordering is a defensible design pattern but requires solver-specific sourcing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Reoptimization Recovery, and cold-start fallback with independent validation is appropriate. The prescribed order for removing factorization, basis or active-set, dual, and primal state is solver-dependent and has no cited support, so the exact algorithm cannot be reviewed as reliable.

children.title: Relaxation Pool-Reuse Interface
children.top_down_role: Sharing relaxation-strengthening information across nodes.

children.title: Cut-Pool Reuse
children.top_down_role: Sharing previously generated relaxation cuts across compatible search nodes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable scope certificate for a cut valid throughout one rooted search subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose cut \(c\) is certified valid for every locally feasible point in the subtree rooted at node \(u\). If the search tree supplies an ancestry witness that target node \(v\) descends from \(u\), then \(c\) is valid for reuse at \(v\). Absence of such ancestry does not certify reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subtree-scoped cut is reusable when recorded ancestry proves that the target descends from the cut's scope root.
assumptions_latex: The cut certificate covers the entire subtree rooted at u.
The recorded search-tree ancestry relation is correct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u\preceq v\land \operatorname{valid}(c,\operatorname{subtree}(u))\Longrightarrow\operatorname{valid}(c,F_v).

notation.meaning: Node u is an ancestor of node v.
Locally feasible set at target node v.

knowledge_statements.title: Subtree-Ancestry Reuse Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Branch-Local Cut Need Not Be Sibling-Valid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp global-versus-local scope boundary for pooled inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original domain be \(0\le x\le1\). At node \(u\), which imposes \(x\le\tfrac12\), the inequality \(x\le\tfrac12\) is valid. At a sibling node \(w\), which imposes \(x\ge\tfrac34\), the same inequality excludes every locally feasible point. Validity in one branch therefore does not authorize unscoped reuse in a sibling branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut valid because of one branch restriction can be invalid in a sibling subtree and therefore requires a scope tag.
assumptions_latex: Local cut validity may depend on inherited branch restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{valid}(c,F_u)\centernot\Longrightarrow\operatorname{valid}(c,F_w).

notation.meaning: Locally feasible sets of sibling nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: A Branch-Local Cut Need Not Be Sibling-Valid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retrieval, violation screening, activation, and reoptimization of reusable cuts at one node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), retrieve only pooled cuts whose recorded scope has been certified to contain \(F_v\). Evaluate each retrieved inequality at the current relaxation point, discard duplicates or numerically rejected entries under the pool policy, and select a finite batch of eligible cuts with violation above the activation tolerance. Add the batch atomically and reoptimize or revalidate the changed relaxation before using its solution, dual state, or objective value. Failure to find an activated cut is only a pool-management outcome and is not a certificate that no valid separating cut exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retrieve scope-valid cuts, screen and activate a finite violated batch, then reoptimize; an unproductive pool scan is not separation completeness.
assumptions_latex: Every retrieved cut has a checkable validity scope.
The target node feasible set is contained in that scope.
Numerical and duplicate filters do not override validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_v\text{ activated}\Longrightarrow F_v\subseteq\bigcap_{c\in C_v}H_c\text{ and the post-activation relaxation must be resolved or revalidated}.

notation.meaning: Locally feasible set at node v.

knowledge_statements.title: Scoped Cut-Pool Activation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: State transition caused by activating a retrieved cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If activation changes \(R_v\) to \(R_v'=R_v\cap H_c\ne R_v\), the stored primal solution, dual solution, status, basis or factorization, and objective value for \(R_v\) are not certificates for \(R_v'\) without revalidation. An independently certified lower bound for the old minimization relaxation remains valid, possibly weaker, because \(R_v'\subseteq R_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activating a cut invalidates the old solve state for the changed relaxation, although an old certified minimization lower bound remains safe.
assumptions_latex: The objective is unchanged and minimized.
The activated cut is valid at the node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_v'\subseteq R_v\Longrightarrow\underline z(R_v)\le\inf_{x\in R_v'}f(x),\quad\operatorname{solveState}(R_v)\not\equiv\operatorname{certificate}(R_v').

notation.meaning: Node relaxations before and after activation.

knowledge_statements.title: Activation Invalidates Pre-Cut Solve State
Cut-Pool Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of previously generated valid inequalities in node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a pool \(\mathcal C\) whose entry \(c\) stores an inequality \(a_c^{\mathsf T}x\le b_c\), its validity domain \(D_c\), and activity metadata. At node \(v\) with feasible region \(F_v\), retain \(c\) for possible insertion only when \(F_v\subseteq D_c\) has been certified. For a relaxation solution \(\bar x_v\), compute the violation \(a_c^{\mathsf T}\bar x_v-b_c\); insert selected eligible cuts whose violation exceeds a prescribed tolerance. Re-solve the relaxation after insertion. A cut may strengthen the node bound but may never delete a feasible integer point in \(F_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store cuts with validity domains, screen them at each node, and reinsert sufficiently violated cuts without excluding feasible integer solutions.
assumptions_latex: Each pooled inequality has a recorded validity domain.
The node feasible region \(F_v\) is known to lie in that domain before insertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inserted pooled cut is valid for \(F_v\), so reuse preserves correctness of the node relaxation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_v\) be a minimization relaxation and \(R_v'=R_v\cap\bigcap_{c\in C}H_c\). Then \(R_v'\subseteq R_v\) and \(\inf_{x\in R_v'}f(x)\ge\inf_{x\in R_v}f(x)\), with \(+\infty\) allowed.

children.title: Column-Pool Reuse
children.top_down_role: Sharing previously generated variables across compatible restricted masters.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of adding eligible pooled columns to a linear minimization restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq P'\) be eligible column sets for the same linear minimization master, and let \(z(P)\) and \(z(P')\) be their restricted-master optimal values, using \(+\infty\) for infeasibility. If every added column variable may take value zero, every solution over \(P\) extends to one over \(P'\), so \(z(P')\le z(P)\). This does not certify full-master optimality, which still requires exhaustive pricing over admissible omitted columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding eligible pooled columns can only improve or preserve a minimization restricted-master value, but cannot replace exact pricing.
assumptions_latex: Both restricted masters use the same rows, objective convention, and column semantics.
Every added column is eligible at the node.
Added column variables admit value zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\subseteq P'\Longrightarrow z(P')\le z(P).
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Monotonicity Under Column Reuse

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable applicability condition for reusing a generated column at a restricted node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a stored column is generated by an object \(y_p\), with master coefficients \(a(y_p)\) and cost \(c(y_p)\). At node \(v\), let \(Y_v\) be the admissible generator set. If \(y_p\in Y_v\) and the target master uses the same verified maps \(a(\cdot)\) and \(c(\cdot)\), inserting the stored column is equivalent to regenerating that admissible object at node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generated column is reusable when its generating object satisfies the node restrictions and its coefficient and cost mappings retain their meanings.
assumptions_latex: y_p\text{ and its generating block are retained with the pool entry.}
Y_v\text{ includes all inherited node restrictions on generated objects.}
a(\cdot)\text{ and }c(\cdot)\text{ have verified target-model meanings.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_p\in Y_v\land\operatorname{sameMap}_v(a,c)\Longrightarrow p\text{ is an admissible target-master column}.

notation.meaning: Generating object associated with stored column p.
Master coefficient vector and objective cost generated by y_p.

knowledge_statements.title: Generated-Column Node-Eligibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pool Exhaustion Is Not a Pricing Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite omitted-column example showing that an unproductive pool scan cannot certify full-master optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x_0-x_1:x_0+x_1=1,\ x_0,x_1\ge0\}\). If the restricted master and reusable pool contain only column \(x_0\), the restricted value is \(1\) and the pool scan finds no entry to add. The omitted admissible column \(x_1\) has negative reduced cost and gives full-master value \(-1\). Thus pool exhaustion does not certify absence of improving admissible columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reusable pool may omit an improving column, so an unproductive pool scan cannot replace exhaustive pricing.
assumptions_latex: The reusable pool is a proper finite subset of the full admissible column family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{noImprovingColumnInPool}\centernot\Longrightarrow\operatorname{noImprovingAdmissibleColumn}.

notation.meaning: Variables associated with the stored and omitted master columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Pool Exhaustion Is Not a Pricing Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Current-Dual Screening of Eligible Pooled Columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retrieval, reduced-cost screening, insertion, and reoptimization for columns already certified eligible at the node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_v\) be the current restricted-master columns and \(E_v\) the finite set of pooled columns certified eligible at node \(v\). Solve the linear restricted master for a certified dual vector \(\pi_v\). For each \(p\in E_v\setminus P_v\), recompute \(\bar c_p=c_p-a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi_v\) under the current master conventions. Insert any selected finite subset with \(\bar c_p<-\varepsilon\), then reoptimize before using new duals or a new restricted-master value. If none passes, invoke the full node-pricing oracle; pool screening alone is not a termination certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score eligible stored columns using current duals, insert selected improving entries, reoptimize, and retain full pricing for termination certification.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is a linear minimization problem.
Every member of \(E_v\) has passed node-eligibility and mapping checks.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists p\in E_v:\bar c_p<-\varepsilon\centernot\Longrightarrow\text{no improving admissible omitted column}.

notation.meaning: Current and eligible pooled column sets.
Current reduced cost of column p.

knowledge_statements.title: Current-Dual Screening of Eligible Pooled Columns
Column-Pool Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of generated master-problem columns across compatible node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a pool \(\mathcal P\) in which each column \(p\) stores its coefficient vector, cost, generating subproblem, and applicability domain \(D_p\). At node \(v\), map every compatible pooled column into the current restricted master and discard any column whose definition or applicability is invalid under the node restrictions. Solve the restricted master, obtain dual multipliers \(\pi_v\), and evaluate pooled reduced costs \(\bar c_p=c_p-\pi_v^{\mathsf T}a_p\). Insert useful eligible columns, but terminate column generation only after the node pricing oracle proves that no admissible omitted column has improving reduced cost within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse compatible columns to seed the restricted master, but retain pricing-oracle certification before declaring column-generation optimality.
assumptions_latex: The master is a minimization problem with a well-defined pricing oracle.
Each pooled column has stable coefficients and a recorded applicability domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pool reuse can accelerate the restricted master but cannot replace the final pricing certificate.

reduced cost of pooled column p
