children.title: Pool Compatibility Screening
children.top_down_role: Node-context checks governing whether pooled entries remain applicable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimensional Agreement Does Not Establish Pool Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic-mapping counterexample to dimension-only screening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stored coefficient vector \((1,0)\) for ordered source variables \((x_1,x_2)\) represents \(x_1\le0\). If the target interprets the same positions as \((x_2,x_1)\), blindly copying \((1,0)\) imposes \(x_2\le0\). The vectors have equal dimensions, yet the entry has changed meaning and may exclude target-feasible points. Thus dimensional agreement alone is not a compatibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A same-sized coefficient vector can refer to different variables after reordering, so dimension matching alone cannot certify compatibility.
assumptions_latex: Coefficient positions obtain meaning from an ordered variable mapping.
The target may reorder or replace model entities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim(a_e)=\dim(M_v)\centernot\Longrightarrow\operatorname{compatible}(e,v).

notation.meaning: Stored coefficient vector of pool entry e.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimensional Agreement Does Not Establish Pool Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional compatibility induced by nested validity scopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let entry \(e\) be applicable on domain \(\Omega_e\), and define scope compatibility with node \(v\) by \(F_v\subseteq\Omega_e\). This relation is directional: an entry valid on a broad domain may be used at a narrower node, while an entry valid only on the narrow domain need not be valid in the broader context. Successful reuse therefore cannot generally be reversed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility is directional: broad-scope information may remain valid at a narrower node even when narrow-scope information is invalid more broadly.
assumptions_latex: Compatibility includes containment of the target feasible domain in the entry's validity domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_v\subseteq\Omega_e\centernot\Longrightarrow\Omega_e\subseteq F_v.

notation.meaning: Validity or applicability domain of entry e.

knowledge_statements.title: Applicability Compatibility Is Generally Asymmetric

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auditable metadata for evaluating a stored entry against a target node model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a pool entry as \(e=(\tau,a,\mathcal I,\nu,\sigma,\Delta,\Omega)\), where \(\tau\) is its type, \(a\) its algebraic payload, \(\mathcal I\) the stable identifiers and semantic roles of referenced model entities, \(\nu\) their recorded versions, \(\sigma\) the coefficient and objective scaling convention, \(\Delta\) the dependency set, and \(\Omega\) the applicability scope. These fields expose the obligations for identity, version, scaling, dependency, and scope screening but do not themselves certify that those obligations hold at a target node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reusable entry can record type, algebra, stable references, versions, scaling, dependencies, and scope so compatibility obligations are auditable.
assumptions_latex: Target models expose corresponding entity, version, and scaling metadata.
The applicability scope supports a target-node membership or containment test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e=(\tau,a,\mathcal I,\nu,\sigma,\Delta,\Omega)\text{ records the stated compatibility obligations without itself proving compatibility}.

notation.meaning: Referenced model entities with stable semantic identities.
Dependencies required by the pool entry.

knowledge_statements.title: Pool-Entry Compatibility Metadata

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-dispatched screening with accept, reject, and unresolved outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Evaluate the checks in the Composed Pool-Compatibility Certificate against the current node version. Return \(\mathsf{accept}\) only if every required check is proved true. Return \(\mathsf{reject}\) if any required identity, version, convention, dependency, scope, or type-specific check is proved false. Return \(\mathsf{unresolved}\) if no check is false but at least one cannot be verified. Only \(\mathsf{accept}\) permits activation; rejected or unresolved entries are withheld and routed to stale-entry handling or later recertification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept only fully certified entries, reject proven mismatches, and withhold entries whose obligations cannot be resolved.
assumptions_latex: Each required check has outcomes true, false, or unverifiable.
Cut and column type-specific validators are available when their certificates are claimed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{screen}(e,v)=\mathsf{accept}\Longleftrightarrow\bigwedge_k\operatorname{check}_k(e,v)=\mathsf{true}.
knowledge_statements.title: Three-Way Pool Compatibility Screening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common positive compatibility predicate for cut and column entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pool entry \(e\) is certified compatible with node model \(M_v\) exactly when a certificate verifies: a semantics-preserving mapping of every referenced entity; agreement of all required versions and coefficient, objective, and scaling conventions; satisfaction of every recorded dependency; containment of the target domain in the entry's applicability scope; and the entry-type obligation—cut validity on \(F_v\) or column-generator feasibility with a well-defined target-master mapping. Only a certified-compatible entry may alter the node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility composes semantic mapping, versions, scaling, dependencies, scope, and the cut- or column-specific validity certificate.
assumptions_latex: The pool entry records the metadata required by each check.
The target model exposes corresponding identities and conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{compatible}(e,v)\iff I_e\land V_e\land S_e\land D_e\land A_e\land T_e.

notation.meaning: Identity, version, scaling, dependency, applicability, and entry-type certificate checks.

review_flags: the concrete witness format is model-interface dependent
knowledge_statements.title: Composed Pool-Compatibility Certificate
Pool Compatibility Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate governing whether a stored cut or column may enter a node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For node model \(M_v\) and pool entry \(e\), define \(\operatorname{compatible}(e,v)\) to hold exactly when: the identifiers and meanings of every referenced row and variable match \(M_v\); the entry's coefficients, objective convention, scaling, and integrality interpretation remain valid; every recorded dependency is present at the required version; and the node domain lies within the entry's applicability domain. For a cut, this includes certified validity over the node feasible set. For a column, it includes feasibility under node restrictions and a well-defined mapping into the current master. Only entries satisfying this predicate may affect the node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An entry is compatible only when its model references, semantics, dependencies, and validity domain all match the current node.
assumptions_latex: Every pool entry carries provenance, dependencies, and an applicability domain.
The node model has stable versioned identifiers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{compatible}(e,v)\) is required before entry \(e\) may alter the relaxation at node \(v\).

notation.meaning: model of the relaxation at node v

review_flags: requires an authoritative source for pool-entry provenance and compatibility semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is correct for Pool Compatibility Screening, and the statement matches the local container. No source supports the proposed provenance, version, scaling, dependency, applicability-domain, cut-validity, and column-feasibility predicate as a unified eligibility rule.

children.title: Stale Pool Entry Handling
children.top_down_role: Treatment of obsolete, invalidated, dominated, or numerically unsuitable pooled information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract handling of a pooled cut or column after its current eligibility becomes unestablished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When an entry \(e\) becomes correctness-stale, deactivate it before it can alter a relaxation. Recheck its provenance, validity scope, and representation against the current model and node domain. Reactivate \(e\) only if those checks re-establish eligibility; otherwise retain it in an inactive or quarantined state or delete it. Using an unvalidated entry can invalidate the relaxation or a bound derived from it, whereas deleting an eligible but inactive entry can only forgo possible computational benefit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deactivate stale entries, revalidate them against the current context, and reactivate only those that pass; unresolved entries remain quarantined or are deleted.
assumptions_latex: Eligibility checking is sound for the current model and node domain.
Inactive or quarantined entries cannot affect the active relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No correctness-stale entry affects a relaxation before current eligibility is re-established.}

notation.meaning: a pooled cut or column entry

review_flags: Specific aging thresholds, retry schedules, and physical-deletion policies are solver-dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Preserving Stale-Entry Lifecycle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifecycle distinction between entries whose current eligibility is unestablished and valid entries retained without recent use.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cached pool entry is correctness-stale when its recorded provenance, validity scope, or model version no longer establishes eligibility for the current relaxation. It is performance-stale when it remains valid and applicable but has not recently been useful. A correctness-stale entry must remain inactive until revalidated; retaining or deleting a performance-stale entry affects resource use and search performance but not relaxation validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An entry with unestablished current eligibility is correctness-stale and must stay inactive; an unused but still valid entry is only performance-stale.
assumptions_latex: Each pooled entry records enough provenance or scope information to determine whether its present eligibility has been established.
An entry is screened before incorporation into a node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Unestablished eligibility requires exclusion, whereas inactivity alone does not imply invalidity.}
knowledge_statements.title: Correctness-Stale and Performance-Stale Pool Entries
Stale Pool Entry Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalidation, revalidation, and eviction of obsolete cut or column pool entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each pool entry \(e\) with dependency versions, an applicability domain, and an activity timestamp. Mark \(e\) stale whenever a referenced model object changes, its validity certificate expires, repeated screening rejects it, or its inactivity exceeds a chosen retention threshold. A stale entry must not affect a node relaxation. Revalidate it against the current model and node domain; if revalidation succeeds, update its metadata and return it to the eligible pool. Otherwise quarantine or delete it. Eviction based only on inactivity may change performance, whereas deletion after failed validity checking is required for correctness whenever the entry could otherwise alter a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stale entries are excluded, revalidated when possible, and otherwise quarantined or evicted; validity failures require exclusion for correctness.
assumptions_latex: Pool entries have versioned provenance and mutable lifecycle metadata.
Eligibility screening occurs before an entry affects a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No stale entry influences the search until its compatibility and validity have been re-established.
review_flags: retention and revalidation policy requires an implementation-oriented source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Stale Pool Entry Handling. The distinction between correctness-driven exclusion and performance-driven inactivity eviction is useful, but the staleness triggers, certificate expiration, revalidation, quarantine, and deletion policy are implementation-specific and uncited.

children.title: Branching-Statistics Reuse
children.top_down_role: Search-wide accumulation of branching information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid branching rule that probes candidates until their accumulated directional statistics reach a reliability threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For branching candidate \(j\) and direction \(d\in\{-,+\}\), let \(n_j^d\) count admissible historical observations and fix \(r\ge1\). If \(n_j^-\ge r\) and \(n_j^+\ge r\), the candidate may be scored from its stored directional estimates. Otherwise, a limited strong-branching probe or declared fallback supplies missing information; only valid probe outcomes update the statistics. Probing is thereby concentrated on candidates whose directional histories have not reached the reliability threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reliability branching probes candidates with insufficient directional history and reuses stored estimates after both directions reach a chosen reliability threshold.
assumptions_latex: Historical observations use a comparable objective and bound convention.
Only valid directional outcomes update the statistics.
\(r\) is a fixed positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: n_j^-\ge r\land n_j^+\ge r\implies j\text{ may be scored without a new reliability probe}.

notation.meaning: Number of admissible observations for candidate j in direction d.

knowledge_statements.title: Reliability Branching from Reused Statistics

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Historical Branching Statistics Are Noncertifying Predictors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for search-wide reuse of empirical branching effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A branching-effect estimate computed at earlier nodes need not equal or bound the effect of the same branch at a later node because domains, active rows, cuts, and relaxation degeneracy may differ. Reused estimates may rank candidates but cannot alone certify a child bound, infeasibility, dominance, or pruning. Arbitrarily inaccurate estimates may change search effort without compromising an exact search whose pruning uses independent certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reused branching statistics can be arbitrarily inaccurate and are suitable for ranking, not for bound or pruning certificates.
assumptions_latex: Exact pruning uses independently certified bounds or infeasibility.
Node relaxations may differ across the tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\Delta_j^d\text{ historical}\centernot\implies\widehat\Delta_j^d\le\Delta_j^d\text{ or }\widehat\Delta_j^d\ge\Delta_j^d.

notation.meaning: Predicted branching effect from reused statistics.
Actual branching effect at the current node.

knowledge_statements.title: Historical Branching Statistics Are Noncertifying Predictors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic maintenance cost for count-and-sum branching statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each candidate-direction pair \((j,d)\) stores an observation count \(n_j^d\) and cumulative scalar \(q_j^d\), incorporating one admissible scalar observation takes \(O(1)\) arithmetic after table access. For \(m\) candidates and two directions, the table uses \(O(m)\) scalar storage. These bounds exclude the cost of producing the branch observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Count-and-sum branching statistics take constant update work and linear storage in the number of candidates.
assumptions_latex: Candidate indices provide direct or expected-constant-time table access.
Each observation updates one candidate-direction pair with one scalar.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{update}}=O(1),\qquad M_{\mathrm{table}}=O(m).
knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Cost Sufficient-Statistic Update

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Objective Transformation of Directional Statistics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of bound-difference statistics under common objective rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every directional observation is an objective-bound difference divided by an unchanged branch displacement. Under \(f'(x)=a f(x)+b\) with \(a>0\), every such observation and its arithmetic mean are multiplied by \(a\), while \(b\) cancels. Therefore candidate rankings produced by the same positively homogeneous score are unchanged under a common transformation. Statistics accumulated under inconsistent scale factors are not comparable by this invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common positive objective rescaling uniformly rescales directional statistics, while translation has no effect; inconsistent scales cannot safely be mixed.
assumptions_latex: All compared observations use the same positive scale factor \(a\).
Observations use objective-bound differences and unchanged branch displacements.
The candidate score is positively homogeneous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_j^{d\prime}=a p_j^d\quad\text{and the common-score ranking is unchanged}.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Objective Transformation of Directional Statistics

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combination of available directional branching-effect estimates into a two-child candidate score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node where integer variable \(x_j\) has fractional part \(f_j\in(0,1)\), let \(p_j^-,p_j^+\ge0\) be directional bound-improvement estimates per unit displacement. Define \(g_j^-=p_j^-f_j\), \(g_j^+=p_j^+(1-f_j)\), and, for fixed \(\mu\in[0,1]\), \(s_j=(1-\mu)\min\{g_j^-,g_j^+\}+\mu\max\{g_j^-,g_j^+\}\). Candidates may be ranked by \(s_j\), but the score certifies neither child bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale directional estimates by branch displacement and combine them with a weighted minimum–maximum score; the result is predictive, not certifying.
assumptions_latex: x_j\text{ is fractional at the current relaxation solution.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational finite-certified count-and-sum update for search-wide directional pseudocost reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For integer candidate \(j\) and direction \(d\in\{-,+\}\), initialize \(n_j^d=q_j^d=0\). An ordinary observation is admissible when the parent and child relaxation optimal values \(B\) and \(B_d\) are finite and certified under one minimization objective scale, the branch displacement \(\delta_j^d>0\), and the child solve is not unresolved or merely cutoff-censored. Set
\[
r_j^d=\frac{\max\{0,B_d-B\}}{\delta_j^d},\qquad n_j^d\leftarrow n_j^d+1,
\qquad q_j^d\leftarrow q_j^d+r_j^d.
\]
When \(n_j^d>0\), define \(p_j^d=q_j^d/n_j^d\); otherwise use a declared default or probe. Infeasible children and censored outcomes require a separately declared finite-imputation convention and must not be silently mixed with ordinary observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update a directional pseudocost from comparable finite certified parent and child relaxation optima; unresolved, cutoff-censored, and untreated infeasible outcomes do not enter the ordinary mean.

\(\delta_j^d>0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-wide updating and reuse of empirical branching effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each integer variable \(j\) and direction \(d\in\{-,+\}\), maintain a count \(n_j^d\) and cumulative normalized bound improvement \(q_j^d\). At a later node, use \(p_j^d=q_j^d/n_j^d\) when \(n_j^d>0\) to predict directional improvement; use a prescribed default or strong-branching probe otherwise. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent branch-and-bound over a shared frontier, incumbent, and in-flight-work state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a synchronized frontier \(Q\) with the root and a shared incumbent \(U=+\infty\). A worker atomically acquires a node, records it as in flight, computes a valid node bound, and either validly fathoms it or inserts exhaustive children. Feasible incumbent updates retain the best objective value atomically. Termination is permitted only after a consistent protocol establishes that both queued and in-flight work are empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers share a synchronized frontier and incumbent, account for in-flight nodes, and terminate only at global quiescence.
assumptions_latex: Branching children exhaustively cover every unresolved parent region.
Every pruning decision uses a valid certificate or bound.
Synchronization prevents lost frontier work and lost improving incumbents.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q=\varnothing\land A=\varnothing\Longrightarrow\text{all generated search regions are closed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Synchronized Shared-Memory Tree Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-memory exhaustion certificate accounting for queued and worker-owned regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A consistent snapshot satisfying \(Q=A=\varnothing\) certifies search exhaustion when every acquired region was validly fathomed or replaced by exhaustive children. A finite incumbent is then globally optimal; if no incumbent exists, the original problem is infeasible. The test \(Q=\varnothing\) alone is insufficient because an in-flight worker may still generate children or an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty queue certifies completion only when no worker owns unresolved work.
assumptions_latex: The quiescence protocol cannot miss concurrent acquisition, insertion, or completion.
All completed node closures are valid and branching coverage is exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q=A=\varnothing\Longrightarrow\bigl(U<+\infty\Rightarrow U=z^*\bigr)\land\bigl(U=+\infty\Rightarrow\text{infeasible}\bigr).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes conservative stale cutoff reads from unsafe lost updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let \(U_{\mathrm{new}}\le U_{\mathrm{old}}\) be values of feasible incumbents. Pruning a node only when \(L_v\ge U_{\mathrm{old}}\) remains sound, although it may miss pruning enabled by \(U_{\mathrm{new}}\). An update protocol that can overwrite the better incumbent by the worse value does not preserve the shared incumbent invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reading an older feasible cutoff only loses pruning power; losing a better incumbent update violates shared-state correctness.
assumptions_latex: Both incumbent values are attained by feasible solutions.
\(L_v\) is a valid lower bound for node \(v\).

Shared-Memory Tree Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent branch-and-bound with a shared frontier, incumbent, and global bound state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a thread-safe frontier \(Q\) with the root node and a shared incumbent value \(U=+\infty\) for minimization. Each worker atomically removes a node \(v\), solves its relaxation to obtain a valid lower bound \(L_v\), and prunes when \(L_v\ge U\). It atomically lowers \(U\) upon finding a better feasible integer solution and otherwise inserts the generated children into \(Q\). Updates of frontier membership, incumbent data, and termination counters must be linearizable or protected by an equivalent synchronization protocol. Terminate only when no queued or in-flight node can have lower bound below \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers process a synchronized shared frontier, update a shared incumbent, and stop only when no queued or active node can improve it.
assumptions_latex: Every node relaxation supplies a valid lower bound for a minimization problem.
Shared state updates obey a synchronization protocol preventing lost work or incumbents.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, the incumbent is globally optimal if it is finite; if no incumbent exists, the problem is infeasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Frontier Bound under Distributed Ownership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of valid bounds over all unresolved distributed search regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F(t)\) contain every unresolved node that is queued, being processed, or in transit at time \(t\). If each \(L_v\) is a valid lower bound for the node region \(X_v\), and \(\{X_v:v\in\mathcal F(t)\}\) covers every unresolved feasible solution, then, whenever \(\mathcal F(t)\ne\varnothing\), \(L(t)=\min_{v\in\mathcal F(t)}L_v\) is a valid lower bound on every unresolved feasible objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum valid bound over all queued, processing, and in-transit nodes is a valid global frontier bound when those nodes cover every unresolved solution.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
Every unresolved feasible solution lies in a region represented in \(\mathcal F(t)\).
Each \(L_v\) is a valid lower bound for \(X_v\).
\(\mathcal F(t)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(t)\le \inf\{f(x):x\text{ is unresolved and feasible}\}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why termination detection must account for node-transfer messages.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inactive workers and empty queues do not imply completion while unresolved work is in transit.

The sender removes \(v\) before receipt.

Delay may therefore add work but cannot by itself remove an improving solution.

\(U_{\mathrm{new}}\le U_{\mathrm{old}}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementation-independent safety invariant for partitioned search.

Coverage is preserved when every unresolved root-feasible solution lies in \(\bigcup_{v\in\mathcal F(t)}X_v\), branching replaces a parent by exhaustive children, transfers continuously represent the moved region, and removed regions are validly fathomed.

Branches exhaust their parent regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion conclusion under abstract distributed-search safety hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-valued minimization problem, suppose distributed search preserves frontier coverage, uses exhaustive branching and valid fathoming, and every accepted transfer completes or is recovered. If a detector certifies that all workers are inactive, all queues are empty, and no unresolved transfer is in transit, then no unresolved feasible solution remains. A validated incumbent is globally optimal; if none exists, the root is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: True global quiescence proves completion when coverage, fathoming, and transfer recovery are sound.
assumptions_latex: The search preserves the distributed frontier coverage invariant.
Branching and fathoming are sound.
Every accepted transfer completes or is recovered.
The detector accounts for every worker, queue, and in-transit record.
Every feasible solution has a finite objective value, and unbounded cases are excluded or separately resolved.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Distributed Quiescence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract crash-recoverable representation of queued, executing, transferred, and closed subtrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a durable table mapping each subtree identifier v to one state in \{\operatorname{owned}(i),\operatorname{inTransit}(i,j,r),\operatorname{owned}(j),\operatorname{closed}\}, where r is a unique transfer identifier. Ownership transitions are durable and linearizable; an in-transit entry retains a durable subtree image, retries with r are idempotent, processing is permitted only to the recorded owner, and closure requires valid fathoming evidence. Recovery reassigns every nonclosed durable entry to a live worker before termination may be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A durable ownership table represents every unresolved subtree exactly once or as a recoverable transfer and prevents termination while durable work remains.
assumptions_latex: Ownership-table transitions are durable and linearizable.
Subtree and transfer identifiers are globally unique.
Every in-transit entry has a durable subtree image.
Only valid fathoming changes an entry to closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every nonclosed subtree has one recorded processing owner or one durable recoverable transfer record.}

knowledge_statements.title: Durable Ownership-Table Distributed Search Protocol

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage and completion under a fixed durable crash-stop recovery model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose branching is exhaustive, every closure is valid, and the durable ownership protocol is followed. After any finite sequence of worker crash-stop failures and recoveries, reassigning every nonclosed durable entry preserves coverage of all unresolved root-feasible solutions. If every surviving entry is eventually processed or validly closed and no ownership transition remains pending, durable global quiescence certifies optimality or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Durable ownership permits recovery from finitely many worker crashes without losing unresolved regions; eventual exhaustion then certifies completion.
assumptions_latex: Only finitely many crash-stop events occur before final recovery.
Durable metadata and subtree images survive the failures.
Branching, bounding, and fathoming are sound.
Every surviving nonclosed entry is eventually processed or validly closed.
Unbounded cases are excluded or separately resolved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_{\mathrm{unresolved}}\subseteq\bigcup_{v:\operatorname{state}(v)\ne\operatorname{closed}}X_v,\qquad\text{final durable quiescence implies exact completion}.

Distributed Tree Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound with partitioned frontiers and coordinated incumbent and bound information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the open-node frontier into local queues \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\). Worker \(i\) repeatedly solves nodes from \(Q_i\), prunes a node \(v\) when its valid lower bound \(L_v\) is no smaller than the latest accepted global incumbent \(U\), broadcasts improved feasible incumbents, and transfers unprocessed subtrees according to the work-balancing protocol. Messages carry unique node identifiers and versioned incumbent data so duplication or delay cannot delete required work or increase the accepted incumbent. Terminate through a distributed detection protocol only after every queue and worker is inactive and no node-transfer message is in transit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers search partitioned frontiers, exchange subtrees and incumbents, and use distributed termination detection that accounts for in-transit work.
assumptions_latex: Node bounds are valid for a common minimization objective.
Communication may be delayed but the protocol detects duplication, loss, and messages in transit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite incumbent returned at certified global quiescence is optimal; absence of an incumbent certifies infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Estimate-Based Allocation Can Approach a Factor Two
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Makespan boundary when equal estimates hide unequal actual subtree work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two workers and three subtrees with equal estimates, suppose an allocation pairs two subtrees on one worker. If their actual works are \(M,M\) and the singleton has work \(1\), that allocation has makespan \(2M\), while assigning one heavy subtree to each worker has makespan \(M+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal estimates can produce an initial allocation whose actual makespan approaches twice optimum.
assumptions_latex: Estimates need not approximate actual work.
Subtrees remain indivisible after allocation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{C}{C^*}=\frac{2M}{M+1}\to2.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unavoidable initial idling with too few indivisible live subtrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(k\) indivisible live subtrees are assigned at most once among \(m>k\) workers, at most \(k\) workers receive work. At least \(m-k\) workers initially idle unless further expansion, splitting, or replication is allowed.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For frontier A, workers i=1,\ldots,m, and estimated processing times p_{iv}\ge0, choose z_{iv}\in\{0,1\} with \sum_i z_{iv}=1 for every v and minimize C subject to \sum_{v\in A}p_{iv}z_{iv}\le C for every i. Estimates remain fixed during assignment.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting with the root, perform a prescribed finite number of expansions, each replacing a selected live node by exhaustive children and retaining closure evidence for every child immediately fathomed. The remaining live nodes form a frontier cut A. Assign every v\in A to exactly one worker with its complete inherited node state. The live regions are pairwise disjoint and, together with the recorded closed regions, cover the root search region.

assumptions_latex: Every branch partitions its parent's unresolved region.
Every removed child has valid closure evidence.
Each live node is assigned to exactly one worker.

Initial Subtree Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assignment of an initial disjoint search partition to parallel workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from the root, branch sequentially until an antichain \(A=\{v_1,\ldots,v_k\}\) of live nodes is obtained, with \(k\ge m\) when possible for \(m\) workers. Estimate each subtree workload by a nonnegative weight \(w(v)\). Choose disjoint assignments \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\) whose union is \(A\), preferably minimizing \(\max_i\sum_{v\in A_i}w(v)\), and initialize worker \(i\)'s frontier with \(A_i\). Preserve any nodes fathomed during the initial expansion as closed. Because the live antichain partitions the remaining root search region, no feasible solution is omitted or assigned to two initial subtrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expand to a live antichain and partition its estimated subtree workloads among workers, preserving complete and nonoverlapping search coverage.
assumptions_latex: Branching children partition the unfathomed feasible region of their parent.
Each live node receives a nonnegative workload estimate.

children.title: Dynamic Work Redistribution
children.top_down_role: Transfer of active subtrees as worker workloads change during search.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Work Sharing and Work Stealing Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Donor-initiated and receiver-initiated variants of runtime subtree redistribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In work sharing, a worker with transferable load offers an open subtree to another worker. In work stealing, an idle or underloaded worker requests an open subtree from a selected victim. Either variant preserves exhaustive search only if every accepted handoff keeps the subtree represented by the sender, receiver, or an in-transit record and results in exactly one active owner.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic redistribution may use donor-initiated work sharing or receiver-initiated work stealing; correctness requires a lossless single-owner handoff.
assumptions_latex: Only open unresolved subtrees are transferable.
The transfer protocol prevents permanent loss and simultaneous active ownership.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A lossless single-owner handoff preserves the union of unresolved search regions.}
knowledge_statements.title: Work Sharing and Work Stealing Variants

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplication caused by retry without idempotent subtree identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sender \(i\) transfers subtree \(v\); receiver \(j\) accepts it, but the acknowledgement is lost. If a retry is treated as a new subtree \(v'\), then \(X_v=X_{v'}\) and both copies may be searched.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lost acknowledgement and non-idempotent retry can duplicate active subtree ownership.
assumptions_latex: Retries lack a stable identity or duplicate check.
The first transfer succeeds but its acknowledgement is lost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_v=X_{v'}\land v\ne v'\Longrightarrow\text{active ownership is not unique}.
review_flags: Duplicate work need not destroy coverage, but invalidates disjoint-ownership and work-count claims.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Ownership Execution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss caused by deleting the sender copy before durable receipt.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If sender \(i\) deletes the only representation of unresolved subtree \(v\) before receiver \(j\) durably records it, loss of the transfer leaves no queued, executing, or in-transit record for \(X_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting the sender copy before durable receipt can permanently omit an unresolved region.
assumptions_latex: Subtree \(v\) has no other active or durable representation.
Transfer can fail after sender deletion but before receiver insertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_v\nsubseteq\bigcup_{u\in\mathcal F}X_u.

notation.meaning: region represented by the transferred subtree

knowledge_statements.title: Lost-Handoff Execution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lossless ownership transition for sharing or stealing one open subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a uniquely identified open subtree v, pause its processing, create transfer identifier r, durably retain a recovery copy, and send (v,r,\operatorname{state}(v)) to receiver j. The receiver durably stages the state under key (v,r), treats repeats as the same insertion, and acknowledges r. Receipt of that acknowledgement commits the transfer: the donor never resumes v and may delete its recovery copy, while the receiver activates the staged copy. A timeout resends the same r. Cancellation may restore donor processing only after confirming that no receiver commit occurred. An executing node is transferable only from a checkpoint representing its complete unresolved continuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Paused processing, durable idempotent staging, acknowledgement, and commit provide a lossless single-owner handoff.
assumptions_latex: Subtree and transfer identifiers are unique.
Durable staging and commit status survive relevant failures.
Duplicate keys are suppressed.
Cancellation is coordinated with commit status.
A checkpoint completely represents any transferred executing continuation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{After recovery, }v\text{ is donor-owned, receiver-owned, or durably staged, and is neither lost nor processed concurrently.}
review_flags: The receiver must not activate before commitment, and cancellation requires authoritative commit-status resolution.
knowledge_statements.title: Idempotent Subtree-Handoff State Machine

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stop-and-wait data-and-acknowledgement bound under bounded consecutive message loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose at most r consecutive data messages and at most r consecutive acknowledgements for one idempotent handoff may be lost, and every timeout resends the same data identifier. Then a successful acknowledgement is obtained after at most (r+1)^2 data transmissions and r+1 acknowledgement transmissions. Without a finite-loss or eventual-delivery assumption, no finite completion or message bound follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded consecutive loss gives a finite stop-and-wait retry bound; arbitrary loss permits unbounded retries.
assumptions_latex: r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
At most r consecutive transmissions of either message type are lost.
Retries use the same idempotency key.
Timeout and nonlost-delivery times are bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{data}}\le(r+1)^2,\qquad N_{\mathrm{ack}}\le r+1.

notation.meaning: maximum consecutive losses in either message phase

review_flags: This bound applies to the stated stop-and-wait phase, not arbitrary transport or multi-phase commit protocols.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Retry Handoff Message Count
Dynamic Work Redistribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime transfer of open subtrees from overloaded workers to underloaded workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let worker \(i\) have estimated queued work \(W_i=\sum_{v\in Q_i}w(v)\). When \(W_i-W_j\) exceeds a prescribed imbalance threshold and worker \(j\) can accept work, select a set \(T\subseteq Q_i\) of complete open subtrees, atomically remove \(T\) from \(Q_i\), serialize their node states, and transfer them to \(Q_j\). The receiver acknowledges durable insertion before the sender deletes its recovery copy. Reject or suppress duplicate transfers by unique subtree identifiers. Transfer only when the predicted reduction in imbalance exceeds the communication and reconstruction cost, and never transfer a node currently being processed without an explicit checkpoint protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move identified open subtrees from overloaded to underloaded workers using acknowledged ownership transfer and a cost-aware imbalance threshold.
assumptions_latex: Open subtrees have unique identifiers and transferable node states.
Work estimates and transfer-cost estimates are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each acknowledged subtree has exactly one active owner, and redistribution preserves the union of unprocessed search regions.

notation.meaning: estimated queued workload of worker i
set of subtrees selected for transfer

review_flags: ownership-transfer and cost-threshold protocol needs a distributed tree-search source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Dynamic Work Redistribution. The acknowledged ownership transfer, recovery-copy deletion, duplicate suppression, checkpoint restriction, and cost-benefit trigger are substantial distributed-system claims with no cited support. A distributed branch-and-bound work-stealing or load-balancing source is required.

children.title: Load-Imbalance Detection
children.top_down_role: Search-state indicators used to identify uneven worker utilization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incoherent Snapshots Can Create Spurious Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of imbalance classification when worker loads are sampled at different logical times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the coherent two-worker load vector changes atomically from \((1,1)\) to \((0,0)\). Reading worker 1 after the change and worker 2 before it yields \((0,1)\). Both coherent states are balanced, but the mixed observation is unequal and can be classified as imbalanced. Thus individually valid asynchronous measurements need not represent any global workload state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Loads read at different logical times can report imbalance even though every coherent system state is balanced.
assumptions_latex: Worker loads may change between monitor reads.
The detector treats separately collected components as one load vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (1,1)\to(0,0)\text{ coherently, while the mixed read }(0,1)\text{ is spuriously imbalanced}.
knowledge_statements.title: Incoherent Snapshots Can Create Spurious Imbalance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Queue Length Is Not Equivalent to Remaining Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Both failures of unweighted queue length as a workload proxy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Queue lengths \((1,1)\) can correspond to works \((M,1)\), while lengths \((M,1)\) can correspond to total works \((1,1)\) when the first queue contains \(M\) jobs of cost \(1/M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal queue lengths can hide severe imbalance, and unequal lengths can represent equal remaining work.
assumptions_latex: Node processing costs may differ.
Queue length is unweighted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (|Q_1|,|Q_2|)=(1,1)\centernot\Rightarrow W_1=W_2,\qquad |Q_1|\ne|Q_2|\centernot\Rightarrow W_1\ne W_2.

notation.meaning: actual remaining work of worker i

knowledge_statements.title: Queue Length Is Not Equivalent to Remaining Work

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oscillation under a single noisy classification threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(I_{2k}=\tau-\varepsilon\) and \(I_{2k+1}=\tau+\varepsilon\), a detector that classifies imbalance exactly when \(I_k>\tau\) changes state at every sample. Separate entry and exit thresholds or a persistence rule exclude this pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise around one threshold can alternate the imbalance state indefinitely.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\).
The detector uses one threshold without persistence or hysteresis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I_{2k}=\tau-\varepsilon,\ I_{2k+1}=\tau+\varepsilon\Longrightarrow\text{classification changes at every sample}.
review_flags: This is a detection boundary, not a redistribution rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Chatter without Hysteresis

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stale Estimates Can Reverse the Imbalance Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporal validity boundary for load measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A detector records \(\widehat W=(M,1)\). Before action, worker 1 completes its load and worker 2 receives work \(M\), giving \(W=(0,M+1)\). The estimated and actual overloaded workers are opposite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formerly accurate snapshot can identify the wrong donor after workloads change.
assumptions_latex: Workloads change between measurement and action.
No freshness check is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmax}_i\widehat W_i\ne\operatorname*{argmax}_iW_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale Estimates Can Reverse the Imbalance Classification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Freshness, persistence, and notification layered over a declared imbalance statistic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At epoch k, collect a coherent or version-validated load vector, compute I_k, and discard the sample when its age exceeds \delta. Enter the imbalanced state only after h_{\mathrm{in}} consecutive valid samples satisfy I_k>\tau_{\mathrm{in}}; exit only after h_{\mathrm{out}} consecutive valid samples satisfy I_k<\tau_{\mathrm{out}}, where 0\le\tau_{\mathrm{out}}<\tau_{\mathrm{in}}. Notify the balancing controller only on a state transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fresh, persistent, hysteretic classifier rejects stale samples and suppresses isolated crossings and threshold chatter.
assumptions_latex: h_{\mathrm{in}},h_{\mathrm{out}}\in\mathbb Z_{>0}.
0\le\tau_{\mathrm{out}}<\tau_{\mathrm{in}}.
Sample versions or a snapshot mechanism detect incoherent observations.
\delta\ge0\text{ is the maximum accepted age}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{An expired sample or one isolated threshold crossing cannot change the detector state.}
review_flags: The detector classifies load only; redistribution remains a separate controller decision.
knowledge_statements.title: Fresh Hysteretic Imbalance Detector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coherently sampled predicate with heterogeneous worker speeds and explicit zero-load behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At one coherent observation epoch, let q_i\ge0 be estimated remaining work at worker i in common work units and s_i>0 its estimated processing rate. Define t_i=q_i/s_i and \bar t=p^{-1}\sum_i t_i. Set I=0 when \bar t=0 and otherwise I=\max_i|t_i-\bar t|/\bar t. For a declared threshold \tau\ge0, classify the snapshot as imbalanced exactly when I>\tau. This classification does not itself authorize redistribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare estimated remaining processing times using a coherent snapshot, heterogeneous speed scaling, and an explicit zero-load convention.
assumptions_latex: p\ge1.
q_i\ge0\text{ are coherently sampled on a common work scale}.
s_i>0\text{ are processing-rate estimates}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I=\begin{cases}0,&\bar t=0,\\\max_i|t_i-\bar t|/\bar t,&\bar t>0.\end{cases}

notation.meaning: estimated remaining processing time at worker i
normalized maximum deviation from mean time load

review_flags: This is one explicit predicate; it assumes rather than constructs calibrated work and speed estimates.
knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Normalized Load-Imbalance Predicate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Declares which distributed work contributes to each worker load estimate and represents prediction uncertainty without prescribing redistribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a coherent observation epoch, let \(Q_i\) be worker \(i\)'s queued tasks, let \(e_i\) be its executing residual work, and let \(A_i\) contain in-transit tasks assigned to it by the ownership protocol. Given common-unit prediction intervals \([\underline c_v,\overline c_v]\) and \([\underline e_i,\overline e_i]\), define
\[
\underline q_i=\underline e_i+\sum_{v\in Q_i\cup A_i}\underline c_v,
\qquad
\overline q_i=\overline e_i+\sum_{v\in Q_i\cup A_i}\overline c_v.
\]
An admissible point summary satisfies \(q_i\in[\underline q_i,\overline q_i]\). Each unresolved task must occur in exactly one queued, executing, or ownership-assigned in-transit contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A comparable worker-load estimate counts queued, executing, and assigned in-transit work exactly once and may expose an interval of prediction uncertainty.
assumptions_latex: The observation is coherent or version-validated.
Every unresolved task has exactly one queued, executing, or in-transit ownership representation.
All predictions use common work units.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_i\in[\underline q_i,\overline q_i]\quad\text{and every represented task is counted exactly once}.

notation.meaning: queued and ownership-assigned in-transit tasks for worker i
interval estimate of worker i's remaining work

review_flags: Prediction calibration and online update rules remain implementation-dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Workload-Estimate Interface

assumptions_latex: There are \(p\ge 1\) active workers at observation time \(t\).
Each worker has a nonnegative estimated remaining workload \(w_i(t)\), measured on a common scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Redistribution is triggered exactly when \(I(t)>\tau\).

notation.meaning: estimated remaining workload assigned to worker i at time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines threshold detection from estimated remaining subtree work, not from elapsed processor time alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar w(t)=p^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{p}w_i(t)\). Define the normalized load imbalance by \[I(t)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle \frac{\max_{1\le i\le p}|w_i(t)-\bar w(t)|}{\bar w(t)},&\bar w(t)>0,\\0,&\bar w(t)=0.\end{cases}\] For a prescribed threshold \(\tau\ge 0\), the workload is classified as imbalanced at time \(t\) precisely when \(I(t)>\tau\). This predicate requires workload estimates on a common scale; queue length alone is valid only when queued subproblems have comparable estimated cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Load imbalance is detected when the largest normalized deviation from mean estimated worker load exceeds a chosen threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Load-Imbalance Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The imbalance statistic is mathematically defined, and condition is an appropriate kind for this leaf. However, no source supports this particular metric or threshold policy. In addition, conclusion_latex says redistribution is triggered exactly when the threshold is exceeded, while statement_latex establishes only an imbalance classification; triggering redistribution is a separate architecture-dependent decision.

children.title: Worker Idling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coordination behavior when workers exhaust local work or await transferable subtrees.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting relation between aggregate worker idleness, makespan, and utilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\) identical unit-rate workers observed for \(T>0\), let \(B_i\) and \(I_i=T-B_i\) be worker \(i\)'s busy and idle times. With \(W=\sum_{i=1}^pB_i\) and \(I=\sum_{i=1}^pI_i\), \(pT=W+I\) and \(W/(pT)=1-I/(pT)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total worker capacity equals busy work plus idle time, so utilization is one minus the aggregate idle-time fraction.
assumptions_latex: Workers are identical and have unit processing rate.
Busy and idle intervals partition each worker's observation interval.
Communication and coordination are classified consistently as busy or idle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U=\frac{W}{pT}=1-\frac{I}{pT}.

notation.meaning: Busy and idle time of worker i.
Aggregate busy work and idle time.

knowledge_statements.title: Idle-Time Utilization Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract condition distinguishing distributed quiescence from temporary worker idleness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every worker is passive, every local work queue is empty, and every communication channel contains no work-bearing message in one consistent global state. If new work can arise only by processing existing work or receiving a work-bearing message, and no external work is injected, then the search is quiescent. Empty local queues alone do not establish quiescence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Passivity and empty local queues certify quiescence only when work in transit is also absent.
assumptions_latex: Work is generated only by processing an existing task or receiving a work-bearing message.
Worker, queue, and channel states form one consistent global state.
No external process injects new search work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\bigwedge_{i=1}^{p}\operatorname{passive}(i)\land Q_i=\varnothing\right)\land\left(\bigwedge_{e\in E}M_e=\varnothing\right)\Longrightarrow\operatorname{quiescent}.

notation.meaning: Local work queue of worker i.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Quiescence Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Empty Local Queues Do Not Imply Global Idleness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: In-transit-work counterexample to termination inference from local queues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With two workers, worker 1 removes unresolved task \(s\) from its queue and sends it to worker 2. After removal but before delivery, \(Q_1=Q_2=\varnothing\) while the communication channel contains \(s\). Thus every local queue is empty although unresolved work remains and worker 2 may later become busy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All local queues can be empty while unresolved work remains in transit.
assumptions_latex: Sending a task removes it from the sender's queue before delivery.
Message delivery need not be instantaneous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\forall i,\ Q_i=\varnothing\right)\centernot\Longrightarrow\operatorname{quiescent}.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty Local Queues Do Not Imply Global Idleness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Protocol-relative classification of temporary and terminal worker inactivity in one consistent distributed state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_i\) be worker \(i\)'s ready queue, \(R_i\) work already assigned or offered to \(i\) but not locally ready, \(W_{-i}\) unresolved work represented elsewhere, and \(T\) a sound global-quiescence predicate. Worker \(i\) is locally idle when \(Q_i=\varnothing\); redistribution-waiting when \(Q_i=\varnothing\) and \(R_i\ne\varnothing\); globally starved when \(Q_i=R_i=\varnothing\), \(W_{-i}\ne\varnothing\), and \(T\) is false; and terminally idle when \(Q_i=R_i=W_{-i}=\varnothing\) and \(T\) is true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An idle worker may be waiting for assigned work, starved while work remains elsewhere, or terminally idle after certified global quiescence.
assumptions_latex: The queue, assignment, remote-work, and termination values belong to one consistent global state.
The quiescence predicate accounts for work-bearing messages in transit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{terminalIdle}(i)\Longleftrightarrow Q_i=R_i=W_{-i}=\varnothing\land T.

notation.meaning: assigned or offered work not yet locally ready
unresolved work represented outside worker i

review_flags: Operational construction of a consistent state is termination-protocol dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Worker Idling State Classification

assumptions_latex: At time \(t\), worker \(i\) has local ready queue \(Q_i(t)\).
A global termination protocol distinguishes temporary lack of local work from exhaustion of all work in transit and in queues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The three regimes are distinguished by \(Q_i(t)\), the availability of transferable work, and the global termination predicate.

notation.meaning: ready subproblems held by worker i at time t
set of transferable subproblems held by other workers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies idling states needed to separate ordinary starvation from certified distributed termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Worker \(i\) is locally idle at time \(t\) when \(Q_i(t)=\varnothing\). It is redistribution-idle when additionally \(D_i(t)\ne\varnothing\), so transferable work exists but has not yet arrived. It is globally starved when \(Q_i(t)=D_i(t)=\varnothing\) while \(T(t)\) is false, meaning that search work or messages may still exist elsewhere. It is terminally idle when \(Q_i(t)=D_i(t)=\varnothing\) and \(T(t)\) is true. Only terminal idling certifies that the worker cannot receive further search work in the current run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An idle worker may be awaiting redistribution, globally starved while work remains elsewhere, or terminally idle after certified global exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.title: Worker Idling Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the idling-regimes leaf, but the distinctions involving transferable work, global starvation, and certified termination depend on the distributed termination protocol. No cited source establishes these semantics or the claim that only the stated terminal regime precludes future work receipt.

children.title: Subtree Transfer Overheads
children.top_down_role: Communication, serialization, synchronization, or state-reconstruction costs of redistribution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-latency saving from batching subtree states in a latency-bandwidth model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(q\ge1\) subtree states of sizes \(b_1,\ldots,b_q\) use a channel with per-message latency \(\ell\) and bandwidth \(\beta\). Ignoring serialization, contention, overlap, and batching delay, separate messages cost \(q\ell+\sum_{j=1}^q b_j/\beta\), while one batch costs \(\ell+\sum_{j=1}^q b_j/\beta\). Batching saves \((q-1)\ell\) in this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batching q subtree states amortizes fixed latency and saves q minus one latency charges in the basic communication model.
assumptions_latex: All states use the same effective bandwidth and fixed per-message latency.
Serialization, contention, overlap, and batching delay are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{sep}}-T_{\mathrm{batch}}=(q-1)\ell.

notation.meaning: Serialized size of subtree state j.
Fixed message latency and effective bandwidth.

knowledge_statements.title: Latency Amortization by Batched Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact comparison after gross saving and net overhead are defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_0\) be completion time without transfer, \(S\ge0\) the gross critical-path saving, and \(H\ge0\) all transfer-induced critical-path delay net of credited overlap. Then \(T_1=T_0-S+H\), and transfer improves predicted completion time exactly when \(S>H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transfer helps exactly when gross critical-path saving exceeds net critical-path overhead.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(H\) use the same completion-time model.
Overlap is counted once.
All transfer-induced critical-path effects are included in \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_1<T_0\iff S>H.
review_flags: The condition does not prescribe how either quantity is estimated.
knowledge_statements.title: Abstract Critical-Path Break-Even Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A transfer that increases completion time despite balancing load.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two workers have remaining loads \((2,0)\). Moving one unit subtree would reduce computation makespan to \(1\), but a nonoverlapped critical-path transfer overhead \(h>1\) gives completion time at least \(1+h>2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer cost can exceed the computation time saved by balancing.
assumptions_latex: The moved subtree requires one unit of processing.
Overhead \(h\) is nonoverlapped.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{redistributed}}\ge1+h>2=T_{\mathrm{local}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Transfer-Dominated Redistribution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Batching Delay Can Exceed Latency Savings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on fixed-latency batching benefits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose batching two states saves one latency charge \(\ell\) but requires waiting \(D\) before critical-path work can be sent. In an additive model where all other costs are equal, batching changes completion time by \(D-\ell\); hence it is slower when \(D>\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Waiting to batch critical work can cost more than the saved message latency.
assumptions_latex: Batching saves exactly one latency charge.
Waiting adds \(D\) to the critical path.
All other costs are equal and nonoverlapped.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{batch}}-T_{\mathrm{separate}}=D-\ell>0.

notation.meaning: batch-formation delay on the critical path

knowledge_statements.title: Batching Delay Can Exceed Latency Savings

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Declared additive architecture model separating gross transfer cost from the portion exposed on the critical path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a serialized subtree state of \(b\) bytes, define the gross cost in a declared additive model by
\[
G(b)=c_{\mathrm{ser}}(b)+\ell+\frac{b}{\beta}+c_{\mathrm{sync}}(b)+c_{\mathrm{recon}}(b)+c_{\mathrm{cont}}(b).
\]
If \(O(b)\) units overlap useful computation, where \(0\le O(b)\le G(b)\), the exposed critical-path overhead is \(H(b)=G(b)-O(b)\). Thus \(0\le H(b)\le G(b)\), with \(H(b)=G(b)\) under no overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The declared transfer model includes serialization, latency, transmission, synchronization, reconstruction, and contention; only its nonoverlapped portion delays the critical path.
assumptions_latex: The displayed components are nonnegative and additive under the declared architecture model.
All terms use one wall-clock convention.
Overlap is credited once and cannot exceed gross transfer cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H(b)=G(b)-O(b),\qquad 0\le H(b)\le G(b).

notation.meaning: gross transfer cost under the declared additive model
transfer delay exposed on the critical path
transfer cost overlapped with useful computation

review_flags: Concrete architectures must instantiate or measure the component functions.
The equality is conditional on the declared additive accounting model.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Subtree-Transfer Cost Decomposition

assumptions_latex: A transferred subtree is represented by \(b\) bytes of state and requires serialization, communication, and reconstruction.
The transfer does not overlap useful computation on the donating or receiving worker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transfer consumes \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}(b)=\ell+b/\beta+c_{\mathrm{ser}}(b)+c_{\mathrm{des}}(b)\), and is beneficial only if its expected saved completion time exceeds this quantity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a latency-bandwidth cost model for transferring one self-contained branch-and-bound subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated no-overlap model, transferring a subtree state of size \(b\) has wall-clock overhead \[T_{\mathrm{tr}}(b)=\ell+\frac{b}{\beta}+c_{\mathrm{ser}}(b)+c_{\mathrm{des}}(b).\] Consequently \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}(b)\ge \ell+b/\beta\). If redistribution is predicted to reduce the remaining makespan by \(\Delta T\), the transfer is beneficial in this model only when \(\Delta T>T_{\mathrm{tr}}(b)\). Contention, synchronization, incumbent propagation, and duplicated node processing require additional nonnegative terms when they are not already included in the measured effective parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtree transfer cost includes latency, transmission, serialization, and reconstruction; redistribution helps only when its predicted makespan saving exceeds that cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Subtree Transfer Overheads

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated equality is a selected latency-bandwidth cost representation and break-even condition, not a complexity bound. Its additivity, no-overlap assumption, and treatment of contention require an authoritative distributed-search source before the formula can be relied upon for this leaf.

children.title: Parallel Search Anomalies
children.top_down_role: Performance and reproducibility effects caused by concurrent search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-tree family isolating delayed incumbent discovery as a source of work inflation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every integer \(M\ge1\), a finite minimization search tree can have ready nodes \(a,b\) such that processing \(a\) finds an incumbent \(U=0\), while processing \(b\) before that discovery exposes an infeasible subtree with at least \(M\) processable nodes of valid lower bound \(0\). A schedule selecting \(a\) first closes \(b\) by \(L_b\ge U\); a schedule postponing \(a\) may process the entire subtree first. Thus the ratio of processed-node counts of two valid schedules is unbounded over this family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delaying a node that supplies a strong incumbent can cause arbitrarily more search work.
assumptions_latex: Minimization pruning uses the valid cutoff test \(L_v\ge U\).
The scheduler may postpone one ready node while exploring another finite subtree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{M\ge1}\frac{N_{\mathrm{late}}(M)}{N_{\mathrm{early}}(M)}=+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Schedule-Induced Work Inflation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-order, work, runtime, and trajectory anomalies caused by concurrent frontier and incumbent updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For otherwise sound branch-and-bound executions, changing the worker count or admissible concurrent schedule can change incumbent-discovery times and node-selection order. Consequently, neither processed-node count nor wall-clock time is generally monotone in the number of workers, and completed runs need not process the same nodes or emit the same event transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concurrent schedules can change incumbent timing and search order, so more workers need not reduce work or runtime and repeated runs need not follow the same trajectory.
assumptions_latex: All executions use valid bounds, sound pruning, and the same mathematical termination tolerances.
Concurrent schedules may expose incumbent or frontier updates in different orders.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p<q\not\Rightarrow N_q\le N_p,\qquad p<q\not\Rightarrow T_q\le T_p.

notation.meaning: number of nodes processed with p workers

knowledge_statements.title: Schedule-Dependent Parallel Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes agreement on the mathematical result from agreement on the concurrent trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every completed execution is an exact sound search for the same instance, all executions return the same optimal value \(z^*\). This does not imply equality of returned solutions when multiple optima exist, processed-node sets, node order, or event transcripts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correct runs may agree on the optimal value while differing in the selected optimum and search trajectory.
assumptions_latex: Every compared execution terminates with an exact sound result for the same optimization instance.
knowledge_statements.title: Value Reproducibility Versus Path Reproducibility

assumptions_latex: A deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm is run with identical mathematical tolerances but different worker counts or message schedules.
Concurrent discoveries may update the incumbent before different frontier nodes are selected or pruned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither processed-node count nor runtime must be monotone in worker count, and repeated concurrent runs need not traverse the same tree.

notation.meaning: number of processed search nodes using p workers
wall-clock solution time using p workers
incumbent objective value at time t for minimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers search-order, speedup, and reproducibility anomalies induced by asynchronous incumbent and frontier updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is no general implication \(p<q\Rightarrow N_q\le N_p\), nor \(p<q\Rightarrow T_q\le T_p\). A schedule that delays a strong incumbent can leave \(U(t)\) larger, causing nodes that another schedule would prune to be processed; conversely, early incumbent discovery can shrink the tree. Thus asynchronous schedules may produce \(N_p<N_q\), superlinear speedup, slowdown, or distinct processed-node sets, even when every completed run returns an objective satisfying the same termination tolerances. Reproducibility requires additional deterministic rules for node ordering, communication, and tie resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concurrent schedules can change incumbent timing and node order, producing slowdown, superlinear speedup, different tree sizes, and nonreproducible search trajectories.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Search Anomalies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is appropriate for the anomaly topic, and the qualitative phenomena are plausible. No source is supplied for the nonmonotonicity, superlinear-speedup, slowdown, or reproducibility claims, whose exact scope depends on scheduling, communication, and deterministic tie-breaking assumptions.

children.title: Numerical Search Integrity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Implementation boundaries affecting correctness, stability, and repeatability.

children.title: Tolerance Classification Effects
children.top_down_role: Search-state changes caused by tolerance conventions.

children.title: Feasibility Tolerance Effects
children.top_down_role: Search-state consequences of approximate constraint-feasibility classification.

assumptions_latex: Let \(n,m\ge 1\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(a_j:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(b_j\in\mathbb R\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\).
Each absolute row-feasibility tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon_j\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tolerance-feasible set satisfies \(F_0\subseteq F_{\varepsilon}\), and the inclusion is strict exactly when some \(x\in X\) satisfies every relaxed row but violates at least one exact row.

notation.meaning: exact feasible set within the ambient domain X
feasible set under absolute row tolerances

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the set-enlargement effect of absolute row-feasibility tolerances for inequality constraints on a specified ambient domain.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F_0=\{x\in X:a_j(x)\le b_j\text{ for every }j=1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(F_{\varepsilon}=\{x\in X:a_j(x)\le b_j+\varepsilon_j\text{ for every }j=1,\ldots,m\}\). Then \(F_0\subseteq F_{\varepsilon}\). The inclusion is strict if and only if there exists \(x\in X\) such that \(a_j(x)\le b_j+\varepsilon_j\) for every \(j\) and \(a_k(x)>b_k\) for at least one \(k\). Equivalently, for \(v_{\varepsilon}(x)=\max_{1\le j\le m}\{a_j(x)-b_j-\varepsilon_j\}\), tolerance-feasibility is the predicate \(v_{\varepsilon}(x)\le 0\). Thus changing \(\varepsilon\) can change the feasibility classification used by a branch-and-bound implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative row tolerances enlarge the exact feasible set; the enlargement is strict precisely when an exactly infeasible point satisfies every tolerance-relaxed row.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Tolerance Effects

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute tolerance representations for equalities and ranged rows, complementing the seed's one-sided inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equalities \(h_k(x)=0\) and tolerances \(\tau_k\ge0\), define \[E_\tau=\{x\in X:|h_k(x)|\le\tau_k\ \forall k\}.\] Then \(E_0\subseteq E_\tau\), with strict inclusion exactly when some \(x\in X\) satisfies every relaxed equality and violates at least one exact equality. A ranged row \(\ell_j\le a_j(x)\le u_j\) is tolerance-feasible exactly when \(a_j(x)\ge\ell_j-\varepsilon_j^-\) and \(a_j(x)\le u_j+\varepsilon_j^+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality and ranged-row tolerances enlarge their exact feasible sets by symmetric or side-specific residual bands.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau_k,\varepsilon_j^-,\varepsilon_j^+\ge0\).
All predicates are evaluated on the declared ambient domain \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_0\subseteq E_\tau,\qquad [\ell_j,u_j]\subseteq[\ell_j-\varepsilon_j^-,u_j+\varepsilon_j^+].

notation.meaning: Set satisfying all equality rows within their absolute tolerances.
Lower- and upper-side tolerances for a ranged row.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality and Two-Sided Feasibility Tolerances

children.title: Integrality Tolerance Effects
children.top_down_role: Search-state consequences of approximate integer-value classification.

assumptions_latex: Let \(n\ge 1\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(I\subseteq\{1,ldots,n\}\) be the nonempty set of integer-constrained coordinate indices.
The absolute integrality tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon_I\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tolerance-accepted set satisfies \(Z_0\subseteq Z_{\varepsilon_I}\), with strict inclusion exactly when \(X\) contains a nonintegral point whose integer-constrained coordinates all lie within \(\varepsilon_I\) of integers.

notation.meaning: distance from a real number to the nearest integer
subset of X accepted under the integrality tolerance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses nearest-integer distance on a specified ambient domain to formalize absolute integrality classification.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Integrality constraints p. 10
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y\in\mathbb R\), define \(d_{\mathbb Z}(y)=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z}|y-k|\). Let \(Z_0=\{x\in X:x_i\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }i\in I\}\) and \(Z_{\varepsilon_I}=\{x\in X:d_{\mathbb Z}(x_i)\le\varepsilon_I\text{ for every }i\in I\}\). Then \(Z_0\subseteq Z_{\varepsilon_I}\). The inclusion is strict if and only if there exists \(x\in X\setminus Z_0\) such that \(d_{\mathbb Z}(x_i)\le\varepsilon_I\) for every \(i\in I\). Hence changing \(\varepsilon_I\) can change whether a relaxation solution is classified as integer-feasible; validity after rounding or reconstruction requires separate feasibility checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrality tolerance contains the exact mixed-integer set and enlarges it precisely when the ambient domain contains a nonintegral point sufficiently close to integers in every constrained coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrality Tolerance Effects

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Integrality constraints p. 10
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Half-Unit Boundary for Absolute Integrality Tolerance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal geometric boundary of nearest-integer classification in one coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(y\in\mathbb R\), \(d_{\mathbb Z}(y)\le1/2\). If \(0\le\varepsilon_I<1/2\) and \(d_{\mathbb Z}(y)\le\varepsilon_I\), the nearest integer is unique. If \(\varepsilon_I\ge1/2\), every real number passes the scalar integrality predicate. At \(d_{\mathbb Z}(y)=1/2\), two nearest integers exist and reconstruction requires a tie rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below one half, every accepted coordinate has a unique nearest integer; at one half ties occur, and at or above one half every real coordinate is accepted.
assumptions_latex: The residual is \(d_{\mathbb Z}(y)=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z}|y-k|\).
\(\varepsilon_I\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varepsilon_I<1/2\Rightarrow\text{accepted }y\text{ has a unique nearest integer};\qquad \varepsilon_I\ge1/2\Rightarrow d_{\mathbb Z}(y)\le\varepsilon_I\ \forall y.

notation.meaning: Distance from a scalar to the integer lattice.

knowledge_statements.title: Half-Unit Boundary for Absolute Integrality Tolerance

children.title: Conflicting Tolerance Classifications
children.top_down_role: Cases where numerical conventions produce inconsistent candidate, node, or solution status.

assumptions_latex: Let \(n,m\ge 1\), let \(I\subseteq\{1,ldots,n\}\) be nonempty, and let the rows be \(a_j(x)\le b_j\) for maps \(a_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(j=1,ldots,m\).

Let \(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_I\ge 0\), and let \(R:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) round every coordinate indexed by \(I\) to a nearest integer, using a fixed rule for ties, while leaving all other coordinates unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In general, simultaneous tolerance-feasibility and tolerance-integrality of \(x\) imply neither exact mixed-integer feasibility of \(x\) nor tolerance-feasibility of its reconstruction \(R(x)\).

notation.meaning: maximum distance of an integer-constrained coordinate to an integer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the absence of general implications between row-tolerance classification, integrality-tolerance classification, and reconstructed feasibility.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Integrality constraints p. 10
