source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(v(x)=\max_{1\le j\le m}\{a_j(x)-b_j\}\) and \(d_I(x)=\max_{i\in I}d_{\mathbb Z}(x_i)\). The simultaneous predicates \(v(x)\le\varepsilon_F\) and \(d_I(x)\le\varepsilon_I\) do not, in general, imply that \(x_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every \(i\in I\), nor do they imply \(v(R(x))\le\varepsilon_F\). Rounding can change row residuals enough to invalidate the reconstructed point. Therefore an implementation that uses both tolerances must specify whether reconstruction occurs and must recheck the applicable row-feasibility predicate after reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point can pass both row and integrality tolerances without being exactly mixed-integer feasible, and its nearest-integer reconstruction can fail the row-feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflicting Tolerance Classifications

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Integrality constraints p. 10
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Margin Condition for Safe Integer Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition under which rounding an integrality-tolerant point preserves row-tolerance feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume each row map \(a_j\) is Lipschitz on a set containing the segment from \(x\) to \(R(x)\), with constant \(K_j\) in a declared norm. If \[a_j(x)-b_j+K_j\|R(x)-x\|\le\varepsilon_F\qquad(j=1,\ldots,m),\] then \(a_j(R(x))\le b_j+\varepsilon_F\) for every \(j\). Without such residual margins or other structural control, passing the pre-reconstruction feasibility and integrality predicates does not imply feasibility after reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding is safe when every row has enough residual margin to absorb its Lipschitz change; otherwise the two tolerance classifications need not be compatible.
assumptions_latex: \(|a_j(y)-a_j(z)|\le K_j\|y-z\|\) along the reconstruction segment for every row \(j\).
\(R(x)\) is the declared integer reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_j(x)-b_j+K_j\|R(x)-x\|\le\varepsilon_F\ \forall j\Rightarrow a_j(R(x))\le b_j+\varepsilon_F\ \forall j.

notation.meaning: Declared integer reconstruction of the candidate point.

knowledge_statements.title: Margin Condition for Safe Integer Reconstruction

children.title: Tolerance-Sensitive Search Decisions
children.top_down_role: Branching, pruning, propagation, or incumbent changes attributable to tolerance settings.

assumptions_latex: A branch-and-bound implementation uses tolerance predicates to accept incumbents, choose branching variables, or fathom nodes.
Two runs differ only in one or more numerical tolerance values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A tolerance change can alter the discrete search trajectory even when the exact optimization model is unchanged.

notation.meaning: search decision selected from state s under tolerances epsilon

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes propagation from tolerance classifications to discrete branch-and-bound decisions.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_{\varepsilon}(s)\) denote the discrete decision made at search state \(s\) using tolerance vector \(\varepsilon\). If two vectors \(\varepsilon\) and \(\varepsilon'\) classify any tested residual, integrality distance, or bound comparison differently, then it is possible that \(D_{\varepsilon}(s)\ne D_{\varepsilon'}(s)\). Because incumbent acceptance, node fathoming, and branching create or remove later states, one changed decision can yield \(\mathcal T_{\varepsilon}\ne\mathcal T_{\varepsilon'}\). No monotonic relation between the two tree sizes follows without additional restrictions on every tolerance-dependent rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing a tolerance can change acceptance, pruning, or branching and thereby produce a different search tree with no guaranteed size ordering.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Sensitive Search Decisions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Run Stability Under Strict Classification Margins
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient robustness condition for reproducing a deterministic finite search trajectory under perturbed numerical tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a deterministic finite search run whose tolerance-dependent decisions are comparisons \(q_t\le\theta_t\), \(t=1,\ldots,N\). Suppose perturbed evaluations satisfy \(|\widehat q_t-q_t|\le e_t\) whenever the same state is reached. If \[|q_t-\theta_t|>e_t\qquad(t=1,\ldots,N),\] then every comparison has the same truth value. The perturbed run therefore makes the same deterministic incumbent, pruning, propagation, branching, and tie-breaking decisions and produces the same processed search tree. Equality or failure of a margin condition removes this guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic finite search is reproducible when every tolerance comparison is separated from its threshold by more than its evaluation error.
assumptions_latex: The reference run is finite, and all state-transition and tie-breaking rules are deterministic.
Each perturbed comparison has a certified error bound \(e_t\) whenever its reference state is reached.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(|q_t-\theta_t|>e_t\ \forall t\bigr)\Rightarrow\widehat{\mathcal T}=\mathcal T.

notation.meaning: Compared quantity and threshold at decision event \(t\).
Certified perturbation bound for the compared quantity.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Run Stability Under Strict Classification Margins

children.title: Numerical Bound-Gap Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Numerical effects in pruning, frontier ordering, and gap reporting.

children.title: Bound-Rounding Effects
children.top_down_role: Changes in stored or reported node bounds caused by rounding conventions.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization integer program with integer-valued objective on every feasible integer solution.
A node relaxation supplies a valid real lower bound \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strengthened integer lower bound is \(\lceil L\rceil\), whereas arbitrary decimal rounding need not preserve validity.

notation.meaning: valid real lower bound at a search node
objective value of a feasible integer solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers mathematically valid bound strengthening when all feasible objective values are integral.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(L\le z\) for every feasible objective value \(z\in\mathbb Z\), then \(\lceil L\rceil\le z\) for every such \(z\). Thus \(\lceil L\rceil\) is a valid lower bound and may replace \(L\) in pruning and gap calculations. By contrast, rounding \(L\) to a fixed number of decimal places by a rule that can increase it beyond \(\lceil L\rceil\), or applying this ceiling operation when feasible objective values are not integral, can create an invalid lower bound and an unsound pruning decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For integer-valued objectives, a valid lower bound may be rounded upward to its ceiling; ordinary decimal rounding lacks this guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Rounding Effects

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalization of integer-objective ceiling to a known affine lattice of feasible values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every feasible objective value lies in \(a+h\mathbb Z\) with \(h>0\), then any valid real lower bound \(L\) may be strengthened to \(L_{\mathrm{lat}}=a+h\left\lceil(L-a)/h\right\rceil\). This is the smallest lattice value not below \(L\). Without the lattice assumption, the upward-rounded value may exceed a feasible objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid lower bound may be rounded upward to the next known feasible objective-lattice value.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible objective value belongs to \(a+h\mathbb Z\).
\(L\) is a valid lower bound and \(h>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathrm{lat}}\le z\quad\text{for every feasible objective value }z.

notation.meaning: known affine lattice containing all feasible objective values

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Lattice Objective Rounding

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Correction of an Approximate Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative conversion of an approximate numerical value into a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an exact valid lower bound \(L\) and its computed approximation \(\widehat L\) satisfy \(|\widehat L-L|\le\varepsilon\), then \(L^-:=\widehat L-\varepsilon\) is also a valid lower bound. Any further downward rounding preserves validity. Using \(\widehat L\) directly or rounding it upward lacks this guarantee without additional objective-lattice information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtract a certified absolute error, then round downward if needed, to obtain a safe lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le z\) for every feasible objective value \(z\).
The absolute error bound \(|\widehat L-L|\le\varepsilon\) is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat L-\varepsilon\le L\le z.

notation.meaning: computed approximation to the exact bound

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Correction of an Approximate Lower Bound

children.title: Gap-Comparison Effects
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of termination or progress assessments to gap-comparison conventions.

assumptions_latex: For minimization, \(L\) is a valid global lower bound and \(U\) is a finite incumbent value with \(L\le U\).
Absolute and relative gap tolerances satisfy \(\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_r\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search may stop when \(U-L\le\varepsilon_a\) or when \((U-L)/\max\{1,|U|\}\le\varepsilon_r\); boundary decisions are sensitive to perturbations of the compared quantities.

notation.meaning: global lower bound and incumbent upper bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixes one explicit relative-gap convention; solver conventions may use different scaling denominators.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14
3.5 Reducing the duality gap p. 28
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(g_a=U-L\) and \(g_r=(U-L)/\max\{1,|U|\}\). Under the stated convention, an absolute-gap stopping test is \(g_a\le\varepsilon_a\), and a relative-gap test is \(g_r\le\varepsilon_r\). If computed bounds are perturbed to \(\widehat L=L+\delta_L\) and \(\widehat U=U+\delta_U\), the computed absolute gap becomes \(\widehat g_a=g_a+\delta_U-\delta_L\). Hence the truth value of the absolute test can change whenever \(|g_a-\varepsilon_a|\le|\delta_U|+|\delta_L|\); analogous sensitivity holds for the relative test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gap termination compares incumbent and bound under a specified scaling; near the tolerance threshold, small numerical perturbations can reverse the result.
knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Comparison Effects

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Optimality Condition via Bounds p. 14
3.5 Reducing the duality gap p. 28
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Pruning Decision Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Node-retention changes caused by numerical treatment of bounds.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with incumbent upper bound \(U\), and node \(n\) has a mathematically valid lower bound \(L_n\).
The implementation compares values \(\widehat L_n\) and \(\widehat U\) satisfying \(|\widehat L_n-L_n|\le\eta_L\) and \(|\widehat U-U|\le\eta_U\), where \(\eta_L,eta_U\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Writing \(E=\eta_L+eta_U\), pruning is guaranteed when \(L_n-U\ge E\), nonpruning is guaranteed when \(U-L_n>E\), and both computed classifications are admissible in the remaining boundary region \(-E\le L_n-U<E\).

notation.meaning: exact node lower bound and incumbent upper bound
absolute error bounds and their sum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the exact perturbation margins for stability of node fathoming under the comparison \(\widehat L_n\ge\widehat U\).

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact bound fathoming prunes node \(n\) when \(L_n\ge U\), and the computed rule prunes when \(\widehat L_n\ge\widehat U\). Let \(E=\eta_L+eta_U\). If \(L_n-U\ge E\), then every admissible perturbation satisfies \(\widehat L_n\ge\widehat U\), so pruning is stable. If \(U-L_n>E\), then every admissible perturbation satisfies \(\widehat L_n<\widehat U\), so nonpruning is stable. If \(-E\le L_n-U<E\), admissible perturbations can produce either \(\widehat L_n\ge\widehat U\) or \(\widehat L_n<\widehat U\); an error-aware rule is then required to prevent unsound pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a non-strict pruning comparison, pruning is stable when its exact margin is at least the combined error, nonpruning requires a strictly larger opposite margin, and either classification is possible between those thresholds.
knowledge_statements.title: Pruning Decision Sensitivity

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided certificates converting computed bounds and certified error radii into sound bound-fathoming conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(|\widehat L_n-L_n|\le\eta_L\) and \(|\widehat U-U|\le\eta_U\). If \[\widehat L_n-\eta_L\ge \widehat U+\eta_U,\] then \(L_n\ge U\), so node \(n\) may be pruned soundly. If \[\widehat L_n+\eta_L<\widehat U-\eta_U,\] then \(L_n<U\) for every admissible exact pair, so bound fathoming is impossible. If neither inequality holds, these intervals alone certify neither conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separated error intervals give checkable pruning or nonpruning certificates; otherwise the bound-fathoming decision remains unresolved.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem using exact bound fathoming \(L_n\ge U\).
\(|\widehat L_n-L_n|\le\eta_L\) and \(|\widehat U-U|\le\eta_U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat L_n-\eta_L\ge\widehat U+\eta_U\Rightarrow L_n\ge U,\qquad \widehat L_n+\eta_L<\widehat U-\eta_U\Rightarrow L_n<U.

notation.meaning: Certified interval containing the exact node lower bound.
Certified interval containing the exact incumbent value.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Aware Pruning and Retention Certificates

children.title: Frontier Ordering Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Active-node ordering changes caused by nearly equal or rounded bounds.

assumptions_latex: Open nodes are selected by increasing computed key \(\widehat k(n)\).
Each computed key satisfies \(|\widehat k(n)-k(n)|\le\eta_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative order of nodes \(a\) and \(b\) is guaranteed only when \(|k(a)-k(b)|>\eta_a+\eta_b\); otherwise either order is numerically admissible.

notation.meaning: exact priority key of frontier node n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies perturbation analysis to best-key frontier selection and excludes unspecified tie-breaking rules.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two frontier nodes \(a\) and \(b\), suppose \(k(a)<k(b)\). If \(k(b)-k(a)>\eta_a+\eta_b\), then \(\widehat k(a)<\widehat k(b)\) for every admissible perturbation, so their order is stable. If \(k(b)-k(a)\le\eta_a+\eta_b\), there exist admissible perturbations for which \(\widehat k(a)\ge\widehat k(b)\), allowing reversal or a tie. Because the selected node may discover an incumbent or generate descendants, one unstable pairwise comparison can change later frontier contents and the processed-node sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Frontier order is numerically stable only when exact priority differences exceed combined key errors; smaller differences permit ties or reversals.
knowledge_statements.title: Frontier Ordering Sensitivity

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tie Breaking Cannot Repair Strict Key Reversal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between deterministic equality resolution and stability of the primary numerical order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A secondary tie breaker used only when computed primary keys are equal makes selection unique at \(\widehat k(a)=\widehat k(b)\). It cannot restore the exact priority when admissible errors produce \(\widehat k(b)<\widehat k(a)\) despite \(k(a)<k(b)\). Stability of the primary order therefore requires a separation margin, not merely deterministic tie resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tie breaking resolves computed equality but cannot correct a strict numerical reversal of primary keys.
assumptions_latex: The smaller computed primary key has strict precedence.
Secondary keys are consulted only at computed equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k(a)<k(b)\land\widehat k(b)<\widehat k(a)\Longrightarrow b\text{ precedes }a.
knowledge_statements.title: Tie Breaking Cannot Repair Strict Key Reversal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-frontier extension of the accepted pairwise separation criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k(n_1)<\cdots<k(n_m)\) and suppose \(|\widehat k(n_i)-k(n_i)|\le\eta_i\). If every adjacent gap satisfies \(k(n_{i+1})-k(n_i)>\eta_i+\eta_{i+1}\), then \(\widehat k(n_1)<\cdots<\widehat k(n_m)\), so the complete computed order is invariant. If an adjacent condition fails and errors vary independently throughout their intervals, that pair can tie or reverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entire frontier order is stable when every adjacent exact-key gap exceeds the corresponding combined errors.
assumptions_latex: Exact frontier keys are distinct and indexed increasingly.
For the converse statement, key errors may vary independently over their stated intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigwedge_{i=1}^{m-1}\left[k(n_{i+1})-k(n_i)>\eta_i+\eta_{i+1}\right]\Longrightarrow\widehat k(n_1)<\cdots<\widehat k(n_m).

notation.meaning: frontier nodes in exact increasing-key order
absolute error bound for node i's key

knowledge_statements.title: Whole-Frontier Order Stability

children.title: Gap Reporting Stability
children.top_down_role: Consistency of displayed progress measures across numerical conventions or execution environments.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quantitative Stability Bound for a Floored Relative Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite perturbation bound for the seed's fixed floored-denominator reporting convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_\delta(U,L)=(U-L)/\max\{\delta,|U|\}\), with \(\delta>0\) and \(L\le U\). If \(|U'-U|\le\eta_U\), \(|L'-L|\le\eta_L\), and \(L'\le U'\), then \[|\rho_\delta(U',L')-\rho_\delta(U,L)|\le \frac{\eta_U+\eta_L}{\delta}+\frac{(U-L)\eta_U}{\delta^2}.\] Consequently, comparison with threshold \(\varepsilon\) is invariant whenever this upper bound is strictly smaller than \(|\rho_\delta(U,L)-\varepsilon|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The denominator floor gives an explicit perturbation bound, so a reported-gap classification is stable when its threshold margin exceeds that bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\delta>0\), \(L\le U\), and \(L'\le U'\).
\(|U'-U|\le\eta_U\) and \(|L'-L|\le\eta_L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\rho_\delta(U',L')-\rho_\delta(U,L)|\le(\eta_U+\eta_L)/\delta+(U-L)\eta_U/\delta^2.

notation.meaning: Absolute perturbation bounds on the incumbent and lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative Stability Bound for a Floored Relative Gap

assumptions_latex: The search is a minimization procedure with finite incumbent bound \(U\), finite valid lower bound \(L\), and \(L\le U\).
A fixed denominator floor \(\delta>0\) and termination tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\) are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_\delta(U_k,L_k)\to\rho_\delta(U,L)\), and any gap-threshold decision having positive margin is eventually unchanged.

notation.meaning: Reported relative optimality gap with a floored denominator.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Continuity of a floored relative-gap formula and robustness of strict threshold comparisons are standard numerical-analysis facts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity and threshold-decision stability for a floored relative gap in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\rho_\delta(U,L)=(U-L)/\max\{\delta,|U|\}\). If \((U_k,L_k)\to(U,L)\), then \(\rho_\delta(U_k,L_k)\to\rho_\delta(U,L)\). Moreover, if \(|\rho_\delta(U,L)-\varepsilon|=m>0\), then there exists \(k_0\) such that, for every \(k\ge k_0\), the Boolean comparisons \(\rho_\delta(U_k,L_k)\le\varepsilon\) and \(\rho_\delta(U,L)\le\varepsilon\) agree. Thus sufficiently small bound perturbations cannot change the gap-threshold classification or gap-based termination decision away from the tolerance boundary; no such guarantee follows when \(m=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A floored relative gap varies continuously with its bounds, and its threshold-based termination decision is unchanged by sufficiently small perturbations whenever the limiting reported gap is separated from the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Gap Reporting Stability

children.title: Deterministic Search Replay Interface
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms governing repeatable search trajectories.

children.title: Tie-Breaking Policies
children.top_down_role: Selection conventions for search events with indistinguishable primary priority.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic selection among finitely many equally eligible search alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(c\) in a finite eligible set \(C\), form a reproducible key \(K(c)=(s_1(c),\ldots,s_r(c),\operatorname{id}(c))\), with fixed component orientations and an identifier injective on \(C\). Select the lexicographically least key, or report no selection when \(C=\varnothing\). The injective final component makes every nonempty selection unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolve a finite tie with a fixed lexicographic key ending in a reproducible unique identifier.
assumptions_latex: The eligible set \(C\) is finite.
All key components, orientations, numerical representations, and identifiers are reproducible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow\left|\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{c\in C}^{\mathrm{lex}}K(c)\right|=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Lexicographic Tie Breaking

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between genuine tie resolution and alteration of the primary policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:C\to P\) be the declared primary priority. A tie-breaking total order \(\preceq\) must refine the primary preorder: if \(p(a)\prec_Pp(b)\), then \(a\prec b\). Secondary keys may distinguish candidates only within a primary equivalence class. A secondary key that overrides a strict primary preference changes the primary policy rather than breaking a tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tie breaker orders equal-primary candidates without overriding any strict primary preference.
assumptions_latex: The candidate set is finite.
The primary priority relation is fixed before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(a)\prec_Pp(b)\Longrightarrow a\prec b.
knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Preserving Tie Refinement

assumptions_latex: At each search decision, the eligible alternatives form a finite set \(C\).
Every alternative has a reproducible primary score and reproducible immutable identifier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected alternative is the unique lexicographic minimizer of its complete deterministic key.

notation.meaning: Finite set of eligible search alternatives.
Complete deterministic key of alternative c.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Lexicographic selection using a unique final identifier is the standard deterministic resolution of finite ties.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic selection among equally scored nodes, variables, cuts, or candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(c\in C\), construct a key \(K(c)=(s_1(c),\ldots,s_r(c),\operatorname{id}(c))\), where the score components and their ascending or descending orientations are fixed before the run and \(\operatorname{id}\) is injective on \(C\). Select \[c^*=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{c\in C}^{\mathrm{lex}}K(c).\] If \(C=\varnothing\), report that no selection is available. Otherwise the injective final component makes \(c^*\) unique. Replay must use the same key components, orientations, numerical representations, and identifiers; an unspecified container iteration order is not a tie-breaking policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order every eligible alternative by a fixed lexicographic key ending in a unique identifier; choose its unique minimum, or report no selection for an empty set.
knowledge_statements.title: Tie-Breaking Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite lexicographic selection algorithm is mathematically precise, its unique final identifier gives a unique minimizer, and algorithm fits the Tie-Breaking Policies leaf. However, no citation supports its use as a tree-search replay policy or the stated requirements on numerical representations and identifiers. The supplied inventory has no locator addressing deterministic tie breaking.

children.title: Deterministic Replay Controls
children.top_down_role: Execution controls used to reproduce a prior search trajectory.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript comparison that certifies exact replay and localizes its first observable failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((r_0,\ldots,r_{m-1})\) be canonical encodings of a reference transcript. Comparing each replay emission \(o_t\) with \(r_t\) before the next dependent step, and comparing canonical terminal-state encodings, certifies exact transcript replay when all comparisons agree. The least mismatching index identifies the first observable divergence but does not by itself identify its cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical event-by-event comparison certifies exact replay and locates the first observable mismatch.
assumptions_latex: Event and terminal-state encodings are canonical and compared exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall t<m,\ o_t=r_t)\land S_m=S_m^{\mathrm{ref}}\Longrightarrow\text{exact recorded replay}.
knowledge_statements.title: Stepwise Replay Validation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient state-and-input controls for exact replay of a discrete search execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Model each replay step by \((S_{t+1},o_t)=F(S_t,i_t;R)\), where \(i_t\) is the recorded external input and \(o_t\) the emitted event. A replay record \(R\) is sufficient if it fixes the initial state, transition implementation and parameters, numerical mode, randomness, deterministic selection rules, scheduling decisions, callback results, and every other future-relevant external input. Equal sufficient records and equal initial states then determine equal states and emitted events at every completed step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact replay requires a deterministic transition system plus a record of every initial-state component, scheduling choice, and external input that can affect it.
assumptions_latex: The transition map is deterministic for fixed state, input, implementation, and replay record.
Every nondeterministic or environmental input consumed by a transition is recorded or deterministically reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_0=S'_0\land R=R'\land i_t=i'_t\ \forall t\Longrightarrow S_t=S'_t\land o_t=o'_t\ \forall t.

notation.meaning: solver state before replay step t
recorded input consumed at step t

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Deterministic Replay Record

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Future-state sufficiency condition for restarting replay at an intermediate point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A checkpoint \(C_t\) is replay-complete when equality of checkpoints and subsequent recorded inputs forces equality of all later states and emitted events under the same deterministic implementation. Frontier data alone is insufficient whenever omitted pseudocosts, pools, random-generator state, incumbent metadata, callback state, or pending messages can affect a later transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intermediate checkpoint must retain every state component capable of changing future execution.
assumptions_latex: The continuation transition system is deterministic once its complete state and recorded inputs are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_t=C'_t\land i_{t:}=i'_{t:}\Longrightarrow S_{t:}=S'_{t:}\land o_{t:}=o'_{t:}.
knowledge_statements.title: Replay-Complete Checkpoint

assumptions_latex: The solver is modeled as a state transition system with initial state \(S_0\), event sequence \((e_t)\), and deterministic transition map \(T\).
All external inputs required by a transition can be recorded and restored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equal replay-control records imply equal states and emitted events at every replay step.

notation.meaning: Solver state after t replay events.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Deterministic replay requires fixed initial data, recorded nondeterministic inputs, deterministic ordering, and deterministic transitions.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient controls for exact replay of a discrete tree-search transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A replay-control record \(R\) is sufficient when it fixes \(S_0\), model and parameter versions, random seeds, numerical mode, worker count and scheduling order, deterministic tie-breaking keys, callback outputs, and every external input consumed by a transition. Replay applies \(S_{t+1}=T(S_t,e_t;R)\) and validates each emitted event against the recorded event. If two executions use equal sufficient records \(R=R'\), equal transition implementations, and equal initial states, then induction of the transition rule requires \(S_t=S'_t\) and \(e_t=e'_t\) for every completed step \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact replay requires fixing initial data, versions, numerical and scheduling modes, tie breaks, randomness, callbacks, and external inputs, then validating every emitted event.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Replay Controls

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is an appropriate knowledge kind, but the claimed event equality does not follow unambiguously from the displayed transition model: \(e_t\) appears both as an input to the transition and as an emitted event, while the deterministic emission and scheduling maps are not separately defined. The asserted completeness of the replay-control list is also implementation-dependent. A source and a precise replay semantics are needed before the mathematical version can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Event-Ordering Stability
children.top_down_role: Repeatability of callback, queue, synchronization, or worker event ordering.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Causality-preserving serialization condition for a concurrent replay history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A concurrent history has a unique serialized replay when each event has a defined linearization point and a deterministic rule selects one total order \(\prec\) extending the history's happens-before relation. If conflicting events are unordered by happens-before and no replay rule orders them, the history alone does not determine a unique transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concurrent replay is stable when causality is extended by a deterministic rule to one total event order.
assumptions_latex: Event transitions are deterministic.
The selected total order respects every happens-before constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e\rightarrow f\Longrightarrow e\prec f,\qquad \prec\text{ uniquely fixed}\Longrightarrow\text{unique serialized event order}.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Linearization Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-event pair whose reversal changes generated children.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let event \(e\) install a feasible incumbent \(U=5\), and let event \(f\) process a node of valid lower bound \(L=7\), generating children whenever the current incumbent does not prune it. From a state without a finite incumbent, \(f\) before \(e\) generates children, whereas \(e\) before \(f\) prunes the node. Hence the two events do not commute.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Installing an incumbent before rather than after processing a dominated node changes whether children are generated.
assumptions_latex: Minimization pruning uses \(L\ge U\).
The node is otherwise eligible for branching.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_e(T_f(S))\ne T_f(T_e(S)).
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent–Expansion Noncommutativity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replay invariance under admissible adjacent exchanges of deterministic events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose two finite schedules differ through adjacent exchanges of event pairs \((e,f)\). An exchange at state \(S\) is admissible when both events remain enabled in either order and \(T_f(T_e(S))=T_e(T_f(S))\). If every exchange is admissible at the state where it occurs, the schedules reach the same final state. Equal event multisets alone do not imply equal states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schedules related only by enabled commuting swaps have the same result; equal event sets without commutation do not suffice.
assumptions_latex: Each event acts through a deterministic transition map.
Every exchanged pair remains enabled in both local orders.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_f(T_e(S))=T_e(T_f(S))\text{ at every exchange}\Longrightarrow S_{\mathrm{final}}=S'_{\mathrm{final}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Commuting-Event Schedule Equivalence

assumptions_latex: Events act on solver states through deterministic maps \(T_e\).
The replay scheduler uses a fixed total order \(\prec\) for noncommuting enabled events.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Permitted reorderings yield the same final state when every inverted event pair commutes on each state where the pair is exchanged.

notation.meaning: State transition associated with event e.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Equality under adjacent swaps of commuting deterministic transitions is a standard trace-equivalence property.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replay invariance under fixed ordering or swaps of commuting solver events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two finite event sequences contain the same events and differ only by adjacent exchanges of pairs \((e,f)\). An exchange is admissible at state \(S\) only if both events are enabled and \(T_f(T_e(S))=T_e(T_f(S))\). If every exchange transforming one sequence into the other is admissible at the state where it occurs, then both sequences produce the same final state from \(S_0\). Consequently, event ordering is stable when all unordered concurrent pairs commute; otherwise replay must serialize them by the fixed total order \(\prec\). Equal event multisets alone do not ensure equal search states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two event schedules have the same result when they differ only by swaps of concurrently enabled commuting events; noncommuting events require a fixed total order.
knowledge_statements.title: Event-Ordering Stability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The adjacent-swap statement is a precise standard trace-equivalence property, plain text and LaTeX agree, and property fits the leaf. No cited source supports the solver-event interpretation, enabledness conditions, or application to deterministic tree-search replay, and none of the inventory locators addresses event-order semantics.

children.title: Replay Divergence Sources
children.top_down_role: Numerical, scheduling, state, or environment differences that alter replayed trajectories.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp discontinuity of best-bound selection under arbitrarily small numerical perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\eta>0\), let two open nodes satisfy \(L(a)=0\), \(L(b)=\eta/4\) in one execution and \(L'(a)=0\), \(L'(b)=-\eta/4\) in another. The bound vectors differ by \(\eta/2<\eta\) in maximum norm, yet best-bound selection chooses \(a\) first in the first execution and \(b\) first in the second. If the resulting processing events do not commute, the later transcripts need not reconverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrarily small perturbation near a bound tie can reverse node selection and initiate persistent replay divergence.
assumptions_latex: Best-bound search selects a node of minimum stored lower bound.
Processing the two nodes can emit noncommuting successor events.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\eta>0\ \exists L,L':\ \|L-L'\|_\infty<\eta\land\operatorname*{arg\,min}L\ne\operatorname*{arg\,min}L'.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Tie Selection Divergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replay failure caused by unrecorded mutable state or environmental input.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a transition consumes a value \(h_t\) not determined by the visible checkpoint and replay record. If two admissible values \(h_t\ne h'_t\) satisfy \(F(S_t,i_t,h_t)\ne F(S_t,i_t,h'_t)\), equality of the visible checkpoint and recorded inputs cannot guarantee equality beyond step \(t\). Such hidden values may include unrecorded randomness, callbacks, iteration order, pending messages, clock input, or environment-dependent numerical results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any omitted input or state that can change a transition defeats an exact replay guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The hidden value is not reconstructible from the replay record.
At least two admissible hidden values yield different transitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_t=C'_t\not\Rightarrow(S_{t+1},o_t)=(S'_{t+1},o'_t).
knowledge_statements.title: Hidden-State Replay Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract exhaustive classification of the first unequal deterministic replay step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For deterministic steps \((S_{t+1},o_t)=F(S_t,i_t)\), two runs cannot first diverge at step \(t\) when their entering states, consumed inputs, and transition implementations are equal. Therefore a first divergence requires a difference in entering state, consumed input, or implementation; an unequal entering state must itself originate at an earlier state-update or event-order difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first replay mismatch must arise from different entering state, input, implementation, or an earlier event-order difference.
assumptions_latex: The transition implementation is deterministic for fixed state and input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (S_t,i_t,F)=(S'_t,i'_t,F')\Longrightarrow(S_{t+1},o_t)=(S'_{t+1},o'_t).
knowledge_statements.title: First-Divergence Classification

assumptions_latex: Best-bound search selects the open node having the smallest stored lower bound.
Processing different selected nodes can generate different noncommuting successor events or subtrees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Arbitrarily small bound perturbations can change the first selected node and, when the resulting successor events do not commute, can cause persistent transcript divergence.

notation.meaning: Stored lower bound of a node.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Discontinuity of an argmin decision at a tie is a standard failure mechanism for deterministic search replay.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp replay failure at a best-bound selection tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\eta>0\), consider two open nodes \(a\) and \(b\). In one execution set \(L(a)=0\) and \(L(b)=\eta/4\); in another set \(L'(a)=0\) and \(L'(b)=-\eta/4\). The bound vectors differ by \(\eta/2<\eta\) in maximum norm, yet best-bound selection chooses \(a\) first in the first execution and \(b\) first in the second. If processing \(a\) and \(b\) emits different noncommuting successor events, the subsequent transcripts need not reconverge. Thus deterministic replay can fail under arbitrarily small numerical perturbations at a selection boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrarily small perturbation can reverse two nearly tied node bounds; if processing the selected nodes produces noncommuting events, the replay transcripts need not reconverge.
knowledge_statements.title: Replay Divergence Sources
